```python
pbr['Specular.RoughnessChannel'] = 'Luminance'
pbr['Coat.Coat'] = 0.2
pbr['Coat.Roughness'] = 0.05

cube.FrontMaterialInput = pbr.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- Metals: set Metalness to 1, and use Base Color for the metal's colour. Specular Color is normally left white.
- Roughness textures are read through the channel selector. `"Luminance"` converts a colour texture to grey, and
  `"R"` is the default.
- Ambient Occlusion is a strength. Connect an occlusion map to `Base.OcclusionMtl` and leave the strength at 1.
- Subsurface Radius sets how far light scatters under the surface. Keep it small for skin or wax, and large for milk-like
  materials.

**See also:** CookTorrance, Blinn, Phong, Reflect, Fast Noise Texture, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Override 3D (`Override3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Ov · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Changes properties of everything in the scene it is connected to, without editing each object. Every override has a
"Do" checkbox that switches it on; the value next to it is then applied to the whole incoming scene. Use it to hide,
matte or re-light a group, or to give a group a new Object or Material ID.

**Use for:** hiding or matting a group, forcing a wireframe, setting lighting or shadow flags for a group, and
assigning Object IDs for later use.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Do Wireframe | `Wireframe.DoWireframe` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the wireframe override on. |
| Wireframe | `Wireframe.Wireframe` | Checkbox | 0 | Forces wireframe display when overridden. |
| Do Visible | `Visibility.DoVisible` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the visibility override on. |
| Visible | `Visibility.IsVisible` | Checkbox | 1 | Visibility applied when overridden. |
| Do Unseen By Cameras | `Visibility.DoIsUnseenByCameras` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the camera visibility override on. |
| Unseen by Cameras | `Visibility.IsUnseenByCameras` | Checkbox | 0 | Camera visibility applied when overridden. |
| Do Affected By Lights | `Lighting.DoAffectedByLights` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the light response override on. |
| Affected by Lights | `Lighting.IsAffectedByLights` | Checkbox | 1 | Light response applied when overridden. |
| Do Shadow Caster | `Lighting.DoShadowCaster` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the shadow caster override on. |
| Shadow Caster | `Lighting.IsShadowCaster` | Checkbox | 1 | Shadow casting applied when overridden. |
| Do Shadow Receiver | `Lighting.DoShadowReceiver` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the shadow receiver override on. |
| Shadow Receiver | `Lighting.IsShadowReceiver` | Checkbox | 1 | Shadow receiving applied when overridden. |
| Do Matte | `Matte.DoMatte` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the matte override on. |
| Is Matte | `Matte.IsMatte` | Checkbox | 0 | Matte state applied when overridden. |
| Do Object ID | `ObjectID.DoObjectID` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the Object ID override on. |
| Object ID | `ObjectID.NewObjectID` | Number | 1 (1–30) | Object ID applied when overridden. |
| Do Material ID | `MaterialID.DoMaterialID` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the Material ID override on. |
| Material ID | `MaterialID.NewMaterialID` | Number | 1 (1–30) | Material ID applied when overridden. |
| Do Blend Mode | `BlendMode.BlendMode` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the blend override on. |
| Hardware blend | `BlendMode.GL.BlendMode` | ID combo | `"Additive"` | Hardware blend applied when overridden. |
| Software blend | `BlendMode.SW.BlendMode` | ID combo | `"Additive"` | Software blend applied when overridden. |

### Example

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'
ov = comp.AddTool('Override3D')
ov.SceneInput = title.Output
ov['ObjectID.DoObjectID'] = 1
ov['ObjectID.NewObjectID'] = 7
ov['Wireframe.DoWireframe'] = 1
ov['Wireframe.Wireframe'] = 1
```

**See also:** Transform 3D, Renderer 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Phong (`MtlPhong`)

**Category:** 3D Material · **Short name:** 3Ph · **Inputs:** `Diffuse.Color.Material` (orange), `Specular.Color.Material` (green), `Specular.Intensity.Material` (magenta), `Specular.Exponent.Material` (teal), `Bumpmap.Material` (white) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

A basic illumination material with a highlight similar to Blinn's. Phong is usually chosen for shiny, polished plastic.
Its diffuse, specular and bump inputs work as they do on Blinn, so a texture can drive the colour, the highlight colour,
the highlight strength and the highlight falloff.

**Use for:** polished plastic, glossy objects and motion graphics surfaces where a clean, sharp highlight is wanted.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diffuse Color | `Diffuse.Color.Red`, `Diffuse.Color.Green`, `Diffuse.Color.Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Base colour. Multiplied by the Diffuse Color texture. |
| Alpha | `Diffuse.Color.Alpha` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Alpha of the surface. |
| Opacity | `Diffuse.Opacity` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Transparency of the surface. |
| Specular Color | `Specular.Color.Red`, `Specular.Color.Green`, `Specular.Color.Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour of the highlight. Multiplied by the Specular Color texture. |
| Specular Intensity | `Specular.Intensity` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Strength of the highlight. Multiplied by the alpha of the Specular Intensity texture. |
| Specular Exponent | `Specular.Exponent` | Number | 50 (slider 1–100) | Falloff of the highlight. Higher values give a smaller, sharper highlight. Multiplied by the alpha of the Specular Exponent texture. |
| Transmittance, Receives, Two Sided, PBR, Material ID | see Common Controls → 3D materials and textures | | | Shared with the other shading materials. |

### Example

A white polished plastic with a sharp highlight whose strength is driven by a Gradient:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

ramp = comp.AddTool('TexGradient')
ramp.Gradient = comp.Gradient({0.0: [0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1], 1.0: [1, 1, 1, 1]})

phong = comp.AddTool('MtlPhong')
phong['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.95
phong['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.95
phong['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.95
phong['Specular.Exponent'] = 90
phong['Specular.Intensity.Material'] = ramp.MaterialOutput

cube.FrontMaterialInput = phong.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- Specular Intensity and Specular Exponent read the **alpha** channel of their textures, the same as Blinn. Put the
  pattern in alpha.
- Turn on Enable PBR Material for a physically based highlight. This changes how the highlight is shaded, so re-check
  Specular Exponent after switching.
- Raise Specular Exponent for a glossier look, and lower it for a broader, softer highlight.

**See also:** Blinn, Cook-Torrance, OpenPBR, Gradient, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Point Light (`LightPoint`)

**Category:** 3D Light · **Short name:** 3PL · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (optional 3D scene) · **Output:** `Output` (3D Data)

A light that shines out in all directions from a point in space, like a bulb or a candle. Its position comes from the
Transform controls (see Common Controls → 3D objects). Decay makes the light fall off with distance, and the shadow
controls set how it casts shadows.

**Use for:** practical lights in a scene, glows around objects, and any local light that should fade with distance
rather than light the whole frame.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | `Enabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the light on or off. |
| Color | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour of the light. |
| Intensity | `Intensity` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Brightness of the light. |
| Decay Type | `DecayType` | Multi-button | 0: No Decay, 1: Linear, 2: Quadratic | How the light fades with distance. No Decay keeps full strength at any distance. |
| Decay Rate | `DecayRate` | Number | 1 (slider 0.001–1) | Strength of the fall-off. Used only when Decay Type is Linear or Quadratic. |
| Enable Shadows | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowsEnabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Casts shadows from this light. |
| Shadow Density | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowDensity` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Opacity of the shadow. |
| Shadow Map Size | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowMapSize` | Number | 2048 (16–16384) | Resolution of the shadow map. |
| Softness | `ShadowLightInputs3D.SoftnessType` | ID combo | `"None"` | `"None"`, `"Constant"`, `"Variable"` or `"VariableFast"`. |
| Constant Softness | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ConstantSoftness` | Number | 0.02 (0–0.1) | Edge softness when Softness is `"Constant"`. |
| Min Softness | `ShadowLightInputs3D.MinSoftness` | Number | 0 (0–30) | Minimum edge softness in the variable modes. |

The other shadow controls (`ShadowLightInputs3D.*`: colour, proxy size, biases, sampling quality, clipping range and
so on) are the same as on the Directional Light. See that section.

### Example

A warm lamp that fades with the square of the distance, with a soft shadow, placed beside a cube:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

lamp = comp.AddTool('LightPoint')
lamp.Red = 1.0
lamp.Green = 0.75
lamp.Blue = 0.45
lamp.Intensity = 2.0
lamp.DecayType = 2                        # Quadratic
lamp.DecayRate = 0.4
lamp['Transform3DOp.Translate.X'] = 0.8
lamp['Transform3DOp.Translate.Y'] = 0.6
lamp['Transform3DOp.Translate.Z'] = -0.5
lamp['ShadowLightInputs3D.SoftnessType'] = 'Constant'
lamp['ShadowLightInputs3D.ConstantSoftness'] = 0.03

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = cube.Output
merge.SceneInput2 = lamp.Output
```

### Tips

- The attenuation is `1 / (1 + DecayRate × d)` for Linear and `1 / (1 + DecayRate × d²)` for Quadratic, where `d` is the
  distance from the light. No Decay gives a constant level at every distance.
- Decay Rate is hidden when Decay Type is No Decay. Set Decay Type first.
- A Point light with shadows on casts a shadow in every direction, so it costs more to render than a Directional light.
  Turn shadows off for lights that don't need them.

**See also:** Spot Light, Directional Light, Ambient Light, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## PointCloud 3D (`PointCloud3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3PC · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Draws a set of points, such as the points from a camera track, as small crosses or dots. The points are display
geometry: they are useful for checking a track or a scene, and can be made renderable.

**Use for:** showing a Camera Tracker point cloud in the scene, checking tracked positions, and marking features.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Locator Style | `LocatorStyle` | ID multi-button | `"Cross"` | `"Cross"` or `"Point"`. |
| Cross Size X | `Cross.Size.X` | Number | 0.25 (0–1) | Size of each cross along X. |
| Cross Size Y | `Cross.Size.Y` | Number | 0.25 (0–1) | Size of each cross along Y. |
| Cross Size Z | `Cross.Size.Z` | Number | 0.25 (0–1) | Size of each cross along Z. |
| Point Size | `Point.Size` | Number | 8 (1–12) | Size of each point. |
| Antialiasing | `Point.Antialiasing` | Checkbox | 1 | Smooths the points. |
| Density | `Density` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Amount of the points shown. |
| Color Red, Green, Blue | `ColorRed`, `ColorGreen`, `ColorBlue` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Colour of the points. |
| Use Per-Point Colors | `UsePerPointColors` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the colour stored with each point. |
| Make Renderable | `MakeRenderable` | Checkbox | 0 | Lets the points appear in a render. |
| Overlay | `RenderAsOverlay` | Checkbox | 0 | Draws the points on top of the image. |

### Example

```python
pts = comp.AddTool('PointCloud3D')
pts['LocatorStyle'] = 'Point'
pts['Point.Size'] = 6
pts['UsePerPointColors'] = 1

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = pts.Output
```

**See also:** Locator 3D, Camera 3D, Merge 3D.

## Projector 3D (`LightProjector`)

**Category:** 3D Light · **Short name:** 3Pj · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (optional 3D scene), `ProjectiveImage` (image) · **Output:** `Output` (3D Data)

Projects an image onto the scene from a point, like a slide projector. In Light mode the image adds light to the surfaces
it hits, and its alpha channel is ignored. In Ambient Light mode it adds ambient light instead. In Texture mode it doesn't
light anything: it stores the projection so that a Catcher material can apply it as a texture.

**Use for:** projecting a plate or a graphic onto geometry, such as a set extension or a light pattern. Use Texture mode
with a Catcher when the projected alpha must cut out part of the geometry.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | `Enabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the projector on or off. |
| Color | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Tint applied to the projected image, in Light and Ambient modes. |
| Intensity | `Intensity` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Brightness of the projection. |
| Projective Image | `ProjectiveImage` | Image input | none | The image to project. |
| Projection Mode | `ProjectionMode` | Multi-button | 0: Light, 1: Ambient Light, 2: Texture | Light adds light from the image, Ambient Light adds it as ambient light, and Texture stores it for a Catcher. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 40 (slider 0–179.9) | Field of view of the projection, in degrees. |
| Fit Method | `Fit` | ID combo | `"Inside"` | `"Inside"`, `"Width"`, `"Height"`, `"Outside"`, `"Stretch"`. How the image fits the projection frame. |
| Projector ID | `ProjectorID` | Number | 1 (1–10) | Identifies this projector. A Catcher can accept only projections with a matching ID. |
| Decay Type | `DecayType` | Multi-button | 0: No Decay, 1: Linear, 2: Quadratic | Fall-off with distance, in Light mode. |
| Enable Shadows | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowsEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Casts shadows from the projection. Off by default on a new projector. |

The other shadow controls (`ShadowLightInputs3D.*`) match the Directional Light. See that section.

### Example

A logo projected in Texture mode onto a cube, through a Catcher and a Blinn material:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

proj = comp.AddTool('LightProjector')
proj.ProjectiveImage = media_in.Output
proj.ProjectionMode = 2                    # Texture
proj.Angle = 50
proj.Fit = 'Inside'

catcher = comp.AddTool('TexCatcher')

blinn = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
blinn['Diffuse.Color.Material'] = catcher.MaterialOutput

cube.FrontMaterialInput = blinn.MaterialOutput
merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = cube.Output
merge.SceneInput2 = proj.Output
```

### Tips

- In Light mode the image's alpha is ignored. In Texture mode, with a Catcher on the receiving surface, the alpha does
  cut out the geometry behind it.
- The Catcher must be on the receiving material, and this projector must be in the scene with its mode set to Texture.
  Otherwise the surface becomes transparent.
- Projector ID is used to choose between several projectors. Projector Priority is not documented.

**See also:** Catcher, Spot Light, Camera 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Reflect (`MtlReflect`)

**Category:** 3D Material · **Short name:** 3RR · **Inputs:** `BackgroundMaterial` (orange), `Reflection.Color.Material` (white), `Reflection.Intensity.Material` (white), `Refraction.Tint.Material` (white), `Bumpmap.Material` (white) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Adds environment reflections and refractions to a surface. The reflected image comes from a colour input, usually a
Sphere Map or a Cube Map, and the strength of the reflection depends on the viewing angle. The Background Material is
the surface that the reflection is added to, such as a Blinn. The material can be used alone, or fed into the diffuse
input of another material.

**Use for:** chrome, glass and glossy surfaces that reflect a set or sky, and refraction through transparent objects.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strength Variability | `Reflection.StrengthVariability` | Multi-button | 1: By Angle (0: Constant, 1: By Angle) | `Constant` gives one reflection strength everywhere. `By Angle` varies it with the surface's angle to the camera. |
| Constant Strength | `Reflection.ConstantStrength` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Reflection strength, when Strength Variability is Constant. |
| Glancing Strength | `Reflection.GlancingStrength` | Number | 0.8 (slider 0–1) | Reflection strength on surfaces seen at a glancing angle, when By Angle. |
| Face On Strength | `Reflection.FaceOnStrength` | Number | 0 (slider 0–1) | Reflection strength on surfaces facing the camera, when By Angle. |
| Falloff | `Reflection.Falloff` | Number | 2 (slider 0–4) | How sharply the strength changes between Face On and Glancing, when By Angle. |
| Separate RGB Indices | `Refraction.RefractiveIndex.SeparateRGBIndices` | Checkbox | 0 | Replaces the single Refractive Index with one index per colour channel. |
| Refractive Index | `Refraction.RefractiveIndex.RGB` | Number | 1.333 (slider 0.01–1) | How much the environment bends when seen through the surface. Used when Separate RGB Indices is off. |
| Red, Green, Blue Index | `Refraction.RefractiveIndex.Red`, `Refraction.RefractiveIndex.Green`, `Refraction.RefractiveIndex.Blue` | Number | 1.333 (slider 0.01–1) | Index for each colour channel, when Separate RGB Indices is on. |
| Refraction Tint | `Refraction.Tint.Red`, `Refraction.Tint.Green`, `Refraction.Tint.Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour the refracted image is multiplied by. |
| Material ID | `MaterialID` | Number | 2 on a new tool (slider 1–30) | Identifies the material for the MatID channel. See Common Controls → 3D materials and textures. |

### Example

Chrome on a cube, reflecting a Sphere Map environment, with a dark Blinn as the surface underneath:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

env = comp.AddTool('SphereMap')
env.Image = media_in.Output

base = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
base['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.05
base['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.05
base['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.05

chrome = comp.AddTool('MtlReflect')
chrome.BackgroundMaterial = base.MaterialOutput
chrome['Reflection.Color.Material'] = env.MaterialOutput
chrome['Reflection.GlancingStrength'] = 1.0
chrome['Reflection.FaceOnStrength'] = 0.4

cube.FrontMaterialInput = chrome.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- The Reflection Color input is the environment. The Sphere Map tool makes an environment from an equirectangular
  image, and Cube Map does the same from six faces or a cross.
- Reflection Intensity multiplies the strength by its alpha channel. Use an alpha-based mask to limit where the
  reflection shows.
- For a mirror-like finish, try By Angle with Glancing near 1 and a moderate Face On value, such as 0.4.
- Refraction Tint colours the refracted image, the same way a tinted glass does.
- Refraction only has an effect where the Background Material has an opacity below 1, as the manual notes.

**See also:** Sphere Map, Cube Map, Blinn, OpenPBR, Falloff, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Relief Map (`ReliefMap`)

**Category:** 3D Texture · **Short name:** 3RM · **Inputs:** `BackgroundInput` (material, yellow in the manual), `ReliefMapInput` (image) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Adds height-based detail to a surface by eroding it with a relief map. Unlike a bump map, the relief is real enough that
the surface can shadow itself, so the detail picks up natural light and occlusion. The Background Input is the material
the relief is applied to, and the Relief Map Input is an image that holds the relief data. The manual makes that image
with a separate CreateReliefMap tool, which is not documented here. The RGB channels of the relief image hold normals,
and its alpha holds the height.

**Use for:** fine, raised or recessed detail such as engraved text, stone, brick and tiles, where a bump map looks flat.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Depth Scale | `DepthScale` | Number | 0.03 (slider 0–0.2) | Overall depth of the relief. |
| Lock U/V | `InLockUV` | Checkbox | 1 | On scales U and V together. Off lets you set the frequency of each separately. |
| Frequency U | `FrequencyU` | Number | 1 (slider 0.1–10) | Repeat of the relief across U. |
| Frequency V | `FrequencyV` | Number | 1 (slider 0.1–10) | Repeat of the relief across V. Used when Lock U/V is off. |
| Map Type | `MapType` | ID combo | `"Relief"` | `"Relief"` or `"Cone"`. Cone looks better and shades faster, at a cost in performance. |
| Quality | `Quality` | Number | 1 (slider 0.5–10) | Detail of the result. Most visible with Relief. |

### Example

Relief detail from an image over a Blinn base:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

base = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
base['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.7
base['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.6
base['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.5

relief = comp.AddTool('ReliefMap')
relief.BackgroundInput = base.MaterialOutput
relief.ReliefMapInput = media_in.Output
relief.DepthScale = 0.05
relief.MapType = 'Cone'
relief.Quality = 4

cube.FrontMaterialInput = relief.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- Set Map Type to Cone for the best surface, and raise Quality if the edges look rough.
- Keep Depth Scale small. Large values make the relief look like it is floating away from the surface.
- Use Frequency U and V to tile the relief across the surface without changing the image.

**See also:** BumpMap, Blinn, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Renderer 3D (`Renderer3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Rn · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image, or DeepImage)

Converts a 3D scene into a 2D image, seen from a camera in the scene or from a default perspective view. Every 3D scene
must end in a Renderer 3D. Its output is an ordinary image, so it can be merged, graded and tracked like any other.
The renderer type decides how the image is made, and the controls below the renderer type belong to that renderer:
the Software renderer runs on the CPU and is the reference for soft shadows and full lighting, while the OpenGL
renderers run on the GPU and give supersampling and depth of field. Motion blur and the other settings common to most
tools are on the Settings tab (see Common Controls).

**Use for:** the final render of any 3D scene, extra channels for compositing (Z, normals, object and material IDs),
projecting an image onto geometry, and depth of field on a camera view.

**Outputs and channels:** the RGBA image is always produced. Extra channels (Z, Normal, ObjectID and so on) are switched on
in the renderer's Channels list and are written into the image, where Channel Booleans, Merge and the 3D-aware tools read them.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Camera | `CameraSelector` | ID combo | `"Default"` | The camera to render from. `"Default"` uses the first camera in the scene, or a default perspective view if there is none. Other entries are the names of cameras connected to the scene, such as `"Camera3D1"`. |
| Renderer Type | `RendererType` | ID combo | `"RendererSoftware"` | `"RendererOpenGL"`, `"RendererOpenGLUV"` or `"RendererSoftware"`. Changes the controls shown below it. |
| Eye | `Eye` | Multi-button | 0: Mono (1: Left, 2: Right, 3: Stack, 4: Layers) | Stereo output. Mono ignores the camera's stereo settings. |
| Output Type | `OutputType` | ID multi-button | `"Image"` | `"Image"`, or `"DeepImage"` for deep compositing. |
| Process Mode | `ProcessMode` | ID combo | `"FullFrames"` | Frame or field processing: `"FullFrames"`, `"NTSC"`, `"PAL"`, `"PALReversed"`, `"NTSCReversed"`. |
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 1920, 1080 | Output size, used when Auto Resolution (`UseFrameFormatSettings`) is off. |
| Depth | `Depth` | Multi-button | 0: Default (1: int8, 2: int16, 3: float16, 4: float32) | Bit depth of the output. The OpenGL renderer respects it, which can be slow at int16 and float32. |
| Software channels | `RendererSoftware.Channels.RGBA`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.Z`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.Coverage`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.BgColor`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.Normal`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.TexCoord0`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.ObjectID`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.MaterialID`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.WorldCoord`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.Vector`, `RendererSoftware.Channels.BackVector` | Checkbox | RGBA 1, others 0 | Extra channels to write. RGBA cannot be turned off. |
| Software: Enable Lighting | `RendererSoftware.LightingEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Lights the objects with the scene's lights. Off means every object renders black if there are no lights. |
| Software: Enable Shadows | `RendererSoftware.ShadowsEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Casts shadows from shadow-casting lights. |
| OpenGL: Enable Lighting | `RendererOpenGL.LightingEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | As for the Software renderer. The OpenGL renderer can't make soft shadows. |
| OpenGL: Enable Shadows | `RendererOpenGL.ShadowsEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Hard shadows only. |
| OpenGL: Transparency | `RendererOpenGL.TransparencySorting` | Combo | 0: Z Buffer (fast) (1: Sorted (accurate), 2: Quick Sort) | How transparent surfaces are ordered. Sorted is most accurate and slowest. |
| OpenGL: Enable Accumulation Effects | `RendererOpenGL.EnableAccumEffects` | Checkbox | 0 | Renders several passes for depth of field and light jitter. |
| OpenGL: Depth of Field | `RendererOpenGL.EnableAccumDepthOfField` | Checkbox | 1 | Uses the camera's Focal Plane for depth of field when accumulation is on. |
| OpenGL: Quality | `RendererOpenGL.AccumQuality` | Number | 32 (0–250) | Number of accumulation passes. |
| OpenGL: Amount of DoF Blur | `RendererOpenGL.DoFBlur` | Number | 0.2 (0–1) | Strength of the depth of field blur. |
| OpenGL: Anti-Aliasing preset | `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.SelectedPreset` | ID combo | `"Color"` | `"Color"` or `"Aux"`. Each preset sets supersampling or multisampling for colour and for auxiliary channels. |
| OpenGL: Supersampling rate | `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.Color.Supersampling.LowQuality.Rate`, `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.Color.Supersampling.HighQuality.Rate` | Number | 1 and 3 (1–16) | Samples per pixel per axis, for low and high quality. |
| OpenGL: Supersampling filter | `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.Color.Supersampling.Filter.Type` | ID combo | `"GaussianSSFilter3D"` | The filter applied to the supersamples. |
| OpenGL: Multisampling | `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.Color.Multisampling.LowQuality.SampleCount`, `RendererOpenGL.AntiAliasing.Presets.Color.Multisampling.HighQuality.SampleCount` | Combo | 2 (4 samples), 3 (8 samples) | Hardware multisample count, for low and high quality. |
| Software: Cryptomatte | `RendererSoftware.EnableCryptomatte` | Checkbox | 0 | Also outputs Cryptomatte layers and metadata, which the Cryptomatte tool decodes into mattes per object or material. |
| Stereo: Stack Vertical, Swap | `StackVertical`, `Swap` | Checkbox | 0 | Stacks the eyes vertically rather than side by side, and swaps left and right. Used with Eye set to Stack. |

Use Common Controls → Settings tab for Motion Blur, Quality, Shutter Angle and Sample Spread. Use the Effect Mask input to
limit the renderer's output. Its alpha is used by default.

### Example

Renders a Text 3D title with a camera and a light. The software renderer is used for lighting and a Z channel is written:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'

cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')
light = comp.AddTool('LightDirectional')

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = title.Output
scene.SceneInput2 = cam.Output
scene.SceneInput3 = light.Output

render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
render.CameraSelector = cam.Name
render['RendererSoftware.LightingEnabled'] = 1
render['RendererSoftware.ShadowsEnabled'] = 1
render['RendererSoftware.Channels.Z'] = 1
render.Depth = 3                       # float16
```

### Tips

- **Lighting is off by default.** A scene with lights renders with no lighting until `LightingEnabled` is on.
  Shadows need lighting, and soft shadows need the Software renderer.
- **Renderer choice:** use Software for final quality and for network renders. Use OpenGL for fast previews and for
  depth of field, which Software doesn't have. OpenGL output can vary between graphics cards and drivers.
- **Channels for compositing:** Z and ObjectID are the usual extras. The Z channel has no anti-aliasing, so edges can
  look hard in depth-based effects. Enable only the channels you use: each one costs memory and time.
- **Projection and plates:** a camera projection (set on the Camera 3D) is light, so it is only visible when the
  Renderer 3D has lighting enabled. Use the rendered result over the plate with a Merge, after matching the camera.
- **Deep output** (`OutputType` `"DeepImage"`) gives a deep image for the Deep tools. The rest of the controls are
  the same.

**See also:** Merge 3D, Camera 3D, Text 3D, Shape 3D, Image Plane 3D, Override 3D, Merge, Channel Booleans, Common
Controls → Settings tab.

## Replace Material 3D (`ReplaceMaterial3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Rpl · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, required), `MaterialInput` (material or image) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Replaces the material on every object in the scene with the material connected to `MaterialInput`. Each of the four
channels (red, green, blue and alpha) of the new material can be kept, replaced, blended or multiplied with the old one,
so a single channel can take a different look. The object and material IDs limit which objects change. Lights and cameras
pass through unchanged.

**Use for:** giving a Text 3D a chrome or glass material (Text 3D has no material input of its own), swapping the look of a
whole imported model, or changing one object's material by its Object ID.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable | `Enable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the replacement on. Off passes the scene through unchanged. |
| Red Mode, Green Mode, Blue Mode, Alpha Mode | `ReplaceMode.RedMode`, `ReplaceMode.GreenMode`, `ReplaceMode.BlueMode`, `ReplaceMode.AlphaMode` | Multi-button | 1 | How each channel is handled: `0: Keep` (the old material's channel stays), `1: Replace`, `2: Blend`, `3: Multiply`. |
| Limit by Object ID | `LimitByObjectID` | Checkbox | 0 | Only objects with the chosen Object ID or IDs change. |
| Limiting Mode (object) | `ObjectIDLimitMode` | Multi-button | 0 | `0: Single`, `1: Range`. |
| Object ID, Min / Max Object ID | `ObjectID`, `MinObjectID`, `MaxObjectID` | Number | 1, 1, 10 (1–30) | The Object ID, or the range, that changes. |
| Limit by Material ID | `LimitByMaterialID` | Checkbox | 0 | Only objects with the chosen Material ID or IDs change. |
| Limiting Mode (material) | `MaterialIDLimitMode` | Multi-button | 0 | `0: Single`, `1: Range`. |
| Material ID, Min / Max Material ID | `MaterialID`, `MinMaterialID`, `MaxMaterialID` | Number | 1, 1, 10 (1–30) | The Material ID, or the range, that changes. |
| Material Input | `MaterialInput` | Material (MtlGraph3D) | | The new material. A 2D image here is used as the diffuse texture of the basic material. A 3D material disables the basic material. |
| Enable PBR Material | `EnablePBRMaterial` | Checkbox | 0 | Switches the basic material to physically based parameters. |
| Receives Shadows | `ReceivesShadows` | Checkbox | 1 | Whether the replaced surface shows shadows. |

When both Object ID and Material ID limits are on, an object has to match both. Objects that don't match keep their own
material.

### Example

A Text 3D with a Blinn material, with the blue and green channels replaced and the red channel kept:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'CHROME'

blinn = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')

replace = comp.AddTool('ReplaceMaterial3D')
replace.SceneInput = title
replace.MaterialInput = blinn
replace['ReplaceMode.RedMode'] = 0     # Keep the red channel of the text's own material
replace['ReplaceMode.GreenMode'] = 1   # Replace green and blue with the new material
replace['ReplaceMode.BlueMode'] = 1

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = replace
```

### Tips

- The Keep, Replace, Blend and Multiply modes apply per channel, so one channel of the old material can be kept while the
  others change.
- With no material connected, the Material tab's basic material is used, so Replace Material 3D can recolour a scene
  without a material tool.
- Use Material ID limits to change only some objects. Give the objects the IDs in their Controls tab (Object ID) and
  Material tab (Material ID), then limit by that ID here.
- Lights and cameras pass through untouched, so the replacement affects only geometry.

**See also:** Material Merge, Blinn, Phong, OpenPBR, Override 3D, Text 3D, Replace Normals 3D, Merge 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects,
3D materials and textures.

## Replace Normals 3D (`ReplaceNormals3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3RpN · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, required) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Recomputes the per-vertex normals and tangents of the geometry in the scene. Normals set how light falls on a surface, so
recomputing them makes a mesh look smooth or flat: a smoothing angle keeps soft edges between faces that meet at a small
angle and makes sharp edges between faces that meet at a large one. Lights, cameras and materials pass through unchanged.

**Use for:** a faceted imported model that needs smooth shading, a hard-edged primitive that should look flat, and
geometry whose normals are wrong after a Displace 3D or Custom Vertex 3D (those tools move positions and don't update normals).

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-Weld Position Vertices | `PreWeld` | Checkbox | 1 | Joins vertices at the same position before computing normals, so a seam doesn't show as a hard edge. |
| Recompute (normals) | `Normals.Recompute` | Multi-button | 0 | `0: Always`, `1: If Not Present`, `2: Never`. |
| Smoothing Angle (normals) | `Normals.SmoothingAngle` | Number | 45 (0–90; allowed 0–360) | Edges between faces that meet at a sharper angle than this stay hard. Hidden when Recompute is Never. |
| Ignore Smooth Groups | `Normals.IgnoreSmoothGroups` | Checkbox | 0 | Ignores smoothing groups stored in the file, and uses only the smoothing angle. |
| Flip Normals | `Normals.Flip` | Checkbox | 0 | Reverses the normals, for surfaces that are inside out. |
| Recompute (tangents) | `Tangents.Recompute` | Multi-button | 2 | `0: Always`, `1: If Not Present`, `2: Never`. The default leaves tangents alone. |
| Smoothing Angle (tangents) | `Tangents.SmoothingAngle` | Number | 45 (0–90; allowed 0–360) | As for the normals. Hidden when Recompute is Never. |
| Ignore Smooth Groups (tangents) | `Tangents.IgnoreSmoothGroups` | Checkbox | 0 | As for the normals. |
| Flip U Tangents, Flip V Tangents | `Tangents.FlipU`, `Tangents.FlipV` | Checkbox | 0 | Reverses the tangent direction on U or V, for bump and normal maps that look inverted. |

Tangents are computed from the UVs, so a mesh without texture coordinates gets no useful tangents.

**See also:** Weld 3D, Displace 3D, Custom Vertex 3D, UV Map 3D, Bender 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Replicate 3D (`Replicate3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Rep · **Inputs:** `Destination` (DataType3D, required), `Input1`, `Input2`, … (DataType3D, the geometry to copy; a new input appears as each is connected) · **Output:** `Data3D` (DataType3D)

Places a copy of the input geometry at each vertex of the destination geometry. The destination can be a mesh (any
Shape 3D, imported model or Ribbon 3D) or the output of a particle system, so every particle or vertex gets its own object.
Each copy can be aligned to the vertex's normal, coloured from the vertex or particle, and jittered at random. With
more than one input, the copies use the inputs in turn or at random.

**Use for:** swarms and crowds (a model at every particle), tile fields and cubes on the surface of a shape, and
attaching geometry to a Ribbon 3D's points. For copies in a regular row or array with no destination geometry, use
Duplicate 3D.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Step | `Step` | Number | 1 (1–10, integer) | Uses every *n*th vertex of the destination. A step of 3 skips two vertices between copies. Also keeps dense meshes fast. |
| Input Mode | `InputMode` | ID combo | `"Loop"` | `"Loop"`: the inputs are used in order around the destination. `"Random"`: each position gets an input chosen at random, using the seed. Has no effect with one input. |
| Time Offset | `TimeOffset` | Number | 0 (−5 to 5) | Time shift per copy, so each copy shows the input's animation a set number of frames earlier or later. |
| Alignment | `Alignment` | Combo | 0 | `0: Not aligned`: copies keep their input's orientation. `1: Aligned`: copies turn to follow the vertex's normal. `2: TBN Aligned`: copies follow the normal, tangent and binormal (most accurate for particles and simple shapes). |
| Color | `PerParticleColors` | Combo | 1 | Colour from the destination: `0: Use Object Color`, `1: Combine Particle Color` (the input's material, tinted by the particle colour), `2: Use Particle Color` (a default material in the particle colour). |
| Translation | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y`, `Translate.Z` | Number | 0 (X, Y: −2 to 2; Z: −10 to 10) | Offset applied to each copy. |
| Rotation | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180 degrees) | Rotation applied to each copy. |
| Rotation Order | `RotationOrder` | ID multi-button | `"XYZ"` | `"XYZ"`, `"XZY"`, `"YXZ"`, `"YZX"`, `"ZXY"`, `"ZYX"`. |
| Pivot | `Pivot.X`, `Pivot.Y`, `Pivot.Z` | Number | 0 | Point each copy's rotation turns about. |
| Lock X/Y/Z | `ScaleLock` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales all three axes together. |
| Scale | `Scale.X`, `Scale.Y`, `Scale.Z` | Number | 1 (0.001 to 5) | Scale applied to each copy. |
| Random Seed | `RandomSeed` | Number | 0 (0–32767, integer) | Starting point for the jitter, the Random input mode and the Jitter Probability. |
| Reseed | `Randomize` | Button | | Picks a new random seed. |
| Jitter Probability | `JitterProbability` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Fraction of copies that receive jitter. |
| Jitter Time Offset | `JitterTimeOffset` | Number | 0 (0–5) | Random time offset per copy, based on the seed. |
| Translation Jitter | `JitterTranslate.X`, `JitterTranslate.Y`, `JitterTranslate.Z` | Number | 0 (0–2) | Random variation in position. |
| Rotation Jitter | `JitterRotate.X`, `JitterRotate.Y`, `JitterRotate.Z` | Number | 0 (0–180) | Random variation in rotation. |
| Pivot Jitter | `JitterPivot.X`, `JitterPivot.Y`, `JitterPivot.Z` | Number | 0 (0–2) | Random variation in the jitter rotation's pivot. |
| Scale Jitter | `JitterScale.X`, `JitterScale.Y`, `JitterScale.Z` | Number | 0 (0–2) | Random variation in scale, as a power of two: a value of 1 can make a copy up to twice as large or half as large. Uses `JitterScaleLock` as Lock X/Y/Z. |

Each jitter control gives every copy a random amount between minus and plus its value, so 0 leaves that axis alone.

### Example

A field of small cubes on a subdivided plane, each cube standing on its vertex and turned to follow the surface:

```python
grid = comp.AddTool('Shape3D')
grid['SurfacePlaneInputs.SubdivisionWidth'] = 8        # Lock Width/Height is on, so this sets both

tile = comp.AddTool('Shape3D')
tile.Shape = 'SurfaceCubeInputs'
tile['SurfaceCubeInputs.Width'] = 0.1                  # Lock Width/Height/Depth is on, so this sets all three

rep = comp.AddTool('Replicate3D')
rep.Destination = grid
rep.Input1 = tile
rep.Alignment = 1                   # Aligned: each cube follows the normal
rep['Translate.Z'] = 0.05           # lift it off the plane
rep['Scale.X'] = 0.8

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = rep
```

### Tips

- Replicate 3D copies the input at **each vertex**, so the number of copies is the number of destination vertices divided
  by **Step**. Subdivide the destination (for a Shape 3D plane, `SurfacePlaneInputs.SubdivisionWidth` and
  `SubdivisionHeight`) to get more copies, but expect the count to climb quickly.
- Every connected input adds another input: connect `Input1`, and `Input2` appears for the next one.
- For a particle system, use the particle output as the **Destination**. Use **Alignment** `2` (TBN Aligned) so the
  copies face the way the particles move, and **Color** `1` to tint each copy with its particle's colour.
- Use **Time Offset** with an animated input (a model with a walk cycle, for example) to stagger the animation across copies.

**See also:** Duplicate 3D, Ribbon 3D, Shape 3D, Displace 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Ribbon 3D (`Ribbon3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Ri · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional), `MaterialInput` (material or image, optional) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Generates a band of parallel lines between a start point and an end point, each line split into subdivisions. The lines
are drawn with texture coordinates, so a 2D texture can run along them. It is used for motion graphics lines and
light trails, and combined with Replicate 3D to attach geometry to the lines or with Displace 3D to make lightning-like
structures. It needs OpenGL: the software renderer in Renderer 3D shows no ribbon.

**Use for:** light trails, energy lines and filaments, and as a source of points for Replicate 3D.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of Lines | `NumberOfLines` | Number | 10 (0–20, integer) | Parallel lines drawn between the start and end. |
| Line Thickness | `LineThickness` | Number | 1 (1–10) | Thickness of the lines. Some graphics cards allow only whole values. |
| Subdivisions | `SubdivisionLevel` | Number | 10 (1–100, integer) | Points along each line between the start and end. More is smoother. |
| Ribbon Width | `RibbonWidth` | Number | 0.2 (0–2) | Distance between the outer lines. |
| Ribbon Rotation | `RibbonRotation` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180 degrees) | Rotates the band around the line from Start to End. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1 | How the lines join at corners: `0: Bevel`, `1: Round`, `2: Miter`, `3: Miter Clip`. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (1–10) | Limit on the length of a mitred corner. Used by the Miter styles. |
| Start X, Y, Z | `Start.X`, `Start.Y`, `Start.Z` | Number | −1, 0, 0 | The start point of the ribbon. |
| End X, Y, Z | `End.X`, `End.Y`, `End.Z` | Number | 1, 0, 0 | The end point of the ribbon. |
| Material Input | `MaterialInput` | Material (MtlGraph3D) | | The material for the lines. A 2D image here is used as the texture. |

The Start and End points are the controls to animate. A ribbon that follows a moving point is made by keying `Start` and
`End` on two Bezier splines. The `Internal` group in the live tool holds a test geometry switch and the closed and reverse
flags for the lines; it is not documented here.

### Tips

- Ribbon 3D relies on OpenGL, so set the Renderer 3D to the OpenGL renderer. The lines don't appear with the software renderer.
- Put a Bender 3D or Displace 3D after the ribbon to make the lines wave or distort.

**See also:** Replicate 3D, Displace 3D, Bender 3D, UV Map 3D, Renderer 3D, Merge 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Shape 3D (`Shape3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Sh · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional), `MaterialInput` (material) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

A single node for the basic solid primitives: a plane, cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus and icosphere. Choose the
primitive with `Shape`, and the controls for that primitive are shown. Its size, subdivision and cap settings are
specific to each shape. Every shape also has the common object controls for visibility, lighting, matte and blending,
and a material (see Common Controls → 3D objects).

**Use for:** simple geometry for motion graphics, such as a sphere behind a title or a cylinder as a column, and sky
domes (the icosphere with Sky Dome on, not documented). For a single flat card with an image, use Image Plane 3D. For a box only, use
Cube 3D.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `Shape` | ID multi-button | `"SurfacePlaneInputs"` | The primitive: `"SurfacePlaneInputs"`, `"SurfaceCubeInputs"`, `"SurfaceSphereInputs"`, `"SurfaceCylinderInputs"`, `"SurfaceConeInputs"`, `"SurfaceTorusInputs"`, `"SurfaceIcoInputs"`. |

The remaining controls depend on `Shape`. The `Shape` is set first, and the IDs below are then valid.

**Plane** (`SurfacePlaneInputs.`): `Width` (Size, 1, 0–10), `Height` (1, 0–10), `SizeLock` (Lock Width/Height, 1),
`SubdivisionWidth`, `SubdivisionHeight` (10, 1–40), `Wireframe` (0).

**Cube** (`SurfaceCubeInputs.`): `Width`, `Height`, `Depth` (1, 0–10), `SubdivisionWidth`, `SubdivisionHeight`,
`SubdivisionDepth` (10, 1–40), `CubeMapping` (Cube Mapping, 0, not documented in the manual), `SizeLock` (1).

**Sphere** (`SurfaceSphereInputs.`): `Radius` (1, 0–10), `SubdivisionLevelBase` (20, 3–100), `SubdivisionLevelHeight`
(20, 3–100), `StartSweep`, `EndSweep` (Start and End Angle, 0 and 360), `StartLat`, `EndLat` (Start and End Latitude,
90 and −90). The latitude range limits the sphere from top to bottom.

**Cylinder** (`SurfaceCylinderInputs.`): `Radius` (1), `Height` (2), `SubdivisionLevelBase` (20), `SubdivisionLevelHeight`
(1), `StartSweep`, `EndSweep` (0 and 360), `BottomCap`, `TopCap` (Cap, 0), `MakeEmpty` (0), `AllTriangles` (0).

**Cone** (`SurfaceConeInputs.`): `Radius` (1), `TopRadius` (0, so a point), `Height` (2), `SubdivisionLevelBase` (20),
`SubdivisionLevelHeight` (1), `StartSweep`, `EndSweep`, `BottomCap`, `TopCap` (0).

**Torus** (`SurfaceTorusInputs.`): `Radius` (1, 0–5), `Section` (thickness of the tube, 0.5, 0–5),
`SubdivisionLevelBase`, `SubdivisionLevelHeight` (20), `StartSweep`, `EndSweep`, `StartLat`, `EndLat` (0 and 360).

**Icosphere** (`SurfaceIcoInputs.`): `Size` (1, 0–10), `SubdivisionLevel` (0, 0–20).

Each shape's Controls also include `Wireframe`, `IsWireframeAntialiased`, and the common visibility, lighting, matte,
blend and object ID controls (`Visibility.`, `Lighting.`, `Matte.`, `BlendMode.` and `ObjectID.`) with the prefix of
the shape. These are described in Common Controls → 3D objects.

### Example

A sphere in a 3D scene, with a warm colour and a little specular shine, placed behind a title by a Merge 3D:

```python
ball = comp.AddTool('Shape3D')
ball.Shape = 'SurfaceSphereInputs'
ball['SurfaceSphereInputs.Radius'] = 0.6
ball['SurfaceSphereInputs.SubdivisionLevelBase'] = 40
ball['SurfaceSphereInputs.SubdivisionLevelHeight'] = 40
ball['MtlStdInputs.Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.9
ball['MtlStdInputs.Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.4
ball['MtlStdInputs.Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.1
ball['MtlStdInputs.Specular.Intensity'] = 0.6
ball['Transform3DOp.Translate.Z'] = -1

cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = ball.Output
scene.SceneInput2 = cam.Output

render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
render.CameraSelector = cam.Name
```

### Tips

- **Set `Shape` first.** Each shape has its own ID prefix, so the subdivision and size controls for one shape are not
  seen when another is selected.
- **Subdivisions** control how smooth the surface looks and how much work the renderer does. Raise them for a sphere
  that is seen close up. With lighting on, more subdivisions also give smoother lighting across the surface.
- **Cap** the cylinder or cone (`BottomCap`, `TopCap`) when you see the inside of it, for example a column that is
  viewed from above.
- **Matte** a shape (`Matte.IsMatte`) to make it a shadow catcher or an occluder that hides what is behind it.

**See also:** Cube 3D, Image Plane 3D, Text 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Replace Material 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## SoftClip (`SoftClip`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** SoftClip · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Fades objects out with distance from the camera: fully opaque up to one distance, fully transparent beyond another, with
a soft transition between. It removes geometry that is too close to the camera without cutting it off hard.

**Use for:** keeping a title or object from filling the frame when the camera moves close to it.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable | `Enable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the clip on. |
| Smooth Transition | `SmoothTransition` | Checkbox | 1 | Blends between the two distances. |
| Radial | `Radial` | Checkbox | 0 | Measures distance from the camera rather than depth. |
| Show In Display Views | `ShowInView` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows the effect in the viewer. |
| Opaque Distance | `OpaqueDistance` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Closer than this, the object is opaque. |
| Transparent Distance | `TransparentDistance` | Number | 0.05 (0–5) | Closer than this, the object is fully transparent. |
| Receives Shadows | `ReceivesShadows` | Checkbox | 1 | Shadows on the clipped surface. |

### Example

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'
clip = comp.AddTool('SoftClip')
clip.SceneInput = title.Output
clip.OpaqueDistance = 2
clip.TransparentDistance = 0.5
```

**See also:** Fog 3D, Camera 3D, Merge 3D.

## SphereMap (`SphereMap`)

**Category:** 3D Texture · **Short name:** 3SpM · **Inputs:** `Image` (equirectangular 2:1 image) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Maps a 2:1 equirectangular image onto the inside of a sphere, so it can be used as an environment for reflections. The
output is an environment material, normally fed into the Reflection Color input of a Reflect material. Start and End
Angle limit the part of the sphere that is used. Angular Mapping spreads the image more evenly near the poles.

**Use for:** reflection environments built from a single panoramic image, such as a sky, a studio or a set.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image | `Image` | Image input | none | The equirectangular environment image. |
| Start Angle | `StartAngle` | Number | 0 (range 0–360) | Start of the longitude range used, in degrees. |
| End Angle | `EndAngle` | Number | 360 (range 0–360) | End of the longitude range used, in degrees. |
| Angular Mapping | `MapMode` | Checkbox | 0 | Spreads the image more evenly towards the poles, which are squashed by the default mapping. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotate.RotOrder` | ID combo | `"XYZ"` | `"XYZ"`, `"XZY"`, `"YXZ"`, `"YZX"`, `"ZXY"`, `"ZYX"`. The order in which the rotations apply. |
| X, Y, Z Rotation | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (slider −180 to 180) | Turns the environment, so you can bring the part you want to the front. |

### Example

A panoramic environment rotated to bring the horizon into view, feeding a chrome Reflect:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

env = comp.AddTool('SphereMap')
env.Image = media_in.Output
env.MapMode = 1                      # Angular Mapping
env['Rotate.Y'] = 45

chrome = comp.AddTool('MtlReflect')
chrome['Reflection.Color.Material'] = env.MaterialOutput

cube.FrontMaterialInput = chrome.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- The image must be 2:1. Other shapes are clamped: a wide image is fitted across, with clamped poles, and a tall one is
  fitted up and down.
- Start and End Angle crop the sphere, so use them for a panorama that covers less than 360 degrees.
- Connecting a texture to a sphere directly, instead of through Sphere Map, squashes or mirrors it differently. Use Sphere Map
  for a normal environment.

**See also:** Cube Map, Reflect, Texture Transform, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Spherical Camera (`SphericalCamera3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3SC · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional), `Stereo.RightCamera` (DataType3D, optional) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

A camera that sees the full sphere around it, rendered in a panoramic layout such as latitude/longitude. Used with the
Renderer 3D, it produces 360-degree and VR images from a 3D scene.

**Use for:** 360-degree and VR content from 3D scenes, and environment maps rendered from a point in the scene.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Layout | `Layout` | ID multi-button | `"LatLong"` | The panoramic layout, such as `"LatLong"` or `"VR180"`. |
| Convention | `Convention` | ID multi-button | `"NegativeZ"` | Axis convention: `"PositiveZ"` or `"NegativeZ"`. |
| Near Clip | `PerspNearClip` | Number | 0.1 (0.1–50000) | Near clipping distance. |
| Far Clip | `PerspFarClip` | Number | 1000 (0.1–10000) | Far clipping distance. |
| Focal Plane | `PlaneOfFocus` | Number | 4 (0.5–10) | Focus distance for depth of field. |
| Eye Separation | `Stereo.EyeSeparation` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Stereo separation for VR. |
| Convergence Distance | `Stereo.ConvergenceDistance` | Number | 1.5 (0–10) | Stereo convergence. |

### Example

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'
pano = comp.AddTool('SphericalCamera3D')
pano.Layout = 'LatLong'

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = pano.Output
scene.SceneInput2 = title.Output

render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
render.CameraSelector = pano.Name
```

**See also:** Camera 3D, Renderer 3D, Merge 3D.

## Spot Light (`LightSpot`)

**Category:** 3D Light · **Short name:** 3SL · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (optional 3D scene) · **Output:** `Output` (3D Data)

A light that shines in a cone from a point in space, like a stage spotlight. The direction of the cone comes from the
Transform rotation. The cone has a fully lit centre, a soft penumbra at its edge and a Dropoff that controls how the
light fades across the cone.

**Use for:** spotlights and pools of light, rim or key lights aimed at a subject, and lights that need a hard or soft
edge.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | `Enabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the light on or off. |
| Color | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour of the light. |
| Intensity | `Intensity` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Brightness of the light. |
| Decay Type | `DecayType` | Multi-button | 0: No Decay, 1: Linear, 2: Quadratic | Fall-off with distance. |
| Decay Rate | `DecayRate` | Number | 1 (slider 0.001–1) | Strength of the fall-off. Used only when Decay Type is Linear or Quadratic. |
| Cone Angle | `ConeAngle` | Number | 40 (slider 0–90) | Full angle of the fully lit cone, in degrees. Hard limit 90; the Penumbra Angle adds to it. |
| Penumbra Angle | `PenumbraAngle` | Number | 1 (slider 0–20) | Extra angle, in degrees, beyond the cone over which the light fades to nothing. |
| Dropoff | `Dropoff` | Number | 1 (slider 0–40) | Shape of the fall-off across the cone. Higher values concentrate the light in the centre. |
| Enable Shadows | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowsEnabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Casts shadows from this light. |
| Shadow Density | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowDensity` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Opacity of the shadow. |
| Shadow Map Size | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ShadowMapSize` | Number | 2048 (16–16384) | Resolution of the shadow map. |
| Softness | `ShadowLightInputs3D.SoftnessType` | ID combo | `"None"` | `"None"`, `"Constant"`, `"Variable"` or `"VariableFast"`. |
| Constant Softness | `ShadowLightInputs3D.ConstantSoftness` | Number | 0.02 (0–0.1) | Edge softness when Softness is `"Constant"`. |

The other shadow controls (`ShadowLightInputs3D.*`) are the same as on the Directional Light. See that section.

### Example

A soft-edged spot from above, aimed at the cube, with a wide penumbra:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

spot = comp.AddTool('LightSpot')
spot.Intensity = 1.5
spot.ConeAngle = 35
spot.PenumbraAngle = 12
spot.Dropoff = 4
spot['Transform3DOp.Translate.Y'] = 1.5
spot['Transform3DOp.Translate.Z'] = -1.0
spot['Transform3DOp.Rotate.X'] = -60
spot['ShadowLightInputs3D.SoftnessType'] = 'Constant'
spot['ShadowLightInputs3D.ConstantSoftness'] = 0.04

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = cube.Output
merge.SceneInput2 = spot.Output
```

### Tips

- The lit area is the Cone Angle plus the Penumbra Angle. Cone Angle is limited to 90 degrees; the penumbra widens the
  lit area beyond that, up to a total of 178 degrees.
- Dropoff is an exponent on the cone's fade. Dropoff 1 falls off steadily from the centre. Raise it for a tighter hot
  spot, and lower it for a flatter, more even pool of light.
- Decay Rate is hidden when Decay Type is No Decay. Set Decay Type first.

**See also:** Point Light, Projector 3D, Directional Light, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Stereo Mix (`MtlStereoMix3D`)

**Category:** 3D Material · **Short name:** 3SMM · **Inputs:** `LeftMaterial` (orange), `RightMaterial` (green) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Takes two materials, one for the left eye and one for the right, and outputs a single material that the renderer uses
for each eye. Swap exchanges the two inputs. Both inputs must be connected, and each can be a 2D image or a material.

**Use for:** stereo output from a 3D scene, such as images for a left and right view or an anaglyph material built from
two images.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swap | `Swap` | Checkbox | 0 | Exchanges the left and right materials. |
| Receives Lighting, Receives Shadows, Material ID | see Common Controls → 3D materials and textures | | | Shared with the other shading materials. |

### Example

Two flat-colour materials for the two eyes, with Swap turned on:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

left = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
left['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 1.0
left['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.0
left['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.0

right = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
right['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.0
right['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.0
right['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 1.0

stereo = comp.AddTool('MtlStereoMix3D')
stereo.LeftMaterial = left.MaterialOutput
stereo.RightMaterial = right.MaterialOutput
stereo.Swap = 1

cube.FrontMaterialInput = stereo.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- This tool only chooses which material goes to which eye. Set up the stereo render in the Renderer 3D.
- Swap is useful when the left and right images are the wrong way round for the viewer.

**See also:** Merge 3D, Camera 3D, Renderer 3D, Blinn, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Text 3D (`Text3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Txt · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

The 3D version of Text+. It generates text as geometry, which can be extruded into a solid, beveled, lit and placed in
a 3D scene alongside other objects. Its layout, text and transform controls match Text+ closely, but it adds an
extrusion (depth and bevel) and a shading tab. Text 3D has its own built-in material, so it has no `MaterialInput`.
Its Shading tab sets the diffuse and specular colour, and any more advanced material is added with a Replace Material 3D
after the text.

**Use for:** 3D titles and logos, extruded lower thirds that fly in on camera, bevelled text on a card or a plane, and
kinetic type in a 3D space.

**Basic setup:** Text 3D → Merge 3D (with a Camera 3D and lights) → Renderer 3D → Merge over the background. Create it
with `comp.AddTool('Text3D', ...)`: the call form `comp.Text3D()` starts with some values at zero, such as extrusion off.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Styled Text | `StyledText` | Text | "" (empty) | The text. Use `\n` for a new line. |
| Font | `Font` | Text | "Open Sans" | Font family, as installed. A font that isn't installed fails to render. |
| Style | `Style` | Text | "Bold" | Typeface within the family. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (0–10) | Text size in scene units. |
| Tracking | `CharacterSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between characters. |
| Line Spacing | `LineSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between lines. |
| H Anchor | `HorizontalLeftCenterRight` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Horizontal anchor: −1 left, 0 centre, 1 right. |
| V Anchor | `VerticalTopCenterBottom` | Number | 1 (−1 to 1) | Vertical anchor. The default is 1 on a new instance. |
| Layout Type | `LayoutType` | Multi-button | 0: Point (1: Text Box, 2: Circle, 3: Path) | How the text is laid out. |
| Layout Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the layout in the frame. |
| Layout Center Z | `CenterZ` | Number | 0 (−5 to 5) | Depth of the layout. |
| Layout Size | `LayoutSize` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Scales the whole layout. |
| Layout Width, Height | `LayoutWidth`, `LayoutHeight` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 | Box size for Text Box, and circle size for Circle. |
| Wrap, Clip | `Wrap`, `Clip` | Checkbox | 1, 0 | Word wrap and clipping in a Text Box. |
| Position on Path | `PositionOnPath` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Where the text sits along a Path layout. Animate it to move text along a path. |
| Layout Angle X, Y, Z | `AngleX`, `AngleY`, `AngleZ` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Rotation of the layout. |
| Write On Start, End | `Start`, `End` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | The visible part of the text. Animate `End` from 0 to 1 to write on. |
| Scroll | `Scroll` | Multi-button | 0: Still (1: Roll, 2: Crawl) | Credits. Animate `ScrollPosition` to move them. |
| Extrusion Style | `ExtrusionStyle` | Multi-button | 0: Classic (1: Custom) | Classic uses depth and bevel sliders. Custom uses a profile spline. |
| Extrusion Depth | `ExtrusionDepth` | Number | 0 (0–0.2) | Depth of the extrusion. The default 0 gives flat text, so set a depth (e.g. 0.08) to extrude. |
| Subdivisions (Classic) | `ExtrusionSubdivisions` | Number | 0 (0–10) | Smoothness of the extruded edges, in Classic style. |
| Bevel Depth | `BevelDepth` | Number | 0 (0–0.2) | Size of the bevel on the edges. Needs extrusion. |
| Bevel Width | `BevelWidth` | Number | 0 (0–0.1) | Width of the bevel. |
| Smoothing Angle | `SmoothingAngle` | Number | 10 (0–60) | Smoothing angle applied to the bevel edges. |
| Front Bevel, Back Bevel | `FrontBevel`, `BackBevel` | Checkbox | 1, 1 | Bevels the front and back faces separately. |
| Extrusion Profile | `ExtrusionProfile` | Spline | | Custom style only: the profile of the extrusion along its depth. |
| Subdivisions (Custom) | `CustomExtrusionSubdivisions` | Number | 40 (10–100) | Smoothness of the custom profile. |

**Shading tab.** Text 3D has one shading element (the controls numbered 1); the inputs numbered 2 to 8 exist but are
unused. Its main controls are:

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | `Enabled1` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the shading on. |
| Opacity | `Opacity1` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Opacity of the element. |
| Blending | `Overlap1` | Combo | 2: Composite (0: Solid, 1: Transparent) | How the element combines with those below it. |
| Appearance | `ElementShape1` | Multi-button | 0: Text Fill (1: Text Outline, 2: Border Fill, 3: Border Outline) | What the element draws. |
| Thickness | `Thickness1` | Number | 0.02 (0–0.1) | Outline or border width. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle1` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | Corners of an outline. |
| Level | `Level1` | Combo | 3: Character (0: Text, 1: Line, 2: Word) | What a border surrounds. |
| Type | `Type1` | Multi-button | 0: Solid (1: Image) | Solid colour, or an image. |
| Colour | `Red1`, `Green1`, `Blue1`, `Alpha1` | Number | 1 | Fill colour for Type Solid. |
| Specular | `SpecularRed`, `SpecularGreen`, `SpecularBlue`, `SpecularIntensity`, `SpecularExponent` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1, 50 | Highlight of the shading. Exponent 1–100. |
| Priority | `PriorityBack1` | Number | 8 (0–25) | Stacking order. |
| Offset | `Offset1` | Point | (0, 0) | Moves the element. |
| Size | `SizeX1`, `SizeY1` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Scales the element. |

The Shading tab also has **Use One Material** (`UseOneMaterial`, default 1). Turn it off to give the bevel its own
colour and specular controls (`RedBevel`, `GreenBevel`, `BlueBevel`, `AlphaBevel`, `SpecularRedBevel`, and so on). The
image for a Type of Image is on `ColorImage` (for the face) or `BevelTexture` (for the bevel).

### Example

An extruded, bevelled title with a gold specular highlight, placed in a Merge 3D and rendered from a camera:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'
title.Font = 'Open Sans'
title.Style = 'Bold'
title.ExtrusionStyle = 0                 # Classic
title.ExtrusionDepth = 0.08
title.BevelDepth = 0.02
title.FrontBevel = 1
title.BackBevel = 1
title.Red1 = 1.0
title.Green1 = 0.8
title.Blue1 = 0.2
title.SpecularIntensity = 0.8

title.End = comp.BezierSpline()          # write on over frames 0-24
title.End[0] = 0
title.End[24] = 1

cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')
light = comp.AddTool('LightDirectional')

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = title.Output
scene.SceneInput2 = cam.Output
scene.SceneInput3 = light.Output

render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
render.CameraSelector = cam.Name
render['RendererSoftware.LightingEnabled'] = 1

over = comp.AddTool('Merge')
over.Background = media_in.Output
over.Foreground = render.Output
```

### Tips

- **Motion graphics titles:** animate `End` or `Start` for a write-on, `Center` or `AngleY` for a move or turn, and
  `ExtrusionDepth` for a grow. Keyframes work on these as they do on 2D inputs.
- **Shading:** Text 3D has a single shading element; set its Appearance to Text Outline or Border Fill for an outline
  or a border instead of a fill. Lighting must be enabled on the Renderer 3D for the specular highlight to show.
- **Materials:** for a metal, glass or textured look, follow Text 3D with a Replace Material 3D, rather than adjusting
  the basic shading.
- **Fonts** must be installed on every render machine. Otherwise the network render fails.

**See also:** Text+, Shape 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Camera 3D, Replace Material 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Texture 2D (`Texture2DOperator`)

**Category:** 3D Texture · **Short name:** 3Tx · **Inputs:** `Input` (image) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Turns a 2D image into a texture for 3D geometry, and sets how the image is placed over the surface with offset and scale
in U and V. Use it to map an image onto a surface when no UV Map tool is in the chain. For more control over the
placement, add a UV Map or Texture Transform tool.

**Use for:** putting a logo, photo or pattern onto a surface, with simple offset, scale and tiling.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U Translation, V Translation | `UOffset`, `VOffset` | Number | 0 (slider −0.5 to 0.5) | Moves the image across the surface. |
| U Scale, V Scale | `UScale`, `VScale` | Number | 1 (slider 0.001–4) | Scales the image across the surface. Values above 1 make it smaller, and values below 1 tile it. |
| Wrap Mode | `WrapMode` | ID combo | `"Clamp"` | `"Wrap"`, `"Clamp"`, `"Black"`, `"Mirror"`. What fills the area beyond the image edges. |
| Texture Depth | `TextureDepth` | Multi-button | 0: Source | 0: Source, 1: int8, 2: int16, 3: float16, 4: float32. |

### Example

A photo tiled twice across a cube, with Wrap so the edges repeat:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

tex = comp.AddTool('Texture2DOperator')
tex.Input = media_in.Output
tex.UScale = 0.5
tex.VScale = 0.5
tex.WrapMode = 'Wrap'

blinn = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
blinn['Diffuse.Color.Material'] = tex.MaterialOutput

cube.FrontMaterialInput = blinn.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- Clamp repeats the colour at the edge. Black makes the area beyond the image transparent, and Mirror reflects it.
- The Texture 2D tool sets the texture placement, so the geometry must have UV coordinates for the image to land correctly.
- Texture 2D and Texture Transform differ in dimension. Texture 2D is simpler and works on the UV coordinates, while
  Texture Transform moves UVW coordinates.

**See also:** Texture Transform, Blinn, Bump Map, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Texture Transform (`TextureTransformOperator`)

**Category:** 3D Texture · **Short name:** 3TT · **Inputs:** `MaterialInput` (image or material) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

Moves, rotates and scales the UVW texture coordinates of a material, without changing the material itself. It takes an
image or a material and gives back a material, so it can sit between a texture and the material that uses it. Pivot sets
the point that rotation and scaling turn around.

**Use for:** placing, tiling and rotating a texture on a surface, for example to align a grain or move a logo.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U, V, W Translation | `Translation.U`, `Translation.V`, `Translation.W` | Number | 0 (slider −0.5 to 0.5) | Shifts the texture along each axis. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotation.RotOrder` | ID combo | `"UVW"` | `"UVW"`, `"UWV"`, `"VUW"`, `"VWU"`, `"WUV"`, `"WVU"`. The order in which the rotations apply. |
| U, V, W Rotation | `Rotation.U`, `Rotation.V`, `Rotation.W` | Number | 0 (slider −180 to 180) | Rotates the texture about each axis, in degrees. |
| U, V, W Scale | `Scale.U`, `Scale.V`, `Scale.W` | Number | 1 (slider 0.001–4) | Scales the texture along each axis. Values above 1 make it smaller, and values below 1 tile it. |
| U, V, W Pivot | `Pivot.U`, `Pivot.V`, `Pivot.W` | Number | 0 (slider −2 to 2) | The point that rotation and scale turn around. |
| Invert Transform | `InvertTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the transform, so it runs in the opposite direction. |

### Example

A noise texture tiled twice and turned 45 degrees about W:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

noise = comp.AddTool('FastNoiseTexture3D')

xf = comp.AddTool('TextureTransformOperator')
xf.MaterialInput = noise.MaterialOutput
xf['Scale.U'] = 0.5
xf['Scale.V'] = 0.5
xf['Rotation.W'] = 45

blinn = comp.AddTool('MtlBlinn')
blinn['Diffuse.Color.Material'] = xf.MaterialOutput

cube.FrontMaterialInput = blinn.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- Scale and Translation work in texture space, not object space. Check the result in the viewer, because the
  texture's direction depends on the object's UVW coordinates.
- Use Pivot to rotate a texture about its centre rather than its corner.
- Texture Transform works on any material, so it can also move a Gradient or Fast Noise Texture.

**See also:** Texture 2D, Gradient, Fast Noise Texture, UV Map 3D, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Transform 3D (`Transform3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3XF · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Moves, rotates and scales everything in a 3D scene that is connected to it, without a Merge 3D. Its Transform tab is the
same as on other 3D objects. Several Transform 3D nodes can be strung
together, which makes a hierarchy: each node moves the output of the one before it, so a child transform inherits
its parent's motion. The transform is applied to the whole incoming scene, and to every object in it.

**Use for:** offsetting a group of objects without moving the group's Merge 3D, building parent and child hierarchies
(an arm that follows a hand, a moon that orbits a planet).

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Translate X, Y, Z | `Transform3DOp.Translate.X`, `Transform3DOp.Translate.Y`, `Transform3DOp.Translate.Z` | Number | 0 (X, Y: −2 to 2; Z: −10 to 10) | Offsets the scene. |
| Rotate X, Y, Z | `Transform3DOp.Rotate.X`, `Transform3DOp.Rotate.Y`, `Transform3DOp.Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180 degrees) | Rotates the scene about its pivot. |
| Rotation Order | `Transform3DOp.Rotate.RotOrder` | ID multi-button | `"XYZ"` | Order the rotations are applied: `"XYZ"`, `"XZY"`, `"YXZ"`, `"YZX"`, `"ZXY"`, `"ZYX"`. |
| Pivot X, Y, Z | `Transform3DOp.Pivot.X`, `Transform3DOp.Pivot.Y`, `Transform3DOp.Pivot.Z` | Number | 0 (−2 to 2) | Point the rotation is taken about. |
| Scale X, Y, Z | `Transform3DOp.Scale.X`, `Transform3DOp.Scale.Y`, `Transform3DOp.Scale.Z` | Number | 1 (0.001 to 5) | Size of the scene along each axis. |
| Lock X/Y/Z | `Transform3DOp.ScaleLock` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales all three axes together. |
| Use Target | `Transform3DOp.UseTarget` | Checkbox | 0 | The scene always rotates to face the target point. |
| Target X, Y, Z | `Transform3DOp.Target.X`, `Transform3DOp.Target.Y`, `Transform3DOp.Target.Z` | Number | 0 | The point to face when Use Target is on. |
| Invert Transform | `Transform3DOp.InvertTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the inverse of the transform. |
| Import Transform | `Transform3DOp.Import` | Button | | Loads transform data from a scene file. Transform data only: use FBX import for geometry and cameras. |

### Example

Two Transform 3D nodes in a chain make a child: the second node moves the scene relative to the first. Here the
scene is spun, then the spin is offset, so the title orbits the origin:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title.StyledText = 'LIVE'
cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')

spin = comp.AddTool('Transform3D')
spin.SceneInput = title.Output
spin['Transform3DOp.Rotate.Y'] = comp.BezierSpline()
spin['Transform3DOp.Rotate.Y'][0] = 0
spin['Transform3DOp.Rotate.Y'][96] = 360

offset = comp.AddTool('Transform3D')
offset.SceneInput = spin.Output
offset['Transform3DOp.Translate.X'] = 0.5

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = offset.Output
scene.SceneInput2 = cam.Output
```

### Tips

- **Transform 3D vs the Merge 3D transform.** Both move a group. Use Transform 3D when you need a chain of transforms,
  or when you want the transform to live inside a branch of the tree. A Merge 3D is best for a final placement of the
  whole scene.
- **Hierarchy:** the transform is applied to the input scene, so a Transform 3D fed by a Merge 3D moves all of its contents,
  and a Transform 3D fed by a single object moves only that object.
- **Rotation about a point:** set `Pivot` to move the centre of rotation, rather than moving the object afterwards.

**See also:** Merge 3D, Override 3D, Camera 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Triangulate 3D (`Triangulate3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3Tri · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, required) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Splits every polygon of the input mesh into triangles, so a quad becomes two triangles and an n-sided face becomes n − 2.
Use it before tools that need triangles, such as Displace 3D or Bender 3D on geometry with quads or n-gons. It changes the
mesh's topology, not its shape.

**Use for:** imported models with quads or n-gons ahead of deformers, and any mesh that needs a consistent triangle layout.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | Multi-button | 0 | Has one option, `0: Triangulate`. There are no other settings. |

**See also:** Weld 3D, Displace 3D, Bender 3D, Replace Normals 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## UV Map 3D (`UVMap`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3UV · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, required), `CameraInput` (DataType3D, shown with Map Mode Camera) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Replaces the texture coordinates (UVs) of the geometry. Each vertex gets a new UV based on a virtual shape around the
object (a plane, cylinder, sphere or cube, or the object's own XYZ position), or on a camera's projection. The tool
doesn't put a texture on anything: the materials that use the UVs do that, so the image comes from a material connected
upstream or downstream.

**Use for:** placing a texture on a primitive or an imported model that has bad or missing UVs, projecting an image through
a Camera 3D onto geometry, and tiling or flipping a texture across a shape.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Map Mode | `MapMode` | ID multi-button | `"Planar"` | `"Planar"`, `"Cylindrical"`, `"Spherical"`, `"CubeMap"`, `"XYZtoUVW"` (positions become UVW, for procedural textures) or `"Camera"` (projects from `CameraInput`). |
| Orientation | `Orientation` | Multi-button | 1 | The axis the mapping shape is aligned to: `0: X`, `1: Y`, `2: Z`. |
| Fit | `FitBBox` | Button | | Sizes the mapping shape to the bounding box of the input. |
| Center | `CenterBBox` | Button | | Moves the mapping shape's centre to the bounding box centre of the input. |
| Lock UVs on Animated Objects | `LockUVs` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps the UVs fixed to the object as it was at Ref Time, so a texture doesn't slide across an animated object. Needs the vertex count to stay the same. |
| Ref Time | `RefTime` | Number | 0 (0–1000, integer) | The frame the UVs are locked to. Shown with Lock UVs. |
| Projection Fit Method | `ProjectionFitMethod` | ID multi-button | `"Inside"` | `"Inside"`, `"Width"`, `"Height"`, `"Outside"` or `"Stretch"`. The source's fit into the camera frustum is commented as unfinished, so this setting is not documented as having an effect. |
| Size X, Y, Z | `Size.X`, `Size.Y`, `Size.Z` | Number | 2 (0.001–10) | Size of the mapping shape. |
| Center X, Y, Z | `Center.X`, `Center.Y`, `Center.Z` | Number | 0 (X, Y: −2 to 2; Z: −10 to 10) | Position of the mapping shape. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotate.RotOrder` | ID multi-button | `"XYZ"` | Order the three rotations are applied. |
| Rotate X, Y, Z | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180 degrees) | Orientation of the mapping shape. |
| Tile U, V, W | `Tile.U`, `Tile.V`, `Tile.W` | Number | 1 (0.001–5) | How many times the texture repeats across each axis. |
| Flip U, V, W | `Flip.U`, `Flip.V`, `Flip.W` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirrors the UVs across the axis. |
| Flip Faces | `FlipFace.PositiveX.U`, … `FlipFace.NegativeZ.V` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirrors the UVs on individual cube faces (CubeMap mode only). Each face has a U and a V checkbox: `PositiveX`, `NegativeX`, `PositiveY`, `NegativeY`, `PositiveZ`, `NegativeZ`. |

### Example

Projecting a plate through a camera onto a plane, so the plane lines up with the shot:

```python
plane = comp.AddTool('Shape3D')

cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')
cam['Transform3DOp.Translate.Z'] = 5

uv = comp.AddTool('UVMap')
uv.SceneInput = plane
uv.CameraInput = cam
uv.MapMode = 'Camera'

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
merge.SceneInput1 = uv
merge.SceneInput2 = cam
```

### Tips

- Put the UV Map after the geometry and before any Transform 3D, so the mapping moves with the object's own coordinates. Moving
  the object's transform upstream makes the texture slide across it.
- The projection doesn't put an image on the surface. Connect the image to the diffuse input of a material. Because it's a
  texture projection, the image's alpha sets the opacity of the surface.
- Use **Tile** to repeat a texture and **Flip** to mirror it. Both change only the UVs.
- **Lock UVs on Animated Objects** fails if the mesh's vertex count changes over time. It doesn't work on many particle
  systems or on duplicates with a time offset.

**See also:** Camera 3D, Projector 3D, Shape 3D, Replace Material 3D, Image Plane 3D, Transform 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects,
3D materials and textures.

## Ward (`MtlWard`)
