**Category:** 3D Material · **Short name:** 3Wd · **Inputs:** `Diffuse.Color.Material` (orange), `Specular.Color.Material` (green), `Specular.Intensity.Material` (magenta), `Specular.SpreadU.Material` (white), `Specular.SpreadV.Material` (white), `Bumpmap.Material` (white) · **Output:** `MaterialOutput` (Material Output)

A basic illumination material with an anisotropic highlight: the highlight can be stretched along the U or the V
direction of the texture coordinates. It suits brushed metal, where the scratches run one way and the highlight follows
them.

**Use for:** brushed and spun metal, satin finishes and any surface whose highlight should stretch in one direction.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diffuse Color | `Diffuse.Color.Red`, `Diffuse.Color.Green`, `Diffuse.Color.Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Base colour. Multiplied by the Diffuse Color texture. |
| Alpha | `Diffuse.Color.Alpha` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Alpha of the surface. |
| Opacity | `Diffuse.Opacity` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Transparency of the surface. |
| Specular Color | `Specular.Color.Red`, `Specular.Color.Green`, `Specular.Color.Blue` | Number | 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour of the highlight. Multiplied by the Specular Color texture. |
| Specular Intensity | `Specular.Intensity` | Number | 1 (slider 0–1) | Strength of the highlight. Multiplied by the alpha of the Specular Intensity texture. |
| Spread U | `Specular.SpreadU` | Number | 0.05 (slider 0.01–0.2) | Width of the highlight across U. Multiplied by the alpha of the Spread U texture. |
| Spread V | `Specular.SpreadV` | Number | 0.16 (slider 0.01–0.2) | Width of the highlight across V. Multiplied by the alpha of the Spread V texture. |
| Transmittance, Receives, Two Sided, PBR, Material ID | see Common Controls → 3D materials and textures | | | Shared with the other shading materials. |

### Example

Brushed steel: a narrow highlight across U and a long one across V, so it stretches along the brushing:

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')

ward = comp.AddTool('MtlWard')
ward['Diffuse.Color.Red'] = 0.7
ward['Diffuse.Color.Green'] = 0.72
ward['Diffuse.Color.Blue'] = 0.75
ward['Specular.SpreadU'] = 0.02
ward['Specular.SpreadV'] = 0.18

cube.FrontMaterialInput = ward.MaterialOutput
```

### Tips

- The Spread textures use their **alpha** channel, multiplied by the Spread slider. A texture with a bright area in
  alpha widens the highlight there.
- Spread U and Spread V are the two directions of the texture coordinates, so the direction of the stretch depends on
  how the geometry's UVs run. Use a UV Map tool to orient it.
- Ward is closely related to Cook-Torrance in use. Choose Ward when the highlight should be directional, and
  Cook-Torrance when it should be even in all directions.

**See also:** Blinn, Cook-Torrance, OpenPBR, Bump Map, Common Controls → 3D materials and textures.

## Weld 3D (`Weld3D`)

**Category:** 3D · **Short name:** 3We · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, required) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Joins vertices that share a position, or nearly do, so a mesh that was split into separate pieces at its seams becomes
one connected surface. Split vertices cause cracks and hard edges, most visibly once a Displace 3D moves them apart, so
weld before displacing. Only positions are welded: the normals and UVs of the joined vertices keep their old values.
Fracture does the reverse and splits every face into its own vertices.

**Use for:** imported meshes with duplicate vertices along their seams, before Displace 3D or Bender 3D, and as a
way to split a mesh into unconnected faces with Fracture.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weld Mode | `WeldMode` | Multi-button | 0 | `0: Weld` joins vertices within the tolerance. `1: Fracture` gives every face its own vertices. |
| Auto Tolerance | `AutoTolerance` | Checkbox | 1 | Chooses the tolerance for each mesh automatically. Tolerance and Coordinate System are shown only when this is off. |
| Tolerance | `Tolerance` | Number | 0.001 (0.0001–0.01) | Vertices closer together than this are joined. |
| Coordinate System | `CoordSystem` | ID multi-button | `"World"` | The space the tolerance is measured in: `"Model"` (the object's own coordinates) or `"World"` (the scene). |

Weld Normals and Weld UVs are present in the live tool but hidden, and their welding is not implemented, so they are not
documented here.

**See also:** Displace 3D, Bender 3D, Replace Normals 3D, Triangulate 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Blur (`Blur`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** Blur · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Blurs the whole image, or only the pixels inside its Effect Mask. The Filter menu chooses the blur algorithm, from a fast
box blur to a smooth Gaussian approximation. Lock X/Y keeps the blur equal on both axes, or lets you blur more on one.

**Use for:** softening a plate or a background, defocusing a layer behind a title, pre-softening a matte before a
Merge, and patchy or masked blurs when the Effect Mask is driven by another image (such as Fast Noise).

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter | `Filter` | ID combo | `"Fast Gaussian"` | The blur method: `"Box"`, `"Bartlett"`, `"Multi-box"`, `"Gaussian"`, `"Fast Gaussian"`. See *Shared blur controls* below. |
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Blur Size applies to both axes. Off: `YBlurSize` is shown and used. |
| Blur Size | `XBlurSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–100) | Amount of blur. With Lock X/Y on, this is the blur on both axes. |
| Y Blur Size | `YBlurSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–100) | Vertical blur, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Num Passes | `Passes` | Number | 4 (slider 1–16) | Number of box passes. Shown in the Inspector only when the filter is `"Multi-box"`. More passes give a smoother result at more cost. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Channels that are blurred. Off channels are copied from the input. These act before the Settings tab channel buttons. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | Edge handling for domain of definition: `"None"`, `"Domain"`, `"Frame"`. See *Shared blur controls*. |
| Blend | `BlendClone` | Number | 1 (0–1) | A clone of the Settings tab Blend. Changing either changes both. |

### Shared blur controls

These apply to the Blur, Glow, Soft Glow, Defocus and Directional Blur tools unless a section says otherwise.

- **Filter.** `"Box"` is the fastest and lowest quality, and gives a linear ramp at edges. `"Bartlett"` is a softer,
  anti-aliased blur. `"Multi-box"` layers box filters over several `Passes` to approximate a Gaussian with no ringing,
  and is the choice for float images where Gaussian overshoot can show. `"Gaussian"` is a smooth, symmetrical blur.
  `"Fast Gaussian"` is the same shape using a faster constant-time approximation and is the default.
- **Blur sizes.** Blur and glow sizes in the blur tools use a pseudo-normalised scale from 0 to 720, where 720 is a huge
  blur roughly the width of the image. The same value gives a similar look at any resolution. Values above the slider
  maximum can be typed in.
- **Lock X/Y.** Locks the X and Y sizes together. Clear it to set each axis separately, for a directional softening.
- **Clipping Mode.** `"Frame"`, the default, uses the full frame, so the result fills the frame and any area
  outside the upstream domain is treated as black or transparent. `"Domain"` respects the upstream domain, which can clip
  the edges of a large blur. `"None"` applies no clipping at all.
- **Glow mask (Glow and Soft Glow).** These tools have a second mask input, `GlowMask`. It pre-masks the source of the
  glow: the glow is taken only from pixels inside the mask, but it can then spread beyond the mask edge. This differs from
  the Effect Mask, which clips the finished result.

### Example

A soft blur on a background plate, stronger horizontally than vertically, limited to the area of a Rectangle Mask:

```python
blur = comp.AddTool('Blur')
blur.Input = media_in.Output
blur.Filter = 'Gaussian'
blur.LockXY = 0                  # set X and Y separately
blur.XBlurSize = 12
blur.YBlurSize = 4

mask = comp.AddTool('RectangleMask')
blur.EffectMask = mask.Output    # the mask's Mask output limits the blur
```

### Tips

- **Use Multi-box on float footage.** Gaussian can overshoot slightly on float images and leave faint ringing at high
  values. Multi-box with about four passes gives a similar result without it.
- **Mask the blur, don't stack effects.** A Blur limited by an Effect Mask is cheaper and easier to control than a
  Blur on a duplicated layer merged back over the plate.
- **For a glow, use the glow tools.** Glow and Soft Glow add a bright halo from the highlights. Blur only softens.

**See also:** Defocus, Glow, Soft Glow, Directional Blur, Sharpen, Unsharp Mask, VariBlur, Vector Motion Blur, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Defocus (`Defocus`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** Dfo · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Simulates an out-of-focus lens. Gaussian is a fast, simple defocus. Lens is a slower, more realistic defocus whose
blur takes the shape of the lens aperture, so bright points form bokeh discs or polygons. Bloom makes the brightest
areas spread into a glow, as they do through a real lens.

**Use for:** depth-of-field effects on a plate or a graphic, out-of-focus backgrounds, lens flare-like bloom on bright
highlights, and bokeh on lights.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter | `Filter` | Multi-button | 1: Lens (0: Gaussian Blur, 1: Lens) | `Gaussian Blur` is the fast simple defocus. `Lens` gives the realistic aperture shape, and is much slower. Lens controls are shown only for Lens. |
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Defocus Size. Off: `YDefocusSize` is used. |
| Defocus Size | `XDefocusSize` | Number | 2 (slider 0–10) | Amount of defocus. Higher values blur more and produce larger blooms. |
| Y Defocus Size | `YDefocusSize` | Number | 2 (slider 0–10) | Vertical defocus, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Bloom Level | `BloomLevel` | Number | 0.9 (slider 0–1) | Intensity and size of the bloom on pixels above the threshold. |
| Bloom Threshold | `BloomThreshold` | Number | 0.75 (slider 0–1) | Pixels brighter than this bloom. Pixels below it are only defocused. |
| Lens Type | `LensType` | Multi-button | 0: NGon Solid, 1: NGon Shaded Out, 2: NGon Shaded In, 3: Circle | Shape of the aperture that creates the bokeh. Lens only. |
| Lens Angle | `LensAngle` | Number | 0 (0–360°) | Rotation of the aperture shape. Visible with the NGon types, not with Circle. Lens only. |
| Lens Sides | `LensSides` | Number | 5 (slider 3–12) | Number of sides of the NGon aperture. Lens only. |
| Lens Shape | `LensShape` | Number | 0 (slider −0.75 to 0.75) | How pointed the NGon is. Higher values give a sharper, starry look. Lens only. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | Edge handling: `"None"`, `"Domain"`, `"Frame"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. |

### Example

A lens-style defocus on a background plate, with a hexagonal aperture and a little bloom on the highlights:

```python
dof = comp.AddTool('Defocus')
dof.Input = media_in.Output
dof.Filter = 1                   # Lens
dof.LensType = 0                 # NGon Solid
dof.LensSides = 6                # hexagonal
dof.XDefocusSize = 4
dof.BloomLevel = 0.5
dof.BloomThreshold = 0.8
```

### Tips

- **Use Gaussian for speed.** `Gaussian Blur` is quick and fine for an ordinary soft background. Switch to `Lens` only
  when the bokeh shape matters.
- **Animate the size for focus pulls.** Keyframe `XDefocusSize` (and `YDefocusSize` with Lock X/Y off) to pull focus
  between depths.
- **Mask the defocus for depth.** Connect a Rectangle or Ellipse Mask to the Effect Mask to defocus only the
  background, or a Fast Noise to vary it across the frame.

**See also:** Blur, Glow, Soft Glow, VariBlur, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Directional Blur (`DirectionalBlur`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** DrBl · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Smears the image along a line, from a centre point, or towards a centre point. Linear blurs in one direction, as in
motion blur. Radial spins the image around the centre, and Zoom streaks it in towards or away from the centre, like a
zoom shot. Glow adds a bright glow to the streaks, which imitates a longer exposure.

**Use for:** simulated motion blur on a moving graphic, light rays and streaks from a bright point, zoom and spin
transitions, and speed lines when limited to part of the frame with the Effect Mask.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0: Linear, 1: Radial, 2: Centered, 3: Zoom | Linear blurs in one direction. Centered gives a similar result, with the blur spread equally on both sides of the image. Radial and Zoom work from `Center`. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The point the Radial and Zoom effects start from. The manual says it applies only to those types; the Inspector shows it for every Type. |
| Length | `Length` | Number | 0 (slider −0.1 to 0.1) | Strength and heading of the effect. 0 does nothing. Negative values blur in the opposite direction to `Angle`. Values beyond the slider can be typed in. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (0–360°) | Direction of Linear and Centered blur. In Radial and Zoom, it turns the effect into a spin, and with `Length` set, a whirl. The Inspector shows it for every Type. |
| Glow | `Glow` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Adds a glow to the blurred streaks, as if the shutter had stayed open longer. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | Edge handling: `"None"`, `"Domain"`, `"Frame"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. |

### Example

A zoom streak from the centre of the frame, which pulls the image towards the viewer over a short shot:

```python
zoom = comp.AddTool('DirectionalBlur')
zoom.Input = media_in.Output
zoom.Type = 3                    # Zoom
zoom.Center = [0.5, 0.5]
zoom.Length = 0.05
zoom.Glow = 0.2
```

For a horizontal motion blur, use `Type` 0 with `Angle` 0 and a small `Length` such as 0.02.

### Tips

- **Keep Length small.** Values around 0.01 to 0.05 suit motion blur. Larger values smear the image beyond recognition.
- **Animate Length for a moving blur.** Keyframe `Length` with a spline, for example to start a zoom at rest and build it
  up for a transition. Set it back to 0 to clear the effect.
- **Mask the streaks.** Connect a mask to the Effect Mask to limit the blur to a moving object or to the edge of the frame.

**See also:** Blur, Glow, Soft Glow, Vector Motion Blur, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Glow (`Glow`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** Glo · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue), Glow Mask (white) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Makes highlights bloom. The image is blurred, the blurred result is brightened, and it is mixed back over the original.
Apply Mode chooses how the glow is added: straight over the image, underneath it, or limited to a range of values with
Threshold. Color Scale tints the glow.

**Use for:** light glows on lamps, neon and sun flares, bloom on titles, and a glow on a shape or a title that is
limited to its bright parts with the Glow Mask input.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter | `Filter` | ID combo | `"Fast Gaussian"` | The blur method: `"Box"`, `"Bartlett"`, `"Multi-box"`, `"Gaussian"`, `"Fast Gaussian"`, `"Blend"`, `"Hilight"`, `"Solarize"`. `"Blend"` adds a glow that is visible in both whites and blacks. `"Hilight"` glows without a halo in the surrounding pixels. `"Solarize"` glows and solarizes the image. |
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Glow Size. Off: `YGlowSize` is used. |
| Glow Size | `XGlowSize` | Number | 10 (slider 0–100) | Size of the glow. Larger values spread the glow further. |
| Y Glow Size | `YGlowSize` | Number | 10 (slider 0–100) | Vertical size, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Num Passes | `Passes` | Number | 4 (slider 1–16) | Passes for the Multi-box filter. Shown in the Inspector only when the filter is `"Multi-box"`. |
| Glow | `Glow` | Number | 0.8 (0–1) | Intensity of the glow. High values blow the image out to white. |
| Apply Mode | `ApplyMode` | Multi-button | 0: Normal, 1: Merge Under, 2: Threshold | Normal adds the glow over the image. Merge Under puts it beneath the image, based on alpha. Threshold clips the glow between `Low` and `High`. |
| Low, High | `Low`, `High` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Threshold range, shown in Threshold mode only. Glow pixels below `Low` go to black, and those above `High` go to white. |
| Color Scale | `RedScale`, `GreenScale`, `BlueScale`, `AlphaScale` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–2) | Per-channel gain on the glow. Lower the blue and green values to warm the glow. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Channels that take part in the glow. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | Edge handling: `"None"`, `"Domain"`, `"Frame"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. |
| Blend | `BlendClone` | Number | 0.2 (0–1) | A clone of the Settings tab Blend. The default is 0.2, not 1. |

Glow Mask (`GlowMask`, a Mask input) limits where the glow comes from, and lets it spread past the mask's edge. The
Effect Mask (`EffectMask`) instead clips the finished glow. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*.

### Example

A warm glow on the highlights of a clip. Threshold keeps only the bright parts, and the glow is added over the clip:

```python
glow = comp.AddTool('Glow')
glow.Input = media_in.Output
glow.Filter = 'Fast Gaussian'
glow.XGlowSize = 30
glow.Glow = 0.6
glow.ApplyMode = 2               # Threshold, so Low and High are shown
glow.Low = 0.7
glow.High = 1.0
glow.BlueScale = 0.5             # warmer glow: less blue
glow.GreenScale = 0.8
```

### Tips

- **Threshold for highlights.** Normal mode glows everywhere, including mid-tones. Threshold with `Low` around 0.7 keeps
  the glow to the brightest areas, and gives cleaner results on dark footage.
- **Output includes the image.** Glow returns the image with the glow added, so it can sit in the chain where
  the image goes. Lower Blend to mix more of the original back in.
- **Hilight for a halo-free glow.** `"Hilight"` adds a glow without a halo in the surrounding pixels.

**See also:** Soft Glow, Blur, Directional Blur, Merge (Screen and Add modes), Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Sharpen (`Sharpen`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** Shrp · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Enhances detail in the image with a convolution filter, overall or on selected channels. Amounts can differ per axis
when Lock X/Y is off.

**Use for:** adding crispness to soft footage, sharpening after a resize or a blur-based effect, and sharpening only the
channels or the area that needs it through the Effect Mask.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Amount. Off: `YAmount` is used. |
| Amount | `XAmount` | Number | 1 (slider 0–100) | Strength of the sharpening. |
| Y Amount | `YAmount` | Number | 1 (slider 0–100) | Vertical strength, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Channels that are sharpened. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | `"None"`, `"Domain"` or `"Frame"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. |
| Blend | `BlendClone` | Number | 1 (0–1) | A clone of the Settings tab Blend. |

### Example

Gentle sharpening of a soft plate:

```python
sharp = comp.AddTool('Sharpen')
sharp.Input = media_in.Output
sharp.XAmount = 0.5
```

### Tips

- **Sharpen the result, not the source.** Sharpening before a Merge or a grade also sharpens the grain and noise
  in that layer. Put it last if the output needs it.
- **Use Unsharp Mask for edges.** Unsharp Mask sharpens only the edges, with a threshold to avoid noise.

**See also:** Unsharp Mask, Blur, Glow.

## Soft Glow (`SoftGlow`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** SGlo · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue), Glow Mask (white) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A glow that is more diffuse and natural than Glow. It runs extra processing on the image before blurring, so the light
spreads softly rather than forming a hard halo. Threshold sets how bright a pixel must be to glow, and Gain sets how
bright the glow is.

**Use for:** atmospheric haze around lights and planets, dreamy or soft-focus looks, skin glow, and any light bloom
where a hard-edged Glow looks too harsh.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter | `Filter` | ID combo | `"Fast Gaussian"` | The blur method: `"Box"`, `"Bartlett"`, `"Multi-box"`, `"Gaussian"`, `"Fast Gaussian"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. The manual names Gaussian as the default; the live default is `"Fast Gaussian"`. |
| Threshold | `Threshold` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Brightness a pixel needs before it contributes to the glow. Higher values limit the glow to the brightest areas. |
| Gain | `Gain` | Number | 2 (slider 0–5) | Brightness of the glow. |
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Glow Size. Off: `YGlowSize` is used. |
| Glow Size | `XGlowSize` | Number | 10 (slider 0–100) | Size of the glow. Larger values spread it further. |
| Y Glow Size | `YGlowSize` | Number | 10 (slider 0–100) | Vertical size, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Num Passes | `Passes` | Number | 4 (slider 1–16) | Passes for the Multi-box filter. Shown in the Inspector only when the filter is `"Multi-box"`. |
| Color Scale | `RedScale`, `GreenScale`, `BlueScale`, `AlphaScale` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–2) | Per-channel gain on the glow, which tints it. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Channels that take part in the glow. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | Edge handling: `"None"`, `"Domain"`, `"Frame"`. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*. |
| Blend | `BlendClone` | Number | 1 (0–1) | A clone of the Settings tab Blend. Lower it to mix the original back over the glow. |

Glow Mask (`GlowMask`) pre-masks the glow source, as on Glow. See Blur → *Shared blur controls*.

### Example

Soft haze around a bright light. The threshold keeps the glow to the light and not the whole frame:

```python
haze = comp.AddTool('SoftGlow')
haze.Input = media_in.Output
haze.Threshold = 0.6            # only the brightest pixels glow
haze.Gain = 1.5
haze.XGlowSize = 40
haze.LockXY = 1
haze.Blend = 1                  # full glow over the image
```

### Tips

- **Threshold first, then Gain.** Raise `Threshold` until only the bright parts glow, then adjust `Gain` for strength.
- **Tint warm for light.** Lower `BlueScale` slightly to give the haze a warm, sunlit colour.
- **Use Glow for a defined bloom.** Soft Glow is the choice for haze and skin; Glow with Threshold gives a more
  defined halo.

**See also:** Glow, Blur, Defocus, Directional Blur, Merge (Add and Screen modes), Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Unsharp Mask (`UnsharpMask`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** USM · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Sharpens only the edges in an image. The image is blurred, the blurred copy is compared with the original, and pixels
that differ strongly from their surroundings (edges) are brightened. This is the classic unsharp-mask method, useful for
low-contrast or soft footage where a plain sharpen would add noise.

**Use for:** recovering detail in soft or low-contrast images, and sharpening edges without emphasising grain.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Size. Off: `YSize` is used. |
| Size | `XSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Size of the blur used to extract the detail. Higher values pick out larger features as detail. |
| Y Size | `YSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Vertical size, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Gain | `Gain` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | How much the detail is boosted. Higher values sharpen more. |
| Threshold | `Threshold` | Number | 0 (slider 0–0.25) | Raises the threshold for what counts as detail. Higher values leave lower-contrast areas unsharpened. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Channels that are sharpened. |

### Example

Sharpening the edges of a soft shot, with the threshold keeping flat areas unchanged:

```python
usm = comp.AddTool('UnsharpMask')
usm.Input = media_in.Output
usm.XSize = 2
usm.Gain = 1.5
usm.Threshold = 0.02
```

### Tips

- **Raise Threshold on noisy footage.** Grain has small differences that look like detail. A small threshold stops
  the noise being sharpened.
- **Size sets the scale of detail.** Small sizes sharpen fine texture; larger sizes sharpen broader edges.

**See also:** Sharpen, Blur, Glow.

## VariBlur (`VariBlur`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** VBl · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Blur Image (green), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A per-pixel variable blur. A second image, the Blur Image, sets how much each pixel is blurred: where the chosen channel is
bright the blur is strong, and where it is dark there is little or none. Any image can drive it, including a gradient,
a shape, text, or a movie, so the blur can follow a pattern or a depth map.

**Use for:** depth-based blur from a depth or matte channel, graded blurs that move across a frame, and a blur shaped by
a gradient or a shape.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | `Method` | Multi-button | 1: Multibox (0: Soften, 1: Multibox, 2: Defocus) | Blur algorithm. Soften keeps detail in less-blurred areas. Multibox gives a better Gaussian approximation at higher Quality. Defocus gives a flat, disc-shaped blur. |
| Quality | `Quality` | Number | 4 (slider 1–10) | Smoothness of the blur. Higher values are smoother and slower. 1 gives a fast box blur for any Method. |
| Blur Channel | `BlurChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Red (1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Alpha, 4: Luma, 5: None) | The channel of Blur Image that controls the amount of blur. |
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Blur Size applies to both axes. Off: `YBlurSize` is used. |
| Blur Size | `XBlurSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Overall amount of blur applied to each pixel. Pixels where the Blur Image is black or missing are still blurred by this amount. |
| Y Blur Size | `YBlurSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Vertical blur, used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Blur Limit | `BlurLimit` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–2) | Limits the usable range of the Blur Image, so very large values (such as infinite depth values) don't skew the blur. |

The Blur Image input (`BlurImage`) is required. The Clipping Mode, Settings tab and Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.
The depth controls `ZScale`, `DepthOfField` and `FocalPoint` are not documented by the manual, so they are not described here.

### Example

A blur driven by a horizontal gradient, so the left of the frame is sharp and the right is soft:

```python
grad = comp.AddTool('Background')
grad.Type = 'Horizontal'
grad.TopLeftRed, grad.TopLeftGreen, grad.TopLeftBlue = 0, 0, 0
grad.TopRightRed, grad.TopRightGreen, grad.TopRightBlue = 1, 1, 1

vb = comp.AddTool('VariBlur')
vb.Input = media_in.Output
vb.BlurImage = grad.Output
vb.BlurChannel = 0               # Red
vb.XBlurSize = 8
vb.Quality = 4
```

### Tips

- **Shape the map.** The brighter the chosen channel, the more blur. Run the Blur Image through a Color Corrector or
  Curves to control where the blur falls.
- **Keep Blur Limit in mind.** Very large values in the Blur Image, such as from a depth pass, would otherwise skew the blur. Blur Limit caps them.

**See also:** Blur, Defocus, Background, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Vector Motion Blur (`VectorMotionBlur`)

**Category:** Blur · **Short name:** VMB · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Vectors (green), Effect Mask (blue), Vector Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Blurs each pixel along its own motion. The motion comes from a vector map: two channels that say how far each pixel
moved in X and in Y. These come from a 3D renderer's motion-vector AOV, from an EXR file, or from an Optical Flow tool.
Vector Motion Blur does not estimate motion itself, so it needs the vectors.

**Use for:** adding motion blur to rendered elements or footage where the vectors exist, and matching the motion blur
of a 3D render to the plate.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Channel | `XVectorChannel` | Multi-button | 3: Vector X (0: Red, 1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Vector X, 4: Vector Y) | The channel that gives the X movement of each pixel. |
| Y Channel | `YChannel` | Multi-button | 4: Vector Y (0: Red, 1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Vector X, 4: Vector Y) | The channel that gives the Y movement of each pixel. |
| Flip X Channel, Flip Y Channel | `FlipX`, `FlipY` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the X or Y vectors, for example when the vectors come from a tool that uses the opposite direction. |
| Lock Scale X/Y | `LockScaleXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Scale. Off: separate `XScale` and `YScale`. |
| Scale | `XScale` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Multiplier on the vector values. A scale of 2 with a vector of 10 gives a move of 20. |
| Y Scale | `YScale` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Vertical multiplier, used when Lock Scale X/Y is off. |
| Vectors | `Vectors` | Image input | | The image that holds the vector channels. Needed when they are not in the Input. |
| Vector Mask | `VectorMask` | Mask input | | A mask on the vectors, limiting where the motion is taken from. |

The Settings tab and the Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.

### Example

Motion blur from a vector pass that is connected as a separate image, at half strength:

```python
render = comp.AddTool('Background')   # stands in for the rendered element
vectors = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')   # stands in for a motion-vector pass

vmb = comp.AddTool('VectorMotionBlur')
vmb.Input = render.Output
vmb.Vectors = vectors.Output
vmb.XScale = 0.5
```

### Tips

- **Check the vector depth.** The vectors need float (16-bit or 32-bit) data to hold negative values. Integer images
  clip them, and the blur only goes in one direction.
- **Use Scale to match the shutter.** Scale multiplies the whole vector, so it sets how long the blur is.
- **Flip if the blur runs backwards.** A vector pass from another package may use the opposite sign convention. Check the
  direction in the viewer, and use the Flip checkboxes if needed.

**See also:** Directional Blur, Blur, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## ACES Transform (`AcesTransform`)

**Category:** Color\ColorFX · **Short name:** ATr · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies an ACES Input Device Transform (IDT, which takes a camera's footage into ACES) and an Output Device Transform (ODT,
which takes ACES to a display or delivery space). The ACES Version chooses which set of transforms is offered: each version
has its own Input Transform and Output Transform menus, with the IDs for that version. The Gamut Compress options
reduce out-of-gamut colours.

**Use for:** taking camera footage into ACES for a compositing pipeline, and converting an ACES result to a display space.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACES Version | `AcesVersion` | ID combo | `"ACES_VERSION_2_0_0"` | `"ACES_VERSION_2_0_0"`, `"ACES_VERSION_1_3_0"`, `"ACES_VERSION_1_2_0"`, `"ACES_VERSION_1_1_0"` or `"ACES_VERSION_1_0_0"`. Chooses which transform menus are shown. |
| Input Transform | `InputTransform200` (also `InputTransform130`, `InputTransform120`, `InputTransform110`, `InputTransform100`) | ID combo | `"IDT_NONE"` | The input device transform for the chosen version. The version's own list, starting with `"IDT_NONE"`. |
| Exposure Index | `ExposureIndex` | ID combo | `"800"` | `"400"` or `"800"`. |
| Output Transform | `OutputTransform200` (also `OutputTransform130`, `OutputTransform120`, `OutputTransform110`, `OutputTransform100`) | ID combo | `"ODT_NONE"` | The output device transform for the chosen version, starting with `"ODT_NONE"`. |
| Output Mid Gray | `OutputMidGray7`, `OutputMidGray15` | Number | 7.2 and 15 (1 to 99) | The output mid grey. Two controls with this label, one shown for each version (which version each belongs to was not checked). |
| Gamut Compress Type | `GamutCompressType` | ID combo | `"ACES_GAMUT_COMPRESS_NONE"` | `"ACES_GAMUT_COMPRESS_NONE"`, `"ACES_GAMUT_COMPRESS_REFERENCE"` or `"ACES_GAMUT_COMPRESS_CREATIVE"`. |
| Cyan, Magenta, Yellow Limit | `CyanLimit`, `MagentaLimit`, `YellowLimit` | Number | 1.147, 1.264, 1.312 (1.001 to 2) | How far each colour can go out of gamut before it's compressed. |
| Cyan, Magenta, Yellow Threshold | `CyanThreshold`, `MagentaThreshold`, `YellowThreshold` | Number | 0.815, 0.803, 0.88 (0 to 1) | Where the compression starts for each colour. |
| Roll-Off | `RollOff` | Number | 1.2 (0.5 to 2) | How gradually the compression rolls off. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the transform and re-multiplies after. On by default. |

The version-specific transform lists are long (several hundred IDs for ACES 2.0.0). Choose them from the drop-down in the
Inspector, or read the list with `tool.InputTransform200.GetAttrs()['INPIDT_ComboControl_ID']`. Some IDs in the live list
contain trailing spaces (for example `"IDT_ARRI_LOGC4_CSC"` followed by spaces); copy them exactly as the list gives them.

### Example

An sRGB image taken into ACES 2.0.0, and an ACES result shown as Rec.709.

```python
aces = comp.AddTool('AcesTransform')
aces.AcesVersion = 'ACES_VERSION_2_0_0'
aces.InputTransform200 = 'IDT_SRGB_CSC'
aces.OutputTransform200 = 'ODT_REC709_100'
aces.GamutCompressType = 'ACES_GAMUT_COMPRESS_NONE'

print(aces.GetInput('AcesVersion'), aces.GetInput('InputTransform200'), aces.GetInput('OutputTransform200'))
```

### Tips

- Set `AcesVersion` first. Only the transform menus for that version are shown; the others are hidden.
- For a camera's IDT, pick it from the Inspector's list, which is long; the example uses sRGB's IDT, which has no trailing spaces.

**See also:** Color Space Transform, Gamut, OCIO ColorSpace.

## Auto Gain (`AutoGain`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** AG · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Stretches the tonal range of an image automatically. The darkest pixels are set to the Low value and the brightest to the
High value, and everything between is stretched to fill the range. By default the darkest pixels go to black and the
brightest to white.

**Use for:** quickly normalising a dull or underexposed image, or setting the black and white points of a plate before a grade.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Do Z | `DoZ` | Checkbox | 0 | Also applies the adjustment to the Z channel (label only; not checked). |
| Low | `Low` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | The value the darkest pixels are set to. |
| High | `High` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | The value the brightest pixels are set to. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the adjustment to the mask. |

### Example

Stretch an image so its darkest pixels go to 0.05 and its brightest to 0.95, to leave some headroom at each end.

```python
ag = comp.AddTool('AutoGain')
ag.Low = 0.05
ag.High = 0.95

print(ag.GetInput('Low'), ag.GetInput('High'))
```

### Tips

- The stretch is set by the image's own darkest and brightest pixels, so the result depends on the content. For a fixed
  correction use Brightness / Contrast.
- Auto Gain's result depends on the image, so its effect was not checked: a scratch comp can't process images.

**See also:** Brightness / Contrast, Color Corrector, Light Trim.

## Brightness / Contrast (`BrightnessContrast`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** BC · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A single-node tone control with gain, lift, gamma, contrast, brightness and saturation, plus a Low/High range remap.
Gamma is applied after gain and before contrast (see Tips). The channel buttons restrict the adjustment to Red, Green,
Blue or Alpha.

**Use for:** quick overall exposure and contrast changes, lifting or pulling the blacks and whites, adjusting saturation, and
remapping a flat image's range with Low and High.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Multi-button (one option each) | Red, Green, Blue 1; Alpha 0 | Channels the adjustment applies to. Alpha is off by default. |
| Gain | `Gain` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Multiplies the pixel values. Affects highlights more than shadows. |
| Lift | `Lift` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Raises or lowers the blacks; affects low values most. |
| Gamma | `Gamma` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Midtone brightness, with black and white unchanged. Above 1 brightens the mids. |
| Contrast | `Contrast` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Stretches (positive) or squeezes (negative) values around the midpoint. |
| Brightness | `Brightness` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Adds the same value to every pixel. |
| Saturation | `Saturation` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | 0 is greyscale, 1 is unchanged. |
| Low | `Low` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | The input level that becomes black. Raising it darkens the shadows. |
| High | `High` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | The input level that becomes white. |
| Direction | `Direction` | Multi-button | 0: Forward, 1: Reverse | Reverse inverts the adjustments, so they can be undone further downstream. |
| Clip Black | `ClipBlack` | Checkbox | 0 | Clips values below 0 in float images. |
| Clip White | `ClipWhite` | Checkbox | 0 | Clips values above 1 in float images. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before the adjustment and re-multiplies after, for premultiplied images. |

### Example

Lift the blacks a little, add contrast, and add a touch of saturation, with the adjustment on RGB only.

```python
bc = comp.AddTool('BrightnessContrast')
bc.Lift = 0.04
bc.Contrast = 0.1
bc.Saturation = 1.1
bc.Alpha = 0                            # keep Alpha unchanged (the default)

print(bc.GetInput('Lift'), bc.GetInput('Contrast'), bc.GetInput('Saturation'))
```

### Tips

- The manual says gamma is applied after gain and before contrast. Not checked against the render, since scratch comps
  can't process images.
- Brightness adds a fixed amount to every pixel, but Gain and Lift vary by level. Use Brightness for an exact offset.
- Low and High remap the range: the manual's example maps a Low of 0.2 and a High of 0.8 so that 0.2 becomes black and 0.8 white.
- Channel buttons are applied by the node before the image is processed, so turning off a channel leaves it out of the
  calculation. The Settings tab's RGBA buttons work differently: they copy the channel back after processing.

**See also:** Color Corrector, Color Gain, Color Curves, Auto Gain, Light Trim.

## Channel Booleans (`ChannelBoolean`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** Bol · **Inputs:** `Background` (orange), `Foreground` (green), Effect Mask (blue), `Matte` (white) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Combines the channels of the foreground with the channels of the background. Each background channel (Red, Green, Blue, Alpha)
gets a source chosen from the foreground's channels, or from the background's own, and an operation (Copy, Add,
Multiply, Maximum and so on) combines them. Only the Background is required. If no foreground is connected, the
foreground choices use the background's channels. The Aux page does the same for auxiliary channels such as Z depth,
object ID and normals, from a 3D render.

**Use for:** moving a channel from one image to another, building a matte from a channel (for example a foreground's
red channel into the background's alpha), inverting or combining channels, and copying Z depth or object IDs between
renders.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | `Operation` | Combo | 0: Copy (see below) | The operation applied to each target channel. |
| To Red | `ToRed` | Combo | 0: Red FG | Source for the background's red channel. |
| To Green | `ToGreen` | Combo | 1: Green FG | Source for the background's green channel. |
| To Blue | `ToBlue` | Combo | 2: Blue FG | Source for the background's blue channel. |
| To Alpha | `ToAlpha` | Combo | 3: Alpha FG | Source for the background's alpha channel. |
| Enable Extra channels | `EnableExtraChannels` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows the Aux page for auxiliary channels. |
| To Z Buffer | `ToZBuffer` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the Z buffer (Aux page). |
| To Z Coverage | `ToZCoverage` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the Z coverage (Aux page). |
| To Object ID | `ToObjectID` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the object ID (Aux page). |
| To Material ID | `ToMaterialID` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the material ID (Aux page). |
| To U Texture, To V Texture | `ToUTexture`, `ToVTexture` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the texture coordinates (Aux page). |
| To X, Y, Z Normal | `ToXNormal`, `ToYNormal`, `ToZNormal` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the surface normal (Aux page). |
| To BG Red, BG Green, BG Blue, BG Alpha | `ToBGRed`, `ToBGGreen`, `ToBGBlue`, `ToBGAlpha` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the background-colour channels (Aux page). |
| To X Vector, To Y Vector | `ToXVector`, `ToYVector` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the motion vectors (Aux page). |
| To X BackVector, To Y BackVector | `ToXBackVector`, `ToYBackVector` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the back motion vectors (Aux page). |
| To X Position, To Y Position, To Z Position | `ToXPosition`, `ToYPosition`, `ToZPosition` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the world position (Aux page). |
| To X Disparity, To Y Disparity | `ToXDisparity`, `ToYDisparity` | Combo | 4: Do Nothing | Source for the stereo disparity (Aux page). |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the operation to the mask. |
| Matte | `Matte` | Mask | none | Combines an external matte with the foreground and background operations. |

**Operation** indexes: 0: Copy, 1: Add, 2: Subtract, 3: And, 4: Or, 5: Exclusive Or, 6: Multiply, 7: Divide,
8: Maximum, 9: Minimum, 10: Negative, 11: Solid, 12: Clear, 13: Difference, 14: Signed Add.

**To Red / To Green / To Blue / To Alpha** (the same list for each, 0 to 39): 0: Red FG, 1: Green FG, 2: Blue FG, 3: Alpha FG,
4: Do Nothing, 5: Red BG, 6: Green BG, 7: Blue BG, 8: Alpha BG, 9: Hue FG, 10: Lightness FG, 11: Saturation FG,
12: Hue BG, 13: Lightness BG, 14: Saturation BG, 15: Black, 16: White, 17: Mid Grey, 18: Z Buffer FG, 19: Z Coverage FG,
20: Object ID FG, 21: Material ID FG, 22: U Texture FG, 23: V Texture FG, 24: X Normal FG, 25: Y Normal FG,
26: Z Normal FG, 27: Background Red FG, 28: Background Green FG, 29: Background Blue FG, 30: Matte, 31: X Vector FG,
32: Y Vector FG, 33: X BackVect FG, 34: Y BackVect FG, 35: X Position FG, 36: Y Position FG, 37: Z Position FG,
38: X Disparity FG, 39: Y Disparity FG.

The Aux channel controls use the same list, but the Aux page's default is 4 (Do Nothing).

### Example

Copy the foreground's red channel into the background's alpha, to use it as a matte, and leave the background's colours
unchanged.

```python
cb = comp.AddTool('ChannelBoolean')
cb.Operation = 0                        # Copy
cb.ToRed = 4                            # Do Nothing: keep the background's red
cb.ToGreen = 4                          # Do Nothing
cb.ToBlue = 4                           # Do Nothing
cb.ToAlpha = 0                          # the foreground's red becomes the alpha

print(cb.GetInput('ToAlpha'), cb.GetInput('Operation'))
```

Connect the foreground with `cb.Foreground = source.Output` for the foreground choices to use a clip.

### Tips

- The Aux page only matters when the image has auxiliary channels from a 3D render or the Dimension tools. Otherwise the
  defaults (Do Nothing) leave them alone.
- Choosing Do Nothing on a channel leaves that channel as it is. Use it to change one channel only.

**See also:** Merge, Copy Aux, Color Corrector.

## Chromatic Aberration Removal (`ChromaticAberrationRemoval`)

**Category:** Color\Revival · **Short name:** CAr · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Corrects the colour fringing that a lens produces at its edges, where red, green and blue focus at slightly different
radii from the lens centre. Each channel is adjusted around the Lens Center to bring the fringes back into line. The Show
Estimated Fringes checkboxes display each channel's fringe against grey, so you can see when the channels are aligned.

**Use for:** removing purple or green fringes around high-contrast edges in wide-angle or low-quality lens footage.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lens Center | `LensCenter` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The optical centre the fringe is measured from. |
| Stronger Correction | `StrongerCorrection` | Checkbox | 0 | A stronger correction (label only). |
| Red / Cyan Balance | `BalanceRed` | Number | 1 (0.7 to 1.3; allowed 0.2 to 5) | Scales the red channel's fringe. |
| Green / Purple Balance | `BalanceGreen` | Number | 1 (0.7 to 1.3; allowed 0.2 to 5) | Scales the green channel's fringe. |
| Blue / Yellow Balance | `BalanceBlue` | Number | 1 (0.7 to 1.3; allowed 0.2 to 5) | Scales the blue channel's fringe. |
| Brightness | `Brightness` | Number | 6 (1 to 20; allowed 0.5 to 50) | Brightness (label only). |
| Red / Cyan Scale | `CurvatureRed` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | Curvature of the red channel's fringe, across the frame. |
| Red / Cyan Edge | `Curvature4thRed` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | The red fringe's correction towards the edges (label-based). |
| Show Estimated Fringes (red) | `IsEstRedFringes` | Checkbox | 0 | Displays the estimated red fringe against grey. |
| Green / Purple Scale | `CurvatureGreen` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | Curvature of the green channel's fringe. |
| Green / Purple Edge | `Curvature4thGreen` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | The green fringe's correction at the edges. |
| Show Estimated Fringes (green) | `IsEstGreenFringes` | Checkbox | 0 | Displays the estimated green fringe against grey. |
| Blue / Yellow Scale | `CurvatureBlue` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | Curvature of the blue channel's fringe. |
| Blue / Yellow Edge | `Curvature4thBlue` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; allowed -5 to 5) | The blue fringe's correction at the edges. |
| Show Estimated Fringes (blue) | `IsEstBlueFringes` | Checkbox | 0 | Displays the estimated blue fringe against grey. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the correction and re-multiplies after. On by default. |

### Example

Turn on the red fringe display so the red channel can be lined up with the others by eye.

```python
car = comp.AddTool('ChromaticAberrationRemoval')
car.LensCenter = [0.5, 0.5]             # the centre of the frame
car.IsEstRedFringes = 1                 # show the red fringe against grey
car.CurvatureRed = 0.02                 # then adjust until the fringe is flat

print(car.GetInput('IsEstRedFringes'), car.GetInput('CurvatureRed'))
```

### Tips

- Adjust one channel at a time, with its Show Estimated Fringes checkbox on, until its fringe is flat against grey.
- The effect of each value was not checked in a render. Stronger Correction is only described by its label.

**See also:** Lens Distort, Color Corrector, Color Space Transform.

## Chromatic Adaptation (`ChromaticAdaptation`)

**Category:** Color\ColorFX · **Short name:** CRa · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Transforms an image that was lit or recorded under one illuminant (a light source such as daylight or tungsten) so that it
appears as if lit under another. You set the source illuminant and the target illuminant, each by standard illuminant,
colour temperature (Kelvin with tint), or CIE1931 chromaticity (x, y). The Method sets the adaptation transform used to
map one white point to the other.

**Use for:** correcting an image shot under tungsten light but graded for daylight, or matching the white point of two
shots taken under different light.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | `CATMethod` | ID combo | `"CAT_CAT02"` | The chromatic adaptation transform: `"CAT_BRADFORD"`, `"CAT_BRADFORD_LINEAR"`, `"CAT_CAT02"`, `"CAT_CMCCAT2000"`, `"CAT_CMCCAT97"`, `"CAT_SHARP"`, `"CAT_VON_KRIES"` or `"CAT_XYZ_SCALE"`. |
| Source Illuminant Type | `SourceIlluminantType` | ID combo | `"Standard"` | How the source is given: `"Standard"` (a named illuminant), `"ColorTemp"` (Kelvin and Tint) or `"CIE1931"` (x and y). |
| Source Std. Illuminant | `SourceStdIlluminant` | ID combo | `"Illuminant::D65"` | The source's named illuminant (`"Illuminant::A"` to `"Illuminant::F12"`, including `"Illuminant::D50"`, `"Illuminant::D55"`, `"Illuminant::D65"` and `"Illuminant::ACES"`). |
| Source Kelvin | `SourceKelvin` | Number | 6500 (2000 to 50000) | The source colour temperature, when the type is ColorTemp. |
| Source Tint | `SourceTint` | Number | about 0.363 on a new instance (registered 0; -150 to 150) | Green-magenta tint of the source, with ColorTemp. |
| Source x, y | `SourceChromaticX`, `SourceChromaticY` | Number | 0.3127, 0.329 (0 to 1) | The source's CIE1931 chromaticity, when the type is CIE1931. |
| Target Illuminant Type | `TargetIlluminantType` | ID combo | `"Standard"` | How the target is given, with the same three values as the source. |
| Target Std. Illuminant | `TargetStdIlluminant` | ID combo | `"Illuminant::D65"` | The target's named illuminant. |
| Target Kelvin, Target Tint | `TargetKelvin`, `TargetTint` | Number | 6500, 0 | The target colour temperature and tint, with ColorTemp. |
| Target x, y | `TargetChromaticX`, `TargetChromaticY` | Number | 0.3127, 0.329 (0 to 1) | The target's CIE1931 chromaticity, with CIE1931. |
| Color Space | `ColorSpace` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | The colour space of the image. |
| Gamma | `Gamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | The gamma of the image. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the transform and re-multiplies after. On by default. |

The Standard illuminant IDs use the form `"Illuminant::D65"`. The Color Space and Gamma IDs are those of Color Space Transform.

### Example

Adapt an image shot under tungsten (3200 K) to look as if it were shot in daylight (6500 K).

```python
ca = comp.AddTool('ChromaticAdaptation')
ca.SourceIlluminantType = 'ColorTemp'
ca.SourceKelvin = 3200
ca.TargetIlluminantType = 'ColorTemp'
ca.TargetKelvin = 6500
ca.CATMethod = 'CAT_CAT02'

print(ca.GetInput('SourceKelvin'), ca.GetInput('TargetKelvin'))
```

### Tips

- Set the illuminant type first. Each type shows its own controls: Standard shows the named illuminant, ColorTemp shows
  Kelvin and Tint, and CIE1931 shows x and y. Checked from script: changing the type changes the visible set this way.
- The adaptation's effect on the image was not checked in a render.

**See also:** White Balance, Color Space Transform, Gamut.

## Color Corrector (`ColorCorrector`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** CC · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), `MatchReference` (green), Effect Mask (blue), `MatchMask` (white) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

The main grading tool. It corrects colour in four tonal ranges (Master, Shadows, Midtones and Highlights): each range has
its own hue, saturation, contrast, gain, lift, gamma and brightness, with per-channel values beside the RGB ones. The
Levels menu remaps black, white and midtone points for each range, the Histogram menu equalises or matches the image to
a reference, and the Suppress menu removes a colour. Master adjustments apply to the whole image, and a range
adjustment affects only the pixels in that range. The Ranges tab sets where the ranges begin and end.

**Use for:** primary and secondary grades: balancing shots, lifting blacks, warming highlights, desaturating shadows,
matching one shot to another, and removing an unwanted colour cast or colour.

The Inspector's Menu and Range menus only choose which controls are shown. Each control keeps its value, and a script
can set any range's controls directly by ID, whatever the menus are set to.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menu | `Menu` | Multi-button | 0: Colors, 1: Levels, 2: Histogram, 3: Suppress | Chooses which set of controls the Correction tab shows. |
| Range | `CorrectionRange` | Multi-button | 0: Master, 1: Shadows, 2: Midtones, 3: Highlights | The tonal range the Colors, Levels and Suppress controls apply to (Master is the whole image). |
| Channel | `Channel` | Multi-button | 0: RGB, 1: Red, 2: Green, 3: Blue | In Colors mode, shows the RGB or per-channel Contrast, Gain, Lift, Gamma and Brightness controls. |
| Hue | `Hue1`, `Hue2`, `Hue3`, `Hue4` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Hue shift for Master, Shadows, Midtones and Highlights. Each is the same input as the matching colour wheel hue (`WheelHue1`…`WheelHue4`). |
| Saturation | `Saturation1`, `Saturation2`, `Saturation3`, `Saturation4` | Number | 1 (0 to 2) | Saturation of each range: 0 is grey, 1 is unchanged. Same input as `WheelSaturation1`…`WheelSaturation4`. |
| Tint Angle | `WheelTintAngle1`…`WheelTintAngle4` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Direction of the tint for each range, shown on the colour wheel. |
| Tint Length | `WheelTintLength1`…`WheelTintLength4` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Strength of the tint for each range. |
| Tint Mode | `TintMode` | Multi-button | 2: Better (0: Fast, 1: Full) | The algorithm for hue and tint. Fast is quicker, for large images. |
| Contrast | `MasterRGBContrast`, `ShadowsRGBContrast`, `MidTonesRGBContrast`, `HighlightsRGBContrast` | Number | 1 (0 to 3) | Stretches or squeezes values around the midpoint. Per-channel IDs insert `Red`, `Green` or `Blue` before `Contrast`, as in `MasterRedContrast`. |
| Gain | `MasterRGBGain`, `ShadowsRGBGain`, `MidTonesRGBGain`, `HighlightsRGBGain` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Multiplier. Affects highlights more than shadows. Per channel: `MasterRedGain` and so on. |
| Lift | `MasterRGBLift`, `ShadowsRGBLift`, `MidTonesRGBLift`, `HighlightsRGBLift` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Raises or lowers the blacks; affects low values most. Per channel: `MasterRedLift` and so on. |
| Gamma | `MasterRGBGamma`, `ShadowsRGBGamma`, `MidTonesRGBGamma`, `HighlightsRGBGamma` | Number | 1 (0 to 3) | Midtone brightness. Above 1 brightens the mids; black and white are unchanged. Per channel: `MasterRedGamma` and so on. |
| Brightness | `MasterRGBBrightness`, `ShadowsRGBBrightness`, `MidTonesRGBBrightness`, `HighlightsRGBBrightness` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Adds a value to every pixel in the range, linearly. Per channel: `MasterRedBrightness` and so on. |
| Levels Low | `MasterRGBLow`, `ShadowsRGBLow`, `MidTonesRGBLow`, `HighlightsRGBLow` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | The input black point (Levels menu). Per channel: `MasterRedLow` and so on. |
| Levels Mid | `MasterRGBMid`, `ShadowsRGBMid`, `MidTonesRGBMid`, `HighlightsRGBMid` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | The midtone control of the Levels menu. |
| Levels High | `MasterRGBHigh`, `ShadowsRGBHigh`, `MidTonesRGBHigh`, `HighlightsRGBHigh` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | The input white point (Levels menu). |
| Output Low | `MasterRGBOutputLow`, `ShadowsRGBOutputLow`, `MidTonesRGBOutputLow`, `HighlightsRGBOutputLow` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | The output black level (Levels menu). |
| Output High | `MasterRGBOutputHigh`, `ShadowsRGBOutputHigh`, `MidTonesRGBOutputHigh`, `HighlightsRGBOutputHigh` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | The output white level. |
| Suppress | `Red1`…`Red4`, `Yellow1`…`Yellow4`, `Green1`…`Green4`, `Cyan1`…`Cyan4`, `Blue1`…`Blue4`, `Magenta1`…`Magenta4` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | How much each colour is suppressed in each range: 1 is no suppression, and lower values suppress more. The number matches the range (1 Master, 2 Shadows, 3 Midtones, 4 Highlights). |
| Suppression Angle | `SuppressionAngle1`…`SuppressionAngle4` | Number | 0 (0 to 0.1667) | Rotates the six suppression handles to target a colour. |
| Ranges Range | `RangesRange` | Multi-button | 0: Result, 1: Shadows, 2: Midtones, 3: Highlights | The Ranges tab display: Result shows the graded image; the others show the range as a matte. |
| Ranges Channel | `RangesChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Luminance, 1: Red, 2: Green, 3: Blue, 4: Alpha | Channel used to show the range. |
| Render Range | `RenderOutputRange` | Checkbox | 0 | Outputs the range matte shown in the viewer as the final render, for use as a mask. |
| Simple / Smooth ranges | `PresetSimpleRanges`, `PresetSmoothRanges` | Button | 0 | Reset the range spline to linear (Simple) or smooth (Smooth, the default). |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before grading and re-multiplies after, for premultiplied images. |
| Process Order | `ProcessOrder` | Combo | 1: Gamma After Levels (0: Gamma Before Levels) | Whether gamma is applied before or after the Levels controls. |
| Histogram Proxy Scale | `HistogramProxyScale` | Number | 3 (1 to 16) | Precision of the histogram calculation. Lower values are more precise. |
| Histogram Ignore Transparent | `HistogramIgnoreTransparent` | Checkbox | 1 | Excludes transparent pixels from the histogram. |

The Histogram menu's Type (`HistogramType`: 0 Keep, 1 Equalize, 2 Match), Match Luminance (`EqualizeLuminance`),
Lock R/G/B (`LockRedGreenBlue`) and Equalize/Match controls (`EqualizeRed`, `EqualizeGreen`, `EqualizeBlue`) work
with a reference image connected to `MatchReference`. Their effect is not verified here, since a scratch comp can't process
images.

### Example

A simple grade: a little more Master gain and midtone gamma, lifted and cooler shadows, and softer highlights.

```python
cc = comp.AddTool('ColorCorrector')

# Master (the whole image)
cc.MasterRGBGain = 1.1
cc.MasterRGBGamma = 0.95
cc.Saturation1 = 1.1                    # Master saturation (same input as WheelSaturation1)

# Shadows
cc.ShadowsRGBLift = 0.03
cc.ShadowsBlueGain = 0.9                # Blue channel only, in the shadows
cc.Saturation2 = 0.8                    # Shadows saturation

# Highlights
cc.HighlightsRGBGain = 0.98
cc.Saturation4 = 0.9                    # Highlights saturation

print(cc.GetInput('MasterRGBGain'), cc.GetInput('ShadowsRGBLift'), cc.GetInput('Saturation4'))
```

The number at the end of a colour wheel or saturation ID gives its range: 1 is Master, 2 Shadows, 3 Midtones and 4 Highlights.

### Tips

- Each range is independent: a Shadows Gain does not change the Highlights Gain. RGB and per-channel values are separate
  inputs. The source applies the RGB value first and then the channel's own value, so the two combine.
- Setting `Hue1` also sets `WheelHue1`, and the other way round. The two are the same input.
- Use `CorrectionRange` only to choose what the Inspector shows. It does not change the controls' values.
- To mask the grade, connect a shape or matte to `EffectMask`, or set `RenderOutputRange` to use a range matte as the output.

**See also:** Color Curves, Hue Curves, Brightness / Contrast, Color Gain, White Balance, Gamut, Color Space Transform.

## Color Curves (`ColorCurves`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** CCv · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), `ReferenceImage` (green), Effect Mask (blue), `MatchMask` (white) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Adjusts each channel with a curve: the horizontal axis is the input value (0 to 1) and the vertical axis is the output
value. Red, Green, Blue and Alpha each have their own curve, and the Edit checkboxes choose which curves the Inspector
edits. The Match and Sample buttons can build a curve that matches the image to a reference, and the Color Space menu
switches the curves to another colour model (RGB, YUV, HLS, YIQ or CMY).

**Use for:** contrast and colour curves on individual channels, such as a red-channel S-curve, a lift in the blues, or
matching the colour balance of one shot to another.

The curves are LUT inputs (`LookUpTable`). They're set from script through a LUTBezier modifier, as described under
*Curves from script* below.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | Combo | 2: No Animation (0: Dissolve Color Correct, 1: Animated Color Correct) | Whether the curves can be animated over time. No Animation applies the curves the same at every frame. |
| Color Space | `ColorSpace` | Combo | 0: RGB (1: YUV, 2: HLS, 3: YIQ, 4: CMY) | Colour model the curves act in. |
| Edit Red, Edit Green, Edit Blue, Edit Alpha | `EditRed`, `EditGreen`, `EditBlue`, `EditAlpha` | Checkbox | 1 | Whether each curve is included in editing. |
| Red | `Red` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Output curve for red. Set through a LUTBezier modifier. |
| Green | `Green` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Output curve for green. |
| Blue | `Blue` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Output curve for blue. |
| Alpha | `Alpha` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Output curve for alpha. |
| Match | `MatchReference` | Button | 0 | Builds the curves from a comparison of the input and the reference image. Needs images, so not checked here. |
| Sample | `SampleReference` | Button | 0 | Samples the reference image for the match. |
| Number of Samples | `NumberOfSamplesOnMatchCurve` | Number | 64 (2 to 256) | Points used to build the match curves. |
| Ignore Transparent | `IgnoreTransparent` | Checkbox | 1 | Excludes transparent pixels from the match. |
| Show Match Rectangle | `MatchShow` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows the area sampled for the match. |
| Match Center | `MatchCenter` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the match area. |
| Match Width, Match Height | `MatchWidth`, `MatchHeight` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Size of the match area. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before the curves and re-multiplies after, for premultiplied images. |

### Curves from script

`Red`, `Green`, `Blue` and `Alpha` are LookUpTable inputs, so they can't be set to a value. Attach a `LUTBezier`
modifier to the curve, then set its keys. A key's position is its input value (0 to 1, in the first number) and its
output value, in a dict with the key `1`. Handles are set automatically if you don't give them. The same method
works for HueCurves and Grain.

```python
m = cc.Red.GetConnectedOutput().GetTool()
m.SetKeyFrames({0.0: {1: 0.0}, 0.5: {1: 0.5}, 1.0: {1: 1.0}})
```

Read the keys back with `m.GetKeyFrames()`. `SetKeyFrames` replaces every key, so give the whole curve each time.

### Example

An S-curve on the red channel: the shadows and highlights are pulled in, and the midtones are kept steep.

```python
cc = comp.AddTool('ColorCurves')

cc.AddModifier('Red', 'LUTBezier')      # attach the curve for Red
red = cc.Red.GetConnectedOutput().GetTool()
red.SetKeyFrames({
    0.0:  {1: 0.0},
    0.25: {1: 0.18},
    0.75: {1: 0.82},
    1.0:  {1: 1.0},
})

print(red.GetKeyFrames())
```

### Tips

- Keys are on the 0 to 1 input range of the curve. Keys outside that range weren't tested.
- The keys' handles are set automatically when you don't give them, so the handle values read back with `GetKeyFrames()`
  can differ from the ones you'd expect.
- `EditRed` and the other Edit checkboxes control which curves the Inspector edits. Their effect on the render was not checked.

### Open items

- The curve's value at an input can't be read from script, since the rendered output isn't available in a scratch comp.
- The effect of `ColorSpace` and the match and sample buttons was not checked in a render.

**See also:** Hue Curves, Color Corrector, Color Gain, Brightness / Contrast.

## Color Gain (`ColorGain`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** Clr · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A lighter-weight version of the Color Corrector's basic controls, which can render faster. It sets gain, lift, gamma and
saturation per channel, and adds a Balance tab that pushes the highs, mids and darks towards a colour pair (red and
cyan, green and magenta, or blue and yellow) or changes their brightness, and a Hue tab that shifts each range's hue
without changing its brightness or saturation.

**Use for:** quick per-channel colour fixes, such as a red cast in the shadows, or a fast hue or balance shift on a
clip, where the full Color Corrector isn't needed.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock R/G/B | `LockRGB` | Checkbox | 0 | In the Inspector, links the red, green and blue Gain, Lift, Gamma and Saturation sliders. Setting one channel from a script does not change the others. |
| Gain | `GainRed`, `GainGreen`, `GainBlue`, `GainAlpha` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Multiplies each channel. Affects bright pixels more than dark ones. |
| Lift | `LiftRed`, `LiftGreen`, `LiftBlue`, `LiftAlpha` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Raises or lowers each channel's blacks. |
| Gamma | `GammaRed`, `GammaGreen`, `GammaBlue`, `GammaAlpha` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Midtone brightness of each channel. Black and white are unchanged. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before the correction and re-multiplies after, for premultiplied images. |
| Saturation | `SaturationRed`, `SaturationGreen`, `SaturationBlue` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Strength of each channel's colour. 0 removes that channel's colour; above 1 intensifies it. |
| Balance (High, Mid, Dark) | `HighRedCyan`, `HighGreenMagenta`, `HighBlueYellow`, HighBrightness, and the same set for Mid and Dark | Number | 0 (-1 to 1; brightness -0.3 to 0.3) | Pushes the range's red towards cyan, green towards magenta and blue towards yellow, and sets its brightness. |
| High / Mid / Dark Hue | `HighHue`, `MidHue`, `DarkHue` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Shifts the hue of each range without changing brightness or saturation. At -1 or 1 the hue completes a cycle and returns to its original value. |
| Color Ranges | `ColorRanges` | Curve | Smooth | The spline that sets the shadow, midtone and highlight ranges. Not scriptable (see Tips). |
| Preset Simple / Smooth | `PresetSimpleRanges`, `PresetSmoothRanges` | Button | 0 | Reset the range spline to Simple (linear) or Smooth (the default). |

The Balance IDs name the range first, then the pair: `HighRedCyan` is the High range's red-cyan balance, and
`DarkBlueYellow` is the Dark range's blue-yellow balance.

### Example

Warm the mids a little, pull the red out of the shadows, and shift the highlights slightly toward yellow.

```python
cg = comp.AddTool('ColorGain')

cg.GammaRed = 1.05                      # midtone red
cg.GainGreen = 0.97                     # a touch less green overall
cg.SaturationBlue = 0.9

cg.DarkRedCyan = 0.05                   # shadows: a little cyan
cg.HighBlueYellow = 0.04                # highlights: toward yellow
cg.MidHue = 0.02                        # shift the mids' hue slightly

print(cg.GetInput('GainGreen'), cg.GetInput('DarkRedCyan'), cg.GetInput('HighBlueYellow'))
```

### Tips

- Lock R/G/B only links the sliders in the Inspector. From script each channel's value is set on its own, as the example does.
- The range spline (`ColorRanges`) has no script access to its points. The two preset buttons set it to Simple or Smooth,
  but no readback is available, so their result wasn't checked.
- For separate Shadows, Midtones and Highlights gain and lift per channel, use the Color Corrector.

**See also:** Color Corrector, Brightness / Contrast, Hue Curves, Color Curves.

## Color Matrix (`CustomColorMatrix`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** CMx · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies a custom colour matrix: each output channel is a weighted sum of the input channels, set in a table. It can mix
channels, invert them, or apply any linear colour transform that you can express as a matrix, such as a channel-swap or a
simple colour-correction matrix from another application. The Invert checkbox inverts the matrix.

**Use for:** applying a colour matrix supplied with a camera or grading tool, swapping or mixing channels, and reproducing
a transform defined as a 3x3 matrix.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix | `Matrix` | Matrix table (custom filter) | none | The colour matrix. Each row sets how an output channel is made from the input channels. |
| Invert | `Invert` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the matrix. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the matrix to the mask. |

### Example

The matrix itself is set in the Inspector. From script, only the Invert checkbox was checked.

```python
ccm = comp.AddTool('CustomColorMatrix')
ccm.Invert = 1                          # invert the matrix (set the Matrix in the Inspector)
print(ccm.GetInput('Invert'))
```

### Tips

- The Matrix is a MatrixTable input with no readable value from script. Assigning a list is accepted, but the value
  can't be read back, so its effect was not verified. Enter the matrix in the Inspector.
- Keep the Invert checkbox for when the matrix needs reversing.

### Open items

- MatrixTable value access from script: not available for readback. Needs Daniel to confirm a route.

**See also:** Color Space Transform, Channel Booleans, Color Corrector.

## Color Space (`ColorSpace`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** CS · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts the image into another colour model and back, so that channels can be worked on as hue, saturation and lightness,
luma and chroma, or other models. Fusion normally works in RGB. Color Space converts to the chosen model (Color Space
Conversion "to Color"), and "to RGB" converts it back. The B W option turns the image into greyscale, using the BW
Red, Green and Blue weights.

**Use for:** working on hue, saturation or luminance as channels, changing the colour model before a channel operation,
and making a greyscale (black and white) image with custom weights.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Color Space Conversion | `ColorSpaceConversion` | Multi-button | 0: None, 1: to Color, 2: to RGB | Converts the image into the chosen colour model (to Color), or back to RGB (to RGB). None does nothing. |
| Color Type | `ColorType` | Multi-button | 0: HSV, 1: YUV, 2: YIQ, 3: CMY, 4: HLS, 5: XYZ, 6: Negative, 7: B W | The colour model used for the conversion. B W gives a greyscale image. |
| BW Red | `BWRed` | Number | 0.299 (0 to 1) | Weight of red in the B W conversion. Shown when Color Type is B W. |
| BW Green | `BWGreen` | Number | 0.587 (0 to 1) | Weight of green in the B W conversion. |
| BW Blue | `BWBlue` | Number | 0.114 (0 to 1) | Weight of blue in the B W conversion. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the conversion to the mask. |

The default BW weights are the Rec. 601 luma coefficients (0.299, 0.587 and 0.114).

### Example

Make a black-and-white version of the image with the weights for a red filter, so red reads brighter.

```python
cs = comp.AddTool('ColorSpace')
cs.ColorSpaceConversion = 1             # to Color
cs.ColorType = 7                        # B W
cs.BWRed = 0.5
cs.BWGreen = 0.4
cs.BWBlue = 0.1

print(cs.GetInput('ColorType'), cs.GetInput('BWRed'), cs.GetInput('BWGreen'), cs.GetInput('BWBlue'))
```

### Tips

- With Color Type set to B W, the BW Red, Green and Blue sliders appear; with any other type they're hidden.
- To convert back, set Color Space Conversion to "to RGB" and Color Type to the model the image is in (for example YUV for a YUV image).
  The Settings tab's R, G and B buttons then refer to the converted channels: after RGB to HLS, Red is hue, Green is
  luminance and Blue is saturation. Alpha is never changed.
- The effect of each model was not checked in a render, so verify the result in the viewer.

**See also:** Color Space Transform, Channel Booleans, Color Corrector, Brightness / Contrast.

## Color Space Transform (`ColorSpaceTransform`)

**Category:** Color\ColorFX · **Short name:** CSt · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts an image from one colour space and gamma to another, using the same colour maths as DaVinci Resolve's Colour
Management, rather than a LUT. It can also tone-map (compress a high dynamic range into a display range) and gamut-map
(bring out-of-gamut colours into the target gamut). Swap exchanges the input and output settings. Each space and gamma
is a fixed ID from the list below, so the names are exact.

**Use for:** moving footage between camera log and linear spaces, converting to and from ACES, and changing the
display or delivery space of a graded image, without a LUT.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input Color Space | `InputColorSpace` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | The colour space of the source image. |
| Input Gamma | `InputGamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | The gamma (transfer curve) of the source image. |
| Output Color Space | `OutputColorSpace` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | The colour space to convert to. |
| Output Gamma | `OutputGamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | The gamma to convert to. |
| Swap | `Swap` | Button | 0 | Exchanges the input and output colour spaces and gammas. |
| Tone Mapping Method | `ToneMappingMethod` | ID combo | `"TM_DRT_V2"` | `"TM_NONE"`, `"TM_CLIP"`, `"TM_SIMPLE"`, `"TM_DRT_V1"`, `"TM_DRT_V2"` or `"TM_DRT_V2_XYZ"`. TM_NONE turns tone mapping off. |
| Use Custom Max. Input | `IsSrcLumMaxCustomEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses `SrcLumMax` as the source's peak luminance. |
| Max. Input (nits) | `SrcLumMax` | Number | 100 (48 to 10000) | The source's peak luminance, when custom. |
| Use Custom Max. Output | `IsDstLumMaxCustomEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses `DstLumMax` as the output's peak luminance. |
| Max. Output (nits) | `DstLumMax` | Number | 100 (48 to 10000) | The output's peak luminance, when custom. |
| Adaptation | `Adaptation` | Number | 9 (1 to 99) | Adaptation level used by tone mapping. Described from its label only (see Open items). |
| Sat. Rolloff Start (nits) | `satRolloffStart` | Number | 100 (1 to 500) | Where the saturation roll-off begins. |
| Sat. Rolloff Limit (nits) | `satRolloffLimit` | Number | 10000 (500 to 20000) | The luminance at which the roll-off ends. |
| Gamut Mapping Method | `GamutMappingMethod` | ID combo | `"GM_NONE"` | `"GM_NONE"`, `"GM_RCM_1"` or `"GM_CLIP"`. |
| Saturation Knee | `SaturationKnee` | Number | 0.9 (0.5 to 1.2) | Where saturation starts to be compressed (RCM gamut mapping). |
| Saturation Max. | `SaturationMax` | Number | 1 (0.5 to 1.2) | The most saturation kept after gamut mapping (RCM gamut mapping). |
| Use HDR Standard Conversions | `UseHDRStandardConversions` | Checkbox | 1 | Uses the standard HDR conversions. |
| HDR 203 Nits Diffuse White | `IsRec2390ScalingEnabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales HDR output to a 203-nit diffuse white. |
| Apply Forward OOTF | `ApplyForwardOOTF` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the forward opto-optical transfer function (scene to display). |
| Apply Inverse OOTF | `ApplyInverseOOTF` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the inverse transfer function (display to scene). |
| Use White Point Adaptation | `UseWhitePointAdaptation` | Checkbox | 1 | Adapts the white point between the two spaces. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the transform and re-multiplies after. On by default. |

Colour space IDs (for `InputColorSpace` and `OutputColorSpace`) include `ACES_COLORSPACE`, `ACES_AP1_COLORSPACE`,
`ADOBE_RGB_COLORSPACE`, `ALEXA3_COLORSPACE`, `ARRI_LOGC4_COLORSPACE`, `BMDFILM_COLORSPACE`, `DWG_COLORSPACE`,
`P3D65_COLORSPACE`, `REC709_COLORSPACE`, `REC2020_COLORSPACE`, `SRGB_COLORSPACE` and `XYZ_COLORSPACE`, and many more.
Gamma IDs (`InputGamma`, `OutputGamma`) include `LINEAR_GAMMA`, `REC709_GAMMA`, `SRGB_GAMMA`, `ACESCC_GAMMA`,
`ACESCCT_GAMMA`, `LOGC4_EI800_GAMMA`, `SONY_SLOG3_GAMMA` and `PQ_GAMMA`, and many more. The full lists are in the
drop-down menus. An unknown ID is accepted silently and fails to render.

### Example

A Rec.709 image, with its display gamma, converted to ACES AP1 with linear gamma and no tone mapping or gamut mapping.

```python
cst = comp.AddTool('ColorSpaceTransform')
cst.InputColorSpace = 'REC709_COLORSPACE'
cst.InputGamma = 'REC709_GAMMA'
cst.OutputColorSpace = 'ACES_AP1_COLORSPACE'
cst.OutputGamma = 'LINEAR_GAMMA'
cst.ToneMappingMethod = 'TM_NONE'
cst.GamutMappingMethod = 'GM_NONE'

print(cst.GetInput('InputColorSpace'), cst.GetInput('OutputGamma'))
```

### Tips

- Setting `Swap` to 1 from script exchanges the input and output settings, which is handy to build the reverse transform.
- The Tone Mapping and Gamut Mapping sections show only the controls their method uses. `TM_CLIP` hides Adaptation and
  the custom source maximum; `TM_NONE` hides the luminance controls; `GM_RCM_1` shows the saturation controls.
- Gamut mapping and tone mapping are separate steps. Leave both on `"..._NONE"` for a plain colour space conversion.

### Open items

- Adaptation, the HDR and OOTF switches, and the custom luminance controls are described from their labels, not the manual.
  Their effect was not checked in a render.

**See also:** Gamut, Color Space, Gamut Limiter, Gamut Mapping, ACES Transform, OCIO ColorSpace, Color Corrector.

## Copy Aux (`Dimension.CopyAux`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** CpA · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Copies an auxiliary channel (such as Z depth, object ID, normals or motion vectors, usually rendered from a 3D application)
into the image's colour channels, or the other way round. Choose the auxiliary channel and a direction (Aux to Color or
Color to Aux). Each channel can be remapped: its range of values is mapped to a new range, so that, for example, a Z depth
of 0 to 1000 can become a visible greyscale from 0 to 1. Remapping of the colour, background colour, Z, texture,
coverage, object ID, material ID, normal, vector, back vector, world position and disparity channels is set in its own group.

**Use for:** visualising a depth or ID channel as a greyscale or colour image, and copying a channel from one render into
another for compositing.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | Multi-button | 0: Aux to Color, 1: Color to Aux | Direction of the copy. |
