| Aux Channel | `Channel` | ID combo | `"Color"` | The auxiliary channel: `"Color"`, `"BgColor"`, `"Z"`, `"Texture"`, `"Coverage"`, `"ObjectID"`, `"MaterialID"`, `"Normal"`, `"Vector"`, `"BackVector"`, `"WorldPos"` or `"Disparity"`. |
| Out Color Depth | `OutColorDepth` | Combo | 0: Match Aux Channel Depth | The bit depth of the output: 0: Match Aux Channel Depth, 1: Match Source Color Depth, 2: Force float32, 3: Force float16, 4: Force int16, 5: Force int8. |
| Channel Missing | `ChannelMissing` | Combo | 0: Fail | What to do when the channel is absent: 0: Fail, 1: Use Default Value. |
| Kill Aux Channels | `KillAuxChannels` | Checkbox | 0 | Removes the auxiliary channels from the output after the copy. |
| Remapping (Color to Color) | `Color.Remap.Enable` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns on the colour remap. |
| Remap From Min, Max | `Color.Remap.From.Min`, `Color.Remap.From.Max` | Number | 0, 1 | The input range of the colour remap. |
| Remap To Min, Max | `Color.Remap.To.Min`, `Color.Remap.To.Max` | Number | 0, 1 | The output range of the colour remap. |
| Remap To Invert | `Color.Remap.To.Invert` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the output range. |
| Remap Detect, Update | `Color.Remap.From.Detect`, `Color.Remap.From.Update` | Button | 0 | Sets the From range from the channel's values. |

The other channels follow the same pattern, with their own `Enable`, `From`, `To` and `Invert` controls: for example
`Z.Remap.Enable`, `Z.Remap.From.Min`, `Z.Remap.From.Max` and `Z.Remap.To.Min`. Their IDs use the channel's name as the
prefix: `BgColor`, `Texture`, `Coverage`, `ObjectID`, `MaterialID`, `Normal`, `Vector`, `BackVector`, `WorldPos` and
`Disparity`. Their default From ranges differ; for example `ObjectID.Remap.From.Max` defaults to 100.

### Example

Visualise a Z depth channel as a greyscale, mapping depths from 0 to 1000 to a white-to-black range.

```python
cpa = comp.AddTool('Dimension.CopyAux')
cpa.Mode = 0                            # Aux to Color
cpa.Channel = 'Z'
cpa['Z.Remap.Enable'] = 1          # dotted IDs use item syntax
cpa['Z.Remap.From.Min'] = 0
cpa['Z.Remap.From.Max'] = 1000
cpa['Z.Remap.To.Min'] = 0
cpa['Z.Remap.To.Max'] = 1

print(cpa.GetInput('Channel'), cpa.GetInput('Z.Remap.From.Max'))
```

### Tips

- Set `Channel` and `Mode` first. Mode changes which options are shown: Color to Aux hides the Out Color Depth,
  Channel Missing and Kill Aux Channels controls.
- `Detect Range` and `Update Range` read the channel's values from the image. They need a rendered input, so they were not
  run here.

**See also:** Channel Booleans, Color Corrector, Merge 3D.

## Film Look Creator (`FilmLookCreator`)

**Category:** Color (ColorFX) · **Short name:** FLc · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A creative look tool. It applies a film-style grade, with a core look, colour and contrast settings, split toning, vignette,
halation and bloom, grain, flicker, gate weave and a film gate, all from one node. A Presets menu sets the controls to a
fixed look, and each part can be turned on or off and adjusted. Colour space overrides at the top let the look work in a
space other than the input's. This tool is not in the manual; the description and values here come from the live tool
and its source.

**Use for:** a fast, stylised film look on a plate, with grain, gate weave and vignette, or a starting point to adjust.

Choose a preset first, then adjust the controls. A preset writes its values to the controls, so anything set before it
is replaced.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Presets | `GlobalPresets` | ID combo | `"GlobalPresetDefault65"` | Sets the look controls to a preset: `"GlobalPresetDefault35"`, `"GlobalPresetAurora"`, `"GlobalPresetCinematic"`, `"GlobalPresetBleachBypass"`, `"GlobalPresetNostalgic"`, `"GlobalPresetNoEffects"`, `"GlobalPresetCleanSlate"`, `"GlobalPresetCustom"`, or `"GlobalPresetDefault65"` (the starting values). |
| Color Blend | `ColorBlend` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Strength of the colour part of the look. |
| Effects Blend | `EffectsBlend` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Strength of the effects (vignette, halation, bloom, grain, flicker, gate weave and gate). |
| 3D LUT Compatible | `IsLutCompatible` | Checkbox | 0 | The label only; its effect was not checked. |
| Input Color Space | `InputColorSpace` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | Colour space the look assumes for the input. Colour space IDs are as in Color Space Transform. |
| Input Gamma | `InputGamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | Gamma the look assumes for the input. |
| Output Color Space | `OutputColorSpace` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | Colour space of the result. |
| Output Gamma | `OutputGamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | Gamma of the result. |
| Output White Point | `outputIlluminant` | ID combo | `"Illuminant::D65"` | White point of the result. |
| Film Look Blend | `FilmLookBlend` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Strength of the core look. |
| Core Look | `FilmLookCoreLook` | ID combo | `"CoreLookCinematic"` | The base look: `"CoreLookCinematic"`, `"CoreLookRochester"`, `"CoreLookAkasaka"`, `"CoreLookElated"`, `"CoreLookVintage"` or `"CoreLookAurora"`. |
| Skin Bias | `FilmLookSkinBias` | Number | 0 | Protects or emphasises skin tones in the core look. |
| Exposure | `ColorExposure` | Number | 0 | Exposure of the colour part. |
| Contrast | `ColorContrast` | Number | 1.25 | Contrast of the colour part. |
| Highlights | `ColorHighlightThreshold` | Number | 0.65 | Where the highlight roll-off starts. Labelled Highlights in the Inspector. |
| Highlight Rolloff | `ColorHighlightRolloff` | Number | 0.5 | How gradually highlights roll off. |
| Fade | `ColorFadeThreshold` | Number | 0 | Where the fade (lifted blacks) starts. |
| Fade Rolloff | `ColorFadeRolloff` | Number | 0.65 | How gradually the fade rolls off. |
| Highlights (second) | `ColorHighlights` | Number | 0.35 | A second highlight control with the same label (see Open items). |
| Fade (second) | `ColorFade` | Number | 0.285 | A second fade control with the same label (see Open items). |
| White Balance | `ColorSourceWB` | Number | 6500 | The source's white balance, in kelvin (label). |
| Tint | `ColorSourceTint` | Number | 10 | The source's tint (label). |
| Subtractive Sat | `ColorPostSat` | Number | 1.2 | Saturation after the look. |
| Richness | `ColorRichness` | Number | 1 | Richness of the colour. |
| Bleach Bypass | `ColorBleachBypass` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Strength of the bleach-bypass look. |
| Enable Split Tone | `SplitIsEnable` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns split toning on. |
| Split Tone Mode | `SplitToneMode` | ID combo | `"SplitModeNatural"` | `"SplitModeNatural"` or `"SplitModeStrong"`. |
| Protect Neutrals | `SplitIsProtectNeutrals` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps neutral greys free of the split tone. |
| Split Amount | `SplitAmount` | Number | 0 | Strength of the split tone. |
| Hue Angle | `SplitAngle` | Number | 20 | Hue angle of the split tone (label). |
| Pivot | `SplitPivot` | Number | 0.3 | Pivot of the split tone (label). |
| Enable Vignette | `VignetteIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns the vignette on. |
| Vignette Amount | `VignetteAmount` | Number | 0.25 | Darkening at the edges. |
| Vignette Size | `VignetteSize` | Number | 0.25 | Vignette size (label). |
| Enable Halation | `HalationIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns halation on. |
| Highlights Only | `HalationIsHighlightsOnly` | Checkbox | 1 | Limits halation to highlights. |
| Halation Amount | `HalationAmount` | Number | 0.25 | Strength of the glow around highlights. |
| Halation Radius | `HalationRadius` | Number | 4 | Spread of the halation. |
| Halation Saturation | `HalationSaturation` | Number | 1 | Colour saturation of the halation. |
| Halation Hue | `HalationHue` | Number | 0.5 | Colour of the halation. |
| Enable Bloom | `BloomIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns bloom on. |
| Bloom Amount | `BloomAmount` | Number | 0.25 | Strength of the bloom. |
| Bloom Radius | `BloomRadius` | Number | 10 | Spread of the bloom. |
| Enable Grain | `GrainIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns grain on. |
| Grain Preset | `GrainPreset` | ID combo | `"GrainPreset65"` | `"GrainPreset65"`, `"GrainPreset35"`, `"GrainPreset16"`, `"GrainPreset8"`, `"GrainPresetAurora"` or `"GrainPresetCustom"`. |
| Grain Amount | `GrainAmount` | Number | 0.125 | Strength of the grain. |
| Grain Size | `GrainSize` | Number | 0 | Size of the grain. |
| Grain Softness | `GrainSoftness` | Number | 0.1 | Softness of the grain. |
| Grain Saturation | `GrainSaturation` | Number | 0.3 | Colour of the grain. |
| Image Defocus | `GrainImageDefocus` | Number | 1 | Image defocus under the grain (label). |
| Apply to Black | `GrainIsApplyToBlack` | Checkbox | 1 | Adds grain to black areas. |
| Enable Flicker | `FlickerIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns flicker on. |
| Flicker Amount | `FlickerAmount` | Number | 0.15 | Strength of the flicker. |
| Flicker Rate | `FlickerRate` | Number | 0.5 | How fast the flicker changes. |
| Enable Gate Weave | `GateWeaveIsEnable` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns gate weave on. |
| Gate Weave Amount | `GateWeaveAmount` | Number | 0.25 | Strength of the frame movement. |
| Gate Weave Rate | `GateWeaveRate` | Number | 0.5 | How fast the frame moves. |
| Enable Film Gate | `FilmGateIsEnable` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns the film gate (a frame mask) on. |
| Film Gate Preset | `FilmGatePreset` | ID combo | `"FilmGatePreset1331"` | `"FilmGatePreset1331"`, `"FilmGatePreset13751"`, `"FilmGatePreset151"`, `"FilmGatePreset1661"`, `"FilmGatePreset1441"`, `"FilmGatePreset241"` or `"FilmGatePresetCustom"`. |
| Film Gate Ratio | `FilmGateRatio` | Point | (1.33, 1) | Aspect of the gate, when the preset is Custom. |
| Enable Curvature | `FilmGateIsCurved` | Checkbox | 1 | Curves the gate's edges. |
| Film Gate Softness | `FilmGateSoftness` | Number | 0.2 | Softness of the gate's edge. |
| Film Gate Padding | `FilmGatePadding` | Number | 0 | Space between the gate and the frame edge. |

The `CoreLook…` controls (the core look's own sphere, split, saturation and lift/gamma/gain values) are internal look data
and aren't documented here (see Open items). Setting them from script is not recommended.

### Example

Start from the Cinematic preset, then add a little more vignette and grain.

```python
flc = comp.AddTool('FilmLookCreator')
flc.GlobalPresets = 'GlobalPresetCinematic'   # sets the look controls
flc.VignetteAmount = 0.35                     # adjust after the preset
flc.GrainAmount = 0.2

print(flc.GetInput('GlobalPresets'), flc.GetInput('ColorContrast'), flc.GetInput('VignetteAmount'))
```

### Tips

- Set `GlobalPresets` before the other look controls. Each preset writes its own values, so a control set earlier is replaced.
- The readback confirms the preset took effect: after `"GlobalPresetCinematic"`, `ColorContrast` reads 1.3 and `HalationAmount`
  reads 0.5, from the default 1.25 and 0.25.
- `"GlobalPresetBleachBypass"` sets `ColorBleachBypass` to 0.5. In the readback, the Cinematic, Aurora and No Effects presets left it at 0.
- Turn a part off with its Enable checkbox rather than setting its amount to 0, so the part can be turned back on
  with its settings intact.

### Open items

- The presets' values come from the source's table (`FilmLookCreator.cpp`). Which values each preset writes beyond those
  read back was not listed in full.
- `GlobalPresetDefault65` is the starting state and is not in the source's preset table, so choosing it may not reset
  the values. Not checked.
- Two controls share a label each: `ColorHighlights` and `ColorHighlightThreshold` are both "Highlights", and `ColorFade`
  and `ColorFadeThreshold` are both "Fade". Their roles are inferred from the order of the controls.
- The labels "Ouput Color Space" and "Ouput Gamma" are misspelt in the live tool. The IDs are `OutputColorSpace` and `OutputGamma`.
- Most look controls (halation, bloom, gate weave, flicker, split tone, grain saturation and the others marked "label") are
  described from their labels. Their effect on a render was not checked.
- The `CoreLook…` values (sphere axis, split tone targets and the core look's lift, gamma, gain and saturation) are not documented.
  Needs Daniel.

**See also:** Film Grain, Color Space Transform, Color Corrector, Cineon Log.

## Gamut (`GamutConvert`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** Gmt · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts an image from one colour gamut (set of primary colours) to another, and removes (linearises) or adds a gamma
curve at either end. The Source Space and Output Space menus name a standard gamut and gamma, or Custom, where you give
the primaries, white point and gamma yourself. Remove Gamma and Add Gamma are the two halves of linearising and then
re-encoding a log or display-referred image. With the Cineon Log node, this is the usual way to convert between camera
spaces.

**Use for:** linearising a camera or display image before compositing, changing an image to ACEScg or Rec.709 for
delivery, and re-applying a display gamma at the end of a node tree.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source Space | `SourceSpace` | ID combo | `"NoChange"` | The gamut of the image coming in. `"Custom"` shows the primaries and gamma below. |
| Remove Gamma | `RemoveGamma` | Checkbox | 1 | Converts the source to linear light, using the source gamma. |
| Output Space | `OutputSpace` | ID combo | `"NoChange"` | The gamut to convert to. `"Custom"` shows the output primaries below. |
| Add Gamma | `AddGamma` | Checkbox | 1 | Applies the output gamma after the gamut is converted. |
| Use White Point Adaptation | `WhiteAdaptation` | Checkbox | 1 | Adapts the white point between the two gamuts. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before the conversion and re-multiplies after. |

**Custom source** (shown when `SourceSpace` is `"Custom"`): `CustomSourceRed`, `CustomSourceGreen`, `CustomSourceBlue`
and `CustomSourceWhite` are the primaries and white point as `[x, y]` chromaticities (defaults Rec.709: Red `[0.64, 0.33]`,
Green `[0.3, 0.6]`, Blue `[0.15, 0.06]`, White `[0.312713, 0.329016]`). `CustomSourceGamma` (2.4), `CustomSourceLimit`
(0.0031308) and `CustomSourceSlope` (12.92) set the transfer curve, including its linear segment.

**Custom output** (shown when `OutputSpace` is `"Custom"`): `CustomOutputRed`, `CustomOutputGreen`, `CustomOutputBlue`,
`CustomOutputWhite`, `CustomOutputGamma`, `CustomOutputLimit` and `CustomOutputSlope` work the same way.

**Source Space and Output Space IDs:** `"NoChange"`, `"ACES"`, `"ACEScg"`, `"Adobe"`, `"AppleLog2"`, `"Apple"`,
`"ARRIDCI"`, `"ARRIRec709"`, `"ARRIWideGamut"`, `"ARRIWideGamut4"`, `"Beta"`, `"BMDFilm46K"`, `"BMDFilm46K3"`,
`"BMDFilm4K"`, `"BMDFilm4K3"`, `"BMDFilm"`, `"BMDPocket4K4"`, `"BMDFilmWide4"`, `"CanonCinema"`, `"CIE"`, `"ColorMatch"`,
`"DWG"`, `"ECI"`, `"ECIv2"`, `"ExtLinDispP3"`, `"Rec601"`, `"Rec709Display"`, `"Rec709"`, `"Rec2020"`, `"NTSC1953"`,
`"P3D60"`, `"P3D65"`, `"DCI"`, `"PALSECAM"`, `"VGamut"`, `"ProPhoto"`, `"RedWideGamut"`, `"SimplifiedsRGB"`, `"SMPTE170"`,
`"SMPTE240"`, `"SMPTEC"`, `"SGamut"`, `"SGamut3Cine"`, `"sRGB"`, `"WideGamut"`, `"XYZCIE"`, `"Custom"`, and `"FromImage"` (Source Space only, taken from the image; not checked) for
the Source Space only. Output Space takes the same list without `"FromImage"`. `"NoChange"` leaves that side untouched.

### Example

Convert a Rec.709 image into ACEScg, linearising it first and returning the result linear.

```python
gc = comp.AddTool('GamutConvert')
gc.SourceSpace = 'Rec709'
gc.OutputSpace = 'ACEScg'
gc.RemoveGamma = 1                      # linearise the Rec.709 source
gc.AddGamma = 0                         # keep the ACEScg result linear

print(gc.GetInput('SourceSpace'), gc.GetInput('OutputSpace'), gc.GetInput('AddGamma'))
```

### Tips

- For a log camera image, linearise with the Cineon Log node first, then convert the gamut here. Cineon Log handles the
  log curve; this node handles the primaries and the gamma.
- A custom primary is entered as `[x, y]` chromaticity, not as an RGB colour.

**See also:** Color Space Transform, Color Space, Gamut Limiter, Cineon Log, White Balance.

## Gamut Limiter (`GamutLimiter`)

**Category:** Color\ColorFX · **Short name:** GMl · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Limits the image to a smaller colour gamut, such as P3 or Rec.709, when the delivery's specification restricts saturation
more than the working space allows. Pixels outside the limit gamut are brought back inside it. The Current Gamut and Current Gamma describe the image as it arrives, and Limit Gamut is the gamut to limit to.

**Use for:** meeting a delivery spec that caps the saturation of a wide-gamut master, for example limiting a Rec.2020
image to P3.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current Gamut | `CurrentGamut` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | The colour space of the image coming in. |
| Current Gamma | `CurrentGamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | The gamma of the image coming in. |
| Limit Gamut | `LimitGamut` | ID combo | `"REC709_COLORSPACE"` | The colour space to limit the image to. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the limit and re-multiplies after. On by default. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the operation to the mask. |

The colour space and gamma IDs are those of Color Space Transform (for example `"P3D65_COLORSPACE"`, `"REC2020_COLORSPACE"`,
`"REC709_COLORSPACE"`; gammas such as `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` and `"REC709_GAMMA"`).

### Example

Limit a Rec.2020 image to P3 D65, linear light.

```python
gl = comp.AddTool('GamutLimiter')
gl.CurrentGamut = 'REC2020_COLORSPACE'
gl.CurrentGamma = 'LINEAR_GAMMA'
gl.LimitGamut = 'P3D65_COLORSPACE'

print(gl.GetInput('CurrentGamut'), gl.GetInput('LimitGamut'))
```

### Tips

- Gamut Limiter limits the gamut only. It doesn't convert the image, so use Color Space Transform for the conversion itself.
- The effect of the limit was not checked in a render.

**See also:** Gamut Mapping, Color Space Transform, Gamut.

## Gamut Mapping (`GamutMapping`)

**Category:** Color\ColorFX · **Short name:** GMp · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Maps an image into a gamut that is much larger or smaller than its own, using saturation compression and tone mapping. It has the same gamut-mapping and tone-mapping controls as the Gamut Mapping section of the Color
Space Transform node, in a node of their own. The Gamma sets the image's transfer function, Tone Mapping Method and Dynamic
Range select how brightness is compressed or expanded, and the Gamut Mapping Method chooses the gamut compression.

**Use for:** bringing an HDR or wide-gamut image into a narrower display, and the reverse for an image that needs more
dynamic range.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gamma | `Gamma` | ID combo | `"LINEAR_GAMMA"` | The gamma of the image. Its IDs are those of Color Space Transform. |
| Tone Mapping Method | `ToneMappingMethod` | ID combo | `"TM_DRT_V2"` | `"TM_NONE"`, `"TM_CLIP"`, `"TM_SIMPLE"`, `"TM_DRT_V1"`, `"TM_DRT_V2"` or `"TM_DRT_V2_XYZ"`. |
| Dynamic Range | `DynamicRange` | ID combo | `"Compress"` | `"Compress"` (reduce the range) or `"Expand"` (increase it). Shown only with `"TM_SIMPLE"`. |
| Max. Input Luminance | `MaxInputLuminance` | Number | 100 (48 to 10000) | The input's peak luminance in nits. Hidden for TM_NONE and TM_CLIP. |
| Max. Output Luminance | `MaxOutputLuminance` | Number | 100 (48 to 10000) | The output's peak luminance in nits. |
| Avg. Input Luminance | `AvgInputLuminance` | Number | 9 (0.01 to 4000) | The input's average luminance. |
| Sat. Rolloff Start (nits) | `SatRolloffStart` | Number | 100 (1 to 500) | Where saturation roll-off starts. |
| Sat. Rolloff Limit (nits) | `SatRolloffLimit` | Number | 10000 (500 to 20000) | The luminance at which roll-off ends. |
| Gamut Mapping Method | `GamutMappingMethod` | ID combo | `"GM_NONE"` | `"GM_NONE"`, `"GM_RCM_1"` or `"GM_CLIP"`. |
| Saturation Knee | `SaturationKnee` | Number | 0.9 (0.5 to 1.2) | Where saturation begins to be compressed (with GM_RCM_1). |
| Saturation Max. | `SaturationMax` | Number | 1 (0.5 to 1.2) | The most saturation kept after mapping (with GM_RCM_1). |
| Apply Forward OOTF | `ApplyForwardOOTF` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the forward transfer function (scene to display). |
| Apply Inverse OOTF | `ApplyInverseOOTF` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the inverse transfer function. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 1 | Divides by Alpha before the mapping and re-multiplies after. On by default. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the mapping to the mask. |

### Example

Compress an HDR image with a 1000-nit peak into a 100-nit display, with the Rec.709 RCM gamut mapping.

```python
gm = comp.AddTool('GamutMapping')
gm.Gamma = 'LINEAR_GAMMA'
gm.ToneMappingMethod = 'TM_DRT_V2'
gm.MaxInputLuminance = 1000
gm.MaxOutputLuminance = 100
gm.GamutMappingMethod = 'GM_RCM_1'

print(gm.GetInput('ToneMappingMethod'), gm.GetInput('MaxInputLuminance'), gm.GetInput('GamutMappingMethod'))
```

### Tips

- The Saturation Knee and Max. controls appear only with `"GM_RCM_1"`. Dynamic Range appears only with `"TM_SIMPLE"`, and the
  luminance controls are hidden for `"TM_NONE"` and `"TM_CLIP"`.
- Gamut Mapping here is the same as the Gamut Mapping section of Color Space Transform. Use this node to apply it on its own,
  without a colour space conversion.
- Not checked in a render: the mapping's visual result.

**See also:** Color Space Transform, Gamut Limiter, Gamut.

## Hue Curves (`HueCurves`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** HCv · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Adjusts colour with curves that run across the hue wheel. Each curve is a function of hue: the horizontal axis is the
image's hue and the vertical axis is the amount of change. There are curves for hue, saturation and luminance, one for
each colour channel, and three suppression curves for removing red, green or blue. The Edit checkboxes choose which
curves the Inspector and the eyedropper edit. Because the axis follows hue, a curve can isolate one colour, such as
sky blue or skin tones, without affecting the rest of the image.

**Use for:** selective colour work: changing one hue's saturation or brightness, shifting a colour, and suppressing an
unwanted colour without a mask.

The curves are LUT inputs (`LookUpTable`) and are set from script through a LUTBezier modifier, as described under
*Curves from script* in Color Curves.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | Combo | 2: No Animation (0: Dissolve, 1: Animated Points) | Whether the curves can be animated over time. No Animation applies them the same at every frame. Dissolve is kept for compatibility. |
| Edit Hue | `EditHue` | Checkbox | 0 | Includes the hue curve in editing and the eyedropper. |
| Edit Sat | `EditSat` | Checkbox | 1 | Includes the saturation curve. |
| Edit Lum | `EditLum` | Checkbox | 0 | Includes the luminance curve. |
| Edit Red, Edit Green, Edit Blue | `EditRed`, `EditGreen`, `EditBlue` | Checkbox | 0 | Includes the red, green or blue curve. |
| Edit Red Suppress, Edit Green Suppress, Edit Blue Suppress | `EditRedSuppress`, `EditGreenSuppress`, `EditBlueSuppress` | Checkbox | 0 | Includes the suppression curves. |
| Hue | `Hue` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Changes the hue of each part of the hue range. |
| Sat | `Sat` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Changes the saturation of each part of the hue range. |
| Lum | `Lum` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Changes the luminance of each part of the hue range. |
| Red, Green, Blue | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Changes the amount of each channel over the hue range. |
| Red Suppress, Green Suppress, Blue Suppress | `RedSuppress`, `GreenSuppress`, `BlueSuppress` | Curve (LookUpTable) | Straight line | Suppresses each channel over the hue range. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by Alpha before the correction and re-multiplies after, for premultiplied images. |

### Example

Reduce saturation through the middle of the hue range, with the curve left unchanged at the ends.

```python
hc = comp.AddTool('HueCurves')

hc.AddModifier('Sat', 'LUTBezier')      # attach the saturation curve
sat = hc.Sat.GetConnectedOutput().GetTool()
sat.SetKeyFrames({
    0.0: {1: 1.0},
    0.5: {1: 0.4},
    1.0: {1: 1.0},
})

print(sat.GetKeyFrames())
```

### Tips

- The Inspector shows a hue curve with control points at the primary colours (red, yellow, green, cyan, blue and magenta).
  A curve attached from script starts as a straight line with two keys, at 0 and 1, so the primary-colour points aren't
  present. Whether the points map to fixed positions on the 0 to 1 axis was not checked.
- The example reads the saturation curve's keys back. Which hue sits at 0.5 on the axis was not checked: that needs a render
  or a check in the UI.
- Edit Sat is on by default. Turn on the Edit checkboxes for the curves you want to change in the Inspector.

### Open items

- The default Inspector curve and its six primary-colour points can't be read or set from script. Attaching a LUTBezier
  replaces that starting shape with a straight line.
- The effect of the curves on an image was not checked, since a scratch comp can't process images.

**See also:** Color Curves, Color Corrector, Color Gain.

## OCIO CDL Transform (`OCIOCDLTransform`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** OCDL · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies an ASC Colour Decision List (CDL) grade through OpenColorIO (OCIO). A CDL has three parts per channel: Slope (gain),
Offset (lift) and Power (gamma), plus a single Saturation. The node can read a CDL file, or take the values set in its
own controls, and can export the grade as a CDL file. Forward applies the grade, and Reverse undoes it.

**Use for:** applying a grade made in another application (such as a colourist's CDL) to an image, keeping the grade
portable between tools, and building a simple CDL in Fusion.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | `Operation` | ID multi-button | `"File"` | `"File"` applies a CDL file; `"Controls"` applies the values in the controls below. |
| Direction | `Direction` | ID multi-button | `"Forward"` | `"Forward"` applies the grade; `"Reverse"` undoes it. |
| CDL File | `LUTFile` | File | none | The CDL file to read, when Operation is `"File"`. |
| CCC ID | `CCCID` | Text | none | The colour correction ID (CCC) within a CDL file, label only. |
| Red, Green, Blue Slope | `RedSlope`, `GreenSlope`, `BlueSlope` | Number | 1 (0 to 4) | Gain for each channel (Controls). |
| Red, Green, Blue Offset | `RedOffset`, `GreenOffset`, `BlueOffset` | Number | 0 (-0.2 to 0.2) | Lift for each channel (Controls). |
| Red, Green, Blue Power | `RedPower`, `GreenPower`, `BluePower` | Number | 1 (0 to 4) | Gamma for each channel (Controls). |
| Saturation | `Saturation` | Number | 1 (0 to 4) | The saturation of the grade (Controls). |
| Export CDL File | `ExportCDLFile` | Button | 0 | Writes the current grade to a CDL file. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the grade to the mask. |

OCIO needs an OCIO setup on the machine, and the file to load, so this node was not run in a scratch comp.

### Example

Set a CDL in the controls: slightly higher gain in the reds, a little lift in the blues, and a saturation boost.

```python
cdl = comp.AddTool('OCIOCDLTransform')
cdl.Operation = 'Controls'
cdl.Direction = 'Forward'
cdl.RedSlope = 1.05
cdl.BlueOffset = 0.01
cdl.Saturation = 1.1

print(cdl.GetInput('Operation'), cdl.GetInput('RedSlope'), cdl.GetInput('Saturation'))
```

### Tips

- Use Reverse with the same values to undo a grade.
- The operation was set and read back from script; the OCIO result was not checked.

**See also:** OCIO File Transform, OCIO ColorSpace, OCIO Display, Color Corrector.

## OCIO ColorSpace (`OCIOColorSpace`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** OCC · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts an image from one colour space to another through an OpenColorIO (OCIO) configuration, and can apply a look.
Choose the OCIO config file, then the Source Space and Output Space from its colour spaces, and an optional Look. Forward
converts from the source to the output; Reverse converts back.

**Use for:** converting footage between the colour spaces of a studio's OCIO config (for example from a camera log to a
working space), and applying the config's look.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OCIO Config File | `OCIOConfig` | File | none | The OCIO configuration file (`.ocio`). The Source Space, Output Space and Look menus fill from it. |
| Source Space | `SourceSpace` | ID combo | `"raw"` | The colour space of the image coming in. Its options come from the config. |
| Output Space | `OutputSpace` | ID combo | `"raw"` | The colour space to convert to. |
| Look | `Look` | ID combo | `"None"` | A look from the config, applied with the conversion. |
| Direction | `Direction` | ID multi-button | `"Forward"` | `"Forward"` converts source to output; `"Reverse"` converts back. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the conversion to the mask. |

The colour space, look and display names aren't fixed; they come from the config file. Without a config, the menus show
only the defaults (`"raw"`, `"None"`).

### Example

Convert a log image from the config's Camera Log space to its working space, with no look.

```python
occ = comp.AddTool('OCIOColorSpace')
occ.OCIOConfig = 'D:/OCIO/config.ocio'  # the path to your config
occ.SourceSpace = 'Camera Log'          # placeholder: a colour space name from your config
occ.OutputSpace = 'Working Space'        # placeholder
occ.Look = 'None'

print(occ.GetInput('SourceSpace'), occ.GetInput('OutputSpace'))
```

### Tips

- Set `OCIOConfig` first; the other menus depend on it, so the names in the example are placeholders for your config's own.
- A misspelt colour space name is accepted silently and fails to render.
- The conversion was not checked in a render, and the config wasn't loaded in a scratch comp.

**See also:** OCIO CDL Transform, OCIO File Transform, OCIO Display, Color Space Transform.

## OCIO Display (`OCIODisplay`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** OCD · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies an OpenColorIO (OCIO) display transform: it takes an image from its source colour space to a display, as set by a
Display and a View in the OCIO configuration (for example a monitor's sRGB view). Use it to see a working-space image as it
will look on a particular display. Load an OCIO configuration (`.ocio` file), then choose the Source Space, Display and View.

**Use for:** previewing an image on a display or delivery view from a studio's OCIO config, without changing the image
itself for the rest of the tree.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OCIO Config File | `OCIOConfig` | File | none | The OCIO configuration file (`.ocio`). The menus fill from it. |
| Source Space | `SourceSpace` | ID combo | `"raw"` | The colour space of the image coming in. |
| Display | `Display` | ID combo | `"default"` | The display the image is for, from the config. |
| View | `View` | ID combo | `"sRGB"` | The view on that display, from the config. |
| Direction | `Direction` | ID multi-button | `"Forward"` | `"Forward"` applies the display transform; `"Reverse"` undoes it. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the transform to the mask. |

The display and view names come from the config. Without a config, the menus show only the defaults.

### Example

Show a working-space image as it looks on an sRGB display, using the config's sRGB view.

```python
ocd = comp.AddTool('OCIODisplay')
ocd.OCIOConfig = 'D:/OCIO/config.ocio'  # the path to your config
ocd.SourceSpace = 'Working Space'       # a colour space name from that config
ocd.Display = 'sRGB'                    # a display name from that config
ocd.View = 'sRGB'

print(ocd.GetInput('Display'), ocd.GetInput('View'))
```

### Tips

- Use OCIO Display as a viewing transform at the end of the tree. It changes what the image looks like, so use it as
  the last step before an output. Keep the working image upstream of it.
- The names in the example are placeholders; use the names from your own config.
- The transform wasn't checked in a render, and a scratch comp can't load a config.

**See also:** OCIO ColorSpace, OCIO File Transform, OCIO CDL Transform, Color Space Transform.

## OCIO File Transform (`OCIOFileTransform`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** OCF · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies a colour transform stored in a file, through OpenColorIO (OCIO): a LUT (a `.cube`, `.3dl` or similar file) or a
CDL. Choose the file, and the Direction. Interpolation sets how the LUT's values are interpolated between its entries.

**Use for:** applying a LUT supplied with footage or a grade (a camera or show LUT) through the OCIO pipeline, in either
direction.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LUT File | `LUTFile` | File | none | The transform file to apply. |
| CCC ID | `CCCID` | Text | none | The ID of the colour correction within a file that holds several. |
| Direction | `Direction` | ID multi-button | `"Forward"` | `"Forward"` applies the transform; `"Reverse"` applies its inverse. |
| Interpolation | `Interpolation` | ID multi-button | `"Linear"` | How the LUT's entries are interpolated: `"Nearest"`, `"Linear"`, `"Tetra"` or `"Best"`. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Limits the transform to the mask. |

### Example

Apply a transform file forward, with linear interpolation. The path is a placeholder.

```python
ocf = comp.AddTool('OCIOFileTransform')
ocf.LUTFile = 'D:/LUTs/show_look.cube'  # the path to your transform file
ocf.Direction = 'Forward'
ocf.Interpolation = 'Linear'

print(ocf.GetInput('Direction'), ocf.GetInput('Interpolation'))
```

### Tips

- Use Reverse to undo a transform you applied with Forward, if the file's inverse is valid.
- The Interpolation options were not compared in a render.
- The transform wasn't checked in a render: a scratch comp can't load and process the file.

**See also:** OCIO CDL Transform, OCIO ColorSpace, OCIO Display, Color Space Transform.

## Set Canvas Color (`SetCanvasColor`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** SCv · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), `Foreground` (green) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Sets the colour of the canvas: the area outside the image's domain of definition (DoD), which is the workspace beyond
the raster and is normally not rendered. By default the canvas is black with zero Alpha (transparent). The colour is set
with four channels (Red, Green, Blue and Alpha), each 0 to 1. If a Foreground is connected, the canvas colour is sampled
from that image instead, and the Controls tab is empty.

**Use for:** giving a fill colour to the area around an image, such as a black or coloured background for a plate that
doesn't cover the frame, or a colour behind a foreground that has transparency.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red | `Red` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Red of the canvas colour. |
| Green | `Green` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Green of the canvas colour. |
| Blue | `Blue` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Blue of the canvas colour. |
| Alpha | `Alpha` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Opacity of the canvas colour. At 0 the canvas is transparent. |

### Example

Give the area outside an image a solid mid-grey, fully opaque.

```python
scv = comp.AddTool('SetCanvasColor')
scv.Red = 0.5
scv.Green = 0.5
scv.Blue = 0.5
scv.Alpha = 1

print(scv.GetInput('Red'), scv.GetInput('Alpha'))
```

### Tips

- Set Alpha to 1 for an opaque canvas. The default of 0 leaves the area transparent.
- Place this node after a transform that leaves empty space around the image (for example a shrunk Transform) so the canvas
  shows. The manual's example does this.
- The canvas fill was not checked in a render, since the area outside the frame is not rendered in a scratch comp.

**See also:** Background, Merge, Color Corrector.

## White Balance (`WhiteBalance`)

**Category:** Color · **Short name:** WB · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Removes a colour cast. The Custom method takes a pixel from the image that should be neutral grey (the black, mid and
white references) and maps it to the result colours. The Temperature method takes the image's colour temperature in
kelvin (the reference) and corrects it to the result temperature. Either way, the Ranges tab sets which parts of the
image count as shadows, midtones and highlights. Lock Black/Mid/White applies one correction to the whole image, and
unlocking it gives each range its own reference and result.

**Use for:** correcting a shot taken under the wrong light, neutralising a cast from a grey card or a neutral part of the
frame, and matching the colour temperature of one shot to another.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Space | `Space` | ID combo | `"Adobe"` | The colour space of the source image. Its gamma is used if Use Gamma is on. The IDs are those of Gamut (`"Custom"` and `"FromImage"` included), without `"NoChange"`. |
| Use Gamma | `UseGamma` | Checkbox | 1 | Takes the gamma of the Space into account when correcting. |
| Method | `Method` | Multi-button | 0: Custom, 1: Temperature | Custom uses picked reference colours; Temperature uses colour temperatures. |
| Lock Black/Mid/White | `LockBlackMidWhite` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one correction for the whole image, using the midtone controls. Off: separate black, mid and white controls. |
| Black Reference (Custom) | `RedInLow`, `GreenInLow`, `BlueInLow` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The shadow reference colour, the pixel that should map to the Black Result. Shown with Method Custom and Lock off. |
| Black Result (Custom) | `RedOutLow`, `GreenOutLow`, `BlueOutLow` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The colour the Black Reference is changed to. |
| Mid Reference (Custom) | `RedInMid`, `GreenInMid`, `BlueInMid` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The midtone reference colour. Shown with Method Custom. |
| Mid Result (Custom) | `RedOutMid`, `GreenOutMid`, `BlueOutMid` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The colour the Mid Reference is changed to. Normally neutral grey. |
| White Reference (Custom) | `RedInHigh`, `GreenInHigh`, `BlueInHigh` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The highlight reference colour. Shown with Method Custom and Lock off. |
| White Result (Custom) | `RedOutHigh`, `GreenOutHigh`, `BlueOutHigh` | Colour | 0.5 (0 to 1) | The colour the White Reference is changed to. |
| Black Temperature Reference | `BlackTemperatureReference` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The shadows' colour temperature in the source. Shown with Method Temperature and Lock off. |
| Black Temperature Result | `BlackTemperatureResult` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The shadows' target temperature. |
| Mid Temperature Reference | `MidTemperatureReference` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The midtones' colour temperature in the source, in kelvin. Shown with Method Temperature. |
| Mid Temperature Result | `MidTemperatureResult` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The midtones' target temperature in kelvin. |
| White Temperature Reference | `WhiteTemperatureReference` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The highlights' colour temperature in the source. Shown with Method Temperature and Lock off. |
| White Temperature Result | `WhiteTemperatureResult` | Number | 6500 (1000 to 12500) | The highlights' target temperature. |
| Red, Green, Blue Primary, White Point, Gamma, Linear Limit, Linear Slope | `CustomSourceRed`, `CustomSourceGreen`, `CustomSourceBlue`, `CustomSourceWhite`, `CustomSourceGamma`, `CustomSourceLimit`, `CustomSourceSlope` | Point / Number | As Gamut's custom source | The source gamut, shown when Space is `"Custom"`. |
| Color Ranges | `ColorRanges` | Curve | Smooth | The shadow, midtone and highlight range spline. Not scriptable (see Tips). |
| Preset Simple / Smooth | `PresetSimpleRanges`, `PresetSmoothRanges` | Button | 0 | Resets the range spline to Simple or Smooth. |

The Black and White reference and result colours are shown as colour controls in the Inspector, with values from 0 to 1.

### Example

Correct a midtone colour cast from a reference of 4200 K, with the result at daylight (6500 K), for the whole image.

```python
wb = comp.AddTool('WhiteBalance')
wb.Method = 1                           # Temperature
wb.LockBlackMidWhite = 1                # one correction for the whole image
wb.MidTemperatureReference = 4200       # what the scene's light was
wb.MidTemperatureResult = 6500          # what it should look like

print(wb.GetInput('MidTemperatureReference'), wb.GetInput('MidTemperatureResult'))
```

### Tips

- Temperature needs the scene's actual colour temperature. With Lock on, only the Mid pair is shown, and that pair
  corrects the whole image.
- Custom needs a reference from the source image, not from this node's output, so pick the reference before the
  correction is applied.
- A reference pixel that is clipped in one channel leaves too little headroom for the correction, as the manual warns.
- Turn off Lock to set each range's reference separately, for example to correct a cast only in the shadows.

### Open items

- Picking a reference from the image (the eyedropper) is a UI action. Reference values can be set from script, but the
  Custom method's results were not checked in a render.
- The Temperature method's result temperature and the Custom references were checked only as readbacks.

**See also:** Gamut, Color Corrector, Chromatic Adaptation, Color Space Transform.

## Dissolve (`Dissolve`)

**Category:** Composite · **Short name:** DX · **Inputs:** Background (orange), Foreground (green), Map, Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Mixes two images, or switches between them, according to the Background/Foreground slider (`Mix`). At 0 the output is
the Background, at 1 the Foreground, and in between the two are blended in the way the Operation sets. The Operation
can be a plain cross dissolve, an additive or erode mix, a random-dot dissolve, an alpha-based merge, a gradient wipe
driven by the Map input, or an SMPTE-style horizontal or vertical wipe. Neither input has to be connected first, and a
missing input passes the other one through.

**Use for:** cross dissolves between clips, wipes and transitions on titles and plates, and switching between two layers
with `Mix`.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | `Operation` | ID combo | `"DFTDissolve"` | `"DFTDissolve"` (Dissolve), `"DFTAddDissolve"` (Additive Dissolve), `"DFTErode"` (Erode), `"DFTRandom"` (Random Dissolve), `"DFTRandomNoise"` (Random Noise Dissolve), `"DFTAlphaMerge"` (Alpha Merge), `"DFTLumaRamp"` (Gradient Wipe), `"DFTWipe"` (SMPTE Wipe). |
| Background/Foreground | `Mix` | Number | 1 (0–1) | 0 shows the Background, 1 the Foreground, and values between blend them, in the way Operation sets. |
| Background | `Background` | Image input | | The first image. |
| Foreground | `Foreground` | Image input | | The second image. |
| Map | `Map` | Image input | | The luminance map for the Gradient Wipe operation. |
| Wipe Style | `DFTWipe.WipeStyle` | Combo | 1: Horizontal - Left To Right, 2: Vertical - Top To Bottom (default 0) | Direction of the SMPTE Wipe. Visible with `"DFTWipe"`. The live list labels only indices 1 and 2. |
| Invert Wipe | `DFTWipe.InvertWipe` | Checkbox | 0 | Reverses the wipe direction. |
| Softness | `DFTWipe.Softness` | Number | 0.1 | Feather of the wipe edge. Visible with `"DFTWipe"`. |
| Border | `DFTWipe.Border` | Checkbox | 0 | Adds a border at the wipe edge. |

The Gradient Wipe controls (`DFTLumaRamp.Softness`, `DFTLumaRamp.Border`) and the Alpha Merge controls (`DFTAlphaMerge.*`,
such as `Operator` and `ApplyMode`, the same as Merge) appear with their own Operation. Two operations aren't covered by
the manual: Erode (`"DFTErode"`) uses the image's luminance as a gradient wipe, and Alpha Merge (`"DFTAlphaMerge"`) does
a standard Over composite while fading the Background out and the Foreground in.

### Example

A cross dissolve that moves from the outgoing clip to the incoming clip over one second, at 24 fps:

```python
dissolve = comp.AddTool('Dissolve')
dissolve.Background = comp.MediaIn1.Output     # the outgoing clip
dissolve.Foreground = comp.MediaIn2.Output     # the incoming clip

dissolve.Mix = comp.BezierSpline()
dissolve.Mix[0] = 0                            # show the Background
dissolve.Mix[24] = 1                           # show the Foreground
```

### Tips

- For a transition with a shape, set `Operation` to `"DFTWipe"`, then animate `Mix` 0 to 1. Use `DFTWipe.Softness` for
  a soft edge.
- For a gradient-driven transition, set `Operation` to `"DFTLumaRamp"` and connect a Fast Noise, a gradient or a
  Background to `Map`. The manual says `Map` is used only by the Gradient Wipe.
- Connect both clips before animating `Mix`. Dissolve doesn't need the Background to be connected first.
- Both inputs should have the same resolution. The manual says that when they differ, the output takes the larger size
  except at the extremes of `Mix`.

**See also:** Merge, MultiMerge, Fast Noise, Transform, MediaIn.

## Merge (`Merge`)

**Category:** Composite · **Short name:** Mrg · **Inputs:** `Background` (orange), `Foreground` (green), Effect Mask (blue)
· **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Layers the Foreground image over the Background, using the foreground's alpha channel. Apply Mode selects the
blend mode (Normal, Screen, Multiply, Overlay and so on). In Normal and Screen modes, an Operator selects the
Porter-Duff operation (Over, In, Held Out, Atop, XOr…). Merge also has a built-in transform for the foreground
(position, size, angle, flip), so a separate Transform is often unnecessary.

**Use for:** every layering job: titles over video, picture-in-picture, adding graphics, light effects with
Screen/Add, and masked composites using the Effect Mask input.

**Resolution:** the output always has the Background's resolution. If only the Foreground is connected, Merge
outputs nothing. Connect the Background first.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Foreground position. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Foreground scale; 1 is pixel for pixel. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Foreground rotation. |
| Flip | `FlipHoriz`, `FlipVert` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirror the foreground. |
| Apply Mode | `ApplyMode` | ID combo | `"Normal"` | `"Normal"`, `"Screen"`, `"Dissolve"`, `"Darken"`, `"Multiply"`, `"Color Burn"`, `"LinearBurn"`, `"DarkerColor"`, `"Lighten"`, `"Color Dodge"`, `"LinearDodge"`, `"LighterColor"`, `"Overlay"`, `"Soft Light"`, `"Hard Light"`, `"VividLight"`, `"LinearLight"`, `"PinLight"`, `"HardMix"`, `"Difference"`, `"Exclusion"`, `"Hue"`, `"Saturation"`, `"Color"`, `"Luminosity"`, `"Hypotenuse"`, `"Geometric"` |
| Operator | `Operator` | ID combo | `"Over"` | `"Over"`, `"In"`, `"Held Out"`, `"Atop"`, `"XOr"`, `"Conjoint"`, `"Disjoint"`, `"Mask"`, `"Stencil"`, `"Under"`. Only used with Normal and Screen. |
| Subtractive/Additive | `SubtractiveAdditive` | Number | 1 (0–1) | 1 (additive) for premultiplied foregrounds, which is most Fusion images. 0 (subtractive) for non-premultiplied ones. Values in between can fix edges that look too bright or too dark. |
| Alpha Gain | `Gain` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Scales the foreground alpha. At 0 with an additive merge, the foreground is simply added: a "glow" or "add" merge. |
| Burn In | `BurnIn` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Like lowering Alpha Gain, but without reducing the foreground. |
| Blend | `BlendClone` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Fades the merge result back to the background. A clone of the Settings tab `Blend`. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 0: Canvas, 1: Wrap, 2: Duplicate, 3: Mirror | What fills the frame outside a shrunken or moved foreground. Wrap tiles it. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor … 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter when the foreground is resized. |
| Invert Transform | `InvertTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the position/size/angle transform. Useful with tracker data. |
| Enable Depth Merge | `PerformDepthMerge` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the inputs' Z channels to decide what's in front (Channels tab). |

### Example

Picture-in-picture: the second clip at 40% size in the top-right corner, sliding in over 12 frames:

```python
pip = comp.AddTool('Merge')
pip.Background = main_clip.Output
pip.Foreground = inset_clip.Output
pip.Size = 0.4

pip.Center = comp.PolyPath()           # a motion path for a Point input
pip.Center[0] = [1.3, 0.75]            # off screen to the right
pip.Center[12] = [0.75, 0.75]
```

### Tips

- Screen and Add (`ApplyMode` `"Normal"` with `Gain` 0) are the usual modes for light effects such as flares,
  glows and sparks.
- To show the foreground only inside the background's alpha, use `Operator` `"In"`. To cut it out there instead,
  use `"Held Out"`.
- Use **MultiMerge** for many layers over one background. Use **Dissolve** to mix or switch between two clips over
  time.

**See also:** MultiMerge, Dissolve, Channel Booleans, Transform, Matte Control.

## MultiMerge (`MultiMerge`)

**Category:** Composite · **Short name:** MMrg · **Inputs:** Background (orange), one Foreground per layer (green), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Layers any number of foreground images over one Background in a single tool. Each layer has its own position, size,
angle, blend mode and Operator, which are the same controls as Merge with a `Layer<n>.` prefix. Layers are numbered from
1, and a new layer is created by connecting the next free `Layer<n>.Foreground` input. The output takes the Background's
resolution, as Merge does.

**Use for:** a stack of titles, logos and graphics over one plate, where a chain of Merges would be harder to edit and
each layer needs its own transform. Use Merge for a single layer.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background | `Background` | Image input | | The plate. Its resolution is the output's resolution. |
| Foreground | `Layer1.Foreground` | Image input | | The image for layer 1. Connecting it adds the next layer's input. |
| Layer name | `LayerName1` | Text | Tool name plus "Layer", e.g. "MultiText1 Layer" | The name shown in the Inspector. |
| Enabled | `LayerEnabled1` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns a layer on or off. |
| Center | `Layer1.Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the layer. |
| Size | `Layer1.Size` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Scale of the layer; 1 is pixel for pixel. |
| Angle | `Layer1.Angle` | Number | 0 (0–360°) | Rotation of the layer. |
| Flip | `Layer1.FlipHoriz` `Layer1.FlipVert` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirrors the layer. |
| Apply Mode | `Layer1.ApplyMode` | ID combo | `"Normal"` | Blend mode, with the same list as Merge's `ApplyMode`. |
| Operator | `Layer1.Operator` | ID combo | `"Over"` | Porter-Duff operation, as Merge's `Operator`. Used with Normal and Screen. |
| Alpha Gain | `Layer1.Gain` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Scales the layer's alpha. |
| Blend | `Layer1.Blend` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Blend amount for the layer; 1 is full. |
| Layer Order | `LayerOrder` | ScriptVal | `{0: 1, 1: 2}` in a two-layer tool | The stacking order, as a dict of position (from 0) to layer number. Layers are merged in this order, so the first is at the bottom and the last on top. |

The table gives layer 1. For layer *n*, use the same IDs with *n* in place of 1 (`Layer2.Center`, `LayerName2`). The other
per-layer controls (Edges, Filter Method, Invert Transform, Subtractive/Additive, Burn In) follow Merge's definitions. The Effect Mask input limits the whole tool's output.

### Example

A title in the lower left and a logo in the bottom right, over the plate. The plate and the logo are the comp's MediaIn
nodes:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('TextPlus')
title.StyledText = 'Jane Smith'
title.Size = 0.06

logo = comp.MediaIn2                       # a logo clip, as a second MediaIn

layers = comp.AddTool('MultiMerge')
layers.Background = comp.MediaIn1.Output
layers['Layer1.Foreground'] = title.Output
layers['Layer1.Center'] = [0.2, 0.2]
layers['LayerName1'] = 'Name'

layers['Layer2.Foreground'] = logo.Output
layers['Layer2.Center'] = [0.9, 0.9]
layers['Layer2.Size'] = 0.4
layers['LayerName2'] = 'Logo'
```

### Tips

- **Adding a layer from a script.** There is no add-layer call. Connect `Layer<n+1>.Foreground` and the next layer
  appears: in testing, connecting `Layer2.Foreground` created `Layer3.Foreground`, and `LayerName2` was set to the
  connected tool's name.
- **Reordering layers.** Set `LayerOrder` to a dict of position to layer number. For example,
  `layers.LayerOrder = {0: 3, 1: 2, 2: 1}` reverses the default order of three layers, putting layer 1 on top. A layer
  left out of the dict is not drawn, so list every layer. Read back, the keys and values are floats (`{0.0: 3.0, ...}`).
- **Dotted IDs** use item syntax, as in `layers['Layer1.Center'] = [0.2, 0.2]`. Points take `[x, y]`.
- **Each layer carries its own transform.** You don't need a Transform node for each foreground.
- **Use one Merge for one layer.** Merge is simpler when a plate has only one foreground.

**See also:** Merge, Dissolve, MultiText, Transform, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## dColor Corrector (`dColorCorrector`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dCC · **Inputs:** `Input` (DeepImage), Effect Mask · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

The Color Corrector for deep images. It works on the samples of a deep image, so the grade is applied at each depth, and it has the same main controls as Color Corrector: colour wheels, lift, gamma and gain per tonal range, levels, histogram matching and colour suppression. The Menu switches the Correction tab between Colors, Levels, Histogram and Suppress, and Range picks which tonal range those controls affect.

**Use for:** grading a deep 3D render or a deep composite before it is flattened, so that the grade follows the depth of each sample.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menu | `Menu` | Multi-button | 0: Colors (1: Levels, 2: Histogram, 3: Suppress) | Which set of correction controls is shown. |
| Range | `CorrectionRange` | Multi-button | 0: Master (1: Shadows, 2: Midtones, 3: Highlights) | The tonal range the Colors, Levels and Suppress controls act on. Master affects the whole image. |
| Master RGB: Gain, Lift, Gamma, Contrast, Brightness | `MasterRGBGain`, `MasterRGBLift`, `MasterRGBGamma`, `MasterRGBContrast`, `MasterRGBBrightness` | Number | Gain 1 (0 to 5); Lift 0 (-1 to 1); Gamma 1 (0 to 3); Contrast 1 (0 to 3); Brightness 0 (-1 to 1) | The colour controls for the whole image. Shadows, MidTones and Highlights have the same set of controls, with the IDs `ShadowsRGB…`, `MidTonesRGB…` and `HighlightsRGB…`. Per-channel versions insert Red, Green or Blue, as in `MasterRedGain`. |
| Hue and Saturation | `Hue1`…`Hue4`, `Saturation1`…`Saturation4` | Number | Hue 0 (-1 to 1); Saturation 1 (0–2) | Hue and saturation for Master, Shadows, Midtones and Highlights. |
| Channel | `Channel` | Multi-button | 0: RGB (1: Red, 2: Green, 3: Blue) | Which channel the Levels controls display. |
| Precision | `Precision` | Multi-button | 2: 16-bit (0: 8-bit, 1: 10-bit) | Precision used for the correction. |
| Tint Mode | `TintMode` | Multi-button | 2: Better (0: Fast, 1: Full) | The algorithm used for hue and saturation changes. |
| Process Order | `ProcessOrder` | Combo | 1: Gamma After Levels (0: Gamma Before Levels) | Whether gamma is applied before or after the levels. |
| Apply Mask Inverted | `ApplyMaskInverted` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the mask channel for the tool. |

The Ranges tab (`RangesRange`, `RangesChannel`, `ColorRanges`) sets the shadow and highlight boundaries that define the ranges, and its Output the range you see as final render option (`RenderOutputRange`) outputs a range's matte instead of the graded image. The Histogram and Suppress controls are on the other menus and are not listed here.

### Tips

- The Range menu decides which controls you are editing. Settings made under one range stay put when you switch to another.
- Use the Ranges tab to make a matte from a tonal range, and feed it to another tool as an effect mask.

**See also:** Color Corrector, dRecolor, Deep To Image, Common Controls → Deep images.

## dCrop (`dCrop`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dCr · **Inputs:** `Image` (DeepImage), Effect Mask · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Crops a deep image by depth. It removes the samples that lie outside a minimum and maximum Z, so only the part of a deep render between two depths passes on. Keep Outside Depth Range swaps the selection, keeping the samples outside the range instead.

**Use for:** isolating a depth band of a deep render, such as a foreground layer, or dropping samples that are too far away to matter before a merge.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Use Minimum Z | `UseMinDepth` | Checkbox | 1 | Crops samples nearer than Minimum Z. |
| Minimum Z | `Min` | Number | 0 (-50 to 50) | The nearest depth kept. Sample in the viewer to pick it. |
| Use Maximum Z | `UseMaxDepth` | Checkbox | 1 | Crops samples further than Maximum Z. |
| Maximum Z | `Max` | Number | 50 (-50 to 50) | The furthest depth kept. |
| Keep Outside Depth Range | `KeepOutsideRange` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the selection: the samples outside the range are kept. |
| Use Mask for Depth Crop | `UseMaskPixelDepth` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the Effect Mask in the depth crop. |
| Apply Mask Inverted | `ApplyMaskInverted` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the mask channel for the tool. |

The Crop Pixels part of the tool, which crops pixels with the input mask, is not shown in the Inspector in the default state, and was not explored. With Use Minimum Z off, the Minimum Z slider stayed visible in a test (the manual doesn't say whether it hides).

### Tips

- Crop before a merge, so that the merge works on fewer samples.
- Use Keep Outside Depth Range to remove a near element, rather than cropping everything else.

**See also:** dMerge, dHoldout, Deep To Image, Common Controls → Deep images.

## Deep To Image (`DeepToImage`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** DtI · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange, DeepImage) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Flattens a deep image into an ordinary 2D image by combining its samples in depth order. The result is a normal image with colour and alpha, ready for Merge, Saver or any 2D tool. Volumetric Composition changes how overlapping samples are blended: on, they are treated as semi-transparent volumes, as in fog or VDB smoke; off, as flat surfaces.

**Use for:** the last step of a deep comp, before the result goes into a 2D chain or a Saver. Use it whenever a deep result has to be combined with 2D elements in a Merge.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Process Mode | `ProcessMode` | ID combo | `"FullFrames"` | Field processing mode: `"FullFrames"`, `"NTSC"`, `"PAL"`, `"PALReversed"`, `"NTSCReversed"`. Leave on FullFrames unless the material is interlaced. |
| Depth | `Depth` | Multi-button | 0: Default (1: int8, 2: int16, 3: float16, 4: float32) | Bit depth of the flattened image. Float gives the most precision and headroom. |
| Flip Depth | `FlipDepth` | Checkbox | 1 | Inverts the depth information before flattening, which changes which samples are in front. |
| Volumetric Composition | `VolumetricComposition` | Checkbox | 1 | On: overlapping samples are blended as semi-transparent volumes (fog, VDB). Off: they are treated as flat surfaces. |

The Image tab's colour space and gamma controls (`Gamut.*`) are also on this tool. They tag the output's colour space and don't convert it, as the manual describes.

### Example

Flattening a deep composite of a plate and a 2D graphic, so that the result can be treated as an ordinary image:

```python
plate = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for the 2D plate
deep_plate = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
deep_plate.Image = plate.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('dMerge')
merge.Background = deep_plate.Output

flat = comp.AddTool('DeepToImage')
flat.Image = merge.Output
flat.VolumetricComposition = 1          # treat overlapping samples as volumes, as for fog
```

### Tips

- Deep To Image accepts only deep images. Connecting a 2D image to its input is refused, so convert plates with Image To Deep first.
- Set the Depth to float (`3` or `4`) if the flattened result will be graded heavily, to keep the highlights.
- Deep compositing works in linear colour. Convert back to your output colour space after flattening.

**See also:** Image To Deep, dMerge, dHoldout, Merge, Common Controls → Deep images.

## Deep To Points (`DeepToPoints`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** DtP · **Inputs:** `Image` (DeepImage), `Camera` (DataType3D) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Turns a deep image into a 3D point cloud, one point for each sample, so the depth of the samples can be seen in the 3D viewer. Connect the scene's camera to the Camera input to place the cloud correctly relative to a 3D scene. The output is a 3D object, so it goes to Merge 3D or Renderer 3D, not to the 2D tools.

**Use for:** checking the depth of a deep render, and placing its samples in a 3D scene. Make Renderable lets the cloud be rendered into the image, which is rarely needed.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Style | `LocatorStyle` | ID multi-button | `"Point"` | `"Point"` or `"Cross"`: how each sample is drawn in the viewer. |
| Point Size | `Point.Size` | Number | 1 (1 to 12) | Size of each point, for Point style. |
| Density | `Density` | Number | 0.1 (0 to 1) | How much the points build up in intensity. |
| Use Per-Point Colors | `UsePerPointColors` | Checkbox | 1 | Each point takes its colour from the source. Off: use Color Red, Green and Blue. |
| Color Red, Green, Blue | `ColorRed`, `ColorGreen`, `ColorBlue` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Default colour of the points. |
| Make Renderable | `MakeRenderable` | Checkbox | 0 | Lets Renderer 3D render the cloud into the image. |
| Scale | `Scale` | Number | 0.005 (0.001 to 0.1) | Overall size of the cloud. |
| Depth Scale | `DepthScale` | Number | 0.025 (0.001 to 0.5) | Stretches the cloud along depth. |
| Flip Depth | `FlipDepth` | Checkbox | 1 | Inverts the depth, flipping points from negative to positive. |
| Camera | `Camera` | 3D input | | The scene's camera, for correct placement. |

The Transform tab (`Transform3DOp.*`) positions, rotates and scales the cloud as on other 3D tools. See Common Controls → 3D objects.

**See also:** Deep To Image, Renderer 3D, Merge 3D, Camera 3D.

## dHoldout (`dHoldout`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dHld · **Inputs:** `Background` (orange, DeepImage), `Foreground` (white, DeepImage) · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Cuts a hole in the Background deep image wherever the Foreground is in front of it. The Foreground's samples act as a holdout: they remove the Background's samples behind them, using their depths, so a 3D object in the Background can be partly hidden by a deep element that is closer to the camera. The output is the Background with that area removed.

**Use for:** putting an element in front of a deep plate or render with its depth respected, for example a 2D element that passes behind part of a 3D scene, or a deep matte that cuts a background object.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background | `Background` | Image input (DeepImage) | | The deep image that is cut. |
| Foreground | `Foreground` | Image input (DeepImage) | | The holdout: its samples remove the Background where they are in front. |
| Compute Occluded Samples | `ComputeOccludedSample` | Checkbox | 0 | For a semi-transparent Foreground. Removes its samples, and recolours the Background seen through it as if seen through a partly transparent layer. |
| Holdout Z Offset | `Offset` | Number | 0 (-50 to 50) | Moves the holdout's depth forward or back. Decreasing it pushes the holdout forward. Sample in the viewer to pick a value. |
| Holdout Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Moves the Foreground across the frame, in X and Y. |

### Example

A deep plate with a 2D element placed in front of it. The element is converted to deep and used as the holdout, so it cuts the plate where the element is nearer than the plate:

```python
plate = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for the deep plate
element = comp.AddTool('Background')    # stands in for the 2D element used as the holdout

plate_deep = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
plate_deep.Image = plate.Output

element_deep = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
element_deep.Image = element.Output
element_deep.Offset = -20               # nearer the camera than the plate

holdout = comp.AddTool('dHoldout')
holdout.Background = plate_deep.Output
holdout.Foreground = element_deep.Output
holdout['Offset'] = 0                   # the holdout's own Z Offset (0 keeps its depth)
```

### Tips

- The Foreground needs a depth, or it has no effect on the Background. Use Image To Deep (with Z Offset) or a deep render for it.
- Turn on Compute Occluded Samples only for a semi-transparent Foreground, such as glass or smoke. It costs more to compute.
- Holdout Center and Holdout Z Offset move the holdout without moving the Background, so they can be animated to sweep an element past a 3D object.

**See also:** dMerge, Image To Deep, Deep To Image, Common Controls → Deep images.

## dMerge (`dMerge`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dMg · **Inputs:** `Background` (orange, DeepImage), `Foreground1` (white, DeepImage); more Foreground inputs appear as you connect · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Combines deep images by merging their samples, so each sample keeps its own depth. The Background is the base. Each Foreground adds its samples to the result, and the samples are sorted by depth as they merge, so an object in one input can pass in front of or behind an object in another. Foreground inputs appear one at a time: connecting Foreground1 adds Foreground2, connecting that adds Foreground3, and so on.

**Use for:** layering deep 3D renders with each other, with 2D elements converted by Image To Deep, and with dHoldout results. Where a 2D Merge would put one layer over the other whatever their depth, dMerge keeps the depth order.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Background | `Background` | Image input (DeepImage) | | The base deep image. Connect it first. |
| Foreground inputs | `Foreground`*n* | Image input (DeepImage) | | Each one added to the result, sorted by depth. Foreground1, then Foreground2 (which appears once Foreground1 is connected), and so on. |
| Process Layers | `ProcessLayers` | ID combo | `":Default"` | Which layers of a multi-layer deep EXR are processed: `":Default"`, `":All"` or `":Custom"`. `":Custom"` uses the Layers list. |
| Background layer, Foreground layer | `Background_LayerSelect`, `Foreground1_LayerSelect` | Layer select | `":Auto"` | The layer of each input to use. |

The Settings tab is described in Common Controls.

### Example

Two deep elements over a deep plate. The plate is a 2D image here, which dMerge converts to deep automatically, and each element goes through Image To Deep first:

```python
plate = comp.AddTool('Background')      # a 2D plate, converted to deep by dMerge
title = comp.AddTool('Background')      # a 2D title
bush = comp.AddTool('Background')       # a 2D element to place in depth

title_deep = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
title_deep.Image = title.Output
title_deep.Offset = -10                 # bring the title forward in depth

bush_deep = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
bush_deep.Image = bush.Output
bush_deep.Offset = 2

merge = comp.AddTool('dMerge')
merge.Background = plate.Output
merge.Foreground1 = bush_deep.Output
merge.Foreground2 = title_deep.Output   # Foreground2 exists once Foreground1 is connected
```

### Tips

- Connect the Background first. The Foreground inputs are ordered by depth in the result, so their order does not matter.
- Flatten the result with Deep To Image before a 2D Merge, Saver, or any tool that does not take deep images.
- Use Merge (2D) instead when the layers have no depth to sort, or use its Enable Depth Merge option with Z channels.
- Deep compositing needs linear colour. Convert the inputs first, and convert back after flattening.

**See also:** Deep To Image, Image To Deep, dHoldout, Merge, MultiMerge, Merge 3D.

## dRecolor (`dRecolor`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dRc · **Inputs:** `Depth` (DeepImage), `Color` (Image) · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Recolours the samples of a deep image with the RGB values of a 2D image. The Depth input supplies the samples, and the Color input is laid over them, so each sample takes the colour of the matching pixel. Target Input Alpha lets the Color image's alpha control the transparency of the samples, and Drop Input Zero Alpha ignores the pixels of the Color image that are fully transparent.

**Use for:** giving a deep render a new colour or texture, for example a painted or graded 2D image, while keeping the render's depth.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Depth | `Depth` | Image input (DeepImage) | | The deep image whose samples are recoloured. A 2D image is converted automatically. |
| Color | `Color` | Image input | | The RGB image that gives the new colour. |
| Center X/Y | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Positions the Color image over the deep image. |
| Target Input Alpha | `TargetInputAlpha` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the Color image's alpha to set the transparency of the samples. Off: only RGB is used. |
| Drop Input Zero Alpha | `DropZeroAlpha` | Checkbox | 1 | Ignores the pixels of the Color image that have zero alpha. |
| Input Alpha Threshold | `InputAlphaThreshold` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Not documented in the manual; its exact effect was not tested. |

### Tips

- Use Drop Input Zero Alpha with a Color image that has a transparent background, so that the empty areas don't clear the render's colour.

**See also:** dColor Corrector, dMerge, Deep To Image, Common Controls → Deep images.

## dResize (`dResize`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dRz · **Inputs:** `Image` (DeepImage) · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Resizes a deep image to a new width and height in pixels, scaling its samples with it. Unlike the 2D resize tools, the size is given in pixels, not as a fraction of the frame.

**Use for:** matching a deep render to the resolution of the comp or the plate before it is merged or flattened.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width | `Width` | Number | 1920 (slider 1 to 4096) | Output width in pixels. Integer. |
| Height | `Height` | Number | 1080 (slider 1 to 4096) | Output height in pixels. Integer. |

**See also:** dTransform, dCrop, Deep To Image, Resize.

## dTransform (`dTransform`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** dXf · **Inputs:** `Image` (DeepImage), Effect Mask · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Moves, scales and rotates a deep image in X and Y, and scales and moves its samples along depth (Z). The depth samples keep their positions relative to each other, so an object moved in X and Y keeps its depth order.

**Use for:** repositioning or resizing a deep element, or pushing it nearer or further in depth, without losing its samples.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scale Z | `Scale` | Number | 1 (slider -2 to 2) | Expands or contracts the depth samples. Larger values spread the depth. |
| Translate Z | `Translate` | Number | 0 (-50 to 50) | Moves the image forward or back in depth. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Moves the image in X and Y. |
| Pivot | `Pivot` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The pivot point of the image, which the manual describes as the point the transform is anchored to. |
| Use Size and Aspect | `UseSizeAndAspect` | Checkbox | 1 | On: Size and Aspect are shown. Off: X Size and Y Size are shown. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Uniform size on both axes, when Use Size and Aspect is on. |
| Aspect | `Aspect` | Number | 1 (0.01 to 5) | Aspect ratio, when Use Size and Aspect is on. |
| X Size, Y Size | `XSize`, `YSize` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Size on each axis, when Use Size and Aspect is off. |
| Mask Mode | `MaskMode` | Multi-button | 1: Output (0: Input, 2: Both) | Which side of the transform the Effect Mask applies to. Not documented in the manual; check the effect in the UI. |

**Use Size and Aspect** is on by default, so the Size and Aspect controls are shown first, as the manual describes.

**See also:** dResize, dCrop, Deep To Image, Transform.

## Image To Deep (`ImageToDeep`)

**Category:** Deep Image · **Short name:** ItD · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (DeepImage)

Converts a 2D image into a deep image, with one sample per pixel at a depth you control. The image keeps its colour and alpha, and gets a Z position in the scene. Once it is deep, it can be layered with other deep images in dMerge, cut with dHoldout, or flattened with Deep To Image. This is the only way a plain plate or graphic enters a deep composite, apart from the automatic conversion that the other deep tools perform.

**Use for:** placing a 2D element, such as a title, a plate or a matte, in front of or behind a deep 3D render, so that the two sort correctly by depth.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image | `Image` | Image input | | The 2D image to convert. |
| Specify Z | `SpecifyDepth` | Checkbox | 0 | When on, hides Z Scale in the Inspector. The manual says this specifies the Z depth directly; the result was not verified (see the notes). |
| Z Scale | `Scale` | Number | -1 (slider -2 to 2) | Expands or contracts the depth samples. Shown only when Specify Z is off. Larger values spread the depth further. |
| Z Offset | `Offset` | Number | 0 (-50 to 50) | Moves the image forward or back in depth. A Sample button in the Inspector picks a value from the viewer. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Moves the 2D image across the frame, in X and Y. |

### Example

A graphic placed in depth behind a deep render: the graphic is converted to deep and given an offset, then merged under the render in dMerge.

```python
render = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for a deep 3D render (a deep EXR in a real comp)
graphic = comp.AddTool('Background')     # stands in for a 2D graphic

deep_graphic = comp.AddTool('ImageToDeep')
deep_graphic.Image = graphic.Output
deep_graphic.Offset = 5                  # move the graphic in depth

merge = comp.AddTool('dMerge')
merge.Background = render.Output         # a 2D image given to a deep tool is converted to deep
merge.Foreground1 = deep_graphic.Output
```

### Tips

- Image To Deep is the only deep tool that is not converted automatically, so connect 2D inputs to it yourself. Any other deep tool will convert a 2D input for you.
- Deep compositing needs linear colour. Convert the graphic to linear before it is converted to deep, if it is in a display or log space.
- Z Offset is the quickest way to move a graphic in depth from a script. Z Scale changes how far the depth samples spread, and is shown only while Specify Z is off.

**See also:** Deep To Image, dMerge, dHoldout, Common Controls → Deep images.

## Ambient Occlusion (`SSAO`)

**Category:** Deep Pixel · **Short name:** SSAO · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, a 2D RGBA image with Z and Normals), `Camera` (green, a 3D camera or scene), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Adds ambient occlusion to a 3D render: the soft darkening in creases, corners and where objects meet, which comes from the light that the scene can't reach. It is a post effect. It reads the Z and Normals channels of the input, and the camera that rendered the image, so it approximates the global lighting that a ray tracer would calculate, without the cost. Output Mode can give the occlusion on its own, as a greyscale pass, or combine it with the image.

**Use for:** contact shadows and depth cues on a 3D render, and as a separate AO pass to multiply over diffuse lighting.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output Mode | `OutputMode` | Multi-button | 1: AO (0: Color) | AO outputs the occlusion alone as greyscale, white for unoccluded areas. Color combines it with the input image. |
| Kernel Type | `KernelType` | Multi-button | 0: Hemisphere (1: Sphere) | Hemisphere follows the surface normal and is the realistic choice. Sphere is stylised: flat surfaces get half the ambient light. |
| Number of Samples | `NumberOfSamples` | Number | 2000 (slider 1 to 4000) | Rays cast per pixel. Increase until the artifacts go; more is slower. |
| Kernel Radius | `KernelRadius` | Number | 5 (0 to 10) | How far in 3D space the occluders are searched for. It depends on the scene's scale: too small misses occluders, too large needs many more samples. |
| Lift | `Lift` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Lifts the occlusion values, for an artistic look. |
| Gamma | `Gamma` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Gamma of the occlusion values. |
| Tint Red, Green, Blue | `TintRed`, `TintGreen`, `TintBlue` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Colours the occlusion. |
| Eye | `Eye` | Multi-button | 0: Mono (1: Left, 2: Right) | Which eye the effect is applied to. Not explained in the manual; check the result in the UI. |
| Camera | `Camera` | 3D input | | The camera that rendered the input, or a scene containing it. Without it, the tool doesn't render. |
| Camera Selector | `CameraSelector` | ID combo | `"Default"` | Which camera to use, when the connected scene has more than one. |

The Settings tab is described in Common Controls. Input and Camera are both required: if either is missing, the tool gives no image.

### Example

Ambient occlusion from a 3D render and its camera, as a greyscale pass:

```python
beauty = comp.AddTool('Background')     # stands in for a Renderer 3D image with Z and Normals
cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')          # the camera that rendered the beauty pass

ao = comp.AddTool('SSAO')
ao.Input = beauty.Output
ao.Camera = cam.Output
ao.OutputMode = 1                       # AO on its own (the default)
ao.KernelRadius = 2.0                   # set from the scene's scale; the default 5 suits a larger scene
ao.NumberOfSamples = 500
```

### Tips
