| Sub-Pixel | `SubPixel` | Multi-button | 0: 1x1, 1: 2x2, 2: 3x3, 3: 4x4, 4: 5x5 | Sub-pixel precision for the gradient. |

### Example

Animated, coloured noise that drifts on its own. The Seethe Rate moves the pattern every frame, so no keyframes are needed:

```python
noise = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')
noise.Type = 0                       # Two Color: the noise blends from Color 1 to Color 2
noise.Color1Red, noise.Color1Green, noise.Color1Blue, noise.Color1Alpha = 0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0
noise.Color2Red, noise.Color2Green, noise.Color2Blue, noise.Color2Alpha = 0.9, 0.95, 1.0, 1.0
noise.Detail = 4
noise.XScale = 3
noise.SeetheRate = 0.05              # the pattern drifts a little each frame
```

### Tips

- **Drive Displace with it.** Seethe Rate is the cheapest way to make heat shimmer or flag-waving. Connect the noise to
  Displace's Foreground input and the title or image to its Input. See the Displace section for a full example.
- **Use Seethe for a set pace.** Seethe Rate runs at its own speed. To time the drift to the shot, keyframe `Seethe`:
  `noise.Seethe = comp.BezierSpline()`, `noise.Seethe[0] = 0`, `noise.Seethe[120] = 1`.
- **Stretch the texture.** Turn Lock X/Y off (`noise.LockXY = 0`) and make `XScale` much larger than `YScale` for streaks
  such as brushed metal or wind. Lock X/Y keeps its own Y Scale value, so set both scales deliberately.
- **Limit the detail.** Connect a soft-edged mask to the Noise Detail Map input. Detail is lost where it is black and
  full where it is white, so fine grain can sit in one area only.
- **Keep detail low for motion.** Each Detail step adds a noise layer, so `Detail` 3 to 5 is usually enough for animated
  fog or cloud work, and it keeps renders quick.
- Fast Noise follows the comp's frame format by default (Auto Resolution on the Image tab). Set the Image tab's size
  when you need a texture at a different resolution.

**See also:** Displace, Background, Dissolve, Plasma, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Mandelbrot (`Mandel`)

**Category:** Generator · **Short name:** Man · **Inputs:** Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Renders the Mandelbrot set: a fractal, zoomable to any depth, with its colour from the number of iterations at each point.
Position sets where the view is centred, Zoom how far in, and Iterations how much detail. The colour bands are set per channel
with repetitions and phases.

**Use for:** abstract or sci-fi backgrounds, title sequences that zoom into a fractal, and a map for distortion or lighting.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position X, Position Y | `XPosition`, `YPosition` | Number | −0.5 (−3 to 2), 0 (−2.1 to 2.1) | The centre of the view. The manual calls this the seed point. |
| Zoom | `Zoom` | Number | 1 (1–10) | How far in the view goes. Has no practical upper limit. |
| Iterations | `Iterations` | Number | 256 (1–1024) | The detail: more iterations show more of the set. Animate it to grow the set. |
| Escape Limit | `EscapeLimit` | Number | 16 (2–16) | The point where the calculation stops. Low values give blurry halos. |
| Rotation | `Rotation` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Rotates the pattern. |
| Grad Method | `GradMethod` | Multi-button | 0: Continuous Potential (1: Iterations) | The gradation at the pattern's edge: smooth, or solid. |
| Gradient Curve | `GradientCurve` | Number | 0.125 (0–1) | The width of the gradation to the background. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha Repetitions | `RedRepetitions` `GreenRepetitions` `BlueRepetitions` `AlphaRepetitions` | Number | 1 (−5 to 5) | How many times each channel's colour band repeats. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha Phase | `RedPhase` `GreenPhase` `BluePhase` `AlphaPhase` | Number | 0 (0–1) | The starting point of each channel's colour band. |

### Example

A view into the seahorse valley, with more iterations for detail:

```python
mandel = comp.AddTool('Mandel')
mandel.XPosition = -0.745
mandel.YPosition = 0.113
mandel.Zoom = 40
mandel.Iterations = 512
mandel.GradMethod = 0            # Continuous Potential
```

### Tips

- **Zoom animation.** Animate Zoom with a spline for a zoom. Each magnification is calculated again, so a fast zoom
  needs more time to render.
- **Iterations.** Keep Iterations at the lowest value that shows the detail you need; high values slow the render.
- **Colour.** Animate a Phase for colour cycling.

**See also:** Plasma, Fast Noise, Background, Day Sky.

## MultiText (`MultiText`)

**Category:** Generator · **Short name:** MTxt · **Inputs:** Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A character generator with several independent text layers in one tool. Each layer has a simplified set of Text+
settings (text, font, layout and shading), with a `Text<n>.` prefix in the script ID. It lacks much of Text+: there
are no character, word, line or text transforms, and shading has only Fill, Outline and Shadow elements with fewer
controls each. Layer 1 exists by default,
and a new layer is added by the Point Layout button (`AddPoint`). Layers are rendered together over a transparent
background, so the tool is merged over a plate in the same way as Text+.

**Use for:** designs with several text blocks that move independently, such as a name and a title in one lower third,
multi-line credits, or a title with a caption under it. Use Text+ for a single block of text.

Per-layer controls are listed here for layer 1 with their Text+ equivalents. For layer *n*, use the same IDs with *n* in
place of 1 (`Text2.StyledText`, `TextName2`). For what each control does, see **Text+**; this table gives the IDs and
differences.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Styled Text | `Text1.StyledText` | Text | "Text 1" | The text of layer n. Text+ `StyledText`. |
| Font, Style | `Text1.Font` `Text1.Style` | Text | "Open Sans", "Semibold" | Font and typeface. The default Style is Semibold, where Text+ uses Bold. |
| Size | `Text1.Size` | Number | 0.08 (0–0.5) | Text size relative to image width. Text+ `Size`. |
| Colour | `Text1.Red` `Text1.Green` `Text1.Blue` `Text1.Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Text colour. |
| Layout Type | `Text1.LayoutType` | Combo | 0: Point, 1: Text Box, 2: Circle | Layout of layer n. Text+ also offers Path; MultiText does not list it. |
| Layout Center | `Text1.Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of layer n. Text+ `Center`. |
| Enabled | `TextEnabled1` | Checkbox | 1 | Turns layer n on or off. |
| Name | `TextName1` | Text | "Text n" | The layer's name in the Inspector. |
| Shading element 1 | `Text1.Enable1` `Text1.Red1` `Text1.Green1` `Text1.Blue1` `Text1.Alpha1` | Checkbox / Number | 1; colour 1, 1, 1, 1 | The fill shading element. Text+ `Enabled1` and `Red1`. |
| Shadow Position | `Text1.ShadowPosition` | Point | (0.05, −0.05) | Offset of shading element 3, the shadow, as in Text+'s element `Offset`. |
| Softness | `Text1.SoftnessX3` `Text1.SoftnessY3` | Number | 5, 5 (0–20) | Blur of the shadow. |
| Scroll | `Text1.Scroll` | Multi-button | 0: Still, 1: Roll, 2: Crawl | Roll or crawl the layer. Text+ `Scroll`. |
| Text Order | `TextOrder` | ScriptVal | `{0: 1}` | The drawing order of the layers, as a dict of position (from 0) to layer number. The first is drawn at the bottom. See Tips. |
| Global Position | `GlobalPosition` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Page-level position, not a layer control. |
| Global Size | `GlobalSize` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Page-level size, not a layer control. |

### Example

A lower third with a name and a title, as two layers. Layer 2 is added with `AddPoint`, then placed under the name, over
the plate:

```python
lower = comp.AddTool('MultiText')
lower['Text1.StyledText'] = 'Jane Smith'
lower['Text1.Size'] = 0.06
lower['Text1.Center'] = [0.2, 0.2]

lower.AddPoint = 1                         # adds layer 2
lower['Text2.StyledText'] = 'Director'
lower['Text2.Size'] = 0.035
lower['Text2.Center'] = [0.2, 0.15]

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = comp.MediaIn1.Output
merge.Foreground = lower.Output
```

### Tips

- **Adding layers.** `AddPoint = 1` adds a Point layout layer, and the new layer's controls appear as `Text2.*`.
  `AddTextBox` and `AddCircle` are the buttons for the other two layouts. Only `AddPoint` has been tested.
- **Reordering layers.** Set `TextOrder` to a dict of position to layer number, e.g. `lower.TextOrder = {0: 2, 1: 1}`
  draws layer 1 over layer 2. A layer left out of the dict is not drawn, so list every layer.
- **Animate per layer.** Keyframe `Text<n>.Center` or `Text<n>.Size` as with Text+.
- **Text+ controls that aren't here.** MultiText has no Write On (`Start` and `End`) controls and no Path layout. For a
  Write On effect, use Text+.
- **Global controls** (`GlobalPosition`, `GlobalSize`) sit on the tool's page, not on a layer. Their effect on every layer
  is not yet tested.

**See also:** Text+, Merge, MultiMerge, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## OGraf Loader (`OGrafLoader`)

**Category:** Generator · **Short name:** OGL · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Plays an OGraf graphics template: an HTML-based broadcast graphic (a lower third, a score bug or a title, for example) packaged
as an `.ograf.json` manifest. The graphic is rendered frame by frame through an embedded Chromium engine, timed to the comp, and
passed out as an image. Its parameters are set from the template, and actions such as Play and Stop can be scheduled.

Not in the Fusion 21 manual. Documented from the tool's dump and source (`OgrafCEF\OGrafLoader.cpp`). Not created in a scratch
comp, since the tool starts its engine when it is added. Its buttons were not pressed.

**Use for:** playing a broadcast graphic that is supplied as an OGraf template, with its own parameters, at a set point in the
timeline.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Template Path | `TemplatePath` | Text (file) | "" | The manifest: `.ograf.json`, `.ograf`, `.json` or `.lottie`. |
| Global In, Global Out | `GlobalIn`, `GlobalOut` | Number | 0, 1000 (0–1000) | The comp frames the graphic is active for. |
| Trim In, Trim Out | `TrimIn`, `TrimOut` | Number | 0, 0 (0–1) | Offsets into the graphic's own timeline, in frames. |
| Time Scale | `TimeScale` | Number | 1 (0.01–20) | The speed of the graphic's animation. |
| Hold First Frame, Hold Last Frame | `HoldFirstFrame`, `HoldLastFrame` | Number | 0 (−100 to 100; 0–100) | Holds the first or last frame of the graphic. |
| Loop Animation | `Loop` | Checkbox | 0 | Repeats the graphic's own animation. |
| Scheduled Action name, time, value | `ScheduledAction_0.Name`, `ScheduledAction_0.Time`, `ScheduledAction_0.Value` (ten slots) | Text, Number, ScriptVal | "playAction", 0 | A scheduled action at a time in the graphic. Ten slots, numbered 0 to 9. |
| Dynamic parameters | `DynParamText`*n*, `DynParamNum`*n*, `DynParamCheck`*n*, `DynParamCombo`*n*, `DynParamColor0_R` `DynParamColor0_G` `DynParamColor0_B` `DynParamColor0_A` | Text, Number, Checkbox, ID combo, Colour | | Up to 20 parameter slots (numbered from 0) that the template defines; labels come from the template. |

The Play, Stop, Add Custom Action, Reload and Delete buttons are not documented here as values to set. Reload is `ReloadAction`.

### Tips

- **Template.** The manifest path is the only thing needed to start. Set the template before the graphic's timing.
- **Schedule.** Actions set in ScheduledActions run at the time given in each slot. A Play at frame 0 and a Stop near the end is
  the usual pattern.
- **Engine.** The graphic is rendered by an embedded engine. Frames from it depend on the engine's state, so check the
  output in the viewer.
- **Buttons.** Don't press Play, Stop or Reload from a script in a scratch comp; they run the template.

**See also:** Text+, MultiText, Global In and Out (Common Controls).

## Plasma (`Plasma`)

**Category:** Generator · **Short name:** Plas · **Inputs:** Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Generates smooth, swirling colour patterns from four overlapping circular waves. Each circle has a type, centre and scale, and
the Operation sets how the circles combine where they overlap. Phase moves the colour bands, and so makes colour cycles when
animated.

**Use for:** abstract motion backgrounds, colour washes behind titles, and a pattern to drive a distortion (Displace, or a
shape's position) or a shadow.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scale | `Scale` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | The size of the whole pattern. |
| Operation | `Operation` | Combo | 0: Add (1: Subtract, 2: Multiply, 3: Divide, 4: Maximum, 5: Minimum, 6: Difference) | How the four circles combine. |
| Circle 1–4 Type | `Circle1Type` `Circle2Type` `Circle3Type` `Circle4Type` | Multi-button | Circle 1: 1 (Type 1); Circles 2–4: 2 (Type 2) | 0: None, 1: Type 1, 2: Type 2. None turns the circle off. |
| Circle 1–4 Center | `Circle1Center` `Circle2Center` `Circle3Center` `Circle4Center` | Point | (0.33, 0.67), (0.67, 0.67), (0.67, 0.33), (0.33, 0.33) | Where each circle is centred. |
| Circle 1–4 Scale | `Circle1Scale` `Circle2Scale` `Circle3Scale` `Circle4Scale` | Number | 1 (0–10) | The size of each circle's pattern. |
| Phase | `Phase` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Shifts the colour of the whole image. Animate it for colour cycling. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha Phase | `RedPhase` `GreenPhase` `BluePhase` `AlphaPhase` | Number | 0.0625, 0.1875, 0.3125, 0.4375 (0–1) | The phase of each channel. Animate them for colour cycling in each channel. |

### Example

Two circles multiplied together, shifted in colour:

```python
plasma = comp.AddTool('Plasma')
plasma.Scale = 2
plasma.Operation = 2                       # Multiply
plasma.Circle1Center = [0.2, 0.8]
plasma.Circle2Center = [0.8, 0.2]
plasma.Phase = 0.25
```

### Tips

- **Colour cycles.** Animate Phase, or the R, G, B and A phases separately, with a linear spline for a steady cycle.
- **Circles.** Set a circle's Type to None to remove it from the pattern.
- **As a map.** Plasma's output can drive a Displace tool or a shape distortion, since it changes smoothly across the frame.

**See also:** Fast Noise, Mandelbrot, Displace, Background.

## Text+ (`TextPlus`)

**Category:** Generator · **Short name:** Txt+ · **Inputs:** Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

The main titling tool. It generates text as a 2D image, laid out at a point, in a text box, around a circle or
along a path. Text+ supports any installed TrueType/OpenType font, styling of individual characters, separate
transforms for characters, words and lines, and up to eight *shading elements*. These are stacked layers of
fill, outline, shadow and border, each with its own colour, softness, offset and image or gradient fill.

**Use for:** titles, lower thirds, credits (Roll/Crawl), kinetic typography (with the Follower modifier),
write-on text, captions and slates (Comp Name, Time Code modifiers).

**Basic setup:** Text+ → Merge (Foreground) over the video or a Background → MediaOut. The text renders on a
transparent background, at the comp's frame format unless set otherwise on the Image tab.

### Text tab

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Styled Text | `StyledText` | Text | "" (empty) | The text. Use `\n` for new lines. |
| Font | `Font` | Text | "Open Sans" | Font family name, as installed. |
| Style | `Style` | Text | "Bold" | Typeface within the family, e.g. "Regular", "Bold", "Italic". |
| Color | `Red1` `Green1` `Blue1` `Alpha1` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Fill colour (shading element 1). The Text tab's colour swatch is a clone of these. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 0.08 (slider 0–0.5) | Text size relative to image width. |
| Tracking | `CharacterSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between characters; 1 is normal. |
| Line Spacing | `LineSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between lines (leading). |
| H Anchor | `HorizontalLeftCenterRight` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | −1 left, 0 centre, 1 right. Also controls which point rotation and spacing work from. |
| H Justify | `HorizontallyJustified` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Blends from the anchor alignment to full justification. Mainly for Text Box layout. |
| V Anchor | `VerticalTopCenterBottom` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | −1 top, 0 centre, 1 bottom. |
| V Justify | `VerticallyJustified` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Blends to full vertical justification. |
| Scroll | `Scroll` | Multi-button | 0: Still, 1: Roll, 2: Crawl | Roll (vertical) and Crawl (horizontal) credits. Animate `ScrollPosition` to move them. |
| Write On | `Start`, `End` | Number | 0 and 1 (0–1) | The visible portion of the text. Animate `End` from 0 to 1 to write on, or `Start` from 0 to 1 to write off. |
| Underline, Strikeout | `Underline`, `Strikeout` | Checkbox | 0 | Emphasis styles. |

Set the anchors with the slider IDs above. The Inspector's anchor buttons are separate inputs
(`HorizontalJustificationLeft` and so on) that aren't kept in sync with each other when set from a script.

### Layout tab

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `LayoutType` | Multi-button | 0: Point, 1: Text Box, 2: Circle, 3: Path | How the text is laid out. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the layout. |
| Size | `LayoutSize` | Number | 1 | Scales the whole layout. |
| Width, Height | `LayoutWidth`, `LayoutHeight` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 | Box size (Text Box layout), or circle size (Circle layout, Width only). |
| Wrap / Clip to Text Box | `Wrap`, `Clip` | Checkbox | 1, 0 | Word wrap and clipping for Text Box layout. |
| Angle X/Y/Z | `AngleX` `AngleY` `AngleZ` | Number | 0 (degrees) | 3D rotation of the layout. `Perspective` (default 1) sets how strong it looks. |
| Position on Path | `PositionOnPath` | Number | 0.5 | Where the text sits along the path (Path layout). Animate it to move text along the path. |
| Background colour | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 0, 0, 0, 0 | Fill behind the text; transparent by default. |

### Transform tab

Transforms that apply to every character, word or line, chosen with `SelectTransform` (0: Characters, 1: Words,
2: Lines). Each level has spacing, offset, rotation, shear and size controls, e.g. `CharacterSpacing`,
`CharacterOffset` (Point), `CharacterOffsetZ`; and the same with `Word…` and `Line…`. These are what the
Follower modifier ripples through the text.

### Shading tab

Eight shading elements, numbered 1–8. Element 1 is enabled by default ("White Solid Fill"). Elements 2–4 are set up
as "Red Outline", "Black Shadow" and "Blue Border" but are off by default. For element *n*:

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | `Enabled`*n* | Checkbox | 1 for n = 1, else 0 | Turns the element on. |
| Appearance | `ElementShape`*n* | Multi-button | 0: Text Fill, 1: Text Outline, 2: Border Fill, 3: Border Outline | What the element draws. |
| Opacity | `Opacity`*n* | Number | 1 (0–1) | |
| Thickness | `Thickness`*n* | Number | 0.02 (0–0.1) | Outline/border thickness. |
| Colour | `Red`*n* `Green`*n* `Blue`*n* `Alpha`*n* | Number | | |
| Softness | `SoftnessX`*n*, `SoftnessY`*n* | Number | 0 (0–20) | Blur; use it for soft shadows and glows. |
| Offset | `Offset`*n* | Point | (0, 0) | Moves the element; e.g. offset a shadow down and right. |
| Priority | `PriorityBack`*n* | Number | 8 (0–25) | Stacking order of the elements. |
| Level | `Level`*n* | Combo | 0: Text, 1: Line, 2: Word, 3: Character | What a Border element surrounds. |
| Round | `Round`*n* | Number | 0 | Rounds the corners of a border. |
| Extend | `ExtendHorizontal`*n*, `ExtendVertical`*n* | Number | 0 | Pads a border beyond the text. |

### Example

A lower-third title that writes on over one second at 24 fps, merged over the incoming video:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('TextPlus')
title.StyledText = 'Jane Smith\nDirector'
title.Font = 'Open Sans'
title.Style = 'Bold'
title.Size = 0.05
title.HorizontalLeftCenterRight = -1   # left-aligned
title.Center = [0.1, 0.18]

title.Enabled3 = 1                     # turn on the shadow element
title.SoftnessX3 = 4
title.SoftnessY3 = 4

title.End = comp.BezierSpline()        # write on, frames 0-24
title.End[0] = 0
title.End[24] = 1

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output     # the clip, e.g. media_in = comp.MediaIn1
merge.Foreground = title.Output
```

### Tips

- For text that moves as a whole, animate Layout `Center` or put a Transform after the Text+. For per-character
  animation, right-click Styled Text → Follower (or `title.AddModifier('StyledText', 'StyledTextFollower')`) and
  animate the Follower's controls.
- Shading elements are cheaper and easier to animate than building outlines and shadows with separate tools.
- **MultiText** (`MultiText`) has the same controls per text layer. Use it when a design needs several independent
  text blocks in one tool.

**See also:** MultiText, sText, Text 3D, Merge, Follower.

## Loader (`Loader`)

**Category:** I/O · **Short name:** LD · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Reads a clip from disk into the comp: a single file, or a sequence found from the numbers in the filename. In Fusion Studio
it is the main footage node, with trim, hold, loop and reverse, and import settings for field order, pixel aspect, bit
depth and colour space. In DaVinci Resolve the manual limits it to EXR files, and MediaIn is the node used for clips.

**Use for:** file-based work in Fusion Studio: image sequences from a renderer or camera, trimmed and looped footage, and
the import settings for a plate. In Resolve, use MediaIn for timeline clips and Media Pool clips (see MediaIn).

Loader's file is named by path. A sequence is found from the last number in the name: `image.0001.exr` and `image.0100.exr`
make one 100-frame sequence, even with frames missing between. A file name that ends in letters, such as `shot.1.fg.jpg`,
isn't treated as a sequence.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clip (Filename) | `Clip` | Text (file) | "" | The file, or any file of the sequence. Filename completion works in the box. |
| Proxy Filename | `ProxyFilename` | Text (file) | "" | A smaller clip loaded when the comp's Proxy mode is on. It must have the same frame count and numbering. |
| Global In, Global Out | `GlobalIn`, `GlobalOut` | Number | 0, 0 (0–1000) | The comp frames the node is active for. Shorter than the clip trims the clip; longer holds the ends. |
| Trim In, Trim Out | `ClipTimeStart`, `ClipTimeEnd` | Number | 0, 0 | Offsets into the clip: 5 in Trim In starts at the fifth frame; 95 in Trim Out stops after the 95th. |
| Hold First Frame, Hold Last Frame | `HoldFirstFrame`, `HoldLastFrame` | Number | 0 (0–100) | Repeats the first or last frame for the given number of frames. |
| Reverse | `Reverse` | Checkbox | 0 | Plays the clip backwards. |
| Loop | `Loop` | Checkbox | 0 | Repeats the clip to the end of the comp, including any holds and trims. |
| Missing Frames | `MissingFrames` | Combo | 0: Fail (1: Hold Previous, 2: Output Color, 3: Wait) | What to output for a frame that can't be loaded. Output Color uses `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` and `Alpha`. The manual calls the option "Output Black". |
| Process Mode | `ProcessMode` | ID combo | `"FullFrames"` | `"FullFrames"`, `"NTSC"`, `"PAL"`, `"PALReversed"` or `"NTSCReversed"`. |
| Depth | `Depth` | Multi-button | 0: Format (1: Default, 2: int8, 3: int16, 4: float16, 5: float32) | Processing bit depth. Format uses the file's own depth. |
| Pixel Aspect | `PixelAspect` | Multi-button | 0: From File (1: Default, 2: Custom) | Pixel aspect. Custom uses `CustomPixelAspect` (Point). |
| Import Mode | `ImportMode` | Multi-button | 0: Normal (1: 2:3 Pullup, 2: 2:3 Pulldown) | Removes or adds 3:2 pulldown. First Frame sets the start of the 3:2 cycle (AA, BB, BC, CD, DD). |
| Make Alpha Solid | `MakeAlphaSolid` | Checkbox | 0 | Sets alpha to solid white. |
| Invert Alpha | `InvertAlpha` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the alpha. |
| Post-Multiply by Alpha | `PostMultiplyByAlpha` | Checkbox | 0 | Multiplies colour by alpha, for converting non-premultiplied footage. |
| Swap Field Dominance | `SwapFieldDominance` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the order the fields play in, without moving the lines. |
| Color Space Type | `Gamut.ColorType` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"` passes the file's colour metadata; `"Space"` tags the source colour space (no conversion; a Gamut tool does that). |
| Curve Type | `Gamut.GammaType` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"`, `"Space"` or `"Log"` (with `Gamut.LogType`). |
| Remove Curve | `Gamut.GammaAction` | Checkbox | 0 | Removes the gamma curve or applies a log-to-linear conversion. |
| Local Cache | `LocalCache` | ID multi-button | `"Default"` | `"Default"`, `"On"` or `"Off"`. Not in the manual. |

The Format tab holds the file-specific controls, such as EXR channel mapping and camera RAW debayering. They change with the
file and aren't in the tool's dump, so they aren't listed here.

### Example

Loading a rendered EXR sequence, trimmed to 50 frames and looped. The comp is locked while the Loader is added, so
Auto Clip Browse doesn't open a file browser:

```python
comp.Lock()
plate = comp.AddTool('Loader')
plate.Clip = 'D:/renders/fx_plate/fx_plate.0001.exr'   # any file of the sequence
comp.Unlock()

plate.ClipTimeStart = 10      # start at the 10th frame of the clip
plate.ClipTimeEnd = 59
plate.Loop = 1
plate.MissingFrames = 1       # hold the previous frame instead of failing
```

### Tips

- **Lock the comp while adding a Loader.** In an unlocked comp with Auto Clip Browse on (the preference
  `Global.UserInterface.AutoClipBrowse`, on by default), adding a Loader with no clip opens a modal file browser, and a
  script waits on it. `comp.Lock()` (or a comp made with `fu.NewComp(True)`) stops the browser; unlock afterwards.
  Verified in a locked scratch comp.
- **Trim and hold.** Changing Global In and Out adjusts the trim and hold values for the clip automatically (manual).
- **Missing frames.** With `MissingFrames` set to Fail, a missing frame stops the render. Wait pauses it until the frame
  appears, which suits a render running alongside a 3D render.
- **Magic Comp path.** `Comp:\` in the path, or the Path Map preference, makes a path relative to the comp file (Fusion Studio).

**See also:** Saver, MediaIn, MediaOut, Common Controls (Settings tab).

## MediaIn (`MediaIn`)

**Category:** I/O · **Short name:** MI · **Inputs:** Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Brings a clip into a Fusion comp in DaVinci Resolve; it replaces the Loader used in Fusion Studio. A comp created on a
media clip in the Timeline starts with `MediaIn1` → `MediaOut1`, where `MediaIn1` is that clip. A comp created as a
Fusion Composition clip starts with only a MediaOut. Any comp can add more MediaIns, set to `"MediaPool"` (a clip in
the Media Pool, which needs its Media ID) or `"Background"` (the composited tracks below this clip).

**Use for:** the plate or clip at the start of every comp, and extra clips such as a logo or second shot in a composite.
Trim and hold controls set the clip's length without changing the source.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Media Source | `MediaSource` | ID multi-button | `"Timeline"` | `"Timeline"` links the clip on the Edit or Cut Timeline. `"Background"` pulls the composited lower tracks. `"MediaPool"` links the clip in the Media Pool, bypassing the Timeline. |
| Media ID | `MediaID` | Text | "" | The identifier of the clip for the chosen source. Not shown in the Inspector; set it from script. |
| Layer | `Layer` | Text | "0" | For a multilayer or PSD file, the layer to use. For a Fusion Clip, the index of the video layer. |
| Clip Name | `ClipName` | Text | "" | The clip's name. Shown for reference. |
| Trim In, Trim Out | `ClipTimeStart`, `ClipTimeEnd` | Number | 0, 0 | The trim range of the clip: the part of the clip used, as frame indices from 0 for the clip's first frame (not file sequence numbers). Filled in from the clip when Media ID is set. |
| Hold First Frame, Hold Last Frame | `HoldFirstFrame`, `HoldLastFrame` | Number | 0 (0–100) | Repeats the first or last frame for the given number of frames. |
| Reverse | `Reverse` | Checkbox | 0 | Plays the clip backwards. |
| Loop | `Loop` | Checkbox | 0 | Repeats the clip when it ends. |
| Global In, Global Out | `GlobalIn`, `GlobalOut` | Number | 0, 1000 | The comp frames the node is active for. |
| Stereo Eye | `StereoEye` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"`, `"Left"`, `"Right"` or `"Layers"`. For stereo clips. |
| Sound Offset | `SoundOffset` | Number | 0 (0–100) | Slips the audio, in subframe steps, in the Fusion page only. |

Only MediaIns added to a comp have the Trim, Hold, Reverse, Loop and Global In/Out controls. The comp's own
timeline-linked `MediaIn1` takes its timing from the clip in the Timeline.

### Example

Add a second clip from the Media Pool, looped, and merge it over the comp's own clip:

```python
project = resolve.GetProjectManager().GetCurrentProject()
clip = project.GetMediaPool().GetRootFolder().GetClipList()[0]   # a MediaPoolItem

logo = comp.AddTool('MediaIn')
logo.MediaSource = 'MediaPool'
logo.MediaID = clip.GetMediaId()       # fills in ClipName and the trim range
logo.Loop = 1

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = comp.MediaIn1       # the clip this comp was created on
merge.Foreground = logo
comp.MediaOut1.Input = merge
```

### Tips

- **Media IDs come from Resolve.** Use `MediaPoolItem.GetMediaId()` from the Resolve scripting API. An invalid ID is
  accepted but the MediaIn has no image.
- **Trim and hold** (added MediaIns only). Use `ClipTimeStart` and `ClipTimeEnd` to cut the clip, and `HoldFirstFrame`
  and `HoldLastFrame` to extend it. The manual says that changing Global In and Out adjusts the trim and hold values
  automatically.
- **`"Background"`** brings in the composited tracks below this clip in the Timeline, for effects that work on
  everything underneath, such as an adjustment-style blur or a transition.
- **The Effect Mask input** limits the clip's image to the mask area, as with other image tools.
- Colour space and gamma for the clip are on the Image tab's Color Space Type and Curve Type controls (Common Controls).

**See also:** MediaOut, Background, Merge, Dissolve, Transform.

## MediaOut (`MediaOut`)

**Category:** I/O · **Short name:** MO · **Inputs:** Input (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Sends the finished composition back to the Timeline on the Edit or Cut page. Every comp made on the Fusion page needs a
MediaOut, and the first one (`MediaOut1`) is the one that renders to the Timeline. It replaces the Saver used in Fusion
Studio. Extra MediaOut nodes can be added to pass mattes to the Color page.

**Use for:** the last tool in every comp, connected to the comp's final image. Also for mattes that the Color page needs
alongside the picture.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input | `Input` | Image input | | The image rendered back to the Timeline. Required. |
| Color Grade | `ColorGrade` | ID multi-button | `"None"` | Preview only, and does not change the output. `"None"` shows the comp alone. `"Color"` adds the Color page adjustments at timeline resolution. `"Mix"` also adds Cut and Edit page effects. |
| Stereo Eye | `StereoEye` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"`, `"Left"` or `"Right"`. For stereo output. |
| Index | `Index` | Text | `"0"` | The output's number: 0 for the first MediaOut, counting up for each new one. Outputs other than the first are available on Resolve's Color page, typically as extra mattes for grading. |

### Example

The final composite of a plate and a logo, sent to the Timeline:

```python
merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = comp.MediaIn1.Output
merge.Foreground = comp.MediaIn2.Output

out = comp.MediaOut1
out.Input = merge.Output
```

### Tips

- **Connect the finished image once.** `MediaOut1` renders to the Timeline, so connect it to the last tool in the comp.
  Changing its `Input` changes what goes back to the Edit page.
- **Color Grade is a preview.** `"Color"` and `"Mix"` only change the view in the Fusion page. The rendered output of
  MediaOut is unchanged.
- **Mattes.** Add another MediaOut (`comp.AddTool('MediaOut')`) and connect a matte to it to pass that matte to the
  Color page, as the manual describes.

**See also:** MediaIn, Merge, MultiMerge, Dissolve.

## Saver (`Saver`)

**Category:** I/O · **Short name:** SV · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, Image) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Writes the image stream to disk, as one file or a numbered sequence, when the comp is rendered. A comp can hold any number of
Savers, each in its own format, and one can sit anywhere in a branch to write an intermediate stage. Its settings are the
file path, the output format and the format's own options, plus the export tab (fields, clipping, colour space and gamma).

**Use for:** file-based work: EXR or other image sequences for another application, scratch renders, several formats of one
comp, and writing a branch at a set point in the tree.

**Resolve note:** a comp made with `fu.NewComp()` can't be rendered in Resolve, so a Saver in such a comp holds its settings
but writes nothing. The Resolve way to get a comp's output is a comp on a timeline clip, which uses MediaIn and MediaOut
(see MediaOut). Loader and Saver are for file-based work, as in Fusion Studio.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filename | `Clip` | Text (file) | "" | The output path. A sequence is numbered at the end of the name; see the Tips for padding. |
| Create Folder During Render | `CreateDir` | Checkbox | 1 | Creates the output folder when a render starts. `CreateDirNow` (Create button) does it immediately. |
| Output Format | `OutputFormat` | ID combo | `"OpenEXRFormat"` | `"FusePicFormat"`, `"RawFormat"`, `"IPLFormat"`, `"JpegFormat"`, `"OpenEXRFormat"`, `"PNGFormat"`, `"TargaFormat"`, `"BMPFormat"`. Changing it doesn't change the file extension in `Clip`. |
| Save Frames | `SaveFrames` | ID combo | `"Full"` | `"Full"` writes frames on a final render. `"HiQInteractive"` writes each frame as it is processed interactively (for painting and rotoscoping). |
| Saver-relative Numbering | `SetSequenceStart` | Checkbox | 0 | Numbers the sequence from `SequenceStartFrame` rather than the comp frame. |
| Frame Offset | `SequenceStartFrame` | Number | 0 (0–100) | The first number of the sequence when Saver-relative Numbering is on. |
| Save Layers | `SaveLayers` | ID combo | `":Default"` | `":Default"`, `":All"` or `":Custom"` (the layers to write, for multilayer formats). |
| Process Mode | `ProcessMode` | ID combo | `"Auto"` | `"FullFrames"`, `"NTSC"`, `"PAL"`, `"PALReversed"`, `"NTSCReversed"` or `"Auto"`. Fields order for interlaced output. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID multi-button | `"Frame"` | `"None"` writes everything outside the frame; `"Frame"` clips to the visible frame. |
| Save Alpha to Color | `SaveAlphaToColor` | Checkbox | 0 | Writes the alpha as a grey image in the colour channels, replacing the colour. |
| Export Mode | `Normal` | ID multi-button | `"Normal"` | `"Normal"` or `"PulldownA"` (SMPTE 3:2 pulldown, 24 to 30 fps). |
| Color Space Type | `Gamut.ColorType` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"` passes the image's colour metadata; `"Space"` converts to `Gamut.ColorSpace` on output. The comp is not changed. |
| Curve Type | `Gamut.GammaType` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | `"Auto"`, `"Space"` (`Gamut.GammaSpace`) or `"Log"` (`Gamut.LogType`). |
| Apply Curve | `Gamut.GammaAction` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the gamma or log curve from Curve Type to the output. |
| Sound Filename | `SoundFilename` | Text (file) | "" | A WAV scratch track (Fusion Studio only). |

**Format-specific controls.** The Format tab changes with `OutputFormat`. Each set is named after its format:

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EXR depth | `OpenEXRFormat.Depth` | Multi-button | 0: Auto (1: float16, 2: float32) | Bit depth of the EXR. |
| EXR compression | `OpenEXRFormat.Compression` | Combo | 3: Zip (16 lines) | 0: None, 1: RLE, 2: Zip (1 line), 3: Zip (16 lines), 4: Piz (wavelet), 5: Pxr24, 6: B44, 7: B44A, 8: DWA (32 lines), 9: DWA (256 lines), 10: HTJ2K (256 lines), 11: HTJ2K (32 lines). |
| EXR Zip level, DWA level | `OpenEXRFormat.ZipCompressionLevel`, `OpenEXRFormat.DWACompressionLevel` | Number | 4 (0–9), 45 (0–100) | Compression strength for Zip and DWA. |
| EXR channels | `OpenEXRFormat.RedEnable`, `OpenEXRFormat.RedName` and the other pairs | Checkbox, Text | 1; names R, G, B, A | Turns each channel on or off and sets its name in the file. Pairs exist for Alpha, Z, ZBack, Coverage, ObjectID, MaterialID, U, V, normals, velocities, positions and disparity. |
| PNG alpha, divide | `PNGFormat.SaveAlpha`, `PNGFormat.PreDivide` | Checkbox | 1, 1 | Saves alpha, and divides colour by alpha on save. |
| PNG depth | `PNGFormat.Depth` | Combo | 0: Auto (1: int8, 2: int16) | Bit depth. |
| PNG compression, gamma | `PNGFormat.CompressionLevel`, `PNGFormat.GammaMode`, `PNGFormat.Gamma` | Number, Multi-button, Number | 6 (0–9), 0: Auto (1: None, 2: sRGB, 3: Gamma), 1 (0–5) | Compression level and the gamma written to the file. |
| JPEG quality | `JpegFormat.Quality` | Number | 97 (0–100) | Compression quality. |
| JPEG options | `JpegFormat.ChromaSubsampling`, `JpegFormat.SetCustomResolution`, `JpegFormat.ResolutionDPI` | Checkbox, Checkbox, Number | 0, 0, 300 | Chroma subsampling, and a custom DPI for the file. |
| IPL quality | `IPLFormat.Quality` | Number | 93 (0–100) | Compression quality. |
| Targa | `TargaFormat.SaveAlpha`, `TargaFormat.Compress` | Checkbox | 1, 1 | Alpha and RLE compression. |
| BMP | `BMPFormat.SaveAlpha` | Checkbox | 1 | Alpha. |
| Raw | `RawFormat.Compression` | Combo | 2: Runlength (0: None, 1: Zlib) | Compression for the Raw format. |

### Example

Writes a float EXR sequence with Piz compression, numbered from 100:

```python
saver = comp.AddTool('Saver')
saver.Input = media_in.Output
saver.Clip = 'D:/Renders/shot/shot.0000.exr'     # four digits of padding
saver.OutputFormat = 'OpenEXRFormat'
saver['OpenEXRFormat.Depth'] = 2                 # float32
saver['OpenEXRFormat.Compression'] = 4           # Piz (wavelet)
saver.SetSequenceStart = 1
saver.SequenceStartFrame = 100
```

### Tips

- **Padding.** Without digits in the name, Saver numbers the sequence with four digits, and numbers under 10000 are padded
  to four. Digits in the name set the padding: `shot.000000.exr` gives six digits, and `shot1.exr` gives none.
- **Extension.** Changing `OutputFormat` doesn't rename the file. Set the extension in `Clip` yourself.
- **Full or interactive.** `"Full"` writes on a final render. `"HiQInteractive"` writes as you paint or roto, but frames
  already saved don't re-render if an earlier spline changes. Do a final render after changing animation.
- **Render.** Scratch comps from `fu.NewComp()` can't render in Resolve, so the files in the examples are never written
  there. The settings are checked on the tool only.
- **Format visibility.** Don't rely on `WindowControlsVisible()` for the format sets: after a change of `OutputFormat`,
  the controls of earlier formats still report visible. Use the table above.
- **Loader.** Read the same kind of file back with Loader, which is for file-based work too (see Loader).

**See also:** Loader, MediaIn, MediaOut, Common Controls (Settings tab).

## Layer Muxer (`LayerMuxer`)

**Category:** Layer · **Short name:** LMx · **Inputs:** `Image1` (Image 1), `Image2` (Image 2) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Combines the layers of two multilayer images: the layers of Image 2 are added to Image 1, and one layer is chosen as the main
(default) layer of the result. Layers are named groups of channels in a multilayer file, such as an EXR with a diffuse, a
specular and a depth pass. Muxer picks which of them go into the output.

**Use for:** adding passes from one render to the layers of another, or choosing one layer from a multilayer file to carry
forward.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Layer | `Layer` | Layer | `":All"` | The layers taken from Image 2: `":Default"` (its default layer), `":All"` or `":Custom"` (a checklist, held in `LayerCustom`). |
| Conflicts | `Conflicts` | ID combo | `"Imagea"` | Which image's layer wins when both have a layer of the same name: `"Imagea"` (Image 1) or `"Image2"`. The selected image becomes the default layer. |

The Conflicts option for Image 1 is the FuID `"Imagea"`, not `"Image1"`. It's the ID in the source.

### Example

Adds the layers of a second pass to a beauty image, with Image 1 winning any name clash:

```python
muxer = comp.AddTool('LayerMuxer')
muxer.Image1 = media_in.Output
muxer.Image2 = comp.AddTool('Background').Output   # stand-in for a pass
muxer.Layer = ':All'
muxer.Conflicts = 'Imagea'
```

### Tips

- **Names.** Layers keep their names; use Layer Regex to rename or filter them first.
- **Defaults.** The default layer is the one that the other tools see when they don't name a layer.
- **Custom.** `":Custom"` shows a checklist of Image 2's layers in the Inspector. Its value is held in `LayerCustom`; the
  list format was not tested from script.

**See also:** Layer Regex, Layer Remover, Swizzler, Channel Booleans.

## Layer Regex (`LayerRegex`)

**Category:** Layer · **Short name:** LRx · **Inputs:** `Image1` (Image 1), `Image2` (Image 2) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Filters or renames the layers of two multilayer images by their names, using a regular expression. Each image has its own
expression, mode and name template. A layer whose name matches the expression can be renamed, kept or removed, and the
expression can also be tested on sample text in the Tester.

**Use for:** renaming passes to a standard (for example "Right.Diffuse" from "diffuse_R"), keeping only some layers, and removing
unwanted ones before a Layer Muxer.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expression | `Expression1`, `Expression2` | Text | `"(.*)"` | The regular expression matched against layer names. |
| Mode | `Mode1`, `Mode2` | ID combo | `"Transform"` | `"Transform"` renames the matches with the template. `"Keep"` keeps only the matches. `"Remote"` (shown as Remove) removes the matches. |
| Name Template | `Template1`, `Template2` | Text | `"$1"` | The new name, with `$1` for the first group in the expression. Shown in Transform mode. |
| Unmatched | `Unmatched1`, `Unmatched2` | ID combo | `"Keep"` | What happens to layers that don't match: `"Keep"` or `"Remote"` (Remove). Shown in Transform mode. |
| Sample | `Sample1`, `Sample2` | Text | "" | Sample text for the Tester. |
| Conflicts | `Conflicts` | ID combo | `"Image1"` | Which image's layer wins a clash: `"Image1"` or `"Image2"`. The selected image becomes the default layer. |

### Example

Puts "Right." in front of every layer name from Image 1:

```python
regex = comp.AddTool('LayerRegex')
regex.Image1 = media_in.Output
regex.Expression1 = '(.*)'
regex.Template1 = 'Right.$1'
```

### Tips

- **Groups.** `$1` is the first group in parentheses. Put the new text before or after it: `$1.Right` gives "Layer1.Right".
- **Whole words.** Use `^` to match the start of a name (`^right(.*)` doesn't match "copyright"). Use `(?i)` for case-insensitive matching.
- **Remove or keep.** To remove copies, use `(copy|right)` with Mode `"Remote"`. Mode `"Keep"` with the same expression keeps only those layers.
- **Name Template.** It doesn't apply in Remove or Keep modes. Shown only in Transform.

**See also:** Layer Muxer, Layer Remover, Swizzler.

## Layer Remover (`LayerRemover`)

**Category:** Layer · **Short name:** LRm · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, Image) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Removes chosen layers from a multilayer image. The Layers control is a checklist of every layer in the input: a checked
layer is removed, and the others pass through. Use it to strip passes that a comp doesn't need, before a Muxer or a Saver.

**Use for:** dropping unneeded passes from an EXR, so that later tools see fewer layers.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Layers | `Layers` | Layer list (ScriptVal) | `{}` | The checklist of the input's layers. A checked layer is removed. Filled from the input's layers in the Inspector. |

### Tips

- **Checklist.** The list is built from the layers the input has, so connect the input before setting it in the Inspector.
- **Script.** The value's format wasn't tested from script (the comp had no layered input), so set layers in the Inspector.
- **Effect Mask.** The tool has no Effect Mask input.

**See also:** Layer Regex, Layer Muxer, Swizzler.

## Swizzler (`Swizzler`)

**Category:** Layer · **Short name:** Swz · **Inputs:** `Input1`, and more as they are added · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Builds new layers from channels taken from one or more images. Each layer in the Swizzler's layer list has its own source
for each channel: red, green, blue, alpha, the auxiliary channels (Z, UV, normals and so on), and background colour. Layers can
be added, renamed and deleted, and an existing multilayer input's layers can be kept with Keep Main Input Layers.

**Use for:** assembling a multilayer file from separate passes, one per input (for example a UV pass, a normal pass and a
depth pass), and assigning Aux channels from RGB sources.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keep Main Input Layers | `KeepLayers` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps the layers of Input 1 in the output, so passes can be added to them. |
| Layer Order | `LayerOrder` | Layer list (ScriptVal) | `{0: 1}` | The layer list. The selected layer is the one the channel controls edit. |
| Layer Name | `LayerName1` | Text | "Layer1" | The name of layer 1. Layers 2 and later use `LayerNameN`. |
| Channels | `Layer1.Channels` | ID multi-button | `"All"` | `"All"` moves every channel into the layer. `"Chans"` uses the Color and Aux selections below. |
| Color | `Layer1.Color` | ID multi-button | `"RGBA"` | The colour channels to take, in Chans mode: `"RGBA"`, `"RGB"`, `"R"` or `"A"`. |
| Aux | `Layer1.Aux` | ID multi-button | `"Aux"` | In Chans mode: `"Aux"` takes the auxiliary channels, `"Z"` the depth. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha source | `Layer1.RInput` `Layer1.GInput` `Layer1.BInput` `Layer1.AInput` | Combo | 1 | The input each channel comes from. The default is 1; the option list was not read from script. |
| Source Layer | `Layer1.RLayer` `Layer1.GLayer` `Layer1.BLayer` `Layer1.ALayer` | Layer | `":Default"` | The layer of that input to take the channel from. |
| Source Channels | `Layer1.RChannels` `Layer1.GChannels` `Layer1.BChannels` `Layer1.AChannels` | ID combo | `"Match"` | The channel of the source layer to take. `"Match"` uses the same name. |
| Aux and Z sources | `Layer1.ZInput`, `Layer1.ZLayer`, `Layer1.ZChannels` | Combo, Layer, ID combo | 1, `":Default"`, `"Match"` | The source for the Z channel and the Aux channels in Chans mode. |
| Background colour | `Layer1.BGColor` | ID multi-button | `"BGRGBA"` | Background colour channels: `"BGRGBA"`, `"BGRGB"`, `"BGR"` or `"BGA"`. Not in the manual. |

Layer 1's controls are shown above with the layer number as in `Layer1.*`. Layer 2 and later use the same pattern with that number
(`Layer2.Color`, and so on), once they are added with the Add Layer button, which was not pressed.

### Example

Sets layer 1's colour channels to RGB from Input 1:

```python
swz = comp.AddTool('Swizzler')
swz.Input1 = media_in.Output
swz['Layer1.Channels'] = 'Chans'  # Color is shown only in Chans mode
swz['Layer1.Color'] = 'RGB'
swz['Layer1.RInput'] = 1
```

### Tips

- **Aux channels.** Use the Color and Aux split to put RGB from one input into the colour channels and the XYZ normals or UV
  from another into Aux. Choose the Source Layer of each pass.
- **Layers.** Add a layer for each pass, then give it a name in the layer list, then choose its inputs.
- **Effect Mask.** The tool has no Effect Mask input.
- **Not verified.** Only the control values were read back. The output channels weren't checked, since the comp can't render.

**See also:** Layer Muxer, Layer Regex, Layer Remover, Channel Booleans.

## File LUT (`FileLUT`)

**Category:** LUT · **Short name:** FLU · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies a lookup table from a file to the image. Unlike Color Curves, the table isn't stored in the comp; only its path is, so
one LUT file can drive many File LUT nodes, and changing the file changes all of them. It reads 1D LUTs and 3D LUTs in the
supported formats: Fusion's `.lut` and `.alut`, DaVinci Resolve's `.cube`, and several other 3D formats.

**Use for:** applying a look or a technical transform (a camera LUT, or a colourist's look) with a file that many comps share.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LUT File | `LUTFile` | Text (file) | "" | The path to the LUT file. The tool reports an error in the console if it can't load the file. |
| Pre-Gain | `PreGain` | Number | 1 (0–5) | A gain before the LUT, for pulling highlights into range before the LUT clips them. |
| Post-Gain | `PostGain` | Number | 1 (0–5) | A gain after the LUT. |
| Color Space | `ColorSpace` | Combo | 0: RGB (1: YUV, 2: HLS, 3: YIQ, 4: CMY) | The colour space the LUT is applied in. The manual lists HSV, which the live tool doesn't offer. |
| Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply | `PreDividePostMultiply` | Checkbox | 0 | Divides by alpha before the LUT and multiplies back after. Stops additive edges on keys and CG. |

### Example

A grading LUT at the end of a branch, at a gain of 1.0 before and 0.9 after:

```python
lut = comp.AddTool('FileLUT')
lut.Input = media_in.Output
lut.LUTFile = 'D:/LUTs/Show_Look.cube'
lut.PreGain = 1.0
lut.PostGain = 0.9
```

### Tips

- **Path.** A LUT path that doesn't exist is accepted and stored; the error appears in the console when the tool processes.
- **Shared looks.** Keep the path to a shared folder, so that every comp uses the same file.
- **Linear.** For a camera LUT on log footage, place the File LUT at the start of the branch, before the grade.
- **Keys.** Turn on Pre-Divide / Post-Multiply for a keyed or CG image so that edges don't brighten.

**See also:** Color Curves, Color Corrector, LUT Cube Creator, LUT Cube Analyzer.

## LUT Cube Analyzer (`Fuse.LUTCubeAnalyzer`)

**Category:** LUT · **Short name:** LCA · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Reads a graded LUT Cube Creator image and writes it to disk as a 3D LUT file: ALUT3, CUBE or 3DL. The image passes through
unchanged, and nothing is shown in the viewer. This is a Fuse, documented from its source (`LUTCubeAnalyzer.fuse`) and not
created in a scratch comp.

**Use for:** turning a grade built on a test cube into a 3D LUT that colourists and other tools can use.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0: ALUT3 (1: CUBE, 2: 3DL) | The LUT format to write. The file extension follows it: `.alut3`, `.cube` or `.3dl`. |
| Filename | `Filename` | Text (file) | "" | The path to write. The extension is replaced with the one for Type. |
| Write File | `WriteFile` | Button | | Writes the file from the connected image. |

The manual lists ITX as a type. The live tool offers ALUT3, CUBE and 3DL only.

### Tips

- **Writing.** Setting Write File to 1 in a script writes the file. The source checks the value on change, so the write runs
  when the value is set. Set Type and Filename first.
- **Image.** The connected image must be a LUT Cube Creator image, graded. The tool reads the cube size from the image's shape.
- **Float.** The manual advises keeping the image in 32-bit float outside Fusion, to keep the colour accurate.
- **Identity.** Feeding the Creator's image straight in gives an unaltered LUT.

**See also:** LUT Cube Creator, LUT Cube Apply, File LUT.

## LUT Cube Apply (`Fuse.LUTCubeApply`)

**Category:** LUT · **Short name:** LCP · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange), `LUTCubeImage` (green, "LUT Cube Image"), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies the colouring of a LUT Cube image to another image, without writing a LUT file. The LUT Cube image comes from LUT Cube
Creator, graded with any tools; `Image` is the footage to colour. This is a Fuse, documented from its source
(`LUTCubeApply.fuse`) and not created in a scratch comp.

**Use for:** trying out a grade in the comp before writing a 3D LUT, or applying a look built on a test cube.

This tool has no controls of its own. The three inputs are `Image`, `LUTCubeImage` and `EffectMask`.

The manual calls the green input "Reference Image". The live input is `LUTCubeImage`, labelled "LUT Cube Image".

### Tips

- **Cube shape.** The LUT image must be a cube layout that the tool can read: a square tile strip, or a rectangle of tiles.
  The source reports "Bad LUTcube image map dimensions" when it can't read the layout. Use LUT Cube Creator's output, unaltered
  except for grading, and it will work.
- **GPU.** The tool uses the GPU path when it can (a compute kernel, from the source).
- **Mask.** The Effect Mask limits the LUT to part of the frame.

**See also:** LUT Cube Creator, LUT Cube Analyzer, File LUT.

## LUT Cube Creator (`Fuse.LUTCubeCreator`)

**Category:** LUT · **Short name:** LCC · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Generates a test image of a colour cube: every combination of red, green and blue at a set number of steps. The image is the
starting point for a 3D LUT. Grade it with any tools, then feed it to LUT Cube Analyzer to write a LUT file, or to LUT Cube
Apply to use it in the comp. This is a Fuse, documented from its source (`LUTCubeCreator.fuse`) and not created in a scratch
comp.

**Use for:** the first step of building a 3D LUT from a grade.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0: Horizontal (1: Vertical, 2: Rect) | The layout of the cube: a long horizontal strip, a long vertical strip, or a rectangle. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 33 (2–257) | The steps on each side of the cube. 33 and 65 are the usual sizes. The sample count is Size cubed. |

### Tips

- **Size.** 33 makes about 36,000 samples; 65 is more precise and much larger.
- **Float.** Keep the image in 32-bit float while grading, to keep colour accuracy.
- **Rect.** The rectangle layout shows the cube as a picture that is easy to check by eye.

**See also:** LUT Cube Analyzer, LUT Cube Apply, File LUT.

## Bitmap Mask (`BitmapMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** Bmp · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange), `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask from an image connected to its orange input. You choose which channel is used: red, green, blue,
alpha, hue, luminance, saturation, or the coverage channel. Low and High then clip the result to a range. The mask
can also be keyed on the Object or Material ID of a 3D render. For a plain mask from an image's alpha, you can
connect the image straight to an EffectMask, but this tool gives the channel choice, clipping and softness.

**Use for:** luminance and colour mattes from a picture, clipping a channel to a range, and combining image-based
mattes with other masks through Paint Mode.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image | `Image` | Image input | (none) | The image to make the mask from. Connect a tool's Output here. |
| Fit Input | `FitInput` | ID multi-button | `"Crop"` | How the image is fitted to the mask size: `"Crop"`, `"Stretch"`, `"Inside"`, `"Width"`, `"Height"` or `"Outside"`. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the image within the mask frame. |
| Channel | `Channel` | ID combo | `"Alpha"` | The channel that becomes the mask: `"Red"`, `"Green"`, `"Blue"`, `"Alpha"`, `"Hue"`, `"Luminance"`, `"Saturation"` or `"Coverage"`. |
| Low, High | `Low`, `High` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Threshold range. Values below Low go to black, and values above High go to white. |
| Clip Black, Clip White | `ClipBlack`, `ClipWhite` | Checkbox | 1, 1 | Clamp the result to 0 (Clip Black) and to 1 (Clip White). |
| Use Object, Object | `UseObject`, `Object` | Checkbox, Number | 0, 0 | With Use Object on, the mask comes from the pixels whose Object ID is `Object`, rather than from the colour channels. |
| Use Material, Material | `UseMaterial`, `Material` | Checkbox, Number | 0, 0 | The same for Material ID. |

### Example

A soft luminance matte from a picture, used to blur only its darker areas:

```python
matte = comp.AddTool('BitmapMask')
matte.Image = media_in.Output
matte.Channel = 'Luminance'
matte.Low = 0.4
matte.High = 1.0
matte.SoftEdge = 0.02

blur = comp.AddTool('Blur')
blur.Input = media_in.Output
blur.EffectMask = matte.Mask
```

### Tips

- Object and Material IDs only exist in images rendered with those channels, such as a 3D render from Renderer 3D.
  Without them, Use Object and Use Material have no effect.
- Chain Bitmap masks by connecting one mask's `Mask` output to the next one's `EffectMask` and setting the Paint
  Mode on the receiving mask. See Common Controls → Mask tools.
- Output Size defaults to `"Source"`, so the mask matches the size of the image connected to `Image`.

**See also:** Ranges Mask, Wand Mask, Mask Paint, Effect masks and Mask tools (Common Controls).

## B-Spline Mask (`BSplineMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** BSp · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask from a B-Spline polyline. It works like the Polygon mask, but each point only pulls the curve toward it
rather than passing through it, so a smooth shape needs far fewer points. The tension of each point sets how
tightly the curve follows it. As with the Polygon mask, the points can be drawn and edited in the viewer, or set and
keyframed from script, and the whole shape can be moved, scaled and rotated.

**Use for:** smooth garbage mattes and soft organic shapes, where a Bézier polygon would need many points.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the whole shape. Can be animated with `PolyPath`. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Scale of the whole shape, without changing the relative positions of its points. |
| X, Y, Z Rotation | `XRotation`, `YRotation`, `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Rotation of the whole shape about each axis. |
| Fill Method | `FillMethod` | Combo | 0: Alternate (1: Non-zero Winding) | How overlapping parts of the polyline are filled. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Combo | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | How corners are joined. Used when Solid is off. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (1–10) | Limit for miter joins. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Combo | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline. Used when Solid is off. |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Write-on, used when Solid is off: where the outline starts, and how much is drawn. Animate Length for a write-on. |
| Polyline | `Polyline` | B-spline polyline | none | The shape's B-Spline points, as offsets from `Center`. Set with `comp.BSplinePolyline()`. Already animated (see Tips). |
| Polyline 2 | `Polyline2` | B-spline polyline | none | The outer shape of a double polyline, which softens part of the edge. Not animated. |

Solid, Border Width and Paint Mode are the same as for every mask tool (see Common Controls → Mask tools).

### Example

A smooth blob from six points. The curve only passes near each point, so it is rounder and smaller than the hexagon
the points make.

```python
mask = comp.AddTool('BSplineMask')
pts = {1: {'X': 0, 'Y': 0.2}, 2: {'X': 0.2, 'Y': 0.1}, 3: {'X': 0.2, 'Y': -0.1},
       4: {'X': 0, 'Y': -0.2}, 5: {'X': -0.2, 'Y': -0.1}, 6: {'X': -0.2, 'Y': 0.1}}
mask.Polyline[0] = comp.BSplinePolyline(pts, True)    # True: closed
mask.SoftEdge = 0.02
```

### Tips

- `Polyline` only takes the objects `comp.BSplinePolyline()` makes: a plain dict, as used for the Polygon mask,
  leaves it empty. Reading it with `mask.GetInput('Polyline')` returns the same kind of object, and its `.Value` gives
  the points. See *Value types* in Conventions.
- `Polyline` is already animated, as on the Polygon mask: set shapes with `mask.Polyline[frame] = ...`. See *Animated
  polylines* in Conventions.
- A point's tension (hold W and drag in the viewer) can only be changed in the viewer.
- Convert a shape between Bézier and B-Spline in the viewer's right-click menu. It keeps the shape and roughly
  doubles the number of points.
- For several shapes in one node, use MultiPoly.

**See also:** Polygon Mask, MultiPoly, Ellipse Mask, Mask tools (Common Controls), sBSpline.

## Ellipse Mask (`EllipseMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** Elp · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask in the shape of an ellipse, which is a circle until Width and Height differ. Angle turns it, and
Solid off draws it as an outline. It is the usual mask for round things and for vignettes. Its shape is set
by the controls below, so it can be animated like any other input.

**Use for:** circular or elliptical reveals and vignettes, limiting an effect to a round area, and cutting
round holes in another mask with Paint Mode.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the ellipse. Can be animated with `PolyPath`. |
| Width | `Width` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–2) | Width of the ellipse. Drag its left or right edge in the viewer to change it. |
| Height | `Height` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–2) | Height of the ellipse. Dragging the diagonal handle changes both Width and Height. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Rotation of the ellipse. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline. Only used with Solid off. |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Write-on, used when Solid is off: where the outline starts, and how much is drawn. Animate Length for a write-on. |

### Example

A vignette: the image is darkened outside a soft-edged ellipse. The Merge's Foreground is black, and the mask's
Invert is on, so the black lands outside the ellipse and the picture stays inside it.

```python
black = comp.AddTool('Background')
black.TopLeftRed, black.TopLeftGreen, black.TopLeftBlue = 0, 0, 0

vignette = comp.AddTool('EllipseMask')
vignette.Width = 1.2
vignette.Height = 0.9
vignette.SoftEdge = 0.15
vignette.Invert = 1                    # the mask's outside is the area to darken

darken = comp.AddTool('Merge')
darken.Background = media_in.Output
darken.Foreground = black.Output
darken.EffectMask = vignette.Mask
```

To animate the vignette, keyframe Width and Height instead of setting them. This version opens the vignette from a
small circle to its full size over frames 0 to 48:

```python
vignette.Width = comp.BezierSpline()
vignette.Width[0] = 0.2
vignette.Width[48] = 1.2
vignette.Height = comp.BezierSpline()
vignette.Height[0] = 0.2
vignette.Height[48] = 1.2
```

### Tips

- Filter sets how Soft Edge is applied. The default, `"Fast Gaussian"`, is quicker; `"Gaussian"` gives a smoother
  falloff at a higher cost.
- A circle needs Width and Height equal. Set both to the same value.
- To cut a round hole in another mask, connect that mask to this ellipse's `EffectMask` and set this ellipse's
  `PaintMode` to `"Subtract"`. The ellipse is subtracted from the mask it's connected to. The Rectangle Mask
  example shows the same chain.
- The mask's own controls and the Image and Settings tab options are in Common Controls → Mask tools.

**See also:** Rectangle Mask, Polygon Mask, B-Spline Mask, Triangle Mask, Merge, Mask tools (Common Controls).

## Mask Paint (`PaintMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** PnM · **Inputs:** `Paint` (image), `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask by painting it directly in the viewer, with brush strokes, primitive shapes and polyline strokes. It is
the freehand option for fixing up a matte: holes can be painted in or out, with pressure-sensitive strokes and
softness set on the node. Each stroke is stored in the node and edited in the viewer and Keyframes Editor.

**Use for:** patching holes in a matte, painting in or out areas that the other masks can't reach, and freehand
masks from a drawing tablet.

**Scripting limit:** the stroke controls may not exist until a stroke type is chosen in the viewer toolbar. Strokes are low priority for scripting, so only the node's settings are covered here. See Tips.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paint | `Paint` | Image input | (none) | Image input of the paint node. |
| Paint Mode | `PaintMode` | ID combo | `"Merge"` | How the painted mask combines with the mask on its `EffectMask` input. See Common Controls → Mask tools. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (−0.2 to 0.2) | Grows or shrinks the painted areas. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | On: the painted areas are filled. Off: only their outlines are drawn. |

Level, Filter, Soft Edge, Invert and the rest are the same as for every mask tool (see Common Controls → Mask tools).

### Example

A Mask Paint that patches a hole in a matte. The matte is a Bitmap Mask of the image, and the Mask Paint is
connected to it with Paint Mode "Add", so strokes painted in the viewer add to the matte:

```python
matte = comp.AddTool('BitmapMask')
matte.Image = media_in.Output
matte.Channel = 'Luminance'

patch = comp.AddTool('PaintMask')
patch.EffectMask = matte.Mask
patch.PaintMode = 'Add'
patch.SoftEdge = 0.02
# Paint the patch strokes in the viewer, with the Mask Paint node selected.
```

### Tips

- **Strokes.** Strokes are drawn in the viewer and stored in the node. Their controls may not exist until a stroke
  type is chosen in the viewer toolbar, and strokes are low priority for scripting.
- Set the mask's own settings from script, such as `PaintMode`, `Level`, `SoftEdge` and `Invert`. Draw the strokes
  in the viewer.
- For a stroke-free mask made by script, use a Bitmap Mask on an image or a shape-based mask instead.


**See also:** Bitmap Mask, Polygon Mask, MultiPoly, Paint (tool), Mask tools (Common Controls).

## MultiPoly (`MultiPoly`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** MPly · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Holds several polygon and B-Spline shapes in one mask node, as a numbered list. Each layer has its own shape,
name, enable switch and mask settings, so one node can replace a chain of Polygon masks. Layers are added with the
Polygon and BSpline buttons, and each one is drawn and animated on its own. The layers are combined in list order.

**Use for:** rotoscoping several objects in one node, or building a matte from several shapes without chaining
separate nodes.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add Polygon | `AddPolygon` | Button | — | Adds a new Polygon layer at the end of the list. Layers are named by type and number, so the first one is "Polygon 1". |
| Add BSpline | `AddBSpline` | Button | — | Adds a new B-Spline layer. |
| Layer name | `PolyMaskName`*n* | Text | "Polygon 1" | Name of layer *n*. Set it to rename the layer. |
| Layer enabled | `PolyMaskEnabled`*n* | Checkbox | 1 | Turns layer *n* on or off in the mask. |
| Polygon Order | `PolyOrder` | ScriptVal | `{0: 1}` | The order the layers are combined in, as a dict of position (from 0) to layer number. See Tips. |

Each layer's own controls use its number as a prefix. For layer 2 they are `PolyMask2.Center`, `PolyMask2.Size`,
`PolyMask2.Angle`, `PolyMask2.PaintMode`, `PolyMask2.Solid`, `PolyMask2.Level`, `PolyMask2.SoftEdge`,
`PolyMask2.BorderWidth`, `PolyMask2.Invert`, `PolyMask2.WriteLength` and so on, with the same types and defaults as
the Polygon and B-Spline masks. `PolyMask2.Polyline` holds the layer's points: a Polyline on a Polygon layer, and a
B-spline polyline on a B-Spline layer (see *Value types* in Conventions). Layer 1's is already animated, as on the
Polygon mask; the layers that `AddPolygon` and `AddBSpline` add are not, until a `comp.BezierSpline()` is connected.

### Example

Two layers: a square, and a smaller square named "Face" that is cut out of it, with its size animated.

```python
mp = comp.AddTool('MultiPoly')
mp['PolyMask1.Polyline'][0] = {1: {'X': -0.2, 'Y': -0.2}, 2: {'X': 0.2, 'Y': -0.2},
                               3: {'X': 0.2, 'Y': 0.2}, 4: {'X': -0.2, 'Y': 0.2}, 'Closed': True}
mp.AddPolygon = 1                          # layer 2, named "Polygon 2"
mp['PolyMask2.Polyline'][0] = {1: {'X': -0.1, 'Y': -0.1}, 2: {'X': 0.1, 'Y': -0.1},
                               3: {'X': 0.1, 'Y': 0.1}, 4: {'X': -0.1, 'Y': 0.1}, 'Closed': True}
mp.PolyMaskName2 = 'Face'
mp['PolyMask2.PaintMode'] = 'Subtract'     # cut layer 2 out of the layers before it

mp['PolyMask2.Size'] = comp.BezierSpline()
mp['PolyMask2.Size'][0] = 1.0
mp['PolyMask2.Size'][24] = 1.5
```

### Tips

- Layers are combined in list order, and each layer's Paint Mode says how it combines with those above it. To change
  the order, set `PolyOrder` to a dict of position to layer number: `mp.PolyOrder = {0: 2, 1: 1}` combines layer 2
  first. A layer left out of the dict is not used, so list every layer.
- `PolyMask`*n*`.Delete` and `.Reset` are buttons in the Inspector and the layer list's right-click menu. Setting
  `Delete` to 1 from script did not remove the layer in testing, so delete layers in the UI.
- A new MultiPoly has Use Frame Format Settings off (0), so its size comes from its own Width and Height. Turn it on
  for the comp's frame size.
- A new MultiPoly already has one Polygon layer, layer 1. `AddPolygon` and `AddBSpline` add layers 2, 3 and so on.
- Set each layer's points as on the Polygon and B-Spline masks. A B-Spline layer only takes
  `comp.BSplinePolyline()` objects. See Polygon Mask and B-Spline Mask.

**See also:** Polygon Mask, B-Spline Mask, Mask tools (Common Controls).

## Polygon Mask (`PolylineMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** Ply · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask from a Bézier polyline: a closed shape of points, each with handles, drawn in the viewer. It is the
main rotoscoping tool, for objects without a regular shape. The polyline and its points can be drawn and edited in
the viewer, where the shape auto-animates as you change it, or set and keyframed from script. The mask can also be
moved, scaled and rotated as a whole.

**Use for:** rotoscoping and garbage mattes, and any solid or outlined shape that the primitive masks can't make.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the whole shape. Can be animated with `PolyPath`. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Scale of the whole shape, without changing the relative positions of its points. |
| X, Y, Z Rotation | `XRotation`, `YRotation`, `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Rotation of the whole shape about each axis. |
| Fill Method | `FillMethod` | Combo | 0: Alternate (1: Non-zero Winding) | How overlapping parts of the polyline are filled. If overlaps leave holes, try Non-zero Winding. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Combo | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | How corners are joined. Used when Solid is off. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (1–10) | Limit for miter joins. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Combo | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline. Used when Solid is off. |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Write-on, used when Solid is off: where the outline starts, and how much is drawn. Animate Length for a write-on. |
| Polyline | `Polyline` | Polyline | none | The shape's points, as offsets from `Center`. Already animated (see Tips). |
| Polyline 2 | `Polyline2` | Polyline | none | The outer shape of a double polyline, which softens part of the edge. Not animated. |

Solid, Border Width and Paint Mode are the same as for every mask tool (see Common Controls → Mask tools).

### Example

A closed diamond that grows over 24 frames. The points are offsets from `Center`, and with no handles the sides are
straight.

```python
mask = comp.AddTool('PolylineMask')
small = {1: {'X': 0, 'Y': 0.1}, 2: {'X': 0.1, 'Y': 0}, 3: {'X': 0, 'Y': -0.1}, 4: {'X': -0.1, 'Y': 0}, 'Closed': True}
big = {1: {'X': 0, 'Y': 0.3}, 2: {'X': 0.3, 'Y': 0}, 3: {'X': 0, 'Y': -0.3}, 4: {'X': -0.3, 'Y': 0}, 'Closed': True}
mask.Polyline[0] = small     # replaces the initial keyframe
mask.Polyline[24] = big
mask.SoftEdge = 0.01
```

### Tips

- A new Polygon mask has no points, and draws nothing until it has a shape. See *Value types* (Polyline) in
  Conventions for the format of the points.
- `Polyline` is already animated, with an initial keyframe at the frame the tool was added. Set shapes with
  `mask.Polyline[frame] = points`. A plain `mask.Polyline = points` replaces all the keyframes with one at the current
  frame. See *Animated polylines* in Conventions.
- The point modes (Click, Draw, Insert, Modify and so on) are only in the viewer.
- To cut the polygon out of another mask, connect that mask to this one's `EffectMask` and set this mask's
  `PaintMode` to `"Subtract"`. See Rectangle Mask.
- For several shapes in one node, use MultiPoly.

**See also:** B-Spline Mask, MultiPoly, Ellipse Mask, Rectangle Mask, Mask tools (Common Controls), sPolygon.

## Ranges Mask (`RangesMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** Rng · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange), `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a mask of the shadows, midtones or highlights of an image, measured on a chosen channel. The tonal ranges are
set with a four-point curve, the same kind used by the Color Corrector, so the mask can match how the grade splits
the image into ranges. The range edges can be changed in the viewer's Mini Spline Editor, or set with one of the two
presets.

**Use for:** grading only the highlights, shadows or midtones of an image, with a mask that follows the grade's own
ranges.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image | `Image` | Image input | (none) | The image the ranges are measured on. |
| Fit Input | `FitInput` | ID multi-button | `"Crop"` | How the image is fitted to the mask size: `"Crop"`, `"Stretch"`, `"Inside"`, `"Width"`, `"Height"` or `"Outside"`. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the image within the mask frame. |
| Range | `RangesRange` | Multi-button | 0: Shadows (1: Midtones, 2: Highlights) | The range that is output as the mask. White means the pixel is in the range. |
| Channel | `RangesChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Luminance (1: Red, 2: Green, 3: Blue, 4: Alpha) | The channel the ranges are measured on. |
| Color Ranges | `ColorRanges` | Spline | (four points and handles) | The range curves, edited in the Mini Spline Editor in the viewer. |
| Simple, Smooth | `PresetSimpleRanges`, `PresetSmoothRanges` | Button | — | Sets the range curves to a straight-line falloff (Simple) or a smoother one (Smooth). |

### Example

A grade that affects only the highlights. The mask follows the image's luminance, and the Color Corrector is
limited by it:

```python
highlights = comp.AddTool('RangesMask')
highlights.Image = media_in.Output
highlights.RangesRange = 2             # 2: Highlights
highlights.RangesChannel = 0           # 0: Luminance

grade = comp.AddTool('ColorCorrector')
grade.Input = media_in.Output
grade.EffectMask = highlights.Mask
```

### Tips

- Shadows, Midtones and Highlights are in the Range control. Midtones is everything between the shadow and
  highlight curves.
- The curves are edited in the viewer, and there's no script access to their points. Start from a preset, then adjust
  it in the viewer if needed.
- Mid-grey pixels are only partly in the range, so they get only part of the grade.

**See also:** Bitmap Mask, Wand Mask, Color Corrector, Mask tools (Common Controls).

## Rectangle Mask (`RectangleMask`)

**Category:** Mask · **Short name:** Rct · **Inputs:** `EffectMask` (blue) · **Output:** `Mask` (Mask)

Makes a rectangle, or a rounded rectangle with Corner Radius. Width and Height set its size independently, and
Angle rotates it. Solid off draws only the outline. Rectangles are the usual choice for hard-edged wipes and
for limiting an effect to a frame-shaped area.

**Use for:** rectangle-shaped wipes and reveals, framing a region for a grade or blur, and building holes or
combined shapes by chaining a rectangle with another mask through Paint Mode.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the rectangle. Can be animated with `PolyPath`. |
| Width | `Width` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–1) | Width of the rectangle. Drag its left or right edge in the viewer to change it. |
| Height | `Height` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–1) | Height of the rectangle. Drag its top or bottom edge in the viewer to change it. |
| Corner Radius | `CornerRadius` | Number | 0 (0–1) | 0 gives sharp corners. 1 applies the largest rounding. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Rotation of the rectangle. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 2: Miter (0: Bevel, 1: Round) | How the corners of an outline are joined. Used when Solid is off. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline. Used when Solid is off. |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Write-on, used when Solid is off: where the outline starts, and how much is drawn. Animate Length for a write-on. |

### Example

A wipe reveal. The title is shown through a rectangle whose left edge stays on the left of the frame and whose
right edge sweeps across over 36 frames. The rectangle drives the Effect Mask of a Merge:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('TextPlus')
title.StyledText = 'Revealed'

wipe = comp.AddTool('RectangleMask')
wipe.Height = 1.0
wipe.Width = comp.BezierSpline()
wipe.Width[0] = 0.0
wipe.Width[36] = 1.0
wipe.Center = comp.PolyPath()
wipe.Center[0] = [0.0, 0.5]           # Center moves by half the Width, so the left edge doesn't move
wipe.Center[36] = [0.5, 0.5]

reveal = comp.AddTool('Merge')
reveal.Background = media_in.Output
reveal.Foreground = title.Output
reveal.EffectMask = wipe.Mask
```

Chaining two masks. A rectangle with a round hole. The ellipse's `EffectMask` takes the rectangle, and the
ellipse's Paint Mode subtracts its own shape from that input:

```python
frame = comp.AddTool('RectangleMask')
frame.Width = 0.8
frame.Height = 0.6

hole = comp.AddTool('EllipseMask')
hole.Width = 0.3
hole.Height = 0.3
hole.EffectMask = frame.Mask
hole.PaintMode = 'Subtract'

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = title.Output
merge.EffectMask = hole.Mask
```

### Tips

- Corner Radius of 1 on a square gives a circle, and on a rectangle gives a pill shape.
