| Region Mode | `RegionMode` | ID combo | `"Ignore"` | Which particles are affected. See _CommonParticles → Region tab. |
| Region | `Region` | ID combo | `"AllRgn"` | The shape used with Region Mode. |

### Example

An attractor near the centre of the frame:

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')
emit.Region = 'RectRgn'
emit['RectRgn.Width'] = 0.9

pull = comp.AddTool('pPointForce')
pull.Input = emit.Output
pull.Strength = 0.2
pull['Translate.X'] = 0.1             # offset from the centre of the frame
pull['Translate.Y'] = 0.0
```

### Tips

- Test Power with a preview of the particles, since its falloff isn't verified with a render.
- Animate Translate with a PolyPath or BezierSpline to move the attractor.

**See also:** pVortex, pDirectionalForce, pGradientForce, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## pRender (`pRender`)

**Category:** Particles · **Short name:** pRn · **Inputs:** `Input` (Particles), `Camera` (DataType3D, optional), `EffectMask` (Mask) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D in ThreeD mode, Image in TwoD mode)

Ends every particle branch. It turns the particle system into either an image (TwoD) or 3D geometry (ThreeD), which must
then go through a Renderer 3D to become an image. Nothing downstream of pEmitter and the forces shows until a pRender is
placed at the end. Its pre-roll controls let the system build up its particles before the frame you are viewing.

**Use for:** the last step of every particle system. TwoD gives a flat image for a Merge; ThreeD lets the particles sit
inside a 3D scene with lights and a camera.

**Choosing the output.** OutputMode (`OutputMode`, ID combo) sets the type:

- `"ThreeD"` (the default) gives `DataType3D`. Connect it to a Renderer 3D's `SceneInput` (the Renderer 3D then makes the
  image), or to a Merge 3D's `SceneInput1`.
- `"TwoD"` gives an `Image`. Connect it straight to a Merge's Foreground, as in the example.

In the Inspector both modes show the same controls, so the 2D and 3D settings can't be told apart by the API. Set the mode
before you connect the output, so the connection has the type you want.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output Mode | `OutputMode` | ID combo | `"ThreeD"` | `"ThreeD"` (3D geometry) or `"TwoD"` (an image). See above. |
| Global In, Global Out | `GlobalIn`, `GlobalOut` | Number | 0, 1000 | The frame range the system renders. |
| Process Mode | `ProcessMode` | ID combo | `"FullFrames"` | `"FullFrames"`, `"NTSC"`, `"PAL"`, `"PALReversed"` or `"NTSCReversed"`: field-based output modes for interlaced video. Not verified beyond the list. |
| Restart | `Restart` | Button | | Clears the particle system so it starts again from the first frame. |
| Pre-Roll | `PreRoll` | Button | | Runs the particle system forward from the first frame up to the current one, so it's populated at that frame. |
| Automatic Pre-Roll | `AutomaticPreRoll` | Checkbox | 1 | Pre-rolls the system automatically when needed. |
| Sub-frame Accuracy | `SubFrameCalculationAccuracy` | Number | 1 (1–10) | Calculated sub-steps per frame. Higher values are more accurate and slower. |
| Pre-Generate Frames | `PreGenerateFrames` | Number | 0 (0–100) | Frames calculated before the first frame, so particles already exist when the shot starts. |
| Integration Method | `NewIntegrationMethod` | ID combo | `"Euler"` | `"Euler"` or `"RK4"` (Runge-Kutta, a more accurate method). |
| Kill Particles That Leave the View | `KillParticlesThatLeaveTheView` | Checkbox | 0 | Removes particles once they move outside the frame, to save work. |
| Depth Merge Particles | `DepthMergeParticles` | Checkbox | 0 | Merges particles by depth rather than by layer order, in 2D. |
| Generate Z Buffer | `GenerateZBuffer` | Checkbox | 0 | Generates a Z buffer for the 2D image. Not verified. |
| Enable PBR Material | `EnablePBRMaterial` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns on PBR material for the particles. Only the name is documented; its effect is not verified. |
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 1920, 1080 | Output size when Auto Resolution is off. |
| Auto Resolution | `UseFrameFormatSettings` | Checkbox | 1 | Uses the comp's frame format for size and pixel aspect. |
| Depth | `Depth` | Multi-button | 0: Default, 1: int8, 2: int16, 3: float16, 4: float32 | Bit depth of the output. |
| Blur, Glow, Blur Blend [2D] | `Blur`, `Glow`, `BlurBlend` | Number | 0, 0, 1 | Blur and glow of the whole 2D particle image. |
| Camera | `Camera` | DataType3D input | | An optional camera (or 3D scene with a camera) that frames the particles in ThreeD mode. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask input | | Limits the particles to a mask. Takes effect in TwoD mode. |

Scene and Grid controls (Zoom, Perspective, Z Clip, Focal Length (35mm motion picture), Show Grid and its settings) are
shown in both modes. Their use in TwoD mode is not verified.

### Example

A 3D particle system through a Renderer 3D, verified as a connection chain (values and connections only):

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')

render = comp.AddTool('pRender')
render.Input = emit.Output
render.OutputMode = 'ThreeD'

scene = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
scene.SceneInput = render.Output        # the 3D particles become an image here
```

### Tips

- For a 2D chain, set `OutputMode` to `"TwoD"` before connecting, and connect `Output` to a Merge's Foreground.
- Pre-roll matters for forces that depend on a particle's previous position (Turbulence, Vortex). Use Automatic Pre-Roll,
  or Pre-Generate Frames for a system that must already be populated at the start of the shot.
- Raise Sub-frame Accuracy only if particles look pulsed: it multiplies the work.
- Every particle branch must end with a pRender. A pEmitter alone doesn't show anything.

**See also:** pEmitter, Renderer 3D, Merge 3D, Merge, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## pSpawn (`pSpawn`)

**Category:** Particles · **Short name:** pSp · **Inputs:** `Input` (Particles) · **Output:** `Output` (Particles)

Makes each affected particle create new particles of its own. The original particle keeps going until its lifespan ends, and each particle it creates is independent. Most controls match pEmitter, so a spawned particle can have its own number, lifespan, velocity, style and sets. Use Conditions (Start Age, End Age) to choose when a particle spawns, for example only near the end of its life.

**Use for:** fireworks (a rising spark that bursts at the top of its life), trails of sparks, branching and cascading effects.

**Typical chain:** pEmitter → pSpawn → pRender. Restrict pSpawn with Start Age and End Age, Probability or Sets; otherwise it runs for every particle on every frame.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number, Number Variance | `Number`, `NumberVariance` | Number | 10 (0–100), 0 | Particles each affected particle creates on each frame. |
| Lifespan, Lifespan Variance | `Lifespan`, `LifespanVariance` | Number | 100 (0–1000), 0 | Lifespan of the new particles. |
| Position Variance | `PositionVariance` | Number | 0 (0–0.1) | Random offset of the new particles from their parent. |
| Color | `Color` | Combo | 0: Use Style Color, 1: Use Color from parent Particle | Colour of new particles: from this node's Style, or from their parent. |
| Temporal Distribution | `TemporalDistribution` | Combo | 0: All at same time, 1: Randomly distributed, 2: Equally distributed | When in the frame the new particles are born. |
| Affect spawned particles | `AffectSpawnedParticles` | Checkbox | 0 | Lets new particles spawn too, on later frames. Can multiply the particle count very quickly. |
| Velocity Transfer | `VelocityTransfer` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Share of the parent's velocity the new particle takes. 1 is all of it. |
| Velocity, Velocity Variance | `Velocity`, `VelocityVariance` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Extra speed given to new particles. |
| Angle, Angle Z | `Angle`, `AngleZ` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Direction of the new particles' motion. |
| Rotation and Spin | `RotationX` … `SpinZVariance` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Starting rotation and per-frame spin of the new particles. |
| Set 1–32 | `NewSet1` … `NewSet32` | Checkbox | 0 | Sets assigned to the new particles. |
| Style | `Style` | ID combo | `"ParticleStylePoint"` | How new particles are drawn. See _CommonParticles → Style tab. |
| Region | `Region` | ID combo | `"AllRgn"` | Shape used with Region Mode. See _CommonParticles → Region tab. |

The Conditions tab (Start Age, End Age, Probability, Set Mode) decides which parent particles spawn.

### Example

Sparks that spawn only in the last 20 per cent of each particle's life:

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')
emit.Number = 5
emit.Lifespan = 60
emit.Velocity = 0.3

burst = comp.AddTool('pSpawn')
burst.Input = emit.Output
burst.StartAge = 0.8                    # from 80 per cent of life
burst.EndAge = 1.0
burst.Number = 20
burst.Lifespan = 15
burst.Velocity = 0.1
burst.Style = 'ParticleStyleLine'

render = comp.AddTool('pRender')
render.Input = burst.Output
render.OutputMode = 'TwoD'
```

### Tips

- Leave Affect spawned particles off unless you need spawns of spawns: it grows the count quickly.
- Velocity Transfer at 0 means each new particle starts still, so gravity alone moves it.
- Set the timing with Start Age and End Age, not with Probability, so that the burst happens at the same point of every particle's life.

**See also:** pEmitter, pKill, pDirectionalForce, pRender, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## pTangentForce (`pTangentForce`)

**Category:** Particles · **Short name:** pTF · **Inputs:** `Input` (Particles) · **Output:** `Output` (Particles)

Pushes particles sideways, perpendicular to the line from the force's centre to each particle, so they circulate around the centre. The centre is set by the Translate offsets. X, Y and Z Strength set the push on each axis.

**Use for:** particles orbiting a point, a rotating ring of sparks, or a sideways drift around a logo.

**Typical chain:** pEmitter → pTangentForce → pRender.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Strength, Y Strength, Z Strength | `XStrength`, `YStrength`, `ZStrength` | Number | 0, 0, 0.1 (−1 to 1) | Tangential push on each axis. |
| Translate X, Y, Z | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y`, `Translate.Z` | Number | 0 | Position of the centre of the force. |
| Region Mode | `RegionMode` | ID combo | `"Ignore"` | Which particles are affected. See _CommonParticles → Region tab. |
| Region | `Region` | ID combo | `"AllRgn"` | The shape used with Region Mode. |

### Example

A sideways push around the centre of the frame:

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')
emit.Number = 20

orbit = comp.AddTool('pTangentForce')
orbit.Input = emit.Output
orbit.ZStrength = 0
orbit.YStrength = 0.1
```

### Tips

- Negative strengths reverse the direction of the push.
- Set the centre with Translate, not with the Region, which only limits where the force is applied.

**See also:** pVortex, pPointForce, pDirectionalForce, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## pTurbulence (`pTurbulence`)

**Category:** Particles · **Short name:** pTr · **Inputs:** `Input` (Particles) · **Output:** `Output` (Particles)

Pushes particles in random, chaotic directions, so that they drift, swirl and flicker as they move. Each axis has its own strength, and Strength Over Life sets how the turbulence changes with the particle's age. Density sets how the random field is spread across the particles: low values move groups of particles together, and high values make each particle move differently.

**Use for:** smoke, fire, dust, fog and any natural, unsteady motion. It works well with a Strength Over Life curve that ramps up as a particle ages.

**Typical chain:** pEmitter → pTurbulence → pRender.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strength X, Y, Z | `XStrength`, `YStrength`, `ZStrength` | Number | 0.1 (0–1) | Amount of chaotic motion along each axis. |
| Strength Over Life | `StrengthOverLifeLUT` | LookUpTable | none | The curve (in the Inspector's Strength Over Life group): the turbulence multiplier across a particle's life. |
| Density | `Density` | Number | 10 (0–100) | Spread of the turbulence field. Low values move groups of particles together; high values make finer, more individual variations. |
| Region Mode | `RegionMode` | ID combo | `"Ignore"` | Limits the turbulence to particles in or out of the Region. See _CommonParticles → Region tab. |
| Region | `Region` | ID combo | `"AllRgn"` | The shape used with Region Mode. |

### Example

Gentle turbulence along X and Y for a rising smoke effect (set Strength Over Life in the Inspector):

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')
emit.Lifespan = 120

turb = comp.AddTool('pTurbulence')
turb.Input = emit.Output
turb.XStrength = 0.05
turb.YStrength = 0.05
```

### Tips

- Use Strength Over Life for motion that changes with age, such as turbulence that grows as a fire particle ages. Its curve is set in the Inspector.
- Use Density below 10 for a turbulence that moves whole clouds; above 50 for scattered, individual jitter.
- Random behaviour follows the Random Seed in Common Controls: change it for a different pattern.

**See also:** pDirectionalForce, pVortex, pFlock, pRender, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## pVortex (`pVortex`)

**Category:** Particles · **Short name:** pVt · **Inputs:** `Input` (Particles) · **Output:** `Output` (Particles)

Applies a rotational force around a centre, drawing particles in and spinning them around it. Strength sets how strongly they are pulled, Power sets how the force changes with distance, and Size sets the reach. The Translate offsets place the centre, and Angle X and Y tilt the plane of rotation.

**Use for:** swirls, whirlpools, tornadoes and smoke or sparks drawn into a spiral.

**Typical chain:** pEmitter → pVortex → pRender.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strength | `Strength` | Number | 1 (−5 to 5) | Amount of rotational force. Negative values reverse the spin. |
| Power | `Power` | Number | 2 (−1 to 10) | How the force changes with distance from the centre. |
| Translate X, Y, Z | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y`, `Translate.Z` | Number | 0 | Position of the vortex centre. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 0.5 (0–1.5) | Reach of the vortex. |
| Angle X, Angle Y | `AngleX`, `AngleY` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Tilts the plane of rotation. |
| Region Mode | `RegionMode` | ID combo | `"Ignore"` | Which particles are affected. See _CommonParticles → Region tab. |
| Region | `Region` | ID combo | `"AllRgn"` | The shape used with Region Mode. |

### Example

A swirl that draws in particles from a spray near the centre of the frame:

```python
emit = comp.AddTool('pEmitter')
emit.Velocity = 0.1

swirl = comp.AddTool('pVortex')
swirl.Input = emit.Output
swirl.Strength = 2
swirl.Size = 0.4
```

### Tips

- Use a negative Strength for the opposite spin.
- Animate Translate to move the centre of the swirl across the frame.

**See also:** pPointForce, pTurbulence, pDirectionalForce, Common Controls → Particle tools.

## Volume Fog (`VolumeFog`)

**Category:** Position · **Short name:** VlF · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange, an image with a World Position pass), `FogImage` (green, optional fog texture), `SceneInput` (magenta, a 3D camera or scene), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Adds volumetric fog to a 2D image, using the world position of each pixel. The image needs a World Position pass (XYZ in its colour channels, as a 32-bit float render or an EXR). The fog is confined to a volume (a sphere or a cube, which you place with its Translation, Rotation and Scale) and can be textured with a Fog image, lit by lights in the 3D scene, and given a noise pattern. Because it works on the 2D image, it updates quickly as you set it up. It is a post effect on the image, not a 3D render.

**Use for:** fog, haze or glow inside a region of a 3D render or a real scene, where the fog must sit in a defined place in space rather than a depth range.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `Shape` | ID multi-button | `"Cube"` | `"Cube"` or `"Sphere"`. |
| X, Y, Z Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y`, `Translate.Z` | Number | 0 (0 to 10) | Position of the volume's centre. |
| X, Y, Z Rotation | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (0 to 360) | Rotation of the volume about its centre, in degrees. Rotation order is `Rotate.RotOrder` (default `"XYZ"`). |
| Lock X/Y/Z, Scale | `ScaleLock`, `Scale.X`, `Scale.Y`, `Scale.Z` | Checkbox, Number | 1, 1 (0 to 5) | Scales the volume. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (0 to 10) | Overall size of the volume. |
| Soft Edge | `SoftEdge` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | How far the fog fades towards the volume's edge. |
| Samples | `Samples` | Number | 16 (1 to 64) | Samples per ray through the volume. More is more detailed and slower. |
| Adaptive Sample | `AdaptiveSample` | Checkbox | 0 | Adjusts how the layers of the volume are blended. |
| Dither | `Dither` | Checkbox | 1 | Adds noise that hides the steps between layers. |
| Z Slices | `ZSlices` | Number | 1 (0 to 16) | How many frames of the Fog image sequence form the volume's depth. |
| First Slice Time | `FirstSliceTime` | Number | 0 (0 to 100) | The frame of the global range that gives the first slice. |
| Color Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Color.Red`, `Color.Green`, `Color.Blue`, `Color.Alpha` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Fog colour, multiplied over any colour from the Fog image. |
| Gain | `Gain` | Number | 1 (0 to 5) | Intensity of the fog. |
| Subtractive/Additive | `SubtractiveAdditive` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Composites the fog additively (1) or subtractively (0), as a Merge does. |
| Fog Only | `FogOnly` | Checkbox | 0 | Outputs the fog on black, to composite or to use as a mask. |
| Detail | `Detail` | Number | 0 (0 to 10) | Adds layers of finer noise to the fog. |
| Noise Gain | `NoiseGain` | Number | 10 (0 to 5) | Brightens the brightest parts of the noise. |
| Noise Brightness | `NoiseBrightness` | Number | 0.25 (-2 to 2) | Overall brightness of the noise, before colour mapping. |
| Seethe | `Seethe` | Number | 0 (0 to 10) | Blends the noise to a different noise pattern, so it drifts. Animate it for motion. |
| Discontinuous | `Discontinuous` | Checkbox | 0 | Hard edges along some noise contours. |
| Inverted | `Inverted` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the noise. Most effective with Discontinuous. |
| Camera | `Camera` | ID combo | `"Default"` | The camera to use, when the Scene input has more than one. |
| X, Y, Z Position | `CameraPos.X`, `CameraPos.Y`, `CameraPos.Z` | Number | 0 (0 to 10) | Camera position when no camera is connected. |
| Do Lighting | `DoLighting` | Checkbox | 0 | Lights the volume from the scene's lights. Needs lights in the Scene input. |
| Do In-Scattering | `DoInScattering` | Checkbox | 1 | Scatters light within the volume. Used when Do Lighting is on. |
| Light Samples | `LightSamples` | Number | 16 (1 to 32) | Accuracy of the lighting. More is slower. |
| Density | `Density` | Number | 1 (0 to 10) | How thick the fog looks to the light. |
| Scattering | `Scattering` | Number | 1 (0 to 10) | How much light is scattered out of the fog. |
| Scattering Red | `ScatteringRed` (and Green, Blue) | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Colour of the scattered light. |
| Asymmetry | `Asymmetry` | Number | 0 (-0.5 to 0.5) | Direction of scattering: positive forward, negative backward, 0 even. |
| Transmission | `Transmission` | Number | 1 (0 to 2) | The colour of light that passes through the fog. Also has Red, Green and Blue. |
| Reflection | `Reflection` | Number | 1 (0 to 10) | Intensity of the light scattered out, before Emission is added. Also has Red, Green and Blue. |
| Emission | `Emission` | Number | 0 (0 to 2) | Adds glow to the fog. Also has Red, Green and Blue. |

The Settings tab is described in Common Controls. The Fog image (`FogImage`) is the green input. The Image input is the orange one. The Scene input (`SceneInput`) takes a 3D camera or a 3D scene that contains one.

In the tests, the lighting controls stayed visible whether Do Lighting was on or off.

### Example

A spherical volume of fog over a render with a World Position pass, textured with a noise image and placed by a camera:

```python
pass_image = comp.AddTool('Background')  # stands in for an image with a World Position pass (32-bit float)
noise = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')        # the fog texture, on the green FogImage input
cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')           # the camera that rendered the pass

fog = comp.AddTool('VolumeFog')
fog.Image = pass_image.Output
fog.FogImage = noise.Output
fog.SceneInput = cam.Output
fog.Shape = 'Sphere'
fog.Size = 1.5
fog.SoftEdge = 0.2
fog.Samples = 32
fog.Gain = 1.2
```

### Tips

- The fog stays where the volume is, so a volume that doesn't cover the parts of the scene you want leaves them clear. Use the sphere and its Soft Edge to shape it, and Size to cover the area.
- Use Fog Only to get the fog on black, and use it as a mask on a Color Corrector or a Merge.
- Turn on Do Lighting only when the Scene input has lights. It is slow on the CPU.
- With Z Slices above 1, make sure Global In and Global Out, and the range of the Fog image source, all fall within First Slice Time plus Z Slices (the manual's rule).

**See also:** Volume Mask, Z to WorldPos, Fog, Fog 3D, Fast Noise, Camera 3D.

## Volume Mask (`VolumeMask`)

**Category:** Position · **Short name:** VlM · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange, an image with a World Position pass), `MaskImage` (green, optional), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Makes a mask from the world position of each pixel. A sphere or a cube is placed in 3D space, and every pixel inside it is selected, so that a colour correction or other effect can be limited to objects in a particular place in the scene, without tracking or rotoscoping. The image needs a World Position pass. Mask Only outputs the mask itself, on black.

**Use for:** isolating an object by its position in a 3D render, to colour-correct or relight it.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `Shape` | ID multi-button | `"Cube"` | `"Cube"` or `"Sphere"`. The manual says rectangular; the live control is named Cube. |
| X, Y, Z Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y`, `Translate.Z` | Number | 0 (0 to 10) | Position of the volume's centre. |
| X, Y, Z Rotation | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (0 to 360) | Rotation of the volume about its centre. |
| Lock X/Y/Z, Scale | `ScaleLock`, `Scale.X`, `Scale.Y`, `Scale.Z` | Checkbox, Number | 1, 1 (0 to 5) | Scales the volume. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (0 to 10) | Overall size of the volume. |
| Soft Edge | `SoftEdge` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | How far the mask fades towards the edge of the volume. |
| Z Slices | `ZSlices` | Number | 1 (0 to 16) | How many frames of the Mask image sequence form the volume's depth. |
| First Slice Time | `FirstSliceTime` | Number | 0 (0 to 100) | The frame that gives the first slice. |
| Color Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Color.Red`, `Color.Green`, `Color.Blue`, `Color.Alpha` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Colour of the mask, added to any colour from the Mask image. |
| Subtractive/Additive | `SubtractiveAdditive` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Composites the mask additively or subtractively, as Merge does. |
| Mask Only | `MaskOnly` | Checkbox | 0 | Outputs the mask on black, to use on a Color Corrector or another tool. |
| Mask Image | `MaskImage` | Image input | | Optional image that refines the mask. |

The manual describes a Camera tab, with a Scene input for a camera or scene, a Camera selector and Translation controls. Those controls are not on this tool in the live dump, so the tool can't take a camera. The volume is placed with Translate and Rotate instead.

### Example

A spherical mask over an object in a 3D render, used to colour-correct only that object:

```python
pass_image = comp.AddTool('Background')  # stands in for an image with a World Position pass
mask = comp.AddTool('VolumeMask')
mask.Image = pass_image.Output
mask.Shape = 'Sphere'
mask['Translate.X'] = 2.0                # move the sphere to the object
mask.Size = 0.8
mask.SoftEdge = 0.3

grade = comp.AddTool('ColorCorrector')   # the correction that the mask limits
grade.Input = pass_image.Output
grade.EffectMask = mask.Output
```

### Tips

- Use Mask Only to see the mask, and check that the volume is where the object is, before using it as an effect mask.
- Use Soft Edge to avoid a hard boundary in the correction.
- The world position must be in World space for the volume to line up with the scene. The manual notes the pass should be 32-bit float.

**See also:** Volume Fog, Z to WorldPos, Color Corrector, Common Controls → Effect masks.

## Z to WorldPos (`ZtoWorldPos`)

**Category:** Position · **Short name:** Z2W · **Inputs:** `Image` (orange), `SceneInput` (magenta, a 3D camera or scene), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Image` (Image)

Converts between a Z (depth) channel and a World Position pass, using a 3D camera. Mode decides the direction. The default, ZtoWorldPos, reads the Z channel and the camera, and produces the XYZ world position of each pixel, as a World Position pass. The other mode, WorldPostoZ, does the reverse: it reads a World Position pass and the camera, and writes a Z channel. Use it when a renderer or tracker supplies one of the two passes but the Volume tools need the other. The output has the same ID as the input, `Image`, so connect the tool itself to a downstream input.

**Use for:** making a World Position pass from a Z pass, for Volume Mask and Volume Fog, or from tracking data that gives a per-pixel depth with a camera.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image | `Image` | Image input | | The Z-depth image (for ZtoWorldPos) or the World Position pass (for WorldPostoZ). |
| 3D Camera | `SceneInput` | 3D input | | A camera that matches the image, or a scene containing one. |
| Mode | `Mode` | ID multi-button | `"ZtoWorldPos"` | `"ZtoWorldPos"` makes a world position pass from Z. `"WorldPostoZ"` makes a Z channel from a world position pass. |
| Camera | `CameraSelector` | ID combo | `"Default"` | Which camera to use, when the scene has more than one. |

The Settings tab is described in Common Controls, and Effect Mask limits where the World Position pass is written.

The quality of the result depends on the quality of the incoming Z channel. The manual says a World Position pass should be rendered in 32-bit float, because the values are positions in 3D space and need the precision.

### Example

Making a World Position pass from a Z-depth pass and the camera that rendered it, then masking an object with Volume Mask:

```python
z_pass = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for an image with a Z channel (32-bit float)
cam = comp.AddTool('Camera3D')           # the camera that matches the pass

world = comp.AddTool('ZtoWorldPos')
world.Image = z_pass.Output
world.SceneInput = cam.Output
world.Mode = 'ZtoWorldPos'               # the default: Z to world position

mask = comp.AddTool('VolumeMask')
mask.Image = world                       # the tool's own output: its Image output has the same ID as the input
mask.Shape = 'Cube'
mask.Size = 1.0
```

### Tips

- Connect the Z-to-WorldPos result with the tool itself (`mask.Image = world`), not with a named output, because the output and the Image input both use the ID `Image`.
- The manual says the camera is vital to this tool. Connect the camera that matches the pass, or the positions will not line up with the scene.
- Set Mode to WorldPostoZ to get a Z channel back, for Depth Blur or Fog, from a world position pass.

**See also:** Volume Mask, Volume Fog, Depth Blur, Fog, Channel Booleans, Camera 3D.

## sBoolean (`sBoolean`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sBol · **Inputs:** `Input1` (base shape, ShapeTree), `Input2` (second shape, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Combines two shapes with a boolean operation: intersection, union, subtraction or XOR. Which shape is on which input matters only for subtraction, where `Input1` is the shape that is cut and `Input2` is the cutter. Like all shape nodes, its result is only visible through **sRender**.

**Use for:** cut-outs and knockouts (a ring, a crescent, a window shape), keeping only the overlap of two shapes, and quickly building a single shape from two primitives so it can then be duplicated or animated as one.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | `Operation` | ID combo | `"Intersection"` | `"Intersection"` keeps only where both shapes overlap. `"Union"` keeps wherever either shape is. `"Subtract"` cuts `Input2` out of `Input1`. `"Xor"` keeps the parts where only one shape is. |
| Style Mode | `StyleMode` | ID combo | `"Replace"` | `"Replace"` gives everything the Style settings of sBoolean itself. `"Keep"` preserves the incoming colours of the two shapes. |
| Input1 | `Input1` | ShapeTree | none | The base shape. In a subtraction, this is the shape that gets cut. |
| Input2 | `Input2` | ShapeTree | none | The second shape. In a subtraction, this is the cutter. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. Applies in Replace mode. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. On sBoolean this setting applies to the result; the inputs' own settings are ignored. |

### Example

A crescent made by cutting a slightly offset circle out of a larger one:

```python
disc = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
disc.Width = 0.5
disc.Height = 0.5

hole = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
hole.Width = 0.42
hole.Height = 0.42
hole['Translate.X'] = 0.08                # shift the cutter to the right

cut = comp.AddTool('sBoolean')
cut.Operation = 'Subtract'
cut.Input1 = disc.Output                  # the shape that is cut
cut.Input2 = hole.Output                  # the cutter

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = cut.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

To animate the cut, keyframe the cutter's offset: `hole['Translate.X'] = comp.BezierSpline()`, then set `hole['Translate.X'][frame] = value` for each key. Moving the cutter changes the thickness of the crescent.

### Tips

- Subtraction is the only operation where the input order matters. For the other three, connect the shapes in either order.
- Keep `StyleMode` at Replace for a single colour across the result. Use Keep to preserve the two shapes' own colours, for example when each one is differently coloured in its own sEllipse or sStar.
- The base and the cutter are both shapes, so either can be animated or duplicated first, for example with sJitter or sDuplicate.

**See also:** sMerge, sEllipse, sRectangle, sStar, sRender, sChangeStyle, sTransform.

## sBSpline (`sBSpline`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sBSp · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

A freely drawn shape or open line like sPolygon, but smoothed with B-splines instead of Bézier curves. Each point only pulls the curve towards it, so a smooth shape needs far fewer points than with sPolygon. The points are stored in the `Polyline` control, and can be drawn in the viewer or set from script with `comp.BSplinePolyline()`. The style, position, size, rotation and write-on can be set and animated from script. It outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen.

**Use for:** organic curves and blobs, smooth swooshes and ribbons, hand-drawn lettering strokes, and smooth outlines that you don't want to place point by point.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Polyline | `Polyline` | B-spline polyline | none | The B-spline's points, as offsets from the frame centre (moved by Offset). Set with `comp.BSplinePolyline()`. Already animated (see Tips). |
| Offset | `Center` | Point | (0, 0) | Moves the whole shape, as an offset from the frame centre, relative to image width. Animate with `comp.PolyPath()`. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Scales the whole shape without changing the points or the animation. |
| Z Rotation | `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the shape's centre. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | How the corners of the path are joined. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (slider 1–10) | Limits how far a Miter join can extend beyond the corner. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square) | Ends of an open line (Length below 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: where the line starts, and how much is drawn. Animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1 to write the line on. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A smooth wave, as an open line through five points, made with `comp.BSplinePolyline()`.

```python
wave = comp.AddTool('sBSpline')
pts = {1: {'X': -0.4, 'Y': 0}, 2: {'X': -0.2, 'Y': 0.15}, 3: {'X': 0, 'Y': 0},
       4: {'X': 0.2, 'Y': -0.15}, 5: {'X': 0.4, 'Y': 0}}
wave.Polyline[0] = comp.BSplinePolyline(pts)   # open; add True for a closed shape
wave.Solid = 0
wave.BorderWidth = 0.006

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = wave.Output
```

### Tips

- The drawing tools are the same as sPolygon's: the shape toolbar in the viewer offers Click, Draw, Insert and Modify, Done, and Smooth or Linear for each point.
- Because each point only influences the curve, use fewer points for a smooth result. A B-spline can't be made to pass exactly through a point, so use sPolygon if the path must hit specific positions.
- `WritePosition` and `WriteLength` only have an effect when `Solid` is off.
- `Polyline` only takes the objects `comp.BSplinePolyline()` makes: a plain dict, as used for sPolygon, leaves it empty. `wave.GetInput('Polyline')` returns the same kind of object, and its `.Value` gives the points. Like sPolygon's, the input is already animated: set shapes with `wave.Polyline[frame] = ...` (see *Animated polylines* in Conventions).

**See also:** sPolygon, sRectangle, sEllipse, sRender, sDuplicate, sOutline.

## sChangeStyle (`sChangeStyle`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sCs · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Gives the whole shape tree passing through it a new colour and opacity. It replaces the style set on the shapes
upstream, including their colour, alpha and Allow Combining settings. Put it where you want the style to change, and
connect its output onward to the rest of the shape chain or to **sRender**.

**Use for:** recolouring a shape chain in one place, rather than editing each generator, and setting a single colour
on a compound or duplicated array.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha | `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 (0–1) | Colour of the shape. Each is set with the Style tab colour controls. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Opacity of the shape. Shown on the Style tab; not in the manual. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | On keeps the alpha value even where copies overlap. Off lets the alpha build up where shapes overlap. |

### Example

Duplicates of an ellipse recoloured to orange in one place, with the overlap alpha kept:

```python
dot = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
dot.Width = 0.08
dot.Height = 0.08

copies = comp.AddTool('sDuplicate')
copies.Input = dot.Output
copies.Copies = 4
copies.XOffset = 0.1

restyle = comp.AddTool('sChangeStyle')
restyle.Input = copies.Output
restyle.Red = 1
restyle.Green = 0.6
restyle.Blue = 0.1
restyle.Alpha = 1
restyle.AllowCombining = 1

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = restyle.Output
```

### Tips

- Animate the colour with `comp.BezierSpline()` on `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` or `Alpha` to fade a shape to another colour.
- The colour applies to the whole upstream chain, so one sChangeStyle is enough to recolour an entire sDuplicate or
  sGrid array.
- Use Opacity to fade the shapes together. Alpha changes the colour's alpha, while Opacity is the Style tab's
  overall opacity.

**See also:** sDuplicate, sGrid, sEllipse, sRectangle, sRender, Merge.

## sDuplicate (`sDuplicate`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sDup · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Makes copies of the incoming shape tree. Each copy is offset from the one before it by the X and Y offset, scaled by
the X and Y size, and turned by the Z rotation. The Axis Mode sets the pivot used for rotation. The Jitter tab then
randomises the position, rotation, size and colour of the copies. Like all shape nodes, it only shows through
**sRender**.

**Use for:** rings and fans of shapes, trails and echoes, repeated patterns with a scatter, and stacks of copies that
show successive frames of an animated source.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Copies | `Copies` | Number (integer) | 0 (slider 0–10; typed up to 1,000,000) | Number of copies. The original is not counted, so 5 gives six shapes. |
| Copy Probability | `CopyProbability` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Chance that each copy is drawn. 1 draws all of them. |
| Time Offset | `TimeOffset` | Number | 0 (−5 to 5) | Shifts any animation of the source shape by this many frames per copy. −1 makes each copy show a frame earlier than the last. |
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset`, `YOffset` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Distance between successive copies, relative to frame width. 0.5 in X moves each copy half the frame width to the right. |
| Z Offset [3D] | `ZOffset` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Depth step between copies. Labelled [3D]. |
| X Size, Y Size | `XSize`, `YSize` | Number | 1, 1 (0–5) | Scale of each copy relative to the previous one. 1 keeps the size; 0.5 halves it at each step. |
| Axis Mode | `AxisMode` | ID combo | `"OriginRelative"` | `"Absolute"`: every copy turns about the image centre. `"OriginAbsolute"` (Origin Absolute): each copy turns about the original shape's own origin, at its duplicated position. `"OriginRelative"`: each copy turns about its own centre. `"Progressive"`: each copy accumulates the rotation, position and so on of the copies before it. |
| X Pivot, Y Pivot | `XPivot`, `YPivot` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Pivot for `"Absolute"` mode only. Hidden in the other modes. |
| X Rotation [3D], Y Rotation [3D] | `XRotation`, `YRotation` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180) | Turn of each copy about the X or Y axis. Labelled [3D]. |
| Z Rotation | `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180) | Turn added at each copy. Each copy turns further than the one before, so copy *n* is turned *n* times this value. |
| Red, Green, Blue, Alpha, Opacity Gain | `RedGain`, `GreenGain`, `BlueGain`, `AlphaGain`, `OpacityGain` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Style tab. Gain multipliers, not colours: each channel of each copy is multiplied by this value, so the colour changes between copies. 1 leaves it unchanged. |
| Duplicate Along Path | `UsePath` | Checkbox | 0 | Places copies along the path in `Polyline`. |
| Path Mode | `PathMode` | Multi-button | 0: Scaled, 1: Absolute, 2: Points | How copies are placed along the path. The manual does not describe the modes. |
| Displacement Scale | `PathDisplacementScale` | Number | 1 (0–2) | Strength of the displacement applied to copies along the path. |
| Displacement Offset | `PathDisplacementOffset` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Shifts the displacement along the path. |
| Align Rotation to Path | `PathAlignRotation` | Checkbox | 0 | Turns each copy to face along the path. |
| Polyline | `Polyline` | Polyline | none | The path, drawn in the viewer or set as a Polyline dict (see *Value types* in Conventions). Not animated. |

**Jitter tab.** Each control randomises the copies. The random values change with **Random Seed** and **Reseed**.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jitter Mode | `JitterMode` | ID combo | `"Fixed"` | `"Fixed"` uses a static jitter that doesn't move. `"Random"` changes the jitter every frame. |
| Random Seed | `RandomSeed` | Number (integer) | 0 (0–32767) | Starting point for the random values. Two copies with the same settings and different seeds look different. |
| Reseed | `Randomize` | Button | 0 | Picks a new seed. Set it to 1 from script. |
| Jitter Probability | `JitterProbability` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Chance that each copy is jittered. |
| Time Offset | `JitterTimeOffset` | Number | 0 (0–5) | Random time offset per copy. Not in the manual. |
| X Offset, Y Offset | `JitterXOffset`, `JitterYOffset` | Number | 0, 0 (0–1) | Random variation in each copy's position. |
| Z Offset [3D] | `JitterZOffset` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Random depth variation. Labelled [3D]. |
| Lock X/Y | `JitterSizeLock` | Checkbox | 1 | Uses the same size jitter on both axes. |
| Size, Y Size | `JitterXSize`, `JitterYSize` | Number | 0, 0 (0–1) | Random variation in scale. `JitterYSize` is used when Lock X/Y is off. |
| X Pivot, Y Pivot | `JitterXPivot`, `JitterYPivot` | Number | 0, 0 (0–1) | Random variation in the rotation pivot. Affects only the jitter rotation, not Z Rotation. |
| Z Rotation (Angle) | `JitterZRotation` | Number | 0 (0–180) | Random Z rotation per copy. |
| X, Y Rotation [3D] | `JitterXRotation`, `JitterYRotation` | Number | 0 (0–180) | Random rotation about the X or Y axis. Labelled [3D]. |
| Gain RGBA, Opacity | `JitterRedGain`, `JitterGreenGain`, `JitterBlueGain`, `JitterAlphaGain`, `JitterOpacityGain` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Random gain per copy for each channel. The default 0 gives no change. |
| Displacement Scale, Offset | `JitterPathDisplacementScale`, `JitterPathDisplacementOffset` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Random variation of the path displacement. |
### Example

A ring of twelve ellipses, turning as one. The original dot is pushed up from the centre, and each copy turns 30
degrees further about the image centre:

```python
dot = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
dot.Width = 0.06
dot.Height = 0.06
dot['Translate.Y'] = 0.3                   # the dot sits above the frame centre

ring = comp.AddTool('sDuplicate')
ring.Input = dot.Output
ring.Copies = 11                           # 12 dots in total
ring.AxisMode = 'Absolute'                 # each copy turns about the image centre
ring.ZRotation = 30                        # each copy turns 30 degrees further

spin = comp.AddTool('sTransform')
spin.Input = ring.Output
spin.ZRotation = comp.BezierSpline()       # turn the whole ring
spin.ZRotation[0] = 0
spin.ZRotation[96] = 360

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = spin.Output
```

### Tips

- For a ring or fan around the image centre, use `"Absolute"`. `"OriginAbsolute"` turns each copy about the original's
  own origin, at its duplicated position. `"Progressive"` builds each copy from the last one's position, rotation and so on.
- Along a path, set the path with `dup.Polyline = points`, a dict of points as for sPolygon. Unlike sPolygon's, this
  input isn't animated, so a plain assignment is enough. Setting `UsePath` to 1 without a path does nothing useful.
- The Style gains are multipliers, not colours. To recolour the whole array, use **sChangeStyle**.
- `TimeOffset` shows successive frames of animated source geometry in each copy.
- For a scattered field, use a larger Copies value with non-zero X and Y jitter. Use `JitterMode` `"Random"` if the
  scatter should change every frame, or `"Fixed"` for a static one. Reseed to change the arrangement.

**See also:** sGrid, sJitter, sTransform, sChangeStyle, sEllipse, sRectangle, sRender.

## sEllipse (`sEllipse`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sElp · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates a circle or ellipse as a vector shape: filled, or as an outline with optional write-on. Like all shape generators it outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen. In between, it can be duplicated, gridded, jittered or combined with other shapes.

**Use for:** dots, rings and halos, light flares and bokeh, circular wipes, progress rings, and the building blocks of dot-grid and orbit animations.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 (slider 0–1) | Size of the ellipse. Equal values make a circle. |
| X/Y Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Offset from the frame centre, relative to image width: 0.5 puts the centre on the right edge. Dotted IDs: `ring['Translate.X'] = 0.25`. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the shape's centre. Visible on an ellipse, or on a short outline; a circle looks the same at any angle. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`, with the centre transparent. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline (Length below 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: where the outline starts, and how much of it is drawn. Animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1 to draw the ring on. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A ring that grows out from the centre and fades away over 24 frames, rendered and merged over the video:

```python
ring = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
ring.Solid = 0
ring.BorderWidth = 0.006
ring.Width = comp.BezierSpline()       # grow from frame 0 to 24
ring.Width[0] = 0.05
ring.Width[24] = 0.6
ring.Height = comp.BezierSpline()
ring.Height[0] = 0.05
ring.Height[24] = 0.6
ring.Opacity = comp.BezierSpline()     # and fade out
ring.Opacity[0] = 1
ring.Opacity[24] = 0

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = ring.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

### Tips

- Keep `Width` and `Height` equal for a circle. Animating them separately gives an ellipse that morphs.
- For a ring that draws itself on, keep `Solid` at 0 and animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1, as sRectangle does.
- Use Offset with a shape duplicator to scatter circles: an sDuplicate or sGrid after the ellipse makes a dot pattern from one ellipse.

**See also:** sRectangle, sNGon, sStar, sRender, sGrid, sDuplicate, sBoolean, Ellipse (mask).

## sExpand (`sExpand`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sExp · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Grows (dilates) or shrinks (erodes) the shape tree passing through it, by the Amount. The Join Style sets how the
corners are drawn as the outline moves. Use it on a single shape or on a compound from sMerge or sBoolean. Like all
shape nodes, it only shows through **sRender**.

**Use for:** thickening or thinning glyph-like shapes, making a halo or base behind a shape, and fine-tuning a
boolean result.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amount | `Amount` | Number | 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | How far the outline moves. A positive value dilates (grows) the shape, and a negative value erodes (shrinks) it. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round; 0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip | How corners are drawn. Bevel squares them off, Round rounds them, and Miter and Miter Clip keep them pointed up to the Miter Limit. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (1–10) | Where a Miter corner turns into a bevel. Only shown for Miter and Miter Clip. |

### Example

A rounded rectangle, dilated slightly with sharp corners, so it can serve as a base behind a title:

```python
panel = comp.AddTool('sRectangle')
panel.Width = 0.3
panel.Height = 0.1
panel.CornerRadius = 0.2

grow = comp.AddTool('sExpand')
grow.Input = panel.Output
grow.Amount = 0.02
grow.JoinStyle = 2                         # 2 = Miter
grow.MiterLimit = 4

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = grow.Output
```

### Tips

- Set Join Style to Miter (2) when you want sharp corners at larger Amounts. Miter Limit caps how far the corner
  points can reach before they are beveled.
- Erode small details by using a negative Amount on the compound, rather than rebuilding the shape at a new size.
- The slider runs from −0.1 to 0.1, so keep the Amount small. Values in that range change the outline by a small
  fraction of the frame.

**See also:** sOutline, sBoolean, sMerge, sRectangle, sEllipse, sRender.

## sGrid (`sGrid`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sGrd · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Repeats the incoming shape tree on a grid of rows and columns. Cells X and Y set how many columns and rows there
are, and X and Y Offset set the spacing between them. An offset of 0 stacks every copy on top of the others. An
offset of 1 spreads the columns across the full frame width. The grid makes the copies at fixed positions, so
**sJitter** is often placed after it to break up the regularity. Like all shape nodes, it only shows through
**sRender**.

**Use for:** tiled patterns, dot matrices, bar charts, and rows of tiles for jittered or animated effects.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grid Cells X, Y | `CellsX`, `CellsY` | Number (integer) | 3, 3 (slider 1–10; typed up to 1,000,000) | Number of columns (X) and rows (Y). The grid grows in both directions from the original's origin, so it stays centred on it. Fractional values are rounded, so 1.6 becomes 2. |
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset`, `YOffset` | Number | 0.2, 0.2 (−1 to 1) | Spacing between columns (X) and rows (Y), in normalised frame units. 0 stacks all copies. 1 spreads the columns across the frame width. |

### Example

A 4 by 3 grid of rounded squares, with the spacing set a little wider than the default:

```python
tile = comp.AddTool('sRectangle')
tile.Width = 0.06
tile.Height = 0.06
tile.CornerRadius = 0.3                    # rounded corners

grid = comp.AddTool('sGrid')
grid.Input = tile.Output
grid.CellsX = 4
grid.CellsY = 3
grid.XOffset = 0.15
grid.YOffset = 0.15

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = grid.Output
```

### Tips

- The offsets are the spacing, not the position of the grid. To move or centre the whole grid, place an sTransform
  after it.
- To fan the copies out over time, keyframe `XOffset` or `YOffset` with `comp.BezierSpline()`, starting at 0 so the
  copies stack first.
- To make the tiles differ, add an sJitter after the grid. Its Random mode can animate each tile on its own.

**See also:** sDuplicate, sJitter, sTransform, sRectangle, sEllipse, sRender.

## sJitter (`sJitter`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sJt · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Randomises the position, size and rotation of each shape in an array from **sGrid** or **sDuplicate**. It can also
jitter the points that make up a single shape, for a wobbly or distressed look. In Fixed mode the ranges are static
and you animate them by keyframing. In Random mode, each parameter moves on its own between the Min and Max of its
range. If every range is left at its default, nothing moves. Like all shape nodes, it only shows through **sRender**.

**Use for:** scattering or settling a grid of tiles, varying the size of a row of dots, wobbly or hand-drawn
motion on a single shape, and animated jitter that builds up or dies away.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jitter Mode | `JitterMode` | ID combo | `"Fixed"` | `"Fixed"`: static offsets, animated by keyframes or modifiers. `"Random"`: each range animates randomly between its Min and Max. |
| Random Seed | `RandomSeed` | Number (integer) | Differs on each new instance (registered default 0; 0–32767) | Starting point for the random values. Different seeds give different patterns with the same ranges. |
| Reseed | `Randomize` | Button | 0 | Picks a new seed. Set it to 1 from script. |
| Shape X Offset | `Shape.OffsetX.Min`, `Shape.OffsetX.Max` | Range | 0, 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Horizontal shift of each shape, between Min and Max. |
| Shape Y Offset | `Shape.OffsetY.Min`, `Shape.OffsetY.Max` | Range | 0, 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Vertical shift of each shape, between Min and Max. |
| Shape X Size | `Shape.SizeX.Min`, `Shape.SizeX.Max` | Range | 1, 1 (0–2) | Horizontal scale of each shape. 1 is unchanged. |
| Shape Y Size | `Shape.SizeY.Min`, `Shape.SizeY.Max` | Range | 1, 1 (0–2) | Vertical scale of each shape. 1 is unchanged. |
| Shape Rotate | `Shape.Rotate.Min`, `Shape.Rotate.Max` | Range | 0, 0 (−360 to 360) | Rotation of each shape, in degrees. |
| Point X Offset | `Point.OffsetX.Min`, `Point.OffsetX.Max` | Range | 0, 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Moves the control points of the shape horizontally, distorting its outline. |
| Point Y Offset | `Point.OffsetY.Min`, `Point.OffsetY.Max` | Range | 0, 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Moves the control points of the shape vertically. |

Set a Min or Max from script with the dotted ID, for example `jt['Shape.OffsetX.Min'] = -0.05`.

### Example

A grid of rounded squares whose jitter starts large and settles into the grid by frame 48:

```python
tile = comp.AddTool('sRectangle')
tile.Width = 0.06
tile.Height = 0.06
tile.CornerRadius = 0.3

grid = comp.AddTool('sGrid')
grid.Input = tile.Output
grid.CellsX = 4
grid.CellsY = 3
grid.XOffset = 0.2
grid.YOffset = 0.2

jt = comp.AddTool('sJitter')
jt.Input = grid.Output
jt.JitterMode = 'Random'
jt.RandomSeed = 7

# Each range starts wide and closes to zero, so the random offsets die away.
for rng, start_min, start_max in (('Shape.OffsetX', -0.04, 0.04), ('Shape.OffsetY', -0.04, 0.04)):
    jt[rng + '.Min'] = comp.BezierSpline()
    jt[rng + '.Min'][0] = start_min
    jt[rng + '.Min'][48] = 0
    jt[rng + '.Max'] = comp.BezierSpline()
    jt[rng + '.Max'][0] = start_max
    jt[rng + '.Max'][48] = 0

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = jt.Output
```

### Tips

- For a settling effect, keyframe the Min and Max of a range towards 0 (as in the example). For a build-up, go the
  other way.
- Shape Size ranges default to 1, which is no change. Setting Min and Max to 1 keeps a size unchanged, while
  changing them makes the shapes vary in size.
- Point ranges move the shape's own control points, not its position. Use them for wobble or a hand-drawn edge.
- Jitter is applied after the grid or duplicate. Put it directly after the node you want randomised, and put an
  sTransform after it to move the result as a unit.

**See also:** sGrid, sDuplicate, sTransform, sRectangle, sEllipse, sRender.

## sMerge (`sMerge`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sMrg · **Inputs:** `Input1`, `Input2`, and more added as needed (ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Combines any number of shape trees into one, the shape equivalent of a Merge tool. Each shape keeps its own style, colour and animation. The inputs are layered in order: the shape on `Input1` is at the bottom, and each later input sits over the one before it. The sMerge tile always shows one free input, so you can keep adding shapes. Like all shape nodes, its result is only visible through **sRender**.

**Use for:** building one graphic out of several shapes (a logo from a ring and a star, a badge from a circle, text and a rule), then duplicating, gridding or jittering the whole group as one unit.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input1, Input2, … | `Input1`, `Input2`, then more as created | ShapeTree | none | Shapes to combine. `Input1` is the bottom layer. A new input appears each time one is connected, so there is always a free one. |
| Override Axis | `OverrideAxis` | Checkbox | 0 | Overrides the axis of the shape. The manual gives no further detail, so check its effect in the viewer. |

sMerge has no Style tab: each input keeps its own colour and Allow Combining setting. Use sChangeStyle downstream to restyle the whole group.

### Example

A logo made of a ring and a five-point star, combined, rendered and laid over the video:

```python
ring = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
ring.Solid = 0
ring.BorderWidth = 0.01
ring.Width = 0.4
ring.Height = 0.4

star = comp.AddTool('sStar')
star.Points = 5
star.Depth = 0.4
star.Width = 0.2
star.Height = 0.2

merge = comp.AddTool('sMerge')
merge.Input1 = ring.Output
merge.Input2 = star.Output

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = merge.Output

merge2d = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge2d.Background = media_in.Output
merge2d.Foreground = render.Output
```

To add a third shape, connect it to the next free input: `merge['Input3'] = star2.Output`. The name of the input follows the number of shapes already connected.

### Tips

- Layering follows the input order, so put the shape that should sit at the back on `Input1`.
- sMerge only combines; it doesn't add an alpha or colour change. For a single colour across the group, use **sChangeStyle** after the merge.
- To move, scale or rotate the whole group together, connect the merge to sTransform, rather than moving each shape.
- To cut one shape out of another, use **sBoolean**, which combines exactly two shapes.

**See also:** sBoolean, sTransform, sChangeStyle, sRender, sDuplicate, sGrid, Merge (2D).

## sNGon (`sNGon`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sNg · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates a regular polygon with a chosen number of sides: a triangle, square, hexagon, octagon and so on. Like all shape generators it outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen. In between, it can be duplicated, gridded, jittered or combined with other shapes.

**Use for:** icons and markers, hexagonal tiles and honeycomb grids, arrows and pointers (a triangle), badges and seals, and spinning geometric accents.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sides | `Sides` | Number | 6 (slider 3–20) | Number of sides, as an integer. Values below 3 are raised to 3. |
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 (slider 0–1) | Size of the polygon. Equal values keep it regular. |
| X/Y Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Offset from the frame centre, relative to image width: 0.5 puts the centre on the right edge. Dotted IDs: `poly['Translate.X'] = 0.25`. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the shape's centre. Animate it to spin the polygon. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`, with the centre transparent. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter) | How the outline's corners are drawn. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline (Length below 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: where the outline starts, and how much of it is drawn. Animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1 to draw the outline on. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A hexagon outline that draws on and turns through a quarter turn over 36 frames:

```python
hexagon = comp.AddTool('sNGon')
hexagon.Sides = 6
hexagon.Solid = 0
hexagon.BorderWidth = 0.008
hexagon.JoinStyle = 1                       # Round corners
hexagon.WriteLength = comp.BezierSpline()   # draw on, frames 0-36
hexagon.WriteLength[0] = 0
hexagon.WriteLength[36] = 1
hexagon.Angle = comp.BezierSpline()         # turn 90 degrees over the same frames
hexagon.Angle[0] = 0
hexagon.Angle[36] = 90

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = hexagon.Output
```

### Tips

- With `Sides` set to 3 and Angle keyed, the triangle points in a chosen direction. This is a quick arrow or pointer.
- Use Miter for sharp corners on an outline. Miter Clip, which sStar and sPolygon offer, is not available here.
- `Sides` accepts more than the slider's 20 from script, but very high counts look like a circle. Use sEllipse for a circle.
- For a honeycomb, follow sNGon with sGrid or sDuplicate and offset the copies.

**See also:** sEllipse, sRectangle, sStar, sRender, sGrid, sDuplicate, sBoolean.

## sOutline (`sOutline`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sOtl · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Turns the incoming shape tree into outlines. Each shape keeps its own style, but the Thickness, Join Style, Cap Style,
Position and Length are applied to all of them together. Length below 1 leaves a gap, and keyframing Length from 0 to 1
gives a write-on effect. Use it on a compound shape from sMerge or sBoolean for an outline around the whole group. Like
all shape nodes, it only shows through **sRender**.

**Use for:** write-on titles and graphics, outlines of boolean shapes, and double outlines from a single shape.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thickness | `Thickness` | Number | 0.01 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Width of the outline. Negative values are accepted. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round; 0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip | How the corners of the outline are drawn. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (1–10) | Where a Miter corner turns into a bevel. Only shown for Miter and Miter Clip. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded; 0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square | Ends of an open outline. Visible only when Length is below 1. |
| Position | `WritePosition` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Where the outline starts. With Length, it positions the gap. |
| Length | `WriteLength` | Number | 1 (0–1) | How much of the outline is drawn. 1 is a closed outline. Keyframe it from 0 to 1 to write the outline on. |

### Example

A circle outlined with a write-on over 48 frames, with rounded caps so the start of the line is smooth:

```python
ring = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
ring.Width = 0.3
ring.Height = 0.3

outline = comp.AddTool('sOutline')
outline.Input = ring.Output
outline.Thickness = 0.01
outline.CapStyle = 1                       # 1 = Rounded
outline.WriteLength = comp.BezierSpline()  # draw on from nothing to a full outline
outline.WriteLength[0] = 0
outline.WriteLength[48] = 1

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = outline.Output
```

### Tips

- Position and Length together place the gap. Animating Position as well as Length should move the gap along the
  outline; this is not verified in the viewer.
- Use **sMerge** or **sBoolean** first, then sOutline, to outline a whole group with one set of controls.
- Cap Style only matters when the outline is open. Flat, Rounded and Square caps are visible only once Length is
  below 1.
- Miter Limit is only used when Join Style is Miter or Miter Clip.

**See also:** sRectangle, sEllipse, sNGon, sPolygon, sMerge, sBoolean, sExpand, sRender.

## sPolygon (`sPolygon`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sPly · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates a freely drawn shape or open line from Bézier curves. The points are stored in the tool's `Polyline` control, and can be drawn in the viewer or set and keyframed from script. Everything else about the shape (its style, position, size, rotation and write-on) can be set and animated from script. Like all shape generators it outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen.

**Use for:** hand-drawn underlines and swooshes, arrows and logos that aren't regular geometry, signatures and write-on lines, and any custom outline that you want to draw on, move or grow.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Polyline | `Polyline` | Polyline | none | The path's points, as offsets from the frame centre (moved by Offset). Already animated (see Tips). |
| Offset | `Center` | Point | (0, 0) | Moves the whole shape, as an offset from the frame centre, relative to image width. Animate with `comp.PolyPath()`. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Scales the whole shape without changing the points or the animation. |
| Z Rotation | `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the shape's centre. X and Y Rotation are 3D controls. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`. Turn it off for a line. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | How the corners of the path are joined. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (slider 1–10) | Limits how far a Miter join can extend beyond the corner. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square) | Ends of an open line (Length below 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: where the line starts, and how much is drawn. Animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1 to write the line on. |
| Fill Method | `FillMethod` | Combo | 1: Non-zero Winding (0: Alternate) | How overlapping parts of a self-crossing path are filled. Switch to Non-zero Winding if the crossings leave holes. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A curved underline that writes on over 24 frames. The handles (`RX`, `RY` out of the first point, `LX`, `LY` into the
second) bow the line upwards.

```python
line = comp.AddTool('sPolygon')
line.Polyline[0] = {1: {'X': -0.3, 'Y': -0.2, 'RX': 0.2, 'RY': 0.1},
                    2: {'X': 0.3, 'Y': -0.2, 'LX': -0.2, 'LY': 0.1}}
line.Solid = 0                         # an open line, drawn as an outline
line.BorderWidth = 0.006
line.WriteLength = comp.BezierSpline()
line.WriteLength[0] = 0
line.WriteLength[24] = 1

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = line.Output
```

### Tips

- **Drawing the path.** A new sPolygon has no points and renders nothing. In the viewer, the shape toolbar sets the mode: Click places a point at each click, and clicking the first point again closes the shape. Draw is freehand. Switch to Done to lock the points. Insert and Modify lets you add or move points.
- **Setting the path from script.** `Polyline` takes a dict of points (see *Value types* in Conventions). It is already animated, so set shapes with `line.Polyline[frame] = points`; a plain `line.Polyline = points` replaces all the keyframes with one at the current frame (see *Animated polylines* in Conventions). The path of sDuplicate takes the same kind of value.
- `WritePosition` and `WriteLength` only have an effect when `Solid` is off.
- Use `Center` (Point) to move the whole shape. `Size` and `ZRotation` scale and turn the path as one piece.
- For a line that is always curved, sBSpline draws the same kind of path with fewer points.

**See also:** sBSpline, sRectangle, sEllipse, sStar, sRender, sDuplicate, sOutline, sChangeStyle.

## sRectangle (`sRectangle`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sRct · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates a rectangle as a vector shape: filled, or as an outline with optional rounded corners. Like all shape
generators it outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen. In between, it can be
duplicated, gridded, jittered or combined with other shapes.

**Use for:** boxes and bars behind titles, frames, progress bars and wipes, and the building blocks of grid and
pattern animations.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 | Size, relative to image width, with the aspect preserved. |
| Corner Radius | `CornerRadius` | Number | 0 (0–1) | 0 gives sharp corners. 1 turns a square into a circle and a rectangle into a pill shape. |
| X/Y Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y` | Number | 0, 0 | Offset from the frame centre, relative to image width: 0.5 puts the centre on the right edge. Dotted IDs: `bar['Translate.X'] = 0.25`. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the shape's centre. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 2: Miter) | How the outline's corners are drawn. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline (Length < 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: the start point, and how much of it is drawn. Animate `WriteLength` from 0 to 1 to draw the outline on. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A rounded bar behind a title that draws its outline on, rendered and merged over the video:

```python
bar = comp.AddTool('sRectangle')
bar.Width = 0.4
bar.Height = 0.08
bar.CornerRadius = 0.3
bar['Translate.X'] = -0.25             # left of centre
bar['Translate.Y'] = -0.2
bar.Solid = 0
bar.BorderWidth = 0.004
bar.WriteLength = comp.BezierSpline()  # draw the outline on, frames 0-18
bar.WriteLength[0] = 0
bar.WriteLength[18] = 1

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = bar.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

**See also:** sEllipse, sNGon, sRender, sGrid, sDuplicate, Rectangle Mask.

## sRender (`sRender`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sRn · **Inputs:** `Input` (ShapeTree, required), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts a shape tree into an image that the rest of the comp can use. Every shape chain ends here: the shape generators, modifiers and combiners are only visible once they are rendered. The output is a normal 2D image, so it connects to Merge, colour tools and everything else. Resolution, bit depth and pixel aspect are on the Image tab, which is described under Common Controls. By default the output takes the comp's frame format.

**Use for:** the final step of every shape graphic. Put shapes over video with a Merge, or use the rendered image as a mask, a background or a layer for other effects.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input | `Input` | ShapeTree | none | The shape tree to render: the output of the last shape node in the chain. |
| Effect Mask | `EffectMask` | Mask | none | Optional blue input. Limits the rendered area to the mask's pixels (see Effect masks in Common Controls). |
| Global In, Global Out | `GlobalIn`, `GlobalOut` | Number | 0, 1000 (range 0–1000) | The frame range over which the node produces images, as on other generators (see Common Controls). |

Set the size with the Image tab's `UseFrameFormatSettings` (Auto Resolution, on by default), `Width` and `Height`, and `Depth` (see Common Controls). Blend, Motion Blur and the other Settings tab controls also apply.

### Example

A star rendered over the video and merged on top, at a fixed 1280 × 720 size:

```python
star = comp.AddTool('sStar')
star.Points = 5

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = star.Output
render.UseFrameFormatSettings = 0     # Auto Resolution off
render.Width = 1280
render.Height = 720

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

### Tips

- Leave Auto Resolution on to match the comp's frame format. Turn it off only when the shapes must be rendered at a different size from the comp.
- Shapes are resolution-independent, so a size set in shape units looks the same at any render size. Only the sRender's pixel count changes the detail.
- Keep one sRender per shape chain. Put a Merge after it to place the result over other images. Combine several chains with sMerge before rendering, rather than with several sRender nodes, unless they need different resolutions or depths.
- A shape node can't feed an Effect Mask input directly. Render the shapes with sRender first, then connect its output to the mask input. The rendered image is an ordinary image, so every mask option applies.
- Use `Depth` float16 or float32 when the shapes are going to be graded or blurred, to avoid banding.

**See also:** sRectangle, sEllipse, sNGon, sStar, sPolygon, sBSpline, sText, sMerge, sBoolean, Merge, Effect masks.

## sStar (`sStar`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sStr · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates a multi-point star as a vector shape, with a chosen number of points and arm depth. Like all shape generators it outputs a shape tree, so it must go through **sRender** to be seen. In between, it can be duplicated, gridded, jittered or combined with other shapes.

**Use for:** sparkles, badges and award stamps, star ratings, twinkles on a title, and burst or starfield patterns made by duplicating one star.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Points | `Points` | Number | 6 (slider 2–20) | Number of points or arms, as an integer. |
| Depth | `Depth` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Depth of the inner radius, so the width of the arms. Near 0 gives hair-thin arms; 1 gives a faceted circle. |
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 (slider 0–1) | Size of the star. Equal values keep it symmetrical. |
| X/Y Offset | `Translate.X`, `Translate.Y` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Offset from the frame centre, relative to image width: 0.5 puts the centre on the right edge. Dotted IDs: `star['Translate.X'] = 0.25`. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (degrees) | Rotation about the star's centre. Animate it to spin the star. |
| Solid | `Solid` | Checkbox | 1 | Off draws only an outline of `BorderWidth`, with the centre transparent. |
| Border Width | `BorderWidth` | Number | 0 (slider −0.2 to 0.2) | Outline thickness, or grows/shrinks a solid shape. |
| Join Style | `JoinStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Round (0: Bevel, 1: Round, 2: Miter, 3: Miter Clip) | How the outline's corners are drawn. Miter keeps the points sharp. |
| Miter Limit | `MiterLimit` | Number | 10 (slider 1–10) | Limits how far a Miter point can extend before it is cut back. |
| Cap Style | `CapStyle` | Multi-button | 1: Rounded (0: Flat, 1: Rounded, 2: Square) | Ends of an open outline (Length below 1). |
| Position, Length | `WritePosition`, `WriteLength` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | Outline only: where the outline starts, and how much of it is drawn. |
| Color | `Red` `Green` `Blue` `Alpha` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Style tab. |
| Opacity | `Opacity` | Number | 1 | Style tab. |
| Allow Combining | `AllowCombining` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps alpha from stacking where copies of the shape overlap. |

### Example

A five-point star that spins a half turn and scales in from nothing over 18 frames:

```python
star = comp.AddTool('sStar')
star.Points = 5
star.Depth = 0.45
star.Width = comp.BezierSpline()       # scale in from frame 0 to 18
star.Width[0] = 0
star.Width[18] = 0.5
star.Height = comp.BezierSpline()
star.Height[0] = 0
star.Height[18] = 0.5
star.Angle = comp.BezierSpline()       # and spin
star.Angle[0] = 0
star.Angle[18] = 180

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = star.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

### Tips

- sStar has no single Size control, so scale it with `Width` and `Height` together. Keyframe both to keep the proportions.
- `Points` is an integer, so a keyframed value changes the arm count in whole steps and rounds in between.
- A small star duplicated with sDuplicate or sGrid makes a starfield. Use sJitter to randomise the sizes.

**See also:** sNGon, sEllipse, sPolygon, sRender, sDuplicate, sGrid, sJitter, sBoolean.

## sText (`sText`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sTxt · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Generates text as vector shapes, the shape version of Text+. It has most of Text+'s controls: the same text, font, layout and shading model, with up to eight shading elements (fill, outline, shadow and border), so the text can then be duplicated, gridded, jittered or combined with other shapes. It doesn't support gradient colours. Like all shape generators it must go through **sRender** to be seen.

**Use for:** text that is then animated as shapes (a grid of letters, jittered type, text cut out with sBoolean or merged with a logo), and write-on titles that need shape-level control.

**Text+ or sText:** for an ordinary title, use Text+. Use sText when the text has to go through a shape operation.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Styled Text | `StyledText` | Text | "" | The text. Use `\n` for new lines. |
| Font | `Font` | Text | "Open Sans" | Font family name, as installed. |
| Style | `Style` | Text | "Bold" | Typeface within the family, e.g. "Regular", "Bold", "Italic". |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 0.08 (slider 0–0.5) | Text size relative to image width. |
| Color | `Red1` `Green1` `Blue1` `Alpha1` | Number | 1, 1, 1, 1 | Fill colour (shading element 1). |
| Character Spacing | `CharacterSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between characters; 1 is normal. |
| Line Spacing | `LineSpacingClone` | Number | 1 (0–4) | Spacing between lines (leading). |
| H Anchor | `HorizontalLeftCenterRight` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | −1 left, 0 centre, 1 right. |
| V Anchor | `VerticalTopCenterBottom` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | −1 top, 0 centre, 1 bottom. |
| Write On Start, End | `Start`, `End` | Number | 0 and 1 (0–1) | The visible portion of the text. Animate `End` from 0 to 1 to write on, or `Start` from 0 to 1 to write off. |
| Scroll | `Scroll` | Multi-button | 0: Still, 1: Roll, 2: Crawl | Roll (vertical) and Crawl (horizontal) credits. Animate `ScrollPosition` to move them. |
| Layout Type | `LayoutType` | Multi-button | 0: Point, 1: Text Box, 2: Circle, 3: Path | How the text is laid out. |
| Layout Center | `Center` | Point | (0, 0) | Position of the layout as an offset from the frame centre, relative to image width. The default (0, 0) is the centre, because this is an offset rather than a position as in Text+. |
