| Layout Size | `LayoutSize` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Scales the whole layout. |
| Layout Width, Height | `LayoutWidth`, `LayoutHeight` | Number | 0.5, 0.5 (0–1) | Box size (Text Box layout), or circle size (Circle layout, Width only). |
| Wrap, Clip | `Wrap`, `Clip` | Checkbox | 1, 0 | Word wrap and clipping for Text Box layout. |
| Position on Path | `PositionOnPath` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Where the text sits along a path (Path layout). Animate it to move text along the path. |
| Element Enable | `Enabled1` … `Enabled8` | Checkbox | 1 for 1, 0 for others | Turns each shading element on or off. Enable an element before setting its other controls. |
| Element Opacity | `Opacity1` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Opacity of shading element 1. Element N uses `OpacityN`. |
| Element Blending | `Overlap1` | Combo | 2: Composite, 0: Solid, 1: Transparent | How element 1 combines with the elements below it. Element N uses `OverlapN`. |
| Element Appearance | `ElementShape1` | Multi-button | 0: Text Fill, 1: Text Outline, 2: Border Fill, 3: Border Outline | What element 1 draws. Element N uses `ElementShapeN`. |
| Element Thickness | `Thickness1` | Number | 0.02 (slider 0–0.1) | Outline thickness for an outline element. Element N uses `ThicknessN`. |

The colour (`RedN`, `GreenN`, `BlueN`, `AlphaN`) and the other element controls exist for elements 2 to 8, and read back as expected once the element's `EnabledN` is set to 1. Setting `RedN` on a disabled element has no effect. Element 1 is enabled by default ("White Solid Fill"), and the elements stack in order.

### Example

A title in gold that writes on over 36 frames, rendered and merged over the video:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('sText')
title.StyledText = 'Fusion Shapes'
title.Font = 'Open Sans'
title.Style = 'Bold'
title.Size = 0.1
title.Red1, title.Green1, title.Blue1 = 1, 0.8, 0.2   # gold fill
title.End = comp.BezierSpline()                        # write on, frames 0-36
title.End[0] = 0
title.End[36] = 1

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = title.Output

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = media_in.Output
merge.Foreground = render.Output
```

### Tips

- Set `Font` and `Style` to the names of installed fonts. An unknown font name is accepted without an error, so check the result in the viewer.
- sDuplicate, sGrid and sJitter act on the whole text as one shape. To move or scale individual characters, use the Transform tab's per-character controls (`CharacterOffset`, `CharacterSizeX` and so on).
- Use sBoolean to cut a sText output out of a shape, or sMerge to combine it with a logo.
- Write-on `End` (or `Start`) and `Size` animate the same way as on Text+. `Center`, the layout offset, is also a Point control.

**See also:** TextPlus, sRectangle, sEllipse, sRender, sMerge, sBoolean, sDuplicate, sGrid, sJitter, sTransform.

## sTransform (`sTransform`)

**Category:** Shape · **Short name:** sXf · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, ShapeTree) · **Output:** `Output` (ShapeTree)

Adds a second set of offset, size, rotation and pivot controls on top of the shape's own. Because it transforms the whole shape tree passing through it, everything upstream moves, scales or turns as one unit. That is how hierarchical animation is built: an inner shape spins on its own Angle, and an outer sTransform carries it around the frame. Like all shape nodes, it only shows through **sRender**.

**Use for:** orbiting or swinging a group of shapes, moving or scaling a whole sMerge or sDuplicate result, and any parent motion under a shape that already animates itself.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset`, `YOffset` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | Moves the shape. Offsets are relative to the frame width, so 0.5 in X puts the centre on the right edge. |
| X Size, Y Size | `XSize`, `YSize` | Number | 1, 1 (0–5) | Scales the shape on each axis. Unequal values skew it. |
| Rotation | `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (degrees, −180 to 180) | Rotates the shape about the pivot. Keyframe it for orbits. Values beyond ±180 are accepted (360 reads back as 360). |
| X Pivot, Y Pivot | `XPivot`, `YPivot` | Number | 0, 0 (−1 to 1) | The point that rotation and scaling turn about. It is relative to the X/Y Offset, not to the image, so it moves with the offset. It appears as a red X in the viewer. |
| Transform Axis | `TransformAxis` | Checkbox | 1 | Applies the transform to the shape's own axis. |

### Example

A small dot that spins on its own, carried around the frame centre by a parent sTransform:

```python
dot = comp.AddTool('sEllipse')
dot.Width = 0.08
dot.Height = 0.08
dot['Translate.X'] = 0.25                  # the dot sits 0.25 right of centre
dot.Angle = comp.BezierSpline()            # the dot spins on its own axis
dot.Angle[0] = 0
dot.Angle[48] = 360

orbit = comp.AddTool('sTransform')
orbit.Input = dot.Output
orbit.ZRotation = comp.BezierSpline()      # the whole group turns about the pivot
orbit.ZRotation[0] = 0
orbit.ZRotation[96] = 360

render = comp.AddTool('sRender')
render.Input = orbit.Output
```

### Tips

- Put the spin on the inner shape's `Angle` and the orbit on the sTransform. Each level then keeps its own timing.
- sTransform can also be placed after an sGrid or sDuplicate to move the whole array in one step, rather than
  moving each copy.
- The pivot sets the point the rotation turns about. Set it before keyframing the rotation, so the keyframes stay
  meaningful when you move the pivot.

**See also:** sEllipse, sRectangle, sDuplicate, sGrid, sJitter, sRender.

## Anaglyph (`Anaglyph`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** Ana · **Inputs:** `Left` (orange), `Right` (green), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Combines a left-eye and a right-eye image into one image of coloured overlaid channels, which is viewed through matching coloured glasses. It is used at the end of a stereo tree, to show or deliver the result. The Method sets how each eye's colour is encoded: Monochrome and Half-color keep one eye's luminance, Color keeps each eye's own colours, Optimised balances the brightness the two eyes see, and Dubois is designed to reduce retinal rivalry for red/cyan glasses. The Anaglyph tool is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** a red/cyan or other colour-glasses preview of a stereo comp, and the final anaglyph deliverable.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | `Method` | Combo | 0: Monochrome (1: Half-color, 2: Color, 3: Optimised, 4: Dubois) | How the eyes are encoded. Dubois is for red/cyan glasses only, so Color Type is hidden when it is chosen. |
| Color Type | `ColorType` | Combo | 0: Red/Cyan (1: Red/Green, 2: Red/Blue, 3: Amber/Blue, 4: Green/Magenta) | The colour of the glasses. Hidden with Dubois. |
| Swap | `Swap` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right eyes. |
| Horiz stack | `HorizStack` | Checkbox | 0 | The input is one side-by-side image: the left half is the left eye, the right half the right eye. Connect it to Left only. |
| Vert stack | `VertStack` | Checkbox | 0 | The input is one stacked image: the bottom half is the left eye, the top half the right eye. Connect it to Left only. |
| Left | `Left` | Image input | | The left-eye image, or the stacked image when a stack option is on. |
| Right | `Right` | Image input | | The right-eye image. Not used with a stack option. |
| Left Layer, Right Layer | `LeftLayer`, `RightLayer` | Layer select | `":Auto"` | The layer of each eye, for a multi-layer file. |

The Settings tab and Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.

### Example

A red/cyan colour anaglyph from separate left and right images:

```python
left = comp.AddTool('Background')       # stands in for the left-eye image
right = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for the right-eye image

ana = comp.AddTool('Anaglyph')
ana.Left = left.Output
ana.Right = right.Output
ana.Method = 2                          # Color
ana.ColorType = 0                       # Red/Cyan
```

### Tips

- Red/Cyan is the most common glasses type. Choose Dubois with it to reduce the rivalry between the eyes in saturated colours.
- For a stacked input from the Combiner, turn on Horiz stack or Vert stack and connect only the Left input.
- Check the result with the glasses you will use. The colours in the preview depend on the glasses type.

**See also:** Combiner, Splitter, Stereo Align, Disparity, Merge.

## Combiner (`Combiner`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** Com · **Inputs:** `Image1` (orange, the left eye), `Image2` (green, the right eye) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Stacks a left-eye and a right-eye image into one image, side by side (Horiz) or one above the other (Vert). The stacked image can be stored or passed on as a single file, and split again with Splitter. Layers keeps the two eyes as named layers instead of stacking them. Combiner is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** packaging a stereo pair as one stacked image for delivery, or for storage as a single EXR, which the manual notes can be more efficient than recalculating disparity each time.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Combine | `Combine` | ID multi-button | `"Horiz"` | `"None"` (no change), `"Horiz"` (side by side, width doubles), `"Vert"` (stacked, height doubles) or `"Layers"` (keep the eyes as named layers). |
| Image 1 | `Image1` | Image input | | The left-eye image. In a Vert stack it appears at the bottom. |
| Image 2 | `Image2` | Image input | | The right-eye image. |
| Swap | `Swap` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the two eyes. |
| Add Metadata | `AddMetadata` | Checkbox | 1 | Adds the stack information to the image metadata. Shown when Combine isn't Layers. |
| Layer 1 Name, Layer 2 Name | `LayerName1`, `LayerName2` | Text | `"Left"`, `"Right"` | Names of the two layers. Shown when Combine is Layers. |

### Example

Stacking a left and right image one above the other, as a single image that the Splitter can take apart again:

```python
left = comp.AddTool('Background')      # stands in for the left-eye image
right = comp.AddTool('Background')     # stands in for the right-eye image

stack = comp.AddTool('Combiner')
stack.Image1 = left.Output
stack.Image2 = right.Output
stack.Combine = 'Vert'                 # stacked: the left eye (Image 1) is at the bottom
```

### Tips

- Stacking to an EXR can be more efficient than calculating disparity each time the comp is viewed, as the manual notes.
- Choose Horiz or Vert to match the Splitter's Split setting when you split the image again.

**See also:** Splitter, Anaglyph, Stereo Align, Disparity.

## Disparity (`Dimension.Disparity`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** Dis · **Inputs:** `Input.Left` (orange), `Input.Right` (green) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

Works out the horizontal and vertical shift of every pixel between the left and right eyes, and writes it into the Disparity channel of each eye's output. The left output holds the left-to-right shift, and the right output the right-to-left shift. Disparity is the basis of several other stereo tools: Disparity To Z, New Eye, Smooth Motion and Stereo Align use it. It is calculated when frames are rendered, so the result isn't visible in a scratch comp.

**Use for:** building the disparity map that other stereo tools need, from a pair of plates. The colours in the two eyes must match, so colour-correct them first and crop away any black borders.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | `Method` | ID multi-button | `"Advanced"` | `"Advanced"` (GPU) or `"Method2"` (Classic, CPU). The Classic method has a Proxy slider and the Edges and Match Weighting controls, which the Advanced method doesn't. |
| Warp Count, Iteration Count, Smoothness | `Advanced.NumWarps`, `Advanced.NumIters`, `Advanced.Smoothness` | Number | 5 (1 to 10), 10 (1 to 20), 10 (1 to 100) | The Advanced method's settings. Fewer warps and iterations are faster. |
| Half Resolution | `Advanced.HalfRes` | Checkbox | 0 | Calculates at half size, for speed. |
| Proxy (for tracking) | `Method2.Proxy` | Number | 2 (1 to 5) | Classic: the image is reduced by this factor for tracking. A proxy of 2 gives about 4 times the speed. |
| Edges, Match Weighting, Mismatch Penalty | `Method2.Edges`, `Method2.MatchWeight`, `Method2.MismatchPenalty` | Number | 5 (1 to 10), 0.75 (0 to 1), 2 (1 to 2) | Classic: how closely the disparity follows the edges, how small details are matched, and how mismatched areas are penalised. |
| Stack Mode | `StackMode` | ID multi-button | `"Separate"` | `"Separate"`, `"HorizontalStack"`, `"VerticalStack"` or `"Layers"`. |
| Swap Eyes | `SwapEyes` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right inputs. |

The manual gives the Classic and Advanced controls in full, and the Left and Right inputs are described there. Layer names for the eyes, `LeftLayer` and `RightLayer`, are shown when Stack Mode is Layers.

**Use for:** a disparity map from a pair of plates, before Disparity To Z or Stereo Align.

**See also:** Disparity To Z, Stereo Align, Smooth Motion, Optical Flow.

## Disparity To Z (`Dimension.DisparityToZ`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** D2Z · **Inputs:** `Input.Left`, `Input.Right` (Image), `Camera` (DataType3D) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

Calculates a Z channel from the disparity in a stereo pair, which can then drive depth-based effects such as Depth Blur and Fog. With a stereo Camera 3D connected, the depth is correct for that camera. Without one, the Camera controls give artistic values. The manual notes that depth values become less accurate as they get more negative, because disparity approaches a constant value. Calculated during rendering, so not verified here.

**Use for:** creating a Z channel for a stereo plate, so depth effects can be applied to it.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output Z To RGB | `OutputZToRGB` | Checkbox | 0 | Writes the Z values into the RGB channels, to view them. |
| Refine Z: Enable | `RefineZ.Enable` | Checkbox | 0 | Refines the Z edges. Shows the controls below when on. |
| HiQ Only, Strength, Radius | `RefineZ.HiQOnly`, `RefineZ.Strength`, `RefineZ.Radius` | Checkbox, Number | 1, 0.001 (0.0001 to 0.01), 0.01 (0.001 to 0.03) | Shown when Refine Z is on. |
| Camera | `Camera` | 3D input | | The stereo camera. |
| Camera Mode | `CameraMode` | Multi-button | 0: External (1: Artistic) | External uses the connected camera. Artistic uses the Foreground and Background values below instead. |
| Foreground Disparity | `ForegroundDisparity` | Number | 0 (0 to 64) | Artistic mode: the disparity of the foreground, sampled from the left eye. |
| Background Disparity | `BackgroundDisparity` | Number | 64 (0 to 64) | Artistic mode: the disparity of the background, sampled from the left eye. |
| Foreground Depth | `ForegroundDepth` | Number | 10 (10 to 100) | Artistic mode: the Z depth of the foreground. |
| Background Depth | `BackgroundDepth` | Number | 100 (10 to 100) | Artistic mode: the Z depth of the background. |
| Falloff | `Falloff` | Number | 0 (0 to 1) | Artistic mode: how the depth changes between the foreground and background values. |

Stack Mode, Swap Eyes, Layer names and Camera Selector are also on the tool.

**See also:** Z To Disparity, Disparity, Depth Blur, Fog.

## Global Align (`Dimension.GlobalAlign`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** GA · **Inputs:** `Input.Left`, `Input.Right` (Image) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

A fast, simple alignment of a stereo pair: it shifts the eyes in X and Y, and rotates one of them, all in one node. It doesn't use optical flow. Use it at the start of a stereo chain to remove large differences between the eyes before Disparity is calculated.

**Use for:** correcting a large horizontal or vertical offset, or a small rotation, between the eyes.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Shift | `Translation.X.Value` | Number | 0 (-0.05 to 0.05) | Horizontal shift of one eye, relative to the frame width. |
| Balance X | `Translation.X.Balance` | Multi-button | 3: Split (0: None, 1: Left, 2: Right) | Which eye the X shift is applied to. Split shares it between them. |
| Snap X | `Translation.X.Snap` | Checkbox | 0 | Snaps the shift to whole pixels. |
| Y Shift | `Translation.Y.Value` | Number | 0 (-0.006 to 0.006) | Vertical shift of one eye. |
| Balance Y | `Translation.Y.Balance` | Multi-button | 2: Right | Which eye the Y shift is applied to. |
| Snap Y | `Translation.Y.Snap` | Checkbox | 0 | Snaps the vertical shift to whole pixels. |
| Angle | `Rotation.Value` | Number | 0 (-2 to 2) | Rotation of one eye. |
| Balance Rotation | `Rotation.Balance` | Multi-button | 2: Right | Which eye the rotation is applied to. |
| Translation Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor … 10: Bessel) | The resampling filter used for the shift. |
| Visualization | `Visualization` | Multi-button | 0: None (1: R-C, 2: Y-B, 3: G-M, 4: Diff) | An anaglyph or difference view of the eyes, to judge the alignment. |
| Swap Eyes | `SwapEyes` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right inputs. |

The Window Method (`WindowMethod`) and Stack Mode settings are also on the tool.

**See also:** Stereo Align, Disparity, Combiner, Anaglyph.

## New Eye (`Dimension.NewEye`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** NE · **Inputs:** `Input.Left`, `Input.Right` (Image) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

Builds a new eye between or beyond the two existing eyes, by interpolating with the disparity channels of the pair. The left and right outputs can be moved to any point along the disparity, so they can be set to a different eye separation, or one eye can be replaced with a warped copy of the other. It also works in Stack mode, where the two outputs carry the same image. New Eye destroys the disparity channels, so run Disparity again after it if they are needed.

**Use for:** changing the eye separation of a stereo pair, or fixing an error in one eye by replacing it with a warped version of the other.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Left: Enable | `Left.Enable` | Checkbox | 1 | Produces the left output. |
| Left: Lock XY | `Left.LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one interpolation factor for both axes. Off: separate X and Y factors. |
| Left: XY Interpolation Factor | `Left.FactorXY` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Where the left eye sits along the disparity. Shown when Lock XY is on. |
| Left: X and Y Interpolation Factor | `Left.FactorX`, `Left.FactorY` | Number | 0 (-1 to 1) | Shown when Lock XY is off. |
| Left: Depth Ordering | `Left.DepthOrdering` | ID combo | `"SmallestDisparityOntop"` | Which surface draws on top: `"LargestDisparityOntop"` or `"SmallestDisparityOntop"`. |
| Left: Clamp Edges, Edge Softness | `Left.ClampEdges`, `Left.ClampSoftness` | Checkbox, Number | 0, 0.01 (0 to 0.1) | Fills the transparent gaps at the frame edges. The softness is shown when Clamp Edges is on. |
| Left: Warp directions | `Left.EnableWarp.LeftForward`, `Left.EnableWarp.RightForward`, `Left.EnableWarp.LeftBackward`, `Left.EnableWarp.RightBackward` | Checkbox | 1, 1, 0, 0 | Which eye and which disparity direction contribute. Ticked ones are blended. |
| Right | (`Right.Enable`, `Right.FactorXY` and so on) | | | The same controls as Left, for the right output, with the interpolation factors at 1. |
| Refine Edges | `RefineEdges.Enable`, `RefineEdges.HiQOnly`, `RefineEdges.Strength`, `RefineEdges.Radius` | Checkbox, Number | 0, 1, 0.001, 0.01 | Refines the edges of the new eye. |
| Swap Eyes | `SwapEyes` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right inputs. |

**See also:** Stereo Align, Disparity, Global Align, Smooth Motion.

## Splitter (`Splitter`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** Spl · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, a stacked stereo image) · **Outputs:** `Image1` (left eye), `Image2` (right eye) (Image)

Splits a stacked stereo image into its two eyes. It is the reverse of the Combiner: the stacked image goes in, and the left and right eye images come out as two separate outputs. Each output is half the size of the input along the stacking direction. Splitter is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** taking a stacked stereo image, such as an EXR from another package or a Combiner result, and working on the eyes separately.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Split | `Split` | ID multi-button | `"Horiz"` | `"None"` (both outputs are the full input), `"Horiz"` (side by side, each output is half the width), `"Vert"` (stacked, each output is half the height) or `"Layers"` (the eyes are read from named layers). |
| Swap | `Swap` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right outputs. |
| Image 1 Layer, Image 2 Layer | `Image1Layer`, `Image2Layer` | Layer select | `":Auto"` | The layer for each eye. Shown when Split is Layers. |

The manual describes two outputs named Left and Right. The live outputs are `Image1` and `Image2`, and the manual's Layers option is also present. The outputs are used by ID, as in `split['Image1']`.

### Example

Working on the left eye of a stacked stereo image, from a separate image that holds both eyes:

```python
stacked = comp.AddTool('Background')    # stands in for a stacked stereo image
split = comp.AddTool('Splitter')
split.Input = stacked.Output
split.Split = 'Horiz'                   # side by side

left_eye = comp.AddTool('Blur')         # any tool; here it takes the left eye
left_eye.Input = split['Image1']
```

### Tips

- Split must match how the image was stacked: Horiz for side by side, Vert for stacked.
- Use Swap if the left and right eyes are reversed in the source.

**See also:** Combiner, Anaglyph, Stereo Align.

## Stereo Align (`Dimension.StereoAlign`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** SA · **Inputs:** `Input.Left`, `Input.Right` (Image) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

Corrects the common stereo problems in one node: the vertical alignment of one eye to the other, the convergence (where the eyes meet in depth), the eye separation, and the depth ordering at edges. It resamples the eyes once, so the image loses less quality than it would from several separate transforms. Like New Eye, it destroys the disparity channels, so run Disparity again afterwards if they are needed. Changing the eye separation can open holes that the other eye can't fill, which may need painting.

**Use for:** fixing vertical offsets, convergence and separation on a stereo pair, after the eyes are roughly aligned by Global Align.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vertical Alignment: Apply to | `VerticalAlignmentNest.ApplyTo` | Multi-button | 1: Right (0: Left, 2: Split) | Which eye the vertical shift is applied to. |
| Vertical Alignment: Mode | `VerticalAlignmentNest.Mode` | Multi-button | 1: Global Y (0: Per Pixel) | Per Pixel uses the disparity to align each pixel. Global Y applies one shift to the whole image. |
| Y Shift (pixels) | `VerticalAlignmentNest.ShiftY` | Number | 0 (-20 to 20) | Shown when Mode is Global Y. |
| Snap to Whole Pixels | `VerticalAlignmentNest.Snap` | Checkbox | 0 | Snaps the vertical shift to whole pixels. |
| Convergence: Apply to, X Shift (pixels) | `Convergence.ApplyTo`, `Convergence.Shift` | Multi-button, Number | 2: Split; 0 (-20 to 20) | Moves the convergence point. |
| Eye Separation: Apply to, Separation | `ApplyTo`, `Separation` | Multi-button, Number | 2: Both; 0 (-0.5 to 0.5) | Changes the distance between the eyes. |
| Left and Right: Depth Ordering, Clamp Edges | `Left.DepthOrdering`, `Right.DepthOrdering`, `Left.ClampEdges`, `Right.ClampEdges` | ID combo, Checkbox | `"SmallestDisparityOntop"`; 0 | Edge handling for each eye, as in New Eye. |
| Refine Edges | `RefineEdges.Enable` | Checkbox | 0 | Refines the edges of the output. |
| Swap Eyes | `SwapEyes` | Checkbox | 0 | Swaps the left and right inputs. |

The per-eye warp directions (`Left.EnableWarp.*`, `Right.EnableWarp.*`) are also on the tool, as in New Eye.

**See also:** New Eye, Global Align, Disparity, Combiner.

## Z To Disparity (`Dimension.ZToDisparity`)

**Category:** Stereo · **Short name:** Z2D · **Inputs:** `Input.Left`, `Input.Right` (Image), `Camera` (DataType3D, a stereo camera) · **Outputs:** `Output.Left`, `Output.Right` (Image)

Creates disparity channels from the Z channel of a stereo pair and a stereo camera. This gives a more accurate disparity than Disparity for CG renders, because the depth is known. The result is written into the disparity channels of each eye's output, ready for Stereo Align, New Eye or Smooth Motion. It is calculated during rendering, so it isn't verified here.

**Use for:** turning the Z pass of a CG stereo render into a disparity map.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output Disparity to RG | `OutputDisparityToRG` | Checkbox | 0 | Writes the disparity into the RG channels, to view it. |
| Refine Disparity: Enable | `RefineDisparity.Enable` | Checkbox | 0 | Refines the disparity edges. Shows the controls below when on. |
| HiQ Only, Strength, Radius | `RefineDisparity.HiQOnly`, `RefineDisparity.Strength`, `RefineDisparity.Radius` | Checkbox, Number | 1, 0.001 (0.0001 to 0.01), 0.01 (0.001 to 0.03) | Shown when Refine Disparity is on. |
| Camera | `Camera` | 3D input | | The stereo camera (a Camera 3D with eye separation, or a tracked L/R camera). |
| Camera Mode | `CameraMode` | Multi-button | 0: External (1: Artistic) | External uses the connected camera. Artistic uses the controls below. |
| Camera Selector | `CameraSelector` | ID combo | `"Default"` | Which camera to use, when the scene has more than one. |
| Convergence Point | `ConvergencePointZ` | Number | -1.5 (-10 to 0) | Artistic mode: the convergence depth. Shown in Artistic mode. |
| Background Disparity | `BackgroundDisparity` | Number | 64 (10 to 64) | Artistic mode: the disparity of the background. Shown in Artistic mode. |

Stack Mode, Swap Eyes and the layer names are also on the tool.

**See also:** Disparity To Z, Disparity, Stereo Align, Depth Blur.

## Camera Tracker (`Dimension.CameraTracker`)

**Category:** Tracking · **Short name:** CTra · **Inputs:** `ImageToTrack` (Image), `TrackMask` (Mask, excludes areas from tracking) · **Output:** `ImageOutput` (Image), `SceneOutput` (DataType3D: the solved camera and points)

Reconstructs the path of a live-action camera in 3D. It finds many features in the shot, tracks them, and solves for the camera's motion and lens, then exports the camera to a 3D scene that a Renderer 3D can use. It is a 3D analysis tool, and its work is done in the UI: tracking and solving run on the processed clip, which a scratch comp can't do.

**Use for:** placing 3D elements into a moving shot, with the camera matched to the plate, and for image planes or projections that need the solved camera.

**Workflow (UI):**
1. Connect the plate to `ImageToTrack`. Optionally connect a mask to `TrackMask` to exclude moving people, reflections and similar false tracks.
2. Set the camera (Camera tab): the focal length and film gate from the shot, and whether the pixel aspect comes from the source.
3. On the Track tab, press Auto Track (or Add User Track for features you pick), then check the tracks.
4. Press Solve (Solve tab). Repeat the cleanup cycle the manual describes: filter by track length and error, refine, solve again.
5. On the Export tab, set the scene transform (origin, orientation, scale) and the ground plane, then press Export. The result is on `SceneOutput`.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto Track | `AutoTrack` | Button | 0 | Finds and tracks features automatically over the render range. |
| Track Selected | `TrackSelected` | Button | 0 | Tracks the selected user tracks. |
| Detection Threshold | `DetectionThreshold` | Number | 2.2 (1.8–3) | How strongly a feature must stand out to be tracked. |
| Track Channel | `TrackChannel` | ID combo | `"Luminance"` | Channel the features are found in: `"Red"`, `"Green"`, `"Blue"` or `"Luminance"`. |
| Track Range | `TrackRange.Mode` | ID combo | `"Render"` | Frames to track: `"Render"`, `"Global"`, `"Valid"` or `"Custom"` (with `TrackRange.StartTime` and `EndTime`). |
| Bidirectional Tracking | `BidirectionalTracking` | Checkbox | 0 | Tracks each feature backwards as well, to lengthen tracks at the start. |
| Focal Length (mm) | `Camera.FocalLength` | Number | 25 (2.5–3500) | The lens focal length, to start the solve. |
| Film Gate | `Camera.FilmGate` | ID combo | `"BMD_URSA_4K_16x9"` | The sensor or film gate size. |
| Resolution Gate Fit | `Camera.ResolutionGateFit` | ID combo | `"Height"` | How the image fits the gate. |
| Use Source Pixel Aspect | `Camera.UseSourcePixelAspect` | Checkbox | 1 | Takes the pixel aspect from the source. |
| Auto Camera Planes | `Camera.AutoCameraPlanes` | Checkbox | 1 | Sets the near and far clip planes automatically. |
| Solve | `DoSolve` | Button | 0 | Solves the camera from the current tracks. |
| Delete | `DeleteSolve` | Button | 0 | Removes the solve. |
| Motion Type | `CameraMotionType` | ID combo | `"FreeCamera"` | The kind of motion the solve assumes: `"FreeCamera"`, `"PureRotation"`, `"Linear"` or `"Planar"`. |
| Accept Solve Error | `AcceptSolveError` | Number | 3 (0.1–20) | Largest solve error accepted for a track to be kept. |
| Clean Tracks By Filter | `CleanFilterTracks` | Button | 0 | Removes tracks that fail the track filters. |
| Maximum Track Error, Maximum Solve Error, Minimum Track Length | `TrackFiltering.MaximumTrackError`, `TrackFiltering.MaximumSolveError`, `TrackFiltering.MinimumTrackLength` | Number | 0.15, 2.5, 6 | The filter thresholds used by the clean-up steps. |
| Export | `RunExporter` | Button | 0 | Exports the solved camera to `SceneOutput`. |
| Auto Update Export After Solves | `UpdateOnSolve` | Checkbox | 1 | Refreshes the export after each solve. |
| Alignment | `SceneTransform.AlignmentMode` | ID combo | `"Aligned"` | Aligns the scene to the origin or leaves it `"Unaligned"`. |
| Scale | `SceneTransform.Scale.Scale` | Number | 1 (0.001–5) | Scale of the exported scene. |
| Show In View (ground plane) | `GroundPlane.Show` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows a ground plane in the viewer, for checking the solve. |

Verified in a scratch comp (settings only, no Auto Track or Solve): `Camera.FocalLength` 35, `Camera.FilmGate` `"ArriAlexa16x9"`, `TrackRange.Mode` `"Custom"` with Start 10 and End 80, and `ImageToTrack` connects, all read back. Solve and Export were not run.

Lens distortion (`k1`, `k2`, `k3`, `p1`, `p2`) and the other solve controls are on the Solve tab, with the workflow described above. The Solve tab's Refine button (`RefineSolve`) is marked "NYI" in the live tool.

### Example

Setting the camera from the lens data of the shot before tracking. The track and solve are then run in the UI:

```python
cam = comp.AddTool('Dimension.CameraTracker')
cam.ImageToTrack = plate.Output
cam['Camera.FocalLength'] = 35              # from the lens used on the shot
cam['Camera.FilmGate'] = 'ArriAlexa16x9'
cam['Camera.UseSourcePixelAspect'] = 1
```

### Tips

- Track and solve on a clip that has no moving people or reflections in the tracked area. Use `TrackMask` to exclude them where you can't avoid them.
- Solve error below 1.0 is good for HD content, and lower is needed for higher resolutions, as the manual states.
- Use `SceneOutput` in a Merge 3D with a Renderer 3D to render elements in the solved camera.

**See also:** Planar Tracker, Tracker, Surface Tracker, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Camera 3D.

## Planar Tracker (`Dimension.PlanarTracker`)

**Category:** Tracking · **Short name:** PTra · **Inputs:** `Background` (Image: the clip with the flat surface), `CornerPin1.Image` (Image: the foreground for Corner Pin mode), Effect Mask (blue, `EffectMask`, Mask), Occlusion Mask (`OcclusionMask`, Mask) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Tracks a flat surface, such as a sign, a licence plate or a wall, through a clip. It follows the surface's perspective as well as its position, so it's a better first choice than the point tracker for a plane. It has four modes: Track (produces the motion for a Planar Transform), Steady (removes the surface's motion, for painting or roto), Corner Pin (maps a foreground onto the surface) and Stabilize (smooths the clip's translation, rotation and scale). The tracking is done in the UI on the processed clip.

**Use for:** replacing a sign or screen, adding a poster to a wall, removing a flat surface's motion for paint, and stabilising a clip while keeping its intended camera move.

**Workflow (UI):**
1. Connect the clip to `Background`. Fix lens distortion first (a Lens Distort tool) if it's strong, because it makes the track slide.
2. Set Operation to Track. Move the playhead to the frame where the surface is largest and clearest, and press Set (Reference Time).
3. Draw the pattern (the region to track) on that frame. Use a closed polygon on the flat area that the subject won't pass over.
4. Optionally connect a mask to `OcclusionMask` for anything that covers the surface.
5. Press Track to End. Check the track by scrubbing in Steady mode.
6. Press Create Planar Transform, to make a Planar Transform (`Dimension.PlanarTransform`) that moves an image or mask with the track.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation Mode | `Operation` | ID combo | `"Track"` | `"Track"`, `"Steady"`, `"CornerPin"` or `"Stabilize"`. |
| Reference Time | `ReferenceTime` | Number | 0 (0–1000) | The frame the pattern is drawn on and tracking starts from. Set (`SetReferenceTimeToNow`) and Go (`GoToReferenceTime`) are buttons. |
| Pattern Center, Size | `Pattern.Center`, `Pattern.Size` | Point, Number | (0.5, 0.5), 1 (0–5) | Centre and size of the pattern. |
| Pattern Polygon | `Pattern.Polygon` | Polyline | none | The outline of the pattern to track, usually drawn in the viewer. It takes a Polyline dict (see *Value types* in Conventions); tracking a scripted pattern is not verified here. |
| Tracker | `TrackerType` | ID combo | `"Point"` | `"Point"` or `"Hybrid"`. The manual says a Hybrid track nearly always needs an occlusion mask. |
| Motion Type | `MotionType` | ID combo | `"Perspective"` | `"Translation"`, `"Euclidean"`, `"Similarity"`, `"Affine"` or `"Perspective"`. Perspective follows a plane's perspective. |
| Output | `OutputMode` | ID combo | `"Background"` | `"Background"`, `"BackgroundPreprocessed"`, `"Mask"` or `"MaskOverBackground"`. |
| Track Channel | `TrackChannel` | ID combo | `"Luminance"` | `"Red"`, `"Green"`, `"Blue"`, `"Luminance"` or `"Custom"` (with the Custom weights). |
| Track to Start, Track to End | `TrackToStart`, `TrackToEnd` | Button | 0 | Track backwards to the start or forwards to the end of the clip. |
| Track Fwd Then Reverse | `TrackBidirectional` | Button | 0 | Tracks forwards, then backwards from the reference frame. |
| Stop | `StopTracking` | Button | 0 | Stops the track. |
| Step to Previous, Next Frame | `TrackToPrevious`, `TrackToNext` | Button | 0 | Steps the track one frame. |
| Trim to Start, Delete, Trim to End | `TrimToStart`, `Delete`, `TrimToEnd` | Button | 0 | Removes the track before the playhead, all of it, or after the playhead. |
| Create Planar Transform | `CreatePlanarTransform` | Button | 0 | Creates a Planar Transform from the track. |
| Steady Time | `SteadyTime` | Number | 0 (0–1000) | The frame the steady view is held to, for Steady mode. |
| Invert Steady Transform | `InvertSteadyTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the steady transform. |
| Merge Mode | `CornerPinMergeMode` | Multi-button | 2: FG over BG (0: BG only, 1: FG only, 3: BG over FG) | How the corner-pinned foreground combines with the background. |
| Number Of Corner Pins | `NumberOfCornerPins` | Number | 1 (0–10) | Number of corner pin layers. Create and remove them with the `+` and `-` buttons. |
| Corner Pin 1 | `CornerPin1.Image`, `CornerPin1.Enable`, `CornerPin1.MappingType` | Image, Checkbox, Multi-button | Enable 1, Mapping 1: Perspective (0: Bi-Linear) | The foreground, its switch, and how it maps. Perspective is the correct choice for a plane. The four corners are `CornerPin1.TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomLeft` and `BottomRight` (Points). |
| Stabilize Method | `Stabilize.Method` | ID combo | `"Smoothing"` | `"Smoothing"`, `"FixedFrames"` or `"Cinematic"`. |
| Stabilize Parameters | `Stabilize.Parameters.Translation.X`, `Stabilize.Parameters.Translation.Y`, `Stabilize.Parameters.Rotation`, `Stabilize.Parameters.Scale` | Checkbox | 1 | Which motions are stabilised. |
| Smoothing Radius | `Stabilize.SmoothingRadius` | Number | 30 (0–100) | Frames each side of the current frame used to smooth the motion. |
| Compute Stabilization | `Stabilize.ComputeStabilization` | Button | 0 | Computes the stabilisation after tracking. |
| Frame Mode | `Stabilize.FrameMode` | ID combo | `"Full"` | `"Full"`, `"Crop"` or `"Zoom"`, for the frame edges left by stabilising. |

### Example

Setting up a Planar Tracker on a background and creating an image for corner pinning. The track itself is run in the UI:

```python
planar = comp.AddTool('Dimension.PlanarTracker')
planar.Background = plate.Output
planar.Operation = 'Track'                # the default; set it explicitly
planar.MotionType = 'Perspective'
planar.TrackerType = 'Point'
```

### Tips

- Draw the pattern on a clean, unoccluded plane. Keep it off the edge of the surface, and off the subject.
- Scrub in Steady mode to see jitter in the track. A track that jitters in Steady mode will jitter in the match move.
- When a track fails, go back to the last good frame and track again from there, rather than tracking through the failure.

**See also:** Planar Transform, Tracker, Camera Tracker, Surface Tracker, Merge, Lens Distort.

## Surface Tracker (`SurfaceTracker`)

**Category:** Tracking · **Short name:** SFt · **Inputs:** `Input` (yellow, Image: the surface to composite onto), `Overlay` (green, Image: the graphic or video to place on the surface), `OcclusionMask` (pink, Mask: regions not to track), Effect Mask (blue, `EffectMask`, Mask) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies a graphic or texture to a flexible, deforming surface such as cloth or skin. You define the area of the surface, a mesh of control points along its folds, track the surface through the clip, and the overlay is warped to follow the folds. It is the most involved tracker, and every step is done in the UI.

**Use for:** a logo on a shirt, a texture on a sheet, or an effect that must bend with a surface. It's not for flat surfaces: use the Planar Tracker for those.

**Workflow (UI):** the manual gives four steps, which the stage buttons (`ProcessStage`) follow in order:
1. **Bounds** (stage 0): click on the screen to define the area of the surface. Each bound should cover one surface, without crossing an object edge.
2. **Mesh** (stage 1): place the control points along the natural folds of the surface within the bounds.
3. **Track** (stage 2): analyse the surface through the clip with that mesh.
4. **Result** (stage 3): composite the overlay onto the moving mesh.

Changing the bounds or the mesh resets the tracking data, so track again after any change. The Tracked Range (`TrackedRange`) shows the start and end frames that hold tracking data.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Process Stage | `ProcessStage` | Multi-button | 1: Mesh (0: Bounds, 2: Track, 3: Result) | Selects the step above, and which step's controls the Inspector shows. Values set for the other steps are kept. |
| Tracked Range | `TrackedRange` | Point | (−1, −1), read only | Start and end frames with tracking data. |
| Track Forward, Track Reverse | `TrackForward`, `TrackReverse` | Button | 0 | Tracks the surface from the current frame forward, or back. Track Fwd Then Reverse (`TrackBidirectional`) and Track Forward/Reverse One Frame are the other transport buttons. |
| Stop Tracking | `StopTracking` | Button | 0 | Stops the track. |
| Remove Tracking Data | `RemoveTrackingDataBeforeThisFrame`, `RemoveTrackingDataAtThisFrame`, `RemoveTrackingDataAfterThisFrame` | Button | 0 | Remove the track before, at, or after the current frame. |
| Bound actions | `BoundaryActionsBounds`, `BoundaryActionsHoles`, `BoundaryActionsDelete`, `BoundaryActionsClear` | Button | 0 | Add a bound, add a hole, delete the selected bound, or clear all bounds. |
| Point Locations | `PointLocations` | ID combo | `"MeshPointLocationAuto"` | `"MeshPointLocationAuto"` places points along the features, `"MeshPointLocationUniform"` spaces them evenly. |
| Point Number Limit | `PointNumberLimit` | Number | 50 (10–200) | Most mesh points allowed. |
| Minimum Point Spacing | `MinPointSpacing` | Number | 10 (5–50) | Closest spacing between points, in pixels. |
| Horizontal, Vertical Spacing | `HorizontalSpacing`, `VerticalSpacing` | Number | 25, 25 (10–100) | Spacing of the uniform grid, in pixels. |
| Motion Range | `MotionRange` | Number | 0.1 (0–1) | How far a point may move between frames. A fast-moving surface needs more. |
| Mesh Rigidity | `MeshRigidity` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | How rigidly the mesh holds its shape. |
| Quality | `TrackingQuality` | ID combo | `"TrackingQualityFaster"` | `"TrackingQualityFaster"` or `"TrackingQualityBetter"`. |
| Output | `WarpOperation` | ID combo | `"WarpOperation2Onto1"` | The warp operation applied to the result: `"WarpOperation2Onto1"`, `"WarpOperationWarp2"`, `"WarpOperationAlpha"`, `"WarpOperationMaskOut"`, `"WarpOperationStabilize"` or `"WarpOperationRewarp"`. The manual does not describe the individual operations; the default is the Result stage. |
| Overlay / Alpha Source | `OverlaySource` | ID combo | `"OverlayFrameEach"` | Which frame of the overlay is used: `"OverlayFrameFirst"`, `"OverlayFrameReference"` or `"OverlayFrameEach"`. |
| Contract / Expand | `EdgeExpansion` | Number | 0 (−0.5 to 1) | Grows or shrinks the overlay's edge. |
| Softness | `EdgeSoftness` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Softens the overlay's edge. |
| Motion Blur | `MotionBlur` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Blurs the overlay with the motion of the surface. |
| Positioning | `CanvasControlMode` | ID combo | `"CanvasControlModeCanvas"` | How the overlay is placed: `"CanvasControlModeSliders"`, `"CanvasControlModeCanvas"` or `"CanvasControlModePins"`. |
| Position X, Position Y, Zoom, Rotate | `SliderPan`, `SliderTilt`, `SliderZoom`, `SliderRotate` | Number | 0, 0, 1, 0 | Overlay placement, when Positioning is Sliders. |
| Width, Height, Pitch, Yaw | `SliderScaleX`, `SliderScaleY`, `SliderPitch`, `SliderYaw` | Number | 1, 1, 0, 0 | Overlay size and perspective. |
| Flip | `IsFlipHorizontal`, `IsFlipVertical` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirrors the overlay. |
| Composite Type | `CompositeType` | Combo | 0: Normal (1: Add, 2: Subtract, 3: Difference, 4: Multiply, 5: Screen, and 20 more) | Blend mode for the overlay. |
| Overlay Opacity | `OverlayOpacity` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Opacity of the overlay. |
| Antialiasing | `OverlayAntialiasing` | Number | 1 (0–1.2) | Anti-aliasing of the overlay's edges. |

Overlay placement follows the Positioning mode: Sliders, Canvas or Pins. `OverlayGoToReference` (Go To Reference) and `OverlayRefSetToCurr` (Set To Current) are buttons that move to, or set, the reference frame.

### Example

Setting up a surface track's first two steps from a script. The bounds, mesh and tracking are clicked in the viewer, so they aren't scripted here:

```python
surf = comp.AddTool('SurfaceTracker')
surf.Input = shirt_plate.Output             # the surface to composite onto
surf.Overlay = logo.Output                  # the logo to place on it
surf.ProcessStage = 1                       # show the Mesh stage (the other stages' settings below are kept)
surf.PointNumberLimit = 80
surf.MotionRange = 0.15
surf.WarpOperation = 'WarpOperation2Onto1'
```

### Tips

- Keep each bound on one surface and clear of object edges. Add holes for anything on the surface that should not be covered, such as buttons.
- Track in short sections on clothing that folds quickly, and check the mesh in the viewer after each one.
- The overlay is placed in the reference frame first. Set the reference frame (`OverlayRefSetToCurr`) on the frame where the logo looks right flat before tracking.

**See also:** Planar Tracker, Tracker, Camera Tracker, Merge, Lens Distort.

## Tracker (`Tracker`)

**Category:** Tracking · **Short name:** Tra · **Inputs:** `Input` (yellow, Image: the image to track), `Foreground` (Image: the image moved by the result), Effect Mask (blue, `EffectMask`, Mask) · **Output:** `Output` (Image), plus published outputs (see Outputs)

The point tracker. It follows one or more small patterns through a clip and stores the paths. It can apply the result itself, as a match move, stabilisation, corner positioning or perspective positioning, or publish the paths so that other tools' controls can connect to them. Used in line, it also acts as a Merge. Used as a branch, it only holds tracking data.

**Use for:** stabilising a shot, match moving an element to a moving object, placing an image in the corners of a sign, removing perspective from a flat area, and making a mask, text or effect follow a point.

**Setup:** connect the image to track to `Input`. Only `Input` is analysed, even if a `Foreground` is connected. Tracking is run in the UI (see Scripting limits).

**Operation and Merge:** `Operation` decides what happens to the `Foreground`: `"None"` (0) only tracks; `"Match Move"` (1) moves it along the path; `"Corner Positioning"` (2) maps its corners to four patterns; `"Perspective Positioning"` (3) uses four patterns to remove perspective. `Merge` chooses the inputs combined: BG only (0, for stabilising the background), FG only (1), FG over BG (2, the default) or BG over FG (3).

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | `Operation` | Multi-button | 0: None (1: Match Move, 2: Corner Positioning, 3: Perspective Positioning) | What the tracker does with the foreground. Corner and Perspective need four patterns. |
| Merge | `Merge` | Multi-button | 2: FG over BG (0: BG only, 1: FG only, 3: BG over FG) | Which inputs the result combines. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 0: Black (1: Wrap, 2: Duplicate, 3: Mirror) | What fills the frame where the moved image leaves it. |
| Mapping type | `MappingType` | Multi-button | 1: Perspective (0: Bi-Linear) | How corner positioning maps the foreground. |
| Corner patterns | `TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomLeft`, `BottomRight` | Combo | 0, 1, 2, 3 | Which pattern drives each corner. The list holds the pattern names. |
| Reference Time | `Reference` | Multi-button | 1: Start Time (0: Select Time, 2: Start & End, 3: End Time, 4: Custom Time) | The frame the image is stabilised to. `"Start & End"` smooths the motion instead, with `ReferenceIntermediatePoints` (0–10) setting how much of the curve remains. |
| Position, Rotation, Scaling | `Position`, `Rotation`, `Scaling` | Checkbox | 1 | Which parts of the motion are applied or corrected. |
| Pivot type | `PivotType` | Multi-button | 0: Tracker average (1: Selected tracker, 2: Manual) | The point stabilising or match moving rotates and scales about. `Tracker` picks the pattern; `Pivot` (Point, default centre) is used for Manual. |
| Adaptive Mode | `AdaptiveMode` | Multi-button | 0: None (1: Every Frame, 2: Best match) | How the pattern is reacquired during a track. `Every Frame` suits a pattern that changes shape; `Best match` ignores a transient shadow. |
| Path Center | `PathCenter` | Multi-button | 0: Pattern Center (1: Track Center (Append)) | Track Center (Append) picks a new pattern after the first leaves the frame and joins the paths. |
| Add Point | `AddPointTracker` | Button | 0 | Adds a point pattern. Setting it to 1 and back to 0 adds `Point 2` (verified). |
| Add IntelliTrack | `AddIntelliTrack` | Button | 0 | Adds an IntelliTrack (DaVinci Neural Engine). Setting it adds `IntelliTrack 3` after the others (verified). |
| Name, Enabled, Delete | `Name1`, `Enabled1`, `Delete1` | Text, Checkbox, Checkbox | `"IntelliTrack 1"`, 1, 0 | Name (settable: `trk.Name1 = 'Ray Gun Tip'` reads back), whether the pattern re-tracks, and delete. |
| Pattern Center | `PatternCenter1` | Point | (0.25, 0.75) | Centre of the pattern box. The pattern number replaces the 1 in the ID. |
| Pattern Width, Height | `PatternWidth1`, `PatternHeight1` | Number | 0.03 and 0.0534 (0.001–0.5) | Pattern box size, relative to image width. (Registered default 0.05; a new instance shows these values.) |
| Search Width, Height | `SearchWidth1`, `SearchHeight1` | Number | 0.125 (0.001–0.5) | Search area. A fast-moving pattern needs a larger one. |
| Tracked Center | `TrackedCenter1` | Point | (0.25, 0.75) | The pattern's position at the current frame. |
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset1`, `YOffset1` | Number | 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Offset of the output position from the pattern centre. |
| Track Forward, Track Reverse | `TrackForward`, `TrackReverse` | Button | 0 | Start a track from the render range start or end. Others: `TrackForwardFromCurrentTime`, `TrackReverseFromCurrentTime`, `TrackBidirectional`. |
| Stop Tracking | `StopTracking` | Button | 0 | Stops the track. |
| Trim to Start, Trim to End, Delete | `TrimToStart`, `TrimToEnd`, `Delete` | Button | 0 | Remove tracking data before the playhead, after it, or all of it. |

The Trackers list and the Operation, Position and Pivot controls are in the Inspector. Patterns 2 to 4 (`Name2`, `PatternCenter2` and so on) appear in the dump with Operation set to Corner Positioning or Perspective Positioning. Verified: with Operation 3 (Perspective), `Name2`, `Name3` and `Name4` read back as `IntelliTrack 2`, `IntelliTrack 3` and `IntelliTrack 4`, and with Operation 2 the same. With Operation 0 they only exist once added with the Add buttons.

### Outputs

Each pattern and the tracker as a whole publish results that other controls can connect to, with no wire to the Tracker. In the UI, use the control's Connect To menu.

- `Position1`: the offset position of pattern 1, the path the pattern follows. `PositionX1` and `PositionY1` give its X and Y as numbers.
- `PerspectivePosition1`, `PerspectivePositionX1`, `PerspectivePositionY1`: the perspective-corrected position.
- `SteadyPosition1` and `UnsteadyPosition1`: the inverse of the motion (for stabilising) and the motion added back.
- `SteadyPosition`, `UnsteadyPosition`, `SteadyAxis`, `SteadySize`, `UnsteadySize`, `SteadyAngle`, `UnsteadyAngle`: the same for the tracker as a whole, using all its patterns and the Match Move settings. Angle and size need at least two patterns.

The dump lists outputs for pattern 1 only. Verified: after `AddPointTracker` (with Operation 2), `Position2` and `SteadyPosition2` connect to a Point input; `PositionX2` (a Number) did not connect to a Point input, which is expected for a type mismatch and was not tested against a Number input. Patterns 3 and 4 are assumed to follow the same naming.

### Example

Making a mask follow a tracked point. Only `Input`, the name and the connection are scripted; the track itself is run in the UI:

```python
trk = comp.AddTool('Tracker')
trk.Input = plate.Output                    # the image that is tracked (the yellow input)
trk.Operation = 0                           # None: track only, and publish the path
trk.Name1 = 'Ray Gun Tip'                   # easier to find in the Connect To menu

ellipse = comp.AddTool('EllipseMask')
ellipse.Width = 0.06
ellipse.Height = 0.06
ellipse.Center = trk.Position1              # the mask follows pattern 1
```

### Tips

- In the UI, keep the pattern on one plane and make the search area larger than the pattern's movement between frames.
- One pattern stabilises position, two add rotation, three or more add scale. Corner and perspective work needs four.
- The Track modifier (`TrackerModifier`, see Track) follows one pattern into a single control, without a Tracker node.

### Scripting limits

- **Tracking can't be started from a script in a scratch comp.** The transport buttons are Number inputs that act like buttons, and a scratch comp can't process frames. They were not pressed during testing. Run tracks in the UI.
- Connections, names, pattern positions and the Add buttons were tested in a scratch comp: `Center` from `Position1` and from `SteadyPosition` connects, `ConnectInput` does too, and a tracker's main Output does not connect to a Point input. Nothing was tracked, so the connected path stays empty until a track is run in the UI.

**See also:** Planar Tracker, Camera Tracker, Surface Tracker, Track, Ellipse Mask, Transform, Merge, Magic Mask.

## Camera Shake (`CameraShake`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** CShk · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Moves and rotates the image with a simulated handheld or mechanical camera shake. It is not a modifier, and it doesn't
drive other parameters: it moves the picture itself. Deviation sets how far the image can move on each axis, Speed sets
how fast it shakes, and Frequency Method sets the shape of the motion. Camera Shake joins with adjacent transform tools
for better quality.

**Use for:** handheld feel on locked-off footage, impact and vibration shakes, and shake on a graphic that should look
as if it was filmed on a camera.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Deviation, Y Deviation | `XDeviation`, `YDeviation` | Number | 0.2, 0.2 (0–1) | Shake on each axis. 1.0 can place the image anywhere within the frame. |
| Rotation Deviation | `RotationDeviation` | Number | 0.2 (0–1) | Shake around the rotation axis. |
| Randomness | `Randomness` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Higher values make the movement more irregular. Lower values make it more predictable. |
| Overall Strength | `OverallStrength` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Scales all the deviations, and blends the shake in and out. 1 applies the settings as given. |
| Speed | `Speed` | Number | 0.8 (0–1) | Rate of the shake. |
| Frequency Method | `FrequencyMethod` | Multi-button | 0: Sine, 1: Rectified Sine, 2: Square Wave | Shape of the shake. Square Wave looks mechanical. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor, 1: Box, 2: Linear, 3: Quadratic, 4: Cubic, 5: Catmull-Rom, 6: Gaussian, 7: Mitchell, 8: Lanczos, 9: Sinc, 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter when the image is moved. |
| Window Method | `WindowMethod` | Combo | 0: Hanning (1: Hamming, 2: Blackman, 3: Kaiser) | Window used with the Sinc and Bessel filters. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 0: Canvas, 1: Wrap, 2: Duplicate, 3: Mirror | What fills the frame where the shake reveals an empty edge. |
| Invert Transform | `InvertTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the transform. Useful with tracker data. |

### Example

A subtle handheld wobble on a locked-off plate, with the edges mirrored so no black is revealed:

```python
shake = comp.AddTool('CameraShake')
shake.Input = media_in.Output
shake.XDeviation = 0.03
shake.YDeviation = 0.03
shake.RotationDeviation = 0.01
shake.Randomness = 0.3
shake.Speed = 0.5
shake.Edges = 3                  # Mirror
```

### Tips

- **Start small.** A deviation around 0.02 to 0.05 suits a handheld look. Values near 1.0 make the picture swing
  across the whole frame.
- **Use Edges.** Canvas reveals black or transparent edges at the sides of the frame. Mirror or Wrap avoids that without
  a Crop.
- **Mask the shake** with the Effect Mask to shake only part of the frame, for example a window or a screen.

**See also:** Transform, Crop, DVE, Letterbox, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Crop (`Crop`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** Crp · **Inputs:** Input (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Cuts out a rectangle of the image, or places the image in a larger or smaller frame by offsetting it. Unlike a mask,
Crop changes the resolution of the image, so everything downstream works at the new size. Sizes and offsets are in pixels.

**Use for:** trimming unwanted edges, cutting out a region before a Merge so the output resolution matches, and
offsetting a plate so it sits inside a new frame.

**Resolution:** Crop sets the resolution of the image it passes on. The Merge or other tool that takes the Background
connection decides the final resolution, so crop the Background to set the output size.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset`, `YOffset` | Number | 0, 0 (slider −1000 to 1000) | Moves the image in pixels. The cropped area moves over it. Values are whole pixels. |
| X Size, Y Size | `XSize`, `YSize` | Number | Frame width and height, 1920 and 1080 by default (slider 1–4096) | Output size in pixels. Values are rounded to whole pixels, and the hard limit is 32767. |
| Reset Size | `ResetSize` | Button | | Sets the size back to the input's size. The result depends on the input image's dimensions, so it takes effect when the comp renders. |
| Reset Offset | `ResetOffset` | Button | | Sets the offsets back to 0. |
| Keep Aspect | `KeepAspect` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps the input's aspect ratio when the size changes. Like Reset Size, it works from the input image's dimensions, so its effect shows when the comp renders. |
| Keep Centered | `KeepCentered` | Checkbox | 0 | Adjusts the offsets automatically so the crop stays centred. |
| Change Pixel Aspect | `ChangePixelAspect` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows `PixelAspect`. |
| Pixel Aspect | `PixelAspect` | Point | (1, 1) | Pixel aspect ratio, shown when Change Pixel Aspect is on. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | `"None"` or `"Frame"`. Frame gives the full frame; None applies no clipping. |

The Auto Crop page has an **Auto Crop** button (`AutoCrop`) that crops to the non-black or non-transparent area. It needs
the image to be processed, so it can't be checked from a script.

### Example

A 16:9 crop of a 4:3 plate, for a wide title card:

```python
crop = comp.AddTool('Crop')
crop.Input = media_in.Output
crop.XSize = 1440
crop.YSize = 810
crop.KeepCentered = 1            # keeps the crop centred on the image
```

### Tips

- **Don't animate Crop.** Crop changes the resolution, so keyframing the sizes makes the frame size change. The manual
  advises against it. To move or reveal an image over time, use Transform or Merge instead.
- **Crop or mask.** To hide part of the image but keep the frame size, use a mask. Crop only when the resolution should change.

**See also:** Letterbox, Resize, Scale, Transform, Merge.

## DVE (`DVE`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** DVE · **Inputs:** Input (orange), DVE Mask (white), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

A 3D image transform in the style of an online tape-based effects system. It rotates the image around a pivot on the
X, Y and Z axes, moves it in Z to zoom, adds perspective, and positions it in the frame. Unlike Transform, DVE can tilt
a picture into space, so it reads as a flip or a turn rather than a flat move. The DVE Mask input pre-masks the image,
before the transform, so only part of it moves.

**Use for:** flips, spins and tumbles of a clip or graphic, push-and-pull zooms with Z Move, and a picture that turns
away to reveal the next scene.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the image on screen. |
| Pivot | `Pivot` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The point the image rotates and scales around. |
| Z Pivot | `ZPivot` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Pivot position along Z. |
| Z Move | `ZMove` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Zooms the image along Z. Visually, it looks like an object moving towards or away from the viewer. |
| Rotation Order | `RotationOrder` | Multi-button | 5: ZYX (0: XYZ, 1: XZY, 2: YXZ, 3: YZX, 4: ZXY, 5: ZYX) | Order in which the X, Y and Z rotations are applied. |
| X Rotation, Y Rotation, Z Rotation | `XRotation`, `YRotation`, `ZRotation` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180°) | Rotation about each axis, around the Pivot. |
| Perspective | `Perspective` | Number | 1 (slider 0.00001–100) | Adds perspective to rotations on the X or Y axis, like changing a camera's field of view and zoom. |
| X Shear, Y Shear | `XShear`, `YShear` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Shear of the image on each axis. |
| Black Background | `BlackBackground` | Checkbox | 0 | Erases the area outside the DVE Mask, before the transform. |
| Fill Black | `FillBlack` | Checkbox | 0 | Erases the area inside the DVE Mask from the input, which cuts the masked area out. With Black Background, only the masked, transformed area shows. |
| Alpha Mode | `AlphaMode` | Multi-button | 2: Additive (0: Ignore Alpha, 1: Subtractive, 2: Additive) | How the transformed image is merged over the untransformed input. Additive suits premultiplied images, which is most Fusion images. Subtractive suits images that are not premultiplied. Ignore Alpha makes the masked area opaque. |
| DVE Mask | `DVEMask` | Mask input | | Pre-masks the image before the transform. Shown on the Masking tab. |

### Example

A quarter turn about the vertical axis over one second at 24 fps, so the clip turns edge-on and away:

```python
dve = comp.AddTool('DVE')
dve.Input = media_in.Output
dve.YRotation = comp.BezierSpline()
dve.YRotation[0] = 0
dve.YRotation[24] = 90
```

### Tips

- **Set the pivot before rotating.** Rotations happen about `Pivot`. Moving the pivot to an edge of the image makes a
  flip that hinges on that edge, rather than one about the middle.
- **Use Perspective with rotations.** Perspective sets how strongly a rotation on Y or X recedes into depth. The default
  of 1 is a moderate effect; raise it for a stronger turn.
- **Mask before turning.** The DVE Mask limits the transform to part of the image, which is useful for a page turn or a
  wipe that turns a section of the frame.

**See also:** Transform, Merge, Letterbox, Camera Shake, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Letterbox (`Letterbox`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** Lbx · **Inputs:** Input (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Fits a widescreen or film image into a frame of another size and aspect ratio. In Letterbox mode the whole picture is
shown, and black bars are added where the aspect differs. In Pan-and-Scan mode the picture fills the height and is
cropped at the sides, and Center chooses which part is visible. Like Crop and Resize, Letterbox changes the image's
resolution.

**Use for:** converting a cinema or film plate to an HD or UHD frame, showing a 2.39:1 image on a 16:9 timeline, and
pan-and-scan reframing of a wide shot.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 1920, 1080 (slider 1–4096) | Output size in pixels. Hard limit 32767. |
| Auto Resolution | `UseFrameFormatSettings` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the frame format for Width and Height. |
| Pixel Aspect | `PixelAspect` | Point | (1, 1) | Pixel aspect ratio of the output. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Visible part of the image in Pan-and-Scan mode. It has no effect in Letterbox mode. |
| Mode | `Mode` | Multi-button | 0: Letterbox / Envelope, 1: Pan-and-Scan | Letterbox / Envelope corrects the aspect and fits the width. Pan-and-Scan fits the height and crops the sides. |
| Only Use Filter in HiQ | `HiQOnly` | Checkbox | 0 | Uses the selected filter only in HiQ renders. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor, 1: Box, 2: Linear, 3: Quadratic, 4: Cubic, 5: Catmull-Rom, 6: Gaussian, 7: Mitchell, 8: Lanczos, 9: Sinc, 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter. |
| Window Method | `WindowMethod` | Combo | 0: Hanning (1: Hamming, 2: Blackman, 3: Kaiser) | Window for the Sinc and Bessel filters. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Frame"` | `"None"` or `"Frame"`. |

### Example

A 2.39:1 cinema plate fitted into a 1920 x 1080 HD frame, with bars added top and bottom:

```python
lb = comp.AddTool('Letterbox')
lb.Input = media_in.Output
lb.Width = 1920
lb.Height = 1080
lb.Mode = 0                      # Letterbox / Envelope
```

For a reframe that fills the height, set `Mode` to 1 and animate `Center` with `comp.PolyPath()` to pan across the picture.

### Tips

- **Choose the mode by what must stay visible.** Letterbox keeps the full picture with bars. Pan-and-Scan fills the
  frame and loses the sides, so use it only when the sides can go.
- **The output size comes from this tool.** `Width` and `Height` set the new size, not the input. A Merge that takes the
  Background from this tool gets the new size.
- **Use Resize for a plain change of size.** Resize changes the size without fitting the aspect, and Letterbox fits it.

**See also:** Crop, Resize, Scale, Transform, Camera Shake.

## Planar Transform (`Dimension.PlanarTransform`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** PXf · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Moves the image so that it follows a plane tracked by a Planar Tracker. The tracker's result is a matrix that this tool
applies to its input on each frame. The tool has few controls of its own: the motion comes from the track, which is made
in the Planar Tracker in the UI.

**Use for:** keeping a graphic, or a Corner Positioner pin, on a surface that moves in the shot, such as a sign or a
screen, once a Planar Tracker has tracked it.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scale to Source | `ScaleToSource` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales the transformed image to match the source plane. |
| Clipping Mode | `TransformClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Domain"` | `"Domain"` or `"Frame"`. |

The track is shown as a Matrix (`Track`) in the Inspector and is not set from a script. It comes from a Planar Tracker that
has been tracked in the UI. The tool's reference time is shown on the tool as a label.

### Tips

- **Track first.** Make the planar track in the Planar Tracker in the UI. This tool has nothing to track by itself.
- **Pair with Corner Positioner.** The manual describes a Planar Transform keeping a Corner Positioner in place as the
  background moves, after which the Planar Tracker can be deleted.

**See also:** Transform, Corner Positioner, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Resize (`BetterResize`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** Rsz · **Inputs:** Input (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Changes the resolution of an image to an exact width and height in pixels. Unlike Transform, which moves and scales the
picture inside the same frame, Resize changes the frame itself. Its registered name is BetterResize; it appears as
Resize in the Inspector and the manual.

**Use for:** converting a plate between formats (film to video, UHD to HD), making a graphic the size of a delivery
frame, and setting the working resolution of a branch of the comp.

**Resolution:** Resize sets the resolution of the image it passes on, which is what a Merge's Background uses. Connect
the resized image as the Background to set the output size.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width, Height | `Width`, `Height` | Number | 1920, 1080 (slider 1–4096) | New size in pixels. Hard limit 32767. |
| Auto Resolution | `UseFrameFormatSettings` | Checkbox | 0 | When on, Width and Height are set from the frame format (the Fusion preferences, or the Resolve timeline). |
| Reset Size | `ResetSize` | Button | | Sets the size back to the input image's size. |
| Keep Frame Aspect | `KeepAspect` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps the input's aspect ratio when the size changes. Shown when Auto Resolution is off. |
| Only Use Filter in HiQ | `HiQOnly` | Checkbox | 0 | On: non-HiQ renders use the fast Nearest Neighbor filter. Off: the selected filter is used for every render. |
| Change Pixel Aspect | `ChangePixelAspect` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows `PixelAspect`. |
| Pixel Aspect | `PixelAspect` | Point | (1, 1) | Pixel aspect ratio, shown when Change Pixel Aspect is on. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor, 1: Box, 2: Linear, 3: Quadratic, 4: Cubic, 5: Catmull-Rom, 6: Gaussian, 7: Mitchell, 8: Lanczos, 9: Sinc, 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter. |
| Window Method | `WindowMethod` | Combo | 0: Hanning (1: Hamming, 2: Blackman, 3: Kaiser) | Window for the Sinc and Bessel filters. |

### Example

Downsizing a UHD plate to HD:

```python
rsz = comp.AddTool('BetterResize')
rsz.Input = media_in.Output
rsz.UseFrameFormatSettings = 0   # set the size yourself
rsz.Width = 1920
rsz.Height = 1080
```

### Tips

- **Check the aspect.** Resize does not keep the aspect unless Keep Frame Aspect is on. Going from 4:3 to 16:9 stretches
  the picture if it is left off.
- **Filter for downscaling.** Catmull-Rom gives a sharper result when an image is made smaller. Linear is a neutral default.
- **Scale for a multiplier.** Scale sets a factor such as 0.5 rather than a fixed size.

**See also:** Scale, Letterbox, Crop, Transform, Merge.

## Scale (`Scale`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** Scl · **Inputs:** Input (orange) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Changes the resolution of an image by a multiplier. 1 leaves the image as it is, 2 doubles it, and 0.5 halves it. Like
Resize, Scale changes the frame size rather than the picture within it. The difference is that Scale works from a
relative size, so it needs no target resolution.

**Use for:** making a half-resolution proxy of a plate for faster working, and scaling a branch of the comp by a known ratio.

**Resolution:** Scale sets the resolution of the image it passes on, so connect the scaled image as the Background of a
Merge to set the output size.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock X/Y | `LockXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Size, applied to both axes. Off: separate X and Y sizes. |
| Size | `XSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Multiplier of the input resolution, with Lock X/Y on. The ID is `XSize` even though the Inspector labels it Size. |
| Y Size | `YSize` | Number | 1 (slider 0–5) | Vertical multiplier, shown when Lock X/Y is off. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 1: Duplicate (0: Canvas) | How the frame edges are filled when the scaling reduces the image. |
| Only Use Filter in HiQ | `HiQOnly` | Checkbox | 0 | As on Resize: on, non-HiQ renders use the fast Nearest Neighbor filter. |
| Change Pixel Aspect | `ChangePixelAspect` | Checkbox | 0 | Shows `PixelAspect`. |
| Pixel Aspect | `PixelAspect` | Point | (1, 1) | Pixel aspect ratio, shown when Change Pixel Aspect is on. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor, 1: Box, 2: Linear, 3: Quadratic, 4: Cubic, 5: Catmull-Rom, 6: Gaussian, 7: Mitchell, 8: Lanczos, 9: Sinc, 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter. |
| Window Method | `WindowMethod` | Combo | 0: Hanning (1: Hamming, 2: Blackman, 3: Kaiser) | Window for the Sinc and Bessel filters. |

### Example

A half-resolution proxy of a plate:

```python
half = comp.AddTool('Scale')
half.Input = media_in.Output
half.XSize = 0.5                 # Lock X/Y is on, so this sets both axes
```

### Tips

- **Scale is relative.** A `XSize` of 2 on a 1920 x 1080 input gives 3840 x 2160, whatever the input size is. Use
  Resize when the output size is fixed.
- **Unlock for a stretch.** Clear Lock X/Y and set `XSize` and `YSize` separately to change the aspect as well as the size.
- **Edges matters only when shrinking.** Edges fills the gap a reduced image leaves at the frame edge.

**See also:** Resize, Letterbox, Crop, Transform, Merge.

## Transform (`Transform`)

**Category:** Transform · **Short name:** Xf · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Moves, rotates, scales, flips and stretches a 2D image, without changing the image's resolution. Unlike a Resize or
Scale tool, it doesn't change the frame's size, and the Edges setting decides what fills the frame where the image doesn't
cover it. The manual says adjacent Transform nodes are concatenated with each other.

**Use for:** moving, scaling, rotating or flipping a clip or graphic, slow push-ins and drifts, and shaping a plate
before it is merged. Use Merge's own position controls when only one foreground is layered.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Position of the image. |
| Pivot | `Pivot` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The point the image rotates and scales around. |
| Use Size and Aspect | `UseSizeAndAspect` | Checkbox | 1 | On: `Size` and `Aspect` apply. Off: `XSize` and `YSize` apply. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Uniform scale. Used when Use Size and Aspect is on. |
| Aspect | `Aspect` | Number | 1 (0.01–5) | Stretches the image between X and Y, with Use Size and Aspect on. |
| X Size, Y Size | `XSize`, `YSize` | Number | 1, 1 (0–5) | Separate scale on each axis, with Use Size and Aspect off. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 0 (0–360°) | Rotation about the Pivot. |
| Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical | `FlipHoriz`, `FlipVert` | Checkbox | 0 | Mirror the image. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 0: Canvas, 1: Wrap, 2: Duplicate, 3: Mirror | What fills the frame outside a moved or shrunken image. |
| Filter Method | `FilterMethod` | Combo | 2: Linear (0: Nearest Neighbor, 1: Box, 3: Quadratic … 10: Bessel) | Resampling filter. Linear is the default. |
| Invert Transform | `InvertTransform` | Checkbox | 0 | Inverts the transform. Useful with tracker data. |

### Example

A slow push-in on a clip over two seconds at 24 fps. Scaling is keyed on the Transform, so the clip's resolution stays
the same:

```python
push = comp.AddTool('Transform')
push.Input = comp.MediaIn1.Output
push.Size = comp.BezierSpline()
push.Size[0] = 1.0
push.Size[48] = 1.1
```

### Tips

- **Scale with Size, or split it.** Keep `UseSizeAndAspect` on for an even scale. Turn it off to set `XSize` and `YSize`
  separately, for example to stretch a picture to a new aspect.
- **Fill the empty edges.** When the image is scaled down or moved, `Edges` sets how the gap is filled. `"Wrap"` (1) tiles
  the image, and `"Mirror"` (3) reflects it, which suits a moved background plate.
- **Animate Center for moves.** Use `Center` with `comp.PolyPath()` for a moving image, as with Merge.

**See also:** Merge, Displace, Dissolve, MediaIn, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## uCamera (`uCamera`)

**Category:** USD · **Short name:** uCa · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (USD, optional, to adjust a camera in an imported scene), `ImageInput` (Image, for the image plane and projection) · **Output:** `Output` (USD)

A virtual camera for viewing a USD scene. It copies the settings of a real camera: focal length, focus distance, F stop,
film back (aperture), shutter, and the clipping planes. Connect it to a uMerge with the scene, then view the render through
it. Its Scene input takes a USD scene, so an existing camera in an imported file can be adjusted through Prim Selection
(the Pick button in the Inspector). By default it's a plain camera. Connecting an image to `ImageInput` adds a distant
textured plane to the scene, sized to fit the footage exactly as the camera sees it, and enables **projection** of the image
through the camera onto the scene. This is for video reprojection and matching a 3D scene to footage.

**Use for:** framing and animating the shot, matching a live-action or 3D camera by its lens and film back, and projecting a
plate or background from the camera's point of view.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Projection Type | `ProjectionType` | ID multi-button | `"Perspective"` | `"Perspective"` (a real lens) or `"Orthographic"` (parallel projection, with no perspective distortion). |
| Near Clip | `Clip.Near` | Number | 0.1 (slider 0.1–50000) | Objects closer than this to the camera are not drawn. |
| Far Clip | `Clip.Far` | Number | 1000 (slider 0.1–10000) | Objects further than this are not drawn. |
| Exposure | `Exposure` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Exposure of the camera's view, as a slider. (See Tips: the manual describes this control differently.) |
| Focal Length | `FocalLength` | Number | 50 (mm; 0.01–100) | Lens focal length. A shorter focal length gives a wider angle of view. |
| Focus Distance | `FocusDistance` | Number | 4 (0.5–10) | Distance from the camera to the focal plane, which sets the depth of field. |
| F Stop | `FStop` | Number | 0 (0–10) | Aperture of the lens. Affects exposure and depth of field. |
| Horizontal Aperture | `HorizontalAperture` | Number | 21.12 (mm; 0.01–10) | Width of the film back (sensor). Sets the horizontal angle of view. |
| Vertical Aperture | `VerticalAperture` | Number | 11.88 (mm; 0.01–10) | Height of the film back. Sets the vertical angle of view. |
| Lens Shift X, Y | `HorizontalApertureOffset`, `VerticalApertureOffset` | Number | 0 (−10 to 10) | Offsets the lens across the film back. |
| Shutter Open, Close | `ShutterOpen`, `ShutterClose` | Number | 0 (−10 to 10) | When the shutter opens and closes. Affects exposure and motion blur. |
| Stereo Role | `StereoRole` | ID multi-button | `"Center"` | Which eye's camera this is: `"Left"`, `"Center"` or `"Right"`. |
| Frustum, View Vector | `FrustumVis`, `ViewVectorVis` | Checkbox | 1 | Show the viewing cone and the centre line in the viewer. |
| Near Clip, Far Clip (viewer) | `PerspNearClipVis`, `PerspFarClipVis` | Checkbox | 0, 1 | Show the clipping planes in the viewer. |
| Focal Plane (viewer) | `PlaneOfFocusVis` | Checkbox | 1 | Show the focal plane in the viewer. |
| Enable Image Plane | `ImagePlaneEnabled` | Checkbox | 1 | Shows the image plane. Needs an image on `ImageInput`. |
| Image Input | `ImageInput` | Image | | The image for the image plane and projection. |
| Fit Method | `Fit` | ID multi-button | `"Height"` | How the image fits the film back: `"Inside"`, `"Width"`, `"Height"` or `"Outside"`. Appears when an image is connected. |
| Depth | `IDepth` | Number | 100 (1–500) | Distance of the image plane from the camera. Appears when an image is connected. |
| Enable Camera Projection | `ProjectionEnabled` | Checkbox | 0 | Projects the image through the camera onto the scene. Appears when an image is connected. |
| Projection Mode | `ProjectionMode` | Multi-button | 1: Texture (0: Light) | `"Light"` adds the image as light; `"Texture"` works with uCatcher. Appears when projection is on. |
| Projection Fit Method | `ProjectionFitMethod` | ID multi-button | `"Inside"` | As Fit Method, with `"Stretch"` as well. Appears when projection is on. |
| Projector ID | `ProjectorID` | Number | 1 (1–10) | Groups projections for uCatcher's Restrict by Projector ID. |
| Projector Priority | `ProjectorPriority` | Number | 0 (0–10) | Which projection wins when several overlap. Not verified. |
| Project on Back Faces | `ProjectOnBackFaces` | Checkbox | 1 | Also projects onto the back faces of geometry (name-based; not verified). |

The Transform tab is common to all USD tools (see Common Controls → USD tools). Controls for the image plane's geometry and
material (`SurfacePlaneInputs.*`, `MtlStdInputs.*`) are not described here.

### Example

A 35 mm camera, five units back from the origin, focused on the scene at 5 units:

```python
cam = comp.AddTool('uCamera')
cam.FocalLength = 35
```
