| Export as Separate Stage | `SeparateStage` | Checkbox | 0 | See Common Controls → USD tools. |

### Example

Choose a variant from a set in a loaded scene:

```python
asset = comp.AddTool('uLoader')
asset.Filename = r'C:\Media\USD\character.usdz'

outfit = comp.AddTool('uVariant')
outfit.SceneInput = asset.Output
outfit.VariantSetSelector = 'outfit'   # the set's name in the file
outfit.VariantSelector = 'winter'      # the variant's name in that set
```

### Tips

- Set the Variant Set before the Variant. Both lists show only `"No Selection"` until a file with variants is loaded.
- The lists fill from the loaded file. In a scratch comp, the Resolve-shipped USD sample stayed at `"No Selection"`, so no
  variant names were read. The names in the example are placeholders, and the sets were not tested against a real file.
- Animate the choice to switch variants over time. Not tested.

**See also:** uLoader, uVisibility, uSwitch, uReplace Material, Common Controls → USD tools.

## uVisibility (`uVisibility`)

**Category:** USD · **Short name:** uVis · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (USD) · **Output:** `Output` (USD)

Shows or hides chosen prims of a USD scene. Choose the prims with Prim Selection, then set Visible on or off. Hidden prims
are removed from the render, but the rest of the scene is untouched. Use it to hide a part of an asset without editing it, or
to show a part only for some frames (the Visible control is animatable in the manual).

**Use for:** removing a part of an imported asset, showing a hidden detail for a shot, or switching between two parts of a
scene by using two uVisibility tools.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Selected Prims | `SelectedPrims` | Text (Prim Selection group) | "" | The prims to show or hide, chosen with the Pick button. |
| Invert Prim Selection | `InvertPrimSelection` | Checkbox | 0 | Applies the visibility to everything except the selected prims. |
| Visible | `VisibilityOverride` | Checkbox | 1 | On shows the selected prims; off hides them. Animatable (manual). |
| Export as Separate Stage | `SeparateStage` | Checkbox | 0 | See Common Controls → USD tools. |

### Example

Hide the prims chosen with Pick in the Inspector (Prim Selection is not set in this example):

```python
asset = comp.AddTool('uLoader')
asset.Filename = r'C:\Media\USD\set.usdz'

hide = comp.AddTool('uVisibility')
hide.SceneInput = asset.Output
hide.VisibilityOverride = 0           # Visible off
```

### Tips

- Prim Selection is the Pick button in the Inspector. The `SelectedPrims` text is what it writes. Prim paths typed from a
  script were not tested.
- uVisibility is the only USD tool with a Visible checkbox. A whole object can also be removed by disconnecting it from its
  uMerge.

**See also:** uTransform, uVariant, uReplace Material, uSwitch, uLoader, Common Controls → USD tools.

## uVolume (`uVolume`)

**Category:** USD · **Short name:** uVo · **Inputs:** none · **Output:** `Output` (USD), `OutEmissionGradientImage` (Image)

Brings a volumetric VDB file (a smoke, fire or cloud simulation, as a single frame or a sequence) into a USD scene. It
adjusts the density and the emission colour of the volume: a flat colour, a field from the file, a blackbody temperature,
or a gradient mapped over a field. Its timing controls trim, loop and retime an animated volume, as on uLoader.

**Use for:** placing a fire, smoke or explosion from a VDB simulation in a USD set, and recolouring it.

**Second output.** `OutEmissionGradientImage` is an Image output that the manual doesn't mention. Its contents (named after
the emission gradient) were not checked.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filename | `Filename` | Text (file) | "" | The VDB file or sequence. Opens a file dialog when the tool is added in the UI. |
| Trim In, Trim Out | `ClipTimeStart`, `ClipTimeEnd` | Number | 0 | Trims the animation. |
| Time Scale | `TimeScale` | Number | 1 | Speed of the animation. |
| Frame Offset | `FrameOffset` | Number | 0 | Frame on which the animation starts. |
| Reverse, Loop | `Reverse`, `Loop` | Checkbox | 0 | Plays the volume backwards, or repeats it. |
| Density Field | `Density.Field` | ID combo | `"none"` | The field in the VDB that sets the density. Lists the fields in the file. |
| Density Scale | `Density.Scale` | Number | 1 | Strength of the density. |
| Emission Mode | `Emission.Mode` | Multi-button | 0: Color (1: Field, 2: Blackbody, 3: Gradient) | How the emission colour is set. |
| Emission Field | `Emission.Field` | ID combo | `"none"` | The field that drives the emission in Field mode. |
| Emission Red, Green, Blue | `Emission.Red`, `Emission.Green`, `Emission.Blue` | Number | 1 | Emission colour in Color mode. |
| Temperature | `Emission.Temperature` | Number | 6500 (K) | Colour temperature in Blackbody mode. |
| Gradient | `Emission.Gradient` | Gradient | | Colours mapped over a field in Gradient mode. |
| Interpolation Space | `Emission.GradientSpace` | ID multi-button | `"RGB"` | The colour space the gradient blends in: `"RGB"`, `"HLS"`, `"HSV"` or `"LAB"`. |
| Emission LUT | `Emission.LUT`, `EmissionLutImage` | Text (file), Image (input) | "" | A lookup image for the emission colour, from a file or a node. Not in the manual; its use wasn't tested. |
| Emission Scale | `Emission.Scale` | Number | 1 | Strength of the emission. |
| Raymarching Step Size | `Advanced.StepSize` | Number | 1 | The step length of the volume's ray marching (name-based; not verified). |
| Minimum Light Scattering | `Advanced.MinScattering` | Number | 0.002 | The minimum light scattering in the volume (name-based; not verified). |
| Field wrap, channel and range | `Emission.UWrapMode`, `Emission.UCoordChannel`, `Emission.UCoordMin`, `Emission.UCoordMax`, `Emission.VWrapMode`, and so on | | | How the field's coordinates map to the gradient. |

The Transform tab is common (see Common Controls → USD tools).

### Example

A fire volume with its emission set to blackbody, at 2500 K as the start point, and a faster playback:

```python
fire = comp.AddTool('uVolume')
fire.Filename = r'C:\Media\VDB\fire_sim.vdb'
fire.TimeScale = 1.5
fire['Emission.Mode'] = 2                 # Blackbody
fire['Emission.Temperature'] = 2500
fire['Emission.Scale'] = 2.0
```

### Tips

- The Density Field and Emission Field lists come from the fields in the VDB file. No VDB file was available to test, so
  the lists were not checked. The example leaves the fields at `"none"`.
- Use Emission Mode `Color` for an overall colour. With white, USD lights don't affect the volume (manual).

**See also:** uLoader, uMerge, uRenderer, uShader, Common Controls → USD tools.

## Immersive Patcher (`ImmersivePatcher`)

**Category:** VR · **Short name:** ImP · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, an immersive or normal 2D image), `Metadata` (image) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts between an immersive video frame and a flat 2D image. Undistort turns a section of the immersive frame into a flat image, which can then be tracked, painted or composited with 2D tools. Distort turns it back. Use two Immersive Patchers in a pair, with the same Rotation and Angle of View on both, so that the picture is restored exactly. The tool is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** editing a patch of an immersive clip in flat 2D, then restoring it into the immersive frame.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | ID multi-button | `"Distort"` | `"Distort"` converts a flat image to immersive. `"Undistort"` converts the immersive clip to a flat image. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotate.RotOrder` | ID multi-button | `"ZYX"` | The order of the three rotations. |
| Rotate X | `Rotate.X` | Number | 0 (-90 to 90) | Pitch of the view. |
| Rotate Y | `Rotate.Y` | Number | 0 (-180 to 180) | Pan of the view: turns to the area being edited. |
| Rotate Z | `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (-90 to 90) | Roll of the view. |
| Angle of View | `AoV` | Number | 90 (1 to 150) | The field of view of the flat section, in degrees. |
| Metadata | `Metadata` | Image input | | The image whose metadata the tool uses. |

The default Mode is Distort, so set Mode to Undistort for the first patcher in a pair.

### Tips

- Set the first patcher to Undistort and the second to Distort. The manual's workflow is undistort, edit, then distort, then merge with the original.
- Copy the first patcher and paste it to make the second: the rotation and angle of view then match exactly.
- The Settings tab is described in Common Controls.

**See also:** LatLong Patcher, PanoMap, Merge, Spherical Stabilizer.

## LatLong Patcher (`LatLongPatcher`)

**Category:** VR · **Short name:** LLP · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, a lat-long image), Effect Mask (blue, rarely used) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Extracts a section of a lat-long (equirectangular) image as a flat, de-warped square, so that it can be painted, tracked or composited with normal 2D tools, and applies the edited square back over the lat-long image. This is the usual way to repair or paint a part of a 360° stitched image. Extract and Apply use the same Rotation and Angle of View, so a patch can be taken out and returned to the same place. The tool is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** removing stitch errors, rig marks and other fixes in a spherical image. The Apply mode is also used for VR180 images with Apply 180.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | ID multi-button | `"Extract"` | `"Extract"` pulls a de-warped 90-degree square out of the lat-long image. `"Apply"` warps a square back onto a lat-long canvas. `"Apply 180"` does the same for a VR180 image, and keeps a square output. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotate.RotOrder` | ID multi-button | `"ZYX"` | The order of the three rotations: `"XYZ"`, `"XZY"`, `"YXZ"`, `"YZX"`, `"ZXY"` or `"ZYX"`. |
| Rotate X | `Rotate.X` | Number | 0 (-90 to 90) | Pitch (tilt) of the sphere. |
| Rotate Y | `Rotate.Y` | Number | 0 (-180 to 180) | Pan (yaw): turns the sphere to the area being patched. |
| Rotate Z | `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (-90 to 90) | Roll of the sphere. |
| Angle of View | `AoV` | Number | 90 (1 to 150) | The field of view of the patch, in degrees. Match the headset's angle of view. |

The Settings tab and Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.

### Example

Extracting a patch from a lat-long image, painting it, and applying it back over the original. The Apply node uses the same rotation and angle of view as the Extract node, and the patched result is merged over the original image:

```python
pano = comp.AddTool('Background')        # stands in for the lat-long (equirectangular) image

extract = comp.AddTool('LatLongPatcher')
extract.Input = pano.Output
extract.Mode = 'Extract'
extract['Rotate.Y'] = 90                 # turn to the area to patch
extract.AoV = 90

paint = comp.AddTool('Blur')             # any 2D work on the flat patch
paint.Input = extract.Output

apply_patch = comp.AddTool('LatLongPatcher')
apply_patch.Input = paint.Output
apply_patch.Mode = 'Apply'
apply_patch['Rotate.Y'] = 90             # the same rotation as the Extract node
apply_patch.AoV = 90

over = comp.AddTool('Merge')
over.Background = pano.Output
over.Foreground = apply_patch.Output     # the Apply output is a lat-long canvas with the patch on it
```

### Tips

- Keep Rotation and Angle of View identical on the Extract and Apply nodes. The easiest way is to copy the first node and paste it for the second.
- The Apply output is not merged over the original by the tool itself. Use Merge, as in the example. Apply is 2:1 (twice the patch's width) and the patch sits on transparent black, so the Merge leaves the rest of the image unchanged.
- Use Apply 180 for a VR180 image. Its output stays square, the same size as the patch.
- The Effect Mask is rarely useful on VR nodes.

**See also:** PanoMap, Immersive Patcher, Merge, Paint, Spherical Stabilizer.

## PanoMap (`PanoMap`)

**Category:** VR · **Short name:** PaM · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, a spherical image), `Metadata` (image, optional), Effect Mask (blue, rarely used) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts a spherical image from one layout to another: for example, from a cube map laid out as a cross to an equirectangular (lat-long) image, or the reverse. It can also rotate the sphere while it converts. Set From to the layout of the input and To to the layout you want. The tool is available only in Fusion Studio and DaVinci Resolve Studio.

**Use for:** changing the layout of a 360° or VR image, so that a tool that needs one layout can be used on a file that arrives in another, such as a cube map that must be treated as lat-long.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| From | `From` | ID multi-button | `"Auto"` | The layout of the input: `"Auto"` (detected from the metadata and frame aspect), `"VCross"`, `"HCross"`, `"VStrip"`, `"HStrip"`, `"LatLong"`, `"VR180"` or `"Immersive"`. |
| Source Metadata | `SrcImMeta` | ID multi-button | `"PaMImMetaMode_Auto"` | How the input's metadata is read, when From is Immersive: `"PaMImMetaMode_Auto"`, `"PaMImMetaMode_SourceInput"` or `"PaMImMetaMode_MetadataInput"` (from the Metadata input). |
| To | `To` | ID multi-button | `"LatLong"` | The layout of the output: `"VCross"`, `"HCross"`, `"VStrip"`, `"HStrip"`, `"LatLong"`, `"VR180"` or `"Immersive"`. |
| Target Metadata | `TgtImMeta` | ID multi-button | `"PaMImMetaMode_Auto"` | How the output's metadata is set, when To is Immersive. The same three choices as Source Metadata. |
| Rotation Order | `Rotate.RotOrder` | ID multi-button | `"ZYX"` | The order of the rotations (see LatLong Patcher). |
| Rotate X, Y, Z | `Rotate.X`, `Rotate.Y`, `Rotate.Z` | Number | 0 (X and Z -90 to 90; Y -180 to 180) | Rotates the sphere while converting. |
| Metadata | `Metadata` | Image input | | The image whose metadata sets the layout, when a Metadata option asks for it. |

The Settings tab and Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.

### Example

Converting a lat-long image to a vertical cross cube map:

```python
plate = comp.AddTool('Background')     # stands in for a lat-long (equirectangular) image

pano = comp.AddTool('PanoMap')
pano.Input = plate.Output
pano.From = 'LatLong'
pano.To = 'VCross'
```

### Tips

- Leave From on Auto unless the input's layout is wrong or has no metadata. Set it by hand for a file that is labelled incorrectly.
- Use the Rotate controls to turn the sphere while converting, rather than making a separate rotation later.
- Convert a cube map to a lat-long image before using LatLong Patcher on it, because LatLong Patcher works on lat-long images only.

**See also:** LatLong Patcher, Immersive Patcher, Spherical Stabilizer.

## Spherical Stabilizer (`SphericalStabilizer`)

**Category:** VR · **Short name:** none · **Inputs:** `Input` (orange, a spherical 360° image) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Stabilises a 360° shot by tracking the camera's rotation through the clip and rotating each frame to cancel it. The tracking is calculated from the footage, using optical flow and a 3D rotation estimate, so a shot is tracked first and then stabilised. The track buttons start the analysis, and they can't run in a scratch comp. This tool is not in the manual; the description here comes from its registration and controls.

**Use for:** removing unwanted camera rotation from a 360° shot, such as a handheld rig that rolls or pans.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Track reverse | `TrackReverse` | Button | | Tracks backward from the end of the shot. Runs the analysis. |
| Track reverse from current time | `TrackReverseFromCurrentTime` | Button | | Tracks backward from the current frame. Runs the analysis. |
| Stop tracking | `StopTracking` | Button | | Stops a running track. |
| Track forward from current time | `TrackForwardFromCurrentTime` | Button | | Tracks forward from the current frame. Runs the analysis. |
| Track forward | `TrackForward` | Button | | Tracks forward from the start of the shot. Runs the analysis. |
| Append to track | `TrackAppend` | Multi-button | 0: Replace (1: Append) | Whether a new track replaces the existing one, or is added to it. |
| Reject Dominant Motion Outliers While Tracking | `RejectOutliers` | Checkbox | 1 | Ignores motion that doesn't match the dominant camera movement while tracking. |
| Stabilize Strength | `StabilizeStrength` | Number | 0.5 (0 to 1) | How much of the tracked rotation is removed. |
| Smoothing | `SmoothingBlend` | Number | 1 (0 to 1) | Blends between the still and the smoothed rotation. |
| Absolute Rotation X, Y, Z | `AbsoluteRotation.X`, `AbsoluteRotation.Y`, `AbsoluteRotation.Z` | Number | 0 (-180 to 180) | Rotation values that the tracking fills in. Not documented in the manual; their exact meaning was not checked. |
| Offset Rotation X, Y, Z | `OffsetRotation.X`, `OffsetRotation.Y`, `OffsetRotation.Z` | Number | 0 (-180 to 180) | A rotation added after stabilisation. Not documented in the manual. |

The Track buttons and Absolute Rotation values need the shot to be tracked before they show anything. Neither the tracking nor the stabilised image was checked here.

**See also:** Immersive Patcher, PanoMap, Planar Tracker, Camera Tracker.

## Coordinate Space (`CoordSpace`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** CdS · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Converts the image between rectangular and polar coordinates. Rectangular to Polar maps the horizontal and vertical positions
of each pixel to an angle and a distance from the centre. Polar to Rectangular does the reverse. The effect is a radial or tunnel distortion, and two
of these tools with different settings, with a Transform or Drip between them, give many patterns.

**Use for:** tunnel and vortex effects in motion graphics, radial patterns from a flat texture, and unwrapping a circular
picture into a strip.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `Shape` | Multi-button | 0: Rectangular to Polar (1: Polar to Rectangular) | The direction of the conversion. |

### Example

A tunnel effect: a flat image wrapped into a circle, with the Shape set to the other direction for a second pass:

```python
wrap = comp.AddTool('CoordSpace')
wrap.Input = media_in.Output
wrap.Shape = 0                   # Rectangular to Polar

unwrap = comp.AddTool('CoordSpace')
unwrap.Input = wrap.Output
unwrap.Shape = 1                 # Polar to Rectangular
```

### Tips

- **Animate the input for a tunnel.** The manual's tunnel example moves a Text+ along a path into the tool, so the text
  appears to approach from a distance.
- **Use a Transform for orientation.** The image may need flipping or rotating before the conversion to read the right
  way round.

**See also:** Vortex, Drip, Transform, Lens Distort, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Corner Positioner (`CornerPositioner`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** CPn · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Pins the four corners of an image to any four points, so a rectangular picture fits a quadrilateral area of the frame.
The image is warped to match, in 2D (Bi-Linear) or with a perspective mapping. The four corners are drawn as points in
the viewer, and each can be moved there. Corners can also be attached to trackers or paths for animation.

**Use for:** replacing a sign, screen or picture frame in a shot, fitting a graphic to a surface that is at an angle, and
any rectangle that must sit on a plane in the scene. Pair it with a Planar Transform (below) to keep the pin locked
onto a tracked background.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mapping Type | `MappingType` | Multi-button | 1: Perspective (0: Bi-Linear) | Bi-Linear warps the image in 2D. Perspective calculates the offsets in 2D and maps them into a 3D perspective. |
| Top Left | `TopLeft` | Point | (0.1, 0.9) | Position of the top-left corner. Drag it in the viewer. |
| Top Right | `TopRight` | Point | (0.9, 1) | Position of the top-right corner. |
| Bottom Left | `BottomLeft` | Point | (0, 0.3) | Position of the bottom-left corner. |
| Bottom Right | `BottomRight` | Point | (1, 0.1) | Position of the bottom-right corner. |
| Top Left Offset X, Y | `TopLeftOffsetX`, `TopLeftOffsetY` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Small nudge to the top-left corner. Useful when a tracker's pattern is not exactly on the corner. |
| Top Right Offset X, Y | `TopRightOffsetX`, `TopRightOffsetY` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Nudge to the top-right corner. |
| Bottom Left Offset X, Y | `BottomLeftOffsetX`, `BottomLeftOffsetY` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Nudge to the bottom-left corner. |
| Bottom Right Offset X, Y | `BottomRightOffsetX`, `BottomRightOffsetY` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Nudge to the bottom-right corner. |
| Reset Offsets | `ResetOffsets` | Button | | Sets all the offsets back to 0. |

The corner positions are relative to the frame, with (0, 0) at the bottom-left and (1, 1) at the top-right.

### Example

Pinning a graphic into a quadrilateral that sits in the upper-left of the frame, in perspective:

```python
pin = comp.AddTool('CornerPositioner')
pin.Input = media_in.Output
pin.MappingType = 1              # Perspective
pin.TopLeft = [0.10, 0.85]
pin.TopRight = [0.45, 0.80]
pin.BottomLeft = [0.10, 0.55]
pin.BottomRight = [0.42, 0.50]
```

### Tips

- **Animate the corners.** To make a pin follow a moving surface, give each corner a motion path, as with Merge's
  `Center`: `pin.TopLeft = comp.PolyPath()`, then `pin.TopLeft[frame] = [x, y]`. The manual also describes attaching the
  corners to trackers in the Inspector; that route is not scripted here.
- **Use Offsets for tracker tweaks.** Leave the tracked corner points where the tracker puts them, and use the offsets
  to correct small errors in the pin.
- **Mask the pinned area.** Connect a mask to the Effect Mask to limit the pinned image to a shape.

**See also:** Perspective Positioner, Planar Transform, Transform, Merge, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Dent (`Dent`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Dnt · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Makes a circular deformation of the image, like a fish-eye lens or a bulge, with six different dent shapes. The area of
effect is a circle set by Size, and Strength sets how far the image is pushed. All the parameters can be keyframed.

**Use for:** bulge and lens-style distortion, a pulsing or growing dent in a title, and circular patterns from a noise
source.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0: Dent 1 (1: Kaleidascope, 2: Dent 2, 3: Dent 3, 4: Cosine Dent, 5: Sine Dent) | Dent filter. Dent 1 bulges. Kaleidascope (the menu spelling) dents, mirrors and inverts. Dent 2 displaces. Dent 3 deforms. Cosine Dent fractures to the centre. Sine Dent gives a smooth, rounded dent. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the dent. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–10) | Size of the area affected. Animate it to make the dent grow. |
| Strength | `Strength` | Number | 1 (slider −5 to 10) | Overall strength. Negative values reverse the dent. |

### Example

A bulge that grows in the centre of the frame over half a second:

```python
dent = comp.AddTool('Dent')
dent.Input = media_in.Output
dent.Type = 0                    # Dent 1, the bulge
dent.Size = comp.BezierSpline()
dent.Size[0] = 0.0
dent.Size[12] = 0.6
```

### Tips

- **Try the Type menu.** Each dent filter gives a different shape from the same Size and Strength, so compare them in the viewer.

**See also:** Vortex, Drip, Lens Distort, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Displace (`Displace`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Dsp · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Foreground (green), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Refracts one image using another as a map. The Input image is shifted pixel by pixel, according to a chosen channel of
the Foreground image. Radial mode pushes pixels towards or away from a centre point. X/Y mode uses one channel to move
pixels horizontally and another to move them vertically, which allows precise distortion and simple morphs. Light
controls add a bevelled highlight along the refraction. The Input and Foreground are both required.

**Use for:** heat shimmer, water ripples, flag waving, glass and bevelled text, and any displacement of a title or
graphic by a noise map. Driven by Fast Noise, it is the usual way to make a still element look like it is moving
through hot air or water.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0: Radial, 1: X Y | Radial displaces outwards from Center using one set of refraction controls. X Y uses two channels and two sets of refraction controls. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | The point pixels move towards or away from. Radial only. |
| Refraction Channel | `Channel` | Multi-button | 4: Luminance (0: Red, 1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Alpha) | The channel of Foreground that drives the displacement. Radial only. |
| X Channel, Y Channel | `XChannel`, `YChannel` | Multi-button | `XChannel` 0: Red, `YChannel` 1: Green | The channel driving horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) displacement. X Y only. Options as for Refraction Channel. |
| Refraction Strength | `RefractionStrength` | Number | 0.1 (−2 to 2) | Strength of the displacement in Radial mode. Higher values refract more strongly. |
| X Refraction, Y Refraction | `XRefraction`, `YRefraction` | Number | 0 (−0.1 to 0.1) | Strength of the horizontal and vertical displacement in X Y mode. |
| X Offset, Y Offset | `XOffset`, `YOffset` | Number | 0 (−0.5 to 0.5) | Offset of the map along each axis in X Y mode. |
| Light Power | `LightPower` | Number | 0 (0–3) | Strength of the simulated bevel highlight. 0 turns it off. |
| Light Angle | `LightAngle` | Number | 135 (0–360°) | Direction the simulated light comes from. |
| Spread | `Spread` | Number | 0 (0–3) | Widens the displacement and softens the edges of the map. |
| Light Channel | `LightChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Color, 1: Red, 2: Green, 3: Blue, 4: Alpha, 5: Luminance | The channel of Foreground used as the light source. |

### Example

A title that shimmers like heat haze. A Fast Noise, seethed on every frame, drives a Displace of the title, which is then
merged over the plate:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('TextPlus')
title.StyledText = 'HEAT'
title.Size = 0.15

noise = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')
noise.XScale = 6
noise.Detail = 3
noise.SeetheRate = 0.2               # the map changes every frame

heat = comp.AddTool('Displace')
heat.Input = title.Output
heat.Foreground = noise.Output
heat.RefractionStrength = 0.02       # small values for a subtle shimmer

merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = comp.MediaIn1.Output
merge.Foreground = heat.Output
```

### Tips

- **Keep Refraction small.** Values near 0.01 to 0.03 suit heat and water. The default is 0.1, which is much stronger.
- **Use X Y for shimmer.** X Y mode with two different noise channels (for example `XChannel` Red and `YChannel` Green)
  gives a more natural wobble than Radial. Set `XRefraction` and `YRefraction` separately.
- **Animate the map, not the image.** To make the distortion move, move the Fast Noise (its Seethe Rate or a keyframed
  Seethe) rather than the title.
- **Add a bevel.** Set `LightPower` above 0 with `LightAngle` 135 for a raised look on glass or chrome text. Use `Spread`
  to soften the edges of the ridges.
- **Mask the effect.** Connect a shape or a gradient to the Effect Mask input to limit the distortion to one area, such as
  above a road or around a logo.

**See also:** Fast Noise, Transform, Merge, Dissolve, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Drip (`Drip`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Drip · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Applies a ripple across the whole image, which can radiate outward from a centre. Shape chooses the pattern of the ripples:
circular, square, random, horizontal or vertical waves, and several star and diamond forms. Amplitude sets the height of
each ripple, Frequency sets how many there are, and Phase moves them.

**Use for:** water-like ripples on a plate or a graphic, a pulse that spreads from a point, and wave distortion on a
title, with Phase animated to make the ripples travel.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shape | `Shape` | Combo | 0: Circular (1: Square, 2: Random, 3: Horizontal, 4: Vertical, 5: Exponential, 6: Star, 7: Radial) | The pattern of the ripples. Horizontal and Vertical move in one direction. Star is an eight-way symmetrical ripple. |
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the drip effect. |
| Aspect | `Aspect` | Number | 1 (slider 0.2–5) | Proportions of the shape. 1 is symmetrical. Smaller values give taller, narrower shapes, and larger values give shorter, wider ones. |
| Amplitude | `Amplitude` | Number | 0.1 (slider 0–1) | Height of each ripple. 0 makes the effect transparent. |
| Dampening | `Dampening` | Number | 0 (slider 0–1) | Falloff of the amplitude away from the centre. Limits the area the ripples affect. |
| Frequency | `Frequency` | Number | 10 (slider 0–100) | Number of ripples from the centre. 0 gives no ripples. |
| Phase | `Phase` | Number | 0 (slider 0–1) | Offset of the ripples. Animate it to make the ripples move outward. |

### Example

Circular ripples spreading out from the centre of a plate, animated with Phase:

```python
drip = comp.AddTool('Drip')
drip.Input = media_in.Output
drip.Shape = 0                   # Circular
drip.Amplitude = 0.05
drip.Frequency = 20
drip.Phase = comp.BezierSpline()
drip.Phase[0] = 0
drip.Phase[48] = 1
```

### Tips

- **Keep Amplitude small.** Values near 0.05 suit a water ripple. Larger values distort the image strongly.
- **Animate Phase to make ripples travel.** The manual suggests animating Phase so the ripples emanate from the centre.

**See also:** Dent, Vortex, Displace, Transform, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Grid Warp (`GridWarp`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Grd · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Warps the image by moving a mesh. A source grid, which is the image's original layout, is matched to a destination grid,
and the image is stretched between the two. The grids and their points are edited by dragging them in the viewer.

**Use for:** bending an image to fit a shape, reshaping a graphic to a curved surface, and freeform distortion where a
corner pin or a single-axis warp isn't enough.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Show | `Show` | Multi-button | 1: Destination (0: Source) | Which grid the viewer shows for editing. |
| Dst X Grid Size, Dst Y Grid Size | `DstXGridSize`, `DstYGridSize` | Number | 8, 8 (slider 1–25) | Number of cells in the destination grid. |
| Dst Subdivisions | `DstSubdivisionLevel` | Number | 3 (slider 0–4) | Smoothness of the destination mesh. More subdivisions give smoother curves, at more cost. |
| Src X Grid Size, Src Y Grid Size | `SrcXGridSize`, `SrcYGridSize` | Number | 8, 8 (slider 1–25) | Number of cells in the source grid. |
| Src Subdivisions | `SrcSubdivisionLevel` | Number | 3 (slider 0–4) | Smoothness of the source mesh. |
| Magnet Type | `MagnetType` | Multi-button | 1: Region (0: Selected, 2: Magnetic) | How dragging a point moves its neighbours. |
| Magnet Distance | `MagnetDistance` | Number | 0.25 (0–1) | Radius of the magnet's effect. |
| Magnet Strength | `MagnetStrength` | Number | 0.5 (0–1) | Strength of the magnet's effect. |
| Render Method | `RenderMethod` | Combo | 2: Render (0: Wire Frame, 1: Color) | How the grid is drawn when the tool outputs an image. |

The grid points and the mesh changes (`SrcGridChange`, `DstGridChange`) are edited in the viewer, and scripting them
has not been tested. The polylines (`SrcPolyline`, `DstPolyline`) take Polyline dicts (see *Value types* in
Conventions), but their effect on the warp is not verified here.

### Tips

- **Shape the mesh in the viewer.** Grid Warp is built for interactive shaping. The controls here set the grid density and
  the magnet behaviour; the points themselves are placed in the viewer.
- **Use more cells for detail.** A higher grid size gives more points to move, at the cost of more work to shape it.

**See also:** Corner Positioner, Perspective Positioner, Displace, Vector Distortion, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Lens Distort (`LensDistort`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Lens · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Removes lens distortion from a plate, or puts it back. A plate shot through a real lens has curved lines where straight
ones should be. Undistort flattens the image so 3D or straight-edged graphics can be composited without mismatch. Distort
restores the original look afterwards. The distortion is described by a lens model, chosen with `Model`, and each model
has its own set of coefficients.

**Use for:** undistorting live-action plates before a 3D or graphic element is added, then distorting the result again
with the same settings, and matching a plate to lens data from a tracking or calibration tool.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `Mode` | Multi-button | 1: Undistort (0: Distort, 1: Undistort) | Undistort removes the lens distortion. Distort brings it back. |
| Edges | `EdgeMode` | Multi-button | 0: Canvas (1: Duplicate) | What fills samples outside the frame. Canvas uses the canvas colour. Duplicate repeats the edge pixels, which avoids dark edges when the image is blurred afterwards. |
| Clipping Mode | `ClippingMode` | ID combo | `"Domain"` | `"Domain"` or `"Frame"`. |
| Output Distortion Map | `OutputDistortionMap` | Checkbox | 0 | Outputs the position of each pixel as a warped screen-coordinate map, instead of the image. |
| Model | `Model` | ID combo | `"DEClassicLDModel"` | The lens distortion model. The table above gives the classic model's coefficients. The other models are under *Models*. |
| Distortion | `DEClassicLDModel.Distortion` | Number | 0 (−0.5 to 0.5) | Classic model. The main radial distortion value. |
| Anamorphic Squeeze | `DEClassicLDModel.AnamorphicSqueeze` | Number | 1 (0.25–4) | Classic model. Horizontal squeeze of an anamorphic lens. |
| Curvature X, Y | `DEClassicLDModel.CurvatureX`, `DEClassicLDModel.CurvatureY` | Number | 0 (−0.5 to 0.5) | Classic model. Curvature of the lines along each axis. |
| Quartic Distortion | `DEClassicLDModel.QuarticDistortion` | Number | 0 (−0.5 to 0.5) | Classic model. Fourth-order radial term. |
| Load Distortion Data | `Load` | Button | | Loads lens data from a file in the Inspector. |
| Supersampling [HiQ] | `Supersampling` | Multi-button | 0: 1x1, 1: 2x2, 2: 4x4, 3: 8x8 | Supersampling used in HiQ renders. |
| Subsample Mode [HiQ] | `SubsampleMode` | Multi-button | 1: Bilinear (0: Nearest) | Sampling used in HiQ renders. |

The Inspector also has a Calibration page (for the Fusion Radial models) and a Camera Settings group (focal length, film gate,
lens shift and pixel aspect). They are not described here.

### Models

The table above lists the classic model's coefficients. Each other model has its own coefficients, whose IDs start with
the model name and a dot, for example `DE4RadialFisheyeDegree8.Degree6`. Set `Model` first, then the values. The model
names follow 3DE (3D Equalizer)'s lens formats, and Fusion's own radial models.

| `Model` value | Coefficient IDs after the model name and a dot |
|---|---|
| `DEClassicLDModel` | `Distortion`, `AnamorphicSqueeze`, `CurvatureX`, `CurvatureY`, `QuarticDistortion` |
| `DE4AnamorphicStandardDegree4` | `Cx02Degree2`, `Cy02Degree2`, `Cx22Degree2`, `Cy22Degree2`, `Cx04Degree4`, `Cy04Degree4`, `Cx24Degree4`, `Cy24Degree4`, `Cx44Degree4`, `Cy44Degree4`, `LensRotation`, `SqueezeX`, `SqueezeY` |
| `DE4AnamorphicDegree6` | As above, plus `Cx06Degree6`, `Cy06Degree6`, `Cx26Degree6`, `Cy26Degree6`, `Cx46Degree6`, `Cy46Degree6`, `Cx66Degree6`, `Cy66Degree6` |
| `DE4RadialFisheyeDegree8Release2` | `DistortionDegree2`, `QuarticDistortionDegree4`, `Degree6`, `Degree8` |
| `DE4RadialFisheyeDegree8` | `DistortionDegree2`, `QuarticDistortionDegree4`, `Degree6`, `Degree8` |
| `DE4RadialStandardDegree4` | `DistortionDegree2`, `UDegree2`, `VDegree2`, `QuarticDistortionDegree4`, `UDegree4`, `VDegree4`, `PhiCylindricDirection`, `BCylindricBending` |
| `FusionRadialDiv` | `LowOrderDistortion`, `HighOrderDistortion`, `FishEyeDistortion`, `TangentialDistortion.X`, `TangentialDistortion.Y`, `PixelAspect`, `LensCenter`, `FocalLength` |
| `FusionRadial` | As `FusionRadialDiv`. Used with the Calibration page. |
| `PFTrack` | `LowOrderDistortion`, `HighOrderDistortion`, `LensCenterX`, `LensCenterY`, `AnamorphicSqueeze` |

Every coefficient is a Number. For the Fusion radial models, the Calibration page (a Calibrate Type and Mode, and Start
Auto Calibration button) solves the values from a checkerboard or line images. That needs the images in the UI, so it
can't be done from a script.

### Example

Undistorting a plate with the classic model, so a 3D element lines up over it, then distorting the composite with the same numbers:

```python
undist = comp.AddTool('LensDistort')
undist.Input = media_in.Output
undist.Mode = 1                  # Undistort
undist.Model = 'DEClassicLDModel'
undist['DEClassicLDModel.Distortion'] = 0.08
undist['DEClassicLDModel.AnamorphicSqueeze'] = 1.0

element = comp.AddTool('Background')   # stands in for a 3D render or graphic
merge = comp.AddTool('Merge')
merge.Background = undist.Output
merge.Foreground = element.Output

redist = comp.AddTool('LensDistort')
redist.Input = merge.Output
redist.Mode = 0                  # Distort: restore the lens look
redist.Model = 'DEClassicLDModel'
redist['DEClassicLDModel.Distortion'] = 0.08
```

### Tips

- **Undistort, work, distort.** Flattening the plate lets straight-edged 3D objects line up. Restoring the distortion at
  the end, with identical settings, puts the original look back.
- **Use Duplicate edges before blur.** With Canvas, black pixels from the frame edge are blurred into the image.
  Duplicate avoids that.
- **Animated distortion.** Each coefficient can be keyframed, for example to follow a zoom that changes the lens's
  distortion. Values from a lens calibration or a tracker are the reliable source; hand-keyed values are a fallback.

**See also:** Vortex, Corner Positioner, Perspective Positioner, Transform, Merge, Camera 3D.

## Perspective Positioner (`PerspectivePositioner`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** PPn · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Takes a picture of a flat object seen in perspective, placed by its four corners, and maps it back to a flat, square
image. It is the reverse of Corner Positioner: where Corner Positioner pins a flat image onto a quadrilateral, this tool
removes the perspective from the quadrilateral. Use it to make a skewed sign or screen face the camera.

**Use for:** rectifying a sign, screen or card that was shot at an angle, so it can be tracked, graded or replaced flat.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mapping Type | `MappingType` | Multi-button | 1: Perspective (0: Bi-Linear) | Bi-Linear maps the corners in 2D. Perspective maps them into a 3D perspective, which is the right choice for a skewed object. |
| Top Left | `TopLeft` | Point | (0.1, 0.9) | Position of the top-left corner of the object in the image. |
| Top Right | `TopRight` | Point | (0.9, 1) | Position of the top-right corner. |
| Bottom Left | `BottomLeft` | Point | (0, 0.3) | Position of the bottom-left corner. |
| Bottom Right | `BottomRight` | Point | (1, 0.1) | Position of the bottom-right corner. |

The corners are relative to the frame, with (0, 0) at the bottom-left and (1, 1) at the top-right. Drag them in the viewer,
or set them from a script.

### Example

Flattening a sign that sits at an angle in the lower-right of the frame:

```python
flat = comp.AddTool('PerspectivePositioner')
flat.Input = media_in.Output
flat.MappingType = 1             # Perspective
flat.TopLeft = [0.55, 0.60]
flat.TopRight = [0.90, 0.68]
flat.BottomLeft = [0.52, 0.30]
flat.BottomRight = [0.92, 0.36]
```

### Tips

- **Choose Perspective for a skewed object.** Bi-Linear is enough when the object is nearly flat to the camera.
- **Work from the flat result.** Once rectified, the sign can be graded, tracked or replaced as a flat image, then
  mapped back with Corner Positioner.

**See also:** Corner Positioner, Grid Warp, Planar Transform, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Vector Distortion (`Distort`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Dst · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Distort (green), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Moves each pixel of the image by an amount given in its vector channels: one channel for the X movement and one for the Y.
The vectors come from the Distort input, or, when nothing is connected there, from the image's own vector channels. The
result is a distortion or a motion-based warp that follows whatever the vector map describes, such as optical flow from
a neighbouring frame.

**Use for:** warping a picture with a motion or displacement map, applying an optical-flow vector pass to an image, and
pushing one image through the motion of another.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X Channel | `XChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Red (1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Vector X, 4: Vector Y) | The channel that drives the X movement, from the Distort input or the image. |
| Y Channel | `YChannel` | Multi-button | 0: Red (1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Vector X, 4: Vector Y) | The channel that drives the Y movement. |
| Flip X Channel, Flip Y Channel | `FlipX`, `FlipY` | Checkbox | 0 | Reverses the direction of the X or Y movement. |
| Lock Scale X/Y | `LockScaleXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Scale. Off: separate `XScale` and `YScale`. |
| Scale | `XScale` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Multiplier on the vector values. |
| Y Scale | `YScale` | Number | 1 (slider 0–10) | Vertical multiplier, used when Lock Scale X/Y is off. |
| Lock Bias X/Y | `LockBiasXY` | Checkbox | 1 | On: one Center Bias. Off: separate `XBias` and `YBias`. |
| Center Bias | `XBias` | Number | −1 (slider −1 to 1) | Shifts the distortion along the X axis, to nudge the warp. |
| Y Center Bias | `YBias` | Number | −1 (slider −1 to 1) | Shifts the distortion along the Y axis, used when Lock Bias X/Y is off. |
| Edges | `Edges` | Multi-button | 0: Duplicate (1: Canvas) | How the edges are filled where the distortion pulls pixels in from outside the frame. |
| Glow | `Glow` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Adds a glow to the distorted result. |
| Distort | `Distort` | Image input | | Optional vector map. When connected, its channels are used in place of the image's own vector channels. |

### Example

Warping a title with the vector channels of a second image, here a noise map used as a vector field:

```python
title = comp.AddTool('TextPlus')
title.StyledText = 'WARP'
title.Size = 0.15

vectors = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')

warp = comp.AddTool('Distort')
warp.Input = title.Output        # the picture to distort
warp.Distort = vectors.Output    # the vector map
warp.XChannel = 0                # Red drives the X movement
warp.YChannel = 1                # Green drives the Y movement
warp.XScale = 0.05
```

### Tips

- **Start with a small Scale.** Vector values are often large; a Scale of 0.1 to 1 usually keeps the distortion readable.
- **Use Flip for the wrong direction.** If the image moves the opposite way to the vectors, flip the matching channel.
- **Use Vector Motion Blur for blur.** Vector Motion Blur uses the same kind of vector map, to blur rather than warp.

**See also:** Displace, Vector Motion Blur, Drip, Grid Warp, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Vortex (`Vortex`)

**Category:** Warp · **Short name:** Vtx · **Inputs:** Input (orange), Effect Mask (blue) · **Output:** `Output` (Image)

Swirls the image around a centre point, like water going down a plughole. The area of effect is a circle set by Size,
the swirl's strength is set by Angle, and Power decides how tightly the swirl is concentrated. Animate the controls to
make the vortex move and grow.

**Use for:** a whirlpool or swirl transition, a twist in a title or logo, a distorted reveal, and a motion graphics
background that turns.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `Center` | Point | (0.5, 0.5) | Centre of the vortex on the image. |
| Size | `Size` | Number | 0.5 (slider 0–10) | Size of the area affected. Drag the circle's edge in the viewer, or use the slider. |
| Angle | `Angle` | Number | 180 (0–360°) | How far the image is rotated. A higher angle makes a stronger swirl. Drag the rotation handle in the viewer, or use the thumbwheel. |
| Power | `Power` | Number | 2 (slider −1 to 10) | Concentrates the swirl. Higher values make the vortex smaller and tighter, within the image area. |

The Settings tab and the Effect Mask are described in Common Controls.

### Example

A vortex that grows and turns over two seconds at 24 fps, centred on the frame:

```python
vtx = comp.AddTool('Vortex')
vtx.Input = media_in.Output
vtx.Center = [0.5, 0.5]
vtx.Size = comp.BezierSpline()
vtx.Size[0] = 0.1
vtx.Size[48] = 0.6
vtx.Angle = comp.BezierSpline()
vtx.Angle[0] = 0
vtx.Angle[48] = 720             # two full turns
```

### Tips

- **Give the image room.** A vortex swirls pixels from outside the text or graphic. If the input has a tight domain,
  the swirl is clipped at its edges. Use a Set Domain or a larger canvas first.
- **Animate Angle for the spin, Size for the growth.** Keep `Center` fixed while the two change, which is the usual
  look.
- **Mask the vortex.** The Effect Mask can limit the swirl to part of the frame, for example a title area.

**See also:** Dent, Drip, Lens Distort, Displace, Effect masks (Common Controls).

## Align 3D (`KD_Align3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3Aln · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Moves a 3D scene so that its bounding box lines up with the origin, on each axis you turn on. For each axis, Align Position picks which point of the box goes to the origin: −1 is the minimum face, 0 the middle and 1 the maximum face. Amount sets how far the move goes, from none to all of it. The Center transform sets the frame the box is measured in, so alignment can follow a rotated object.

**Use for:** centring a title or object on the origin before scaling or rotating it, or standing an object on the floor, so that a later transform acts on its middle or its base.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center | `CenterPositionX`, `CenterPositionY`, `CenterPositionZ`; `CenterRotationOrder`, `CenterRotationX`, `CenterRotationY`, `CenterRotationZ`; `CenterScaleLock`, `CenterScaleX`, `CenterScaleY`, `CenterScaleZ` | Transform | 0, 0, 0; XYZ; 0°; scale 1 | The frame the bounding box is measured in. Set it to rotate the frame, for example to align along a tilted surface. |
| Align X | `AlignX` | Checkbox | 0 | Aligns the scene along X. |
| Align X Position | `AlignXPosition` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | Which point of the box goes to the origin: −1 minimum face, 0 middle, 1 maximum face. |
| Align X Amount | `AlignXAmount` | Number | 1 (0–1) | How far the scene moves: 0 none, 1 all the way. |
| Align Y | `AlignY` | Checkbox | 0 | Aligns the scene along Y. |
| Align Y Position | `AlignYPosition` | Number | −1 (−1 to 1) | As for X. The default puts the bottom of the scene at the origin. |
| Align Y Amount | `AlignYAmount` | Number | 1 (0–1) | As for X. |
| Align Z | `AlignZ` | Checkbox | 0 | Aligns the scene along Z. |
| Align Z Position | `AlignZPosition` | Number | 0 (−1 to 1) | As for X. |
| Align Z Amount | `AlignZAmount` | Number | 1 (0–1) | As for X. |

### Example

A title is centred on X and Z, and stood on the floor, so later scaling and rotation act from its base.

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title['StyledText'] = 'Hello'

stand = comp.AddTool('KD_Align3D')
stand.SceneInput = title.Output
stand.AlignX = 1                 # centre on X
stand.AlignXPosition = 0
stand.AlignZ = 1                 # centre on Z
stand.AlignZPosition = 0
stand.AlignY = 1                 # bottom on the origin
stand.AlignYPosition = -1

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = stand.Output
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- The Align Y default of −1 puts the bottom on the origin, which is the usual choice for standing objects. Use 0 to centre vertically.
- Amount below 1 leaves part of the offset in place, which can be animated to slide an object into place.

**See also:** Objectify 3D, Kill 3D, Connect 3D, Transform 3D, Text 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview.

## Connect 3D (`KD_Connect3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3Con · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `ConnectionMaterialInput` (material, for the links), `VertexMaterialInput` (material, for the vertex dots) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Draws links between the vertices of a 3D scene: a rod, or an axis-aligned run of rods, for each pair it chooses. The Type decides which pairs are linked. All links every pair of vertices, Continuous makes one chain through them in a chosen order, and Edges links the vertices along each polygon's edges, which turns an object into a wireframe. Links can be thinned with Probability, filtered by colour or size with Selective, and given a Radius, a Twist or a Displace. Each link is a new object, so the output can be rendered or passed on like any other scene.

**Use for:** wireframe and cage effects on a mesh, network and string-like connections between points, and cables or threads that join objects.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `Type` | Multi-button | 0 (0: All, 1: Continuous, 2: Edges) | Which vertices are linked: every pair, one chain, or along polygon edges. |
| Shape | `Shape` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Direct, 1: Axial) | Direct makes one link per pair. Axial makes a run of rods aligned to the axes, in the order set by Axial Order. |
| Axial Order | `AxialOrder` | Multi-button | 5 (0: XYZ … 5: ZYX, 6: Random) | The axis order of an Axial link. |
| Order | `Order` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Object, 1: Clossest, 2: Random) | For Continuous only: the order of the chain. Object follows the vertices' order, Clossest picks the nearest next vertex, Random shuffles. (The live label is spelled "Clossest".) |
| Object Step | `ObjectStep` | Number | 1 (1–10) | For Object order: the chain visits every nth vertex in turn (0, n, 2n…, then 1, n+1…), so neighbours in the chain are n vertices apart. |
| Clossest Measure | `ClossestMeasure` | Multi-button | 0: XYZ, 1: XY, 2: YZ, 3: ZX, 4: X, 5: Y, 6: Z | For Clossest order: the distance used to pick the next vertex. |
| Radius | `Radius` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Thickness of the links. |
| Radius Jitter | `RadiusJitter` | Number | 0 (0–5) | Random variation in thickness. |
| Radius Relative To Particle Size | `RadiusRelativeToParticleSize` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales the link's thickness by the particle size at each end. |
| Full Radius Min, Max | `FullRadiusMin`, `FullRadiusMax` | Range | 0 to 1 | Within the Length band, the part of the length range that gets full thickness. Outside it, the link tapers. Not documented beyond the source reading. |
| Subdivision Round | `SubdivisionRound` | Number | 3 (2–10) | Roundness of the link's cross-section. |
| Length Measure | `LengthMeasure` | Multi-button | 0: XYZ, 1: XY, 2: YZ, 3: ZX, 4: X, 5: Y, 6: Z | The distance used to test link length. |
| Length Minimum, Maximum | `LengthMinimum`, `LengthMaximum` | Number | 0, 0.5 | Only links longer than Minimum and no longer than Maximum are drawn. Length is measured with Length Measure. |
| Rotation | `Rotation` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Turns each link about its own axis. |
| Twist | `Twist` | Number | 0 (0–360) | Twists each link along its length. |
| Curve | `Curve` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Bends each link. |
| Probability | `Probability` | Number | 1 (0–1) | The share of possible links that are drawn. |
| Selective | `Selective` | Combo | 0 (0: None, 1: By Color Difference, 2: By Size Difference) | Keeps only links whose two ends differ in colour or size, within Selective Minimum and Maximum. |
| Selective Color Channel | `SelectiveColorChannel` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Red, 1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Alpha, 4: Luminance) | The channel compared when Selective is By Color Difference. |
| Selective Minimum, Maximum | `SelectiveMinimum`, `SelectiveMaximum` | Number | 0.9, 1 (0–1) | The difference range that a link must fall within. |
| Selective Fade | `SelectiveFade` | Number | 0.1 (0–1) | Softens the edges of the Selective range. |
| Limit | `Limit` | Number | 100 (0–1000) | Stops drawing once the output holds this many thousand polygons. |
| Vertex Type | `VertexType` | Multi-button | 0 (0: None, 1: Points) | Points adds a sphere at each vertex. |
| Vertex Radius | `VertexRadius` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Size of the vertex spheres. |
| Vertex Subdivision | `VertexSubdivision` | Number | 3 (3–10) | Smoothness of the vertex spheres. |
| Colors | `Colors` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Keep, 1: Random, 2: Selected, 3: Jitter) | How links get their colour. Keep uses the vertices' colours. Selected uses the Color 1–64 swatches, with Number of Colors. |
| Full Color Min, Max | `FullColorMin`, `FullFullMax` | Range | 0 to 1 | Within the Length band, the part of the length range that keeps full colour. Not documented beyond the source reading. |
| Displace Amount | `DisplaceAmount` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Wave-shapes each link. Direction, Phase, Altitude and Frequency set the wave. |
| Displace Direction | `DisplaceDirectionX`, `DisplaceDirectionY`, `DisplaceDirectionZ` | Number | 0, −1, 0 (−10 to 10) | The direction of the wave's displacement. |
| Range (Min, Max, Type, Length, Overlap, Curve, Seeds) | `RangeMin`, `RangeMax`, `RangeType`, `RangeLength`, `RangeOverlap`, `RangeCurve`, `RangeSeeds` | Range and others | see Kill 3D | The sweep that fades links in or out. See Kill 3D → Range, and the Krokodove: 3D overview. |
| Material | `ConnectionMaterialInput`, `VertexMaterialInput`, `MMaterialSelect` | Material input, combo | Connection | The materials for links and vertex spheres. Material Select (0: Connection, 1: Vertex) chooses which one the Material tab edits. |

### Example

A wireframe cage: a thin link along every edge of a cube.

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')
cube['SurfaceCubeInputs.Width'] = 2           # Lock Width/Height/Depth is on, so this sets all three

cage = comp.AddTool('KD_Connect3D')
cage.SceneInput = cube.Output
cage.Type = 2                    # Edges: a link along each polygon edge
cage.Radius = 0.03

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = cage.Output
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- All links every pair, so the link count grows fast. Use Limit, Probability or Selective to keep it manageable, and check the render time before raising Limit.
- For a chain through points, use Continuous with Object order. With Object Step 2, the chain runs through every second vertex first, then the others.
- Radius relative to particle size means thick vertices make thick links. Turn that checkbox off for a constant thickness.
- The Material tab's `Connection` and `Vertex` sets are separate. Set one, then use Material Select to switch.

**See also:** Kill 3D, Align 3D, Objectify 3D, PolyPlay 3D, Cube 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Kill 3D (`KD_Kill3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3Kil · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `Region` (Region) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Removes the parts of a 3D scene that lie inside a region. Each polygon is tested at its centre against the Region, and the Range controls decide how far the removal has got, so animating the range makes objects disappear one after another. A polygon that is only partly affected, at a soft edge of the region or the range, is shrunk and faded instead of removed, using Dead Scale and Dead Opacity. See the Krokodove: 3D overview for how the Range controls work.

**Use for:** breaking up an object, such as a title or a block that dissolves into pieces, and removing geometry inside a box or sphere.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Region | `Region` | Region input | none | The region from rCube, rSphere or another region tool. Polygons inside it are killed. Unconnected, nothing is killed. |
| Dead Opacity | `DeadOpacity` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Opacity of a partly killed polygon. Fully killed polygons are removed, so this shows only at soft edges. |
| Dead Scale | `DeadScale` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Size of a partly killed polygon, relative to its centre. 1 leaves it at full size. |
| Range Type | `RangeType` | Multi-button | 0: Forward, 1: Outside In, 2: Random | The order in which polygons are reached by the range. |
| Range Min, Range Max | `RangeMin`, `RangeMax` | Range | 0 to 1 | The part of the sweep that is in play. Animate Range Max from 0 to 1 to kill the object progressively. |
| Range Length | `RangeLength` | Number | 1 (0–5) | How much of the sweep each polygon takes. Longer values make the change gentler. |
| Range Overlap | `RangeOverlap` | Number | 0 (0–1) | How much the polygons' sweeps overlap. 0 is one after another; 1 is all at once. |
| Range Seeds | `RangeSeeds` | Number | 1 (1–10) | Number of start points for Forward and Outside In. |
| Range Seeds Jitter | `RangeSeedsJitter` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Randomises the start points. |
| Range Random Seed | `RangeRandomSeed` | Number | 0 (0–32767) | Seed for the Random range type and the seeds. |
| Range Random One By One | `RangeRandomOneByOne` | Checkbox | 0 | Shuffles the order one polygon at a time, for Random. Not documented beyond that. |
| Range Curve | `RangeCurve` | Multi-button | 0: Linear, 1: Ease In, 2: Ease Out, 3: Ease In/Out | Shape of each polygon's transition. |

### Example

A cube that breaks apart: a box region removes the middle of the cube as the range sweeps in.

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')
cube['SurfaceCubeInputs.Width'] = 2           # Lock Width/Height/Depth is on, so this sets all three

box = comp.AddTool('KD_Region3DCube')
box.SoftnessX = 0.1

kill = comp.AddTool('KD_Kill3D')
kill.SceneInput = cube.Output
kill.Region = box.Output
kill.RangeType = 1                     # Outside In: the sweep starts at the edges
kill.RangeMax = comp.BezierSpline()
kill.RangeMax[0] = 0.0
kill.RangeMax[48] = 1.0

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = kill.Output
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- Dead Opacity and Dead Scale only show on polygons at a soft edge. To fade the whole object as it's killed, animate the Range instead, or use Objectify 3D with its Object Opacity.
- Set Range Length low (close to 0) for a sharp, simultaneous cut, and high for a slow ripple across the object.
- The region is tested at each polygon's centre, so a large polygon can be removed when most of it is outside the region. Use smaller geometry, such as Tube Create 3D or the subdivided Heightfield Create 3D, for finer cuts.

**See also:** Objectify 3D, PolyPlay 3D, Align 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview, Krokodove: Region overview, rCube (`KD_Region3DCube`), rSphere (`KD_Region3DSphere`), Cube 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Mapped Duplicate 3D (`KD_MappedDuplicate3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3MDup · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `MapTimeXY`, `MapTimeYZ`, `MapTimeZX`, `MapProbabilityXY`, … (images, optional; one set per control group) · **Output:** `Data3D` (DataType3D; display name "3D Data")

Makes a grid of copies of a 3D scene, arranged over a box of Size X, Y and Z, and gives each copy its own offset, rotation, scale, time and chance of appearing. Each property is driven either by a single base value or by images. The images are sampled once per grid cell, so a picture of 8 × 8 pixels can set the value of each copy in an 8 × 8 grid. The Range group fades copies in or out, and Probability decides which copies are drawn at all.

**Use for:** grids and fields of objects, such as a wall of tiles, a cloud of cubes, or a set of copies that each start at a different time.

Note the output ID: this tool outputs `Data3D`, not `Output`. Connect it as `dup.Data3D`.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicates X, Y, Z | `DuplicatesX`, `DuplicatesY`, `DuplicatesZ` | Number | 8 (1–16) each | Copies along each axis. The grid has X × Y × Z copies. |
| Size X, Y, Z | `SizeX`, `SizeY`, `SizeZ` | Number | 10 (0–100) | Size of the box the grid is spread over. The first and last copies sit at its edges. |
| Time Relative to Main Time | `TimeRelativetoMainTime` | Checkbox | 1 | On: each copy's time is the main time plus its offset. Off: the offset is applied to time zero. |
| Time Base | `TimeBase` | Number | 0 (−100 to 100) | Base time offset of every copy, in frames. |
| Times Combine | `TimesCombine` | Multi-button | 1 (0: Multiply, 1: Add, 2: Minimum, 3: Maximum) | How the time maps combine with Time Base. |
| Map Time XY, YZ, ZX | `MapTimeXY`, `MapTimeYZ`, `MapTimeZX` | Image | none | Images that set each copy's time offset, sampled per grid cell on each face. |
| Time Channel XY, YZ, ZX | `TimeChannelXY`, `TimeChannelYZ`, `TimeChannelZX` | Multi-button | 4 (0: Red, 1: Green, 2: Blue, 3: Alpha, 4: Luminance) | The channel each time map reads. |
| Time Black, White | `TimeBlack`, `TimeWhite` | Number | 0, 25 (−100 to 100) | What a map value of 0 and 1 mean, in frames. |
| Probability Base | `ProbabilityBase` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Base chance that a copy is drawn. |
| Probability Combine | `ProbabilityCombine` | Multi-button | 1 (0: Multiply, 1: Add, 2: Minimum, 3: Maximum) | How the probability maps combine with the base. See Tips. |
| Map Probability XY, YZ, ZX | `MapProbabilityXY`, `MapProbabilityYZ`, `MapProbabilityZX` | Image | none | Images that set each copy's chance of appearing. |
| Probability Channel XY, YZ, ZX | `ProbabilityChannelXY`, `ProbabilityChannelYZ`, `ProbabilityChannelZX` | Multi-button | 4 (Luminance) | The channel each probability map reads. |
| Probability Black, White | `ProbabilityBlack`, `ProbabilityWhite` | Number | 0, 1 (0–1) | What a map value of 0 and 1 mean. |
| Random Seed | `RandomSeed` | Number | 0 (0–32767) | Seed for the probability rolls. |
| Offset Base X, Y, Z | `OffsetBaseX`, `OffsetBaseY`, `OffsetBaseZ` | Number | 0 (−5 to 5) | Extra offset of every copy, in scene units. |
| Offsets Combine | `OffsetsCombine` | Multi-button | 1 (0: Multiply, 1: Add, 2: Minimum, 3: Maximum) | How the offset maps combine with the base. |
| Map Offset XY, YZ, ZX | `MapOffsetXY`, `MapOffsetYZ`, `MapOffsetZX` | Image | none | Images that set each copy's offset. |
| Offset Channel XY (Lock) | `OffsetChannelXY`, `OffsetChannelXYLock` | Multi-button, checkbox | 4: Luminance (lock on) | The channel for X, and whether Y and Z read that same channel. Turn Lock off to set `OffsetChannelXYForY` and `OffsetChannelXYForZ`. The same pattern applies to YZ and ZX. |
| Offset Black, White X, Y, Z | `OffsetBlackX`…`OffsetWhiteZ` | Number | Black 0, White 1 (−5 to 5) | What a map value of 0 and 1 mean for each axis. |
| Offset Ignore Global Size | `OffsetIgnoreGlobalSize` | Checkbox | 0 | On: the grid position is dropped, so copies are placed by offset alone. |
| Rotation Order | `RotationOrder` | Multi-button | 0 (XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX) | Order of the rotation axes. |
| Rotate Base X, Y, Z | `RotateBaseX`, `RotateBaseY`, `RotateBaseZ` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Base rotation of every copy. |
| Rotations Combine | `RotationsCombine` | Multi-button | 1 (0: Multiply, 1: Add, 2: Minimum, 3: Maximum) | How the rotation maps combine with the base. |
| Map Rotate XY, YZ, ZX | `MapRotateXY`, `MapRotateYZ`, `MapRotateZX` | Image | none | Images that set each copy's rotation. |
| Rotate Black, White X, Y, Z | `RotateBlackX`…`RotateWhiteZ` | Number | Black 0, White 360 (0–360 degrees) | What a map value of 0 and 1 mean. |
| Scale Lock XYZ | `ScaleLockXYZ` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales all three axes together. |
| Scale Base X, Y, Z | `ScaleBaseX`, `ScaleBaseY`, `ScaleBaseZ` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Base scale of every copy. |
| Scales Combine | `ScalesCombine` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Multiply, 1: Add, 2: Minimum, 3: Maximum) | How the scale maps combine with the base. |
| Map Scale XY, YZ, ZX | `MapScaleXY`, `MapScaleYZ`, `MapScaleZX` | Image | none | Images that set each copy's scale. |
| Scale Black, White X, Y, Z | `ScaleBlackX`…`ScaleWhiteZ` | Number | Black 0, White 1 (0–5) | What a map value of 0 and 1 mean. |
| Range | `RangeMin`, `RangeMax`, `RangeType`, `RangeLength`, `RangeOverlap`, `RangeCurve`, `RangeSeeds` | Range and others | see Kill 3D | Fades copies in or out by scale, in the order set by Range Type. A copy at scale 0 is removed. See Kill 3D → Range. |

### Example

A grid of 6 × 6 cubes whose sizes come from a noise image and whose start times are staggered by the same image.

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')
cube['SurfaceCubeInputs.Width'] = 0.5           # Lock Width/Height/Depth is on, so this sets all three

noise = comp.AddTool('FastNoise')

grid = comp.AddTool('KD_MappedDuplicate3D')
grid.SceneInput = cube.Output
grid.DuplicatesX = 6
grid.DuplicatesY = 6
grid.DuplicatesZ = 1
grid.SizeX = 6
grid.SizeY = 6
grid.MapScaleXY = noise.Output          # Scales Combine is Multiply, so the map shrinks copies
grid.MapTimeXY = noise.Output           # copies start at different times
grid.TimesCombine = 1                   # Add: time offsets are added to the main time

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = grid.Data3D
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- Probability is only meaningful with Probability Combine set to Multiply. With the default Add, the base of 1 plus any map value is never below 1, so every copy is drawn. Set Probability Base to 0 and use Add, or Multiply with Base 1.
- Each map is sampled at the centre of every grid cell and stretched across the grid, so its resolution doesn't matter. Use a map with blocks of flat colour for per-copy control, and a smooth one for fields.
- Each map control group has Black and White values. Set White below Black to invert a map.
- Turning Offset Ignore Global Size on lets Offset Base and the maps place every copy at the origin. Use it to stack copies, or to spread them with offsets alone.

**See also:** Kill 3D, Connect 3D, Align 3D, Objectify 3D, PolyPlay 3D, Cube 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Objectify 3D (`KD_Objectify3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3Obj · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `Region` (Region) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Moves and fades whole objects, or the elements inside them, by a transform and an opacity. A Region sets how much each object or element is affected: where the region is strongest, the object takes the full Transform and Object Opacity, and elsewhere it stays put and fully opaque. Groups are taken either by object, which treats each object in the scene as one unit, or by element, which treats each connected piece on its own.

**Use for:** moving a group of objects that sits inside a region, fading one object in a scene, and lifting or tilting the parts of a model that a region touches.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Region | `Region` | Region input | none | The region that sets the effect for each object or element. Unconnected, every object is affected at full strength. |
| Grouping | `Grouping` | Multi-button | 0 (0: By Object, 1: By Element) | Whether each object or each element is one unit. By Element tests each element's centre. |
| Object Opacity | `ObjectOpacity` | Number | 1 (0–1) | Opacity of an object at full effect. |
| Overall Transformation | `OverallTransformation` | Number | 1 (0–1) | No effect in the current source. Not documented beyond that. |
| Transform Position X, Y, Z | `TransformPositionX`, `TransformPositionY`, `TransformPositionZ` | Number | 0 (−10 to 10) | Position of a unit at full effect. |
| Transform Rotation Order | `TransformRotationOrder` | Multi-button | 0 (XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX) | Order of the rotation axes. |
| Transform Rotation X, Y, Z | `TransformRotationX`, `TransformRotationY`, `TransformRotationZ` | Number | 0 (−180 to 180 degrees) | Rotation at full effect. |
| Transform Scale Lock | `TransformScaleLock` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales all three axes together. |
| Transform Scale X, Y, Z | `TransformScaleX`, `TransformScaleY`, `TransformScaleZ` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Scale at full effect. |
| Transform Jitter | `TransformJitterPositionX`, `TransformJitterPositionY`, `TransformJitterPositionZ`, `TransformJitterRotationX`, `TransformJitterRotationY`, `TransformJitterRotationZ`, `TransformJitterScaleX`, `TransformJitterScaleY`, `TransformJitterScaleZ`, `TransformJitterScaleLock`, `TransformJitterRotationOrder`, `TransformJitterSeed` | Number | 0; scales 1 | Shown in the Inspector, but has no effect in the current source. |

The Transform block is the same kind as on Transform 3D, with its IDs prefixed `Transform`. Its effect is blended by the region: at 0 the object is untouched, at 1 the full transform applies, and in between the transform is interpolated.

### Example

A title object that tilts and lifts inside a box region, leaving the rest of the scene alone.

```python
title = comp.AddTool('Text3D')
title['StyledText'] = 'Hello'

box = comp.AddTool('KD_Region3DCube')
box.SoftnessX = 0.2

lift = comp.AddTool('KD_Objectify3D')
lift.SceneInput = title.Output
lift.Region = box.Output
lift.TransformPositionY = 0.3
lift.TransformRotationX = 25
lift.ObjectOpacity = 0.5

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = lift.Output
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- Use By Element on a model made of several parts (or a Heightfield Create 3D or Tube Create 3D output) so each part moves on its own.
- Don't use the Transform Jitter group or Overall Transformation for randomness: neither has an effect. For random variation, use a Mapped Duplicate 3D with its Offset, Rotation and Scale maps.
- The region is tested at the object's origin (By Object) or at each element's centre (By Element). A region that touches only the edge of a large object may not affect it at all.

**See also:** Poly Play 3D, Kill 3D, Mapped Duplicate 3D, Align 3D, Transform 3D, Text 3D, rCube (`KD_Region3DCube`), Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview, Common Controls → 3D objects.

## Poly Play 3D (`KD_PolyPlay3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D · **Short name:** 3PP · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D), `Region` (Region) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D)

Moves, turns, scales, extrudes and recolours the individual polygons of a 3D scene. Each polygon is handled on its own: its offset, rotation and scale are applied in a frame that is set by its normal, so "Normal Offset Z" pushes a polygon out from its face. The amount is set by the Range and by the Region at the polygon's centre, so the change happens where the region is, or as the range sweeps across the object. Each polygon can also be given a colour, from a random one, a palette, or none.

**Use for:** pushing a surface out or in, scattering and tilting the faces of a mesh, colouring a region of an object, and turning a flat cube or sphere into a faceted, exploding form.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Region | `Region` | Region input | none | The region that limits the effect. Unconnected, the whole object is affected by the Range alone. |
| Random Seed | `RandomSeed` | Number | 0 (0–32767) | Seed for the jitter values. |
| Normal Type | `NormalType` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Average, 1: Actual) | The normal used for each polygon. Average is the normalised average of its vertex normals. Actual is the polygon's own face normal. |
| Normal Offset X, Y, Z | `NormalOffsetX`, `NormalOffsetY`, `NormalOffsetZ` | Number | 0 (−2 to 2) | Offset in the polygon's frame. Z is along the face normal. |
| Normal Offset Jitter X, Y, Z | `NormalOffsetJitterX`, `NormalOffsetJitterY`, `NormalOffsetJitterZ` | Number | 0 (−2 to 2) | Random offset added to each polygon. |
| Normal Rotation Order | `NormalRotationOrder` | Multi-button | 0 (XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX) | Order of the rotation axes. |
| Normal Rotate X, Y, Z | `NormalRotateX`, `NormalRotateY`, `NormalRotateZ` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Rotation of each polygon in its own frame. |
| Normal Rotate Jitter X, Y, Z | `NormalRotateJitterX`, `NormalRotateJitterY`, `NormalRotateJitterZ` | Number | 0 (0–360 degrees) | Random rotation added to each polygon. |
| Normal Scale Lock XYZ | `NormalScaleLockXYZ` | Checkbox | 1 | Scales all three axes together. |
| Normal Scale X, Y, Z | `NormalScaleX`, `NormalScaleY`, `NormalScaleZ` | Number | 1 (0–5) | Scale of each polygon at full effect. |
| Normal Scale Jitter X, Y, Z | `NormalScaleJitterX`, `NormalScaleJitterY`, `NormalScaleJitterZ` | Number | 0 (0–5) | Random scale added to each polygon. |
| Normals Orthogonal | `NormalsOrthogonal` | Number | 0 (0–1) | Blends each vertex normal toward the polygon's face normal: 0 keeps the smooth shading, 1 makes each polygon flat. |
| Extrude | `Extrude` | Number | 0 (0–5) | Depth of an extrusion from each polygon, along its normal. 0 adds none. |
| Extrude Taper | `ExtrudeTaper` | Number | 1 (0–2) | Taper of the extrusion's sides. 1 is no taper. Not documented beyond the source reading. |
| Extrude Keep Original | `ExtrudeKeepOriginal` | Checkbox | 0 | Keeps the original polygon alongside the extruded copy. |
| Color Random Seed | `ColorRandomSeed` | Number | 0 (0–32767) | Seed for random colours and for the Jitter option. |
| Unaffected Transparent | `UnaffectedTransparent` | Checkbox | 0 | Makes polygons outside the effect fully transparent, rather than leaving them their colour. |
| Colors | `Colors` | Multi-button | 0 (0: Keep, 1: Random, 2: Selected, 3: Jitter) | How each polygon is coloured. Keep leaves its colour. Random gives a random colour. Selected picks one of the Color swatches. Jitter does nothing in this build (see Tips). |
| Number of Colors | `NumberofColors` | Number | 3 (1–63) | How many swatches Selected chooses from. |
| Color 1–64 (Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) | `Color1Red`, `Color1Green`, `Color1Blue`, `Color1Alpha` … `Color64Alpha` | Color | varied default swatches | The palette used when Colors is Selected. Only the number set in Number of Colors is used. |
| Range (Min, Max, Type, Length, Overlap, Curve, Seeds, Random One By One) | `RangeMin`, `RangeMax`, `RangeType`, `RangeLength`, `RangeOverlap`, `RangeCurve`, `RangeSeeds`, `RangeRandomOneByOne` | Range and others | see Kill 3D | Sweeps the effect across the polygons. See Kill 3D → Range. |

### Example

Polygons inside a sphere region are pushed out along their normals, turned a little and tinted red. The rest of the cube is unchanged.

```python
cube = comp.AddTool('Cube3D')
cube['SurfaceCubeInputs.Width'] = 2           # Lock Width/Height/Depth is on, so this sets all three

ball = comp.AddTool('KD_Region3DSphere')

poly = comp.AddTool('KD_PolyPlay3D')
poly.SceneInput = cube.Output
poly.Region = ball.Output
poly.NormalOffsetZ = 0.4            # pushed out along each face normal
poly.NormalRotateX = 20             # degrees, in each polygon's frame
poly.Colors = 2                     # Selected
poly.NumberofColors = 1
poly.Color1Red = 1.0
poly.Color1Green = 0.25
poly.Color1Blue = 0.1

scene = comp.AddTool('Merge3D')
scene.SceneInput1 = poly.Output
render = comp.AddTool('Renderer3D')
render.SceneInput = scene.Output
```

### Tips

- Normal Offset Z, the face normal, is the usual push. X and Y move polygons sideways across the surface. Combine with Normal Offset Jitter for a scattered look.
- A polygon's effect is measured at its centre, so a finer mesh gives a finer edge. A subdivided Heightfield Create 3D is a good source for one.
- For an exploding look, animate the Range, or animate Region's transform, rather than the offsets alone.
- Colors Jitter (3) has no effect in this build: the source marks it TODO. Use Random or Selected.
- The Range selects which polygons are extruded, all or nothing; it doesn't change how far each one is extruded. For a sweep, animate the Range so more polygons are included over time.

**See also:** Kill 3D, Objectify 3D, Connect 3D, Align 3D, Tube Create 3D, Heightfield Create 3D, rSphere (`KD_Region3DSphere`), rCube (`KD_Region3DCube`), Cube 3D, Merge 3D, Renderer 3D, Krokodove: 3D overview.

## Fold Create 3D (`KD_FoldCreate3D`)

**Category:** Krokodove: 3D Create · **Short name:** 3FldC · **Inputs:** `SceneInput` (DataType3D, optional), `MaterialInput` (material; the Material tab's basic material is used if it's empty) · **Output:** `Output` (DataType3D; display name "3D Data")

Creates a sheet of quads, divided into a grid, that folds over itself. The folds run in a sequence, set by the Type: in Parallel every strip folds the same way, in Zig Zag each strip folds the opposite way to the one before, and in Mapped each cell folds when a value in the Fold Map image reaches it. Grow In and Grow Out set how far through the fold the sheet is, so animating Grow Out from 0 to 1 unfolds it. The sheet is a 3D surface, so it can be lit, shadowed and moved with the common 3D controls.

**Use for:** origami and paper-fold reveals, accordion and pleated surfaces, and a sheet that unfolds across a scene.

| Control | ID | Type | Default / range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lock Width/Height | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.SizeLock` | Checkbox | 1 | Keeps Height equal to Width. Not shown in the Inspector; set it from script. |
| Size | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.Width` | Number | 1 (0–10) | Width of the sheet. Not shown in the Inspector; set it from script. |
| Height | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.Height` | Number | 1 (0–10) | Height of the sheet. Not shown in the Inspector; set it from script. |
| Subdivision Width, Height | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.SubdivisionWidth`, `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.SubdivisionHeight` | Number | 10 (1–40) | Number of strips in each direction. More strips make a finer fold. |
| Grow In, Grow Out | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.GrowIn`, `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.GrowOut` | Range | 0, 1 (0–1) | How far through the fold the sheet is. Grow Out at 1 leaves it fully folded out. |
| Type | `KD_DataFoldCreateInputs3D.Type` | Multi-button | 1 (0: Mapped, 1: Parallel, 2: Zig Zag) | The fold sequence. Mapped uses the Fold Map image. Mapped with no map acts as Parallel. |
